She just looks like a Barbie doll come to life—it's almost uncanny."<ref>{{cite web |last=Romanchick |first=Shane |date=April 27, 2022 |title=Margot Robbie Is 'Barbie' in First Image Revealed at CinemaCon |url=https://collider.com/barbie-margot-robbie-image/ |access-date=April 4, 2023 |website=Collider |archive-date=December 26, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226203251/https://collider.com/barbie-margot-robbie-image/ |url-status=live}}</ref> On June 15, 2022, a second still featuring Ryan Gosling as Ken was released.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Browning |first=Justine |title=Ryan Gosling is a real-life Ken doll with abs in first character photo from ''Barbie'' movie |url=https://ew.com/movies/ryan-gosling-ken-barbie-movie-first-photo/ |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=June 15, 2022 |access-date=April 4, 2023 |archive-date=December 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221215212132/https://ew.com/movies/ryan-gosling-ken-barbie-movie-first-photo/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Despite noting similarities between his look in the image and his previous roles, ''[[The Guardian]]'' asserted that "there is a very strong chance that this will be [Gosling's] defining role".<ref>{{cite news |title=Ryan Gosling as Ken in the new Barbie film is a masterstroke of casting|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Stuart|last=Heritage |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2022/jun/16/ryan-gosling-as-ken-in-the-new-barbie-film-is-a-masterstroke-of-casting|date=June 16, 2022 |access-date=April 14, 2023 |archive-date=April 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230414183246/https://amp.theguardian.com/film/2022/jun/16/ryan-gosling-as-ken-in-the-new-barbie-film-is-a-masterstroke-of-casting |url-status=live}}</ref>

In June 2023, a French ''Barbie'' poster [[went viral]] for including the tagline "Elle peut tout faire. Lui, c'est juste Ken" ("She can do everything. He's just Ken"). {{lang|fr|Ken}} is the ''[[verlan]]'' slang term for "fuck" in French—i.e. the phonological inversion of ''nique'', while ''c'est'' ("he is") is a [[homophone]] for {{lang|fr|sait}} ("he knows how")—so the tagline could also be read as "She can do everything. He just knows how to fuck." Analysts concluded that the pun was most likely intentional, as the slang term is common knowledge among French speakers; Warner Bros. would neither confirm nor deny this.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Roxborough |first=Scott |date=June 22, 2023 |title=Warner Bros. Knew Exactly What It Was Doing With That Racy French 'Barbie' Poster — Here's Why |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/warner-bros-raunchy-french-barbie-poster-meaning-1235519470/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623002343/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/warner-bros-raunchy-french-barbie-poster-meaning-1235519470/ |archive-date=June 23, 2023 |access-date=June 23, 2023 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

[[File:Barbie Billboard.jpg|thumb|alt=An all pink billboard used to promote Barbie. This image depicts a pink field, with the words 'July 21st' written in a stylized font in the bottom right-hand corner.|An all-pink billboard used to promote the film.]]
Leading up to the release, pink billboards, blank apart from the film's release date, appeared worldwide, and a real-world "[[Barbie Dreamhouse]]" in Malibu, California became available to rent through Airbnb.<ref>{{cite news |date=July 13, 2023 |title=Barbie movie: How the marketing campaign has got everyone talking |agency=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-66184513 |access-date=July 13, 2023 |archive-date=July 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713162812/https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-66184513 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Actress Margot Robbie received praise for her red carpet fashion while promoting the tour. Designers including [[Vivienne Westwood]], [[Hervé Léger]], and [[Schiaparelli (fashion house)|Schiaparelli]] created custom outfits inspired by recognizable Barbie doll clothes.<ref>{{cite news |date=2023-07-17 |title=This Barbie Is Now on Strike |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/17/style/margot-robbie-barbie-premiere-outfits.html |access-date=2026-03-27 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

magazine |last=Ford |first=Lucy |date=July 19, 2023 |title=''Barbie'' is a greater study of existential dread than ''Oppenheimer'' |url=https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/barbie-oppenheimer-review |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230721135729/https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/article/barbie-oppenheimer-review |archive-date=July 21, 2023 |access-date=July 21, 2023 |magazine=[[British GQ]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Thompson |first1=Stephen |last2=Holmes |first2=Linda |last3=Harris |first3=Aisha |last4=Choudhury |first4=Bedatri D. |last5=Katzif |first5=Mike |last6=Isaacs |first6=Anne |last7=Reedy |first7=Jessica |date=July 21, 2023 |title='Barbie' invites you into a Dream House stuffed with existential angst |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/07/12/1187344442/barbie-invites-you-into-a-dream-house-stuffed-with-existential-angst |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230721135734/https://www.npr.org/2023/07/12/1187344442/barbie-invites-you-into-a-dream-house-stuffed-with-existential-angst |archive-date=July 21, 2023 |access-date=July 21, 2023 |publisher=[[NPR]]}}</ref> Lucy Ford of ''[[GQ]]'' wrote that the film "ruminates on the very idea of what makes us human, the idea of '[[Other (philosophy)|the other]]', whether there's truly such a thing as [[autonomy]] or if we're all simply pawns to be picked up and disposed of when we are no longer useful". Ford observed that, in the film, Barbie and Ken go on "opposite but equal" journeys of self-discovery, after venturing out into the real world and learning that it is an oppressive [[patriarchal]] society as opposed to the [[Feminist utopia|matriarchal utopia]] that is Barbieland, and get "caught in the crosshairs of being both [[sentient]] and someone else's idea, battling with free will and the omnipresent predetermined rules about where to go and how to act".<ref name="Ford-2023"/> In [[Clark University]], Professor of Philosophy Wiebke Deimling compared a scene in the film, in which Barbie has to [[Red pill and blue pill|make a choice between going back to her perfect life in Barbieland or learning the truth about her existence in the real world]],<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://time.com/6295889/barbie-movie-the-matrix-the-godfather-references/ |title=An Exhaustive List of (Almost) Every Single Reference in the Barbie Movie |date=July 21, 2023 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |last=Dockterman |first=Eliana |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230906082934/https://time.com/6295889/barbie-movie-the-matrix-the-godfather-references/ |archive-date=September 6, 2023 |url-status=live |url-access=limited}}</ref> to the [[experience machine]], a [[thought experiment]] by American philosopher [[Robert Nozick]]. Diemling also observed that [[Gender performance|gender in Barbieland is performative]], noting how the Kens behave before and after a patriarchy is established.<ref>{{cite web |title=Challenge. Change. "Barbie's Existential Crisis and the Philosophy Behind it" (S03E53) |publisher=[[Clark University]] |date=July 26, 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cUjqp0S7QcA |access-date=July 27, 2023 |archive-date=July 27, 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230727034749/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cUjqp0S7QcA&gl=US&hl=en |url-status=live |via=YouTube}}</ref> Alissa Wilkinson of ''[[Vox (website)|Vox]]'' compared Barbieland to the biblical [[Garden of Eden]], with Barbie and Ken as inverted parallels of [[Adam and Eve]]. She saw Barbie and Ken's first impression "that they're suddenly self-conscious and aware of being looked at" in the real world as the film's version of [[Fall of man|the Fall]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilkinson |first=Alissa |date=July 20, 2023 |title=In the beginning, there was Barbie |url=https://www.vox.com/culture/23800753/barbie-review-bible-eden |access-date=July 21, 2023 |website=Vox |archive-date=July 21, 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230721135730/https://www.vox.com/culture/23800753/barbie-review-bible-eden |url-status=live}}</ref> Chinese film critic Li Jingfei ({{Lang|zh-HANS|李竞菲}}) compared Barbie's sudden awareness of death to the moment when [[Siddhārtha Gautama]] left the palace of his birth and first learned of suffering and death, which eventually led to his enlightenment.<ref name="Vistopia2023"/>

===Feminism===
Katie Pickles of ''[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]]'' said that ''Barbie'' shows how the matriarchy can be "as bad" as the patriarchy, with the Kens being the [[Objectification|objectified]] and [[Second-class citizen|excluded sex]] in Barbieland. Pickles further comments that the true heroes were outcasts such as Weird Barbie and Allan, who deprogrammed the Barbies from tolerating the ''status quo''. She believes that this aligns with Gerwig's conception of feminism, where "everyone stands in the sunshine".<ref>{{cite web |last=Pickles |first=Katie |date=July 21, 2023 |title=In Greta Gerwig's Barbie Land, the matriarchy can be just as bad as the patriarchy |url=https://theconversation.com/in-greta-gerwigs-barbie-land-the-matriarchy-can-be-just-as-bad-as-the-patriarchy-209317 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725082326/https://theconversation.com/in-greta-gerwigs-barbie-land-the-matriarchy-can-be-just-as-bad-as-the-patriarchy-209317 |archive-date=July 25, 2023 |website=[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]]|access-date=July 21, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Bramesco |first1=Charles |title=Barbie: the patriarchy, the existentialism, the capitalism – discuss with spoilers |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/jul/24/barbie-movie-spoilers-themes |access-date=July 30, 2023 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=July 24, 2023 |archive-date=July 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230729200055/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2023/jul/24/barbie-movie-spoilers-themes |url-status=live}}<br />{{cite news |last1=Rao |first1=Sonia |title=Why 'Barbie' and 'Oppenheimer' are the perfect double feature |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/arts-entertainment/2023/07/26/barbenheimer-barbie-oppenheimer-patriarchy/ |access-date=July 30, 2023 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=July 24, 2023 |archive-date=August 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230803185437/https://www.washingtonpost.com/arts-entertainment/2023/07/26/barbenheimer-barbie-oppenheimer-patriarchy/ |url-status=live }}<br />{{cite news |last1=Rosenblatt |first1=Kalhan |title=Why America Ferrera's 'Barbie' monologue resonates with women |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/america-ferrera-barbie-monologue-resonates-young-women-rcna96043 |access-date=July 30, 2023 |agency=[[NBC News]] |date=July 25, 2023 |archive-date=July 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230729204926/https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/america-ferrera-barbie-monologue-resonates-young-women-rcna96043 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Jack Butler of ''[[National Review]]'' rejected the perception of the film as a "shallow, man-hating, and repulsive screed" and argued that the film is instead a "[[post-feminist]] satire of what feminists imagine a perfect world looking like and of what they imagine male dominance is like", noted that in the real world, "Ken is rebuffed in all of his attempts to join the male hierarchy that purportedly dominates the world. He must return to Barbie land to institute it; what he institutes there is so shallow that it collapses almost as quickly as it is set up. Meanwhile, though Robbie's Barbie restores female dominance in Barbieland, she chooses not to stay there, electing instead to become fully human."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Butler |first=Jack |date=July 25, 2023 |title=Conservatives Are Getting Barbie Wrong |url=https://www.nationalreview.com/2023/07/conservatives-are-getting-barbie-wrong/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726122040/https://www.nationalreview.com/2023/07/conservatives-are-getting-barbie-wrong/ |archive-date=July 26, 2023 |access-date=July 26, 2023 |magazine=[[National Review]]}}</ref>

[[Ross Douthat]] writing in ''[[The New York Times]]'' argued that the film "is a movie with a feminist default, but also [has] complicated and sometimes muddled feelings about what the [[sexual revolution]] has done and where feminism ought to go". Douthat comments that the female-centric nature of Barbieland is dystopian, where men are nothing more than "arm-candy", and where pregnant women and children are marginalized. He describes the film as "against the resilient patriarchy, but wary of the [[girlboss]] alternative. It wants womanhood and motherhood, but it doesn't want the Kens back in charge, and it doesn't really know what purpose men should serve".<ref>{{cite news |last=Douthat |first=Ross |date=August 9, 2023 |title=Why Barbie and Ken Need Each Other |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/09/opinion/barbie-ken-ideology.html |url-access=registration |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231217163201/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/09/opinion/barbie-ken-ideology.html |archive-date=December 17, 2023 |access-date=December 17, 2023 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Many journalists coupled ''Barbie'' with [[the Eras Tour]] by [[Taylor Swift]] for the concurrent representation of recontextualized mainstream femininity.<ref>{{cite news |last=Faughnder |first=Ryan |date=August 15, 2023 |title=From Taylor Swift's Eras tour to 'Barbie,' women drive blockbusters. Will Hollywood notice? |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/newsletter/2023-08-15/taylor-swift-greta-gerwig-and-power-great-stuff-made-by-women-the-wide-shot |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230818213833/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/newsletter/2023-08-15/taylor-swift-greta-gerwig-and-power-great-stuff-made-by-women-the-wide-shot |archive-date=August 18, 2023 |access-date=August 19, 2023 |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref><ref name="QureshiNPR" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Steele |first1=Anne |last2=Krouse |first2=Sarah |date=August 10, 2023 |title=Women Own This Summer. [[coming-of-age]] stories marked by existential crises and bitter confrontations with sexism".<ref>{{cite news |last=Goldberg |first=Michelle |date=July 24, 2023 |title=The Hunger Fed by 'Barbie' and ===Masculinity===
In the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', Jean Guerrero presented a [[subtext]] to the film's feminist exterior, in which "a world that disregards men and their feelings is an inverted form of patriarchy and also cruel", and added: "The film is a rare product of [[mainstream culture]] that invites men to reimagine [[Gender|masculinity]] for their own sake. It acknowledges the identity crisis and loss of hope, economic promise and life purpose among American men. These struggles are often ignored by progressives, but conveniently and poisonously exploited by [[Manosphere|right-wing manfluencers]] from [[Andrew Tate]] to [[Josh Hawley]]&nbsp;... The film's reception has focused on its messages of women's empowerment, but what makes it a radical story is that it also invites women to reimagine feminism so that it doesn't ignore male struggles."<ref>{{cite news |last=Guerrero |first=Jean |date=August 4, 2023 |title=Column: The 'Barbie' movie's radical message: We all need more 'Kenpathy' |url=https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2023-08-04/beyond-being-feminist-barbie-preaches-more-kenpathy |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230806022725/https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2023-08-04/beyond-being-feminist-barbie-preaches-more-kenpathy |archive-date=August 6, 2023 |access-date=August 5, 2023 |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref>

Nicholas Balaisis contended in ''[[Psychology Today]]'' that ''Barbie'' provides a "relatively nuanced portrayal of [[masculinity]]" in two cases that resonated with issues and concerns frequent in [[clinical psychology]] and [[therapy]]: In the first case, which concerns the "over-valuation of a woman's [[gaze]] and attention on male sense of self-esteem, and even an existential sense of identity", Ken turns to patriarchal expression and masculine dominance "over other men, women or objects" because he does not receive the "sense of attractiveness, worth, and general self-value" he wants from Barbie's gaze and attention. In the second case, which concerns "the relationship to shame or existential solitude and the conversion to sex-as-soothing", when Barbie approaches Ken in the third act of the film for consolation, he interprets it as a sexual advance and tries to kiss her, which Dr. Balaisis likened to "the same way that shame can quickly morph into resentment and anger, here we see loneliness and existential angst being converted into a sexual plea — for sex to solve and resolve these bad feelings."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Balaisis |first=Nicholas |date=July 28, 2023 |title=What "Barbie" Gets Right About Male Psychology |url=https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/our-devices-our-selves/202307/what-the-movie-barbie-gets-right-about-male-psychology |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230728210613/https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/our-devices-our-selves/202307/what-the-movie-barbie-gets-right-about-male-psychology |archive-date=July 28, 2023 |access-date=July 29, 2023 |magazine=[[Psychology Today]]}}</ref>

Megan Garber of ''[[The Atlantic]]'' found that Ken and his journey of self-discovery "mimics [[adolescence]]", writing: "Like any teenager, Ken is figuring out who he is, and trying the world's possibilities on for size. But his immaturity is not contained, and this is its problem. His adolescent approach to the world, instead, inflicts itself on everyone else." Garber concluded that Ken embodies a "core idea" in the film "that patriarchy is a profound form of immaturity".<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Garber |first1=Megan |date=July 28, 2023 |title=Sympathy for the Ken |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2023/07/barbie-movie-ken/674852/ |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728134903/https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2023/07/barbie-movie-ken/674852/ |archive-date=July 28, 2023 |access-date=January 22, 2024 |magazine=[[The Atlantic]]}}</ref> Eliana Dockterman of ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' noted that Ken's radicalization resembles the [[men's rights movement]], particularly in his "feelings of [[emasculation]]", [[male fragility]] and [[evangelization]] of the patriarchy.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Dockterman |first=Eliana |date=July 21, 2023 |title=Barbie Is a Movie About Male Fragility. Let's Dig In |url=https://time.com/6287484/barbie-male-fragility-ken/ |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725140138/https://time.com/6287484/barbie-male-fragility-ken/ |archive-date=July 25, 2023 |access-date=August 5, 2023 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]}}</ref>

In August 2023, it was announced that the film would be re-released in [[IMAX]] theaters on September 22, 2023, for one week only, along with a new [[post-credit scene]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Murphy |first=J. Kim |title='Barbie' Sets Imax Release With New Post-Credits Footage |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/barbie-imax-release-new-footage-1235703431/ |access-date=August 26, 2023 |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=August 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230826094746/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/barbie-imax-release-new-footage-1235703431/ |archive-date=August 26, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> The IMAX edition starts with an onscreen introduction by Greta Gerwig, who notes the advantages of the IMAX format. ===Barbenheimer===
{{Main|Barbenheimer}}

Robert Oppenheimer]] written and directed by [[Christopher Nolan]] based on the 2005 book ''[[American Prometheus]]'', and distributed by Universal Pictures. Due to the tonal and genre contrast between the two films, many [[social media]] users created [[Internet meme|memes]] and [[irony|ironic posts]] about how the two films appealed to different ===Censorship===
====Nine-dash line controversy====
{{See also|Territorial disputes in the South China Sea|Nine-dash line}}
The controversy over the alleged appearance of the [[nine-dash line]] (a depiction of the [[South China Sea]] from Chinese perspective) in the film began when [[Vietnam]]'s film censorship authority banned the film for allegedly displaying such lines. In contrast, the counterpart from the [[Philippines]] requested that the lines in question be blurred. Both countries have banned the films ''[[Abominable (2019 film)|Abominable]]'' (2019) and ''[[Uncharted (film)|Uncharted]]'' (2022) for featuring the actual nine-dash line.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Frater|first=Patrick|date=July 3, 2023|title='Barbie' Banned in Vietnam Over Disputed Map Scene|url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/barbie-banned-vietnam-movie-warner-bros-1235660317/|magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=July 4, 2023|archive-date=July 4, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704155742/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/barbie-banned-vietnam-movie-warner-bros-1235660317/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Tartaglione |first=Nancy |title=Philippines Deliberating Permit For 'Barbie'; Senators Alternately Call For Ban, Disclaimer Over South China Sea Map Scene |url=https://deadline.com/2023/07/philippines-barbie-movie-decision-south-china-sea-controversy-1235430129/ |access-date=July 6, 2023 |website=Deadline Hollywood|date=July 5, 2023 |archive-date=July 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705144719/https://deadline.com/2023/07/philippines-barbie-movie-decision-south-china-sea-controversy-1235430129/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The nine-dash line is controversial due to maritime border disputes between China, Vietnam, Taiwan, Malaysia, Brunei, and the Philippines.<ref>{{cite news |last=Young |first=Jin Yu |title=How 'Barbie' Landed in Hot Water in Vietnam |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/04/world/asia/barbie-vietnam-south-china-sea.html |access-date=July 6, 2023 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 4, 2023 |archive-date=July 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705051533/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/04/world/asia/barbie-vietnam-south-china-sea.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

=====Vietnam=====<!--Do NOT change to 'level 4' (four equal signs on both sides). Not all users use the "Vector (2022)" skin, which does not distinguish levels 4 and 5.-->
On July 3, 2023, Vietnamese newspaper ''[[Tuổi Trẻ]]'' quoted {{ill|Vi Kiến Thành|vi}}, head of the [[Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (Vietnam)#Ministerial units|Department of Cinema]], as announcing that ''Barbie'' would be banned in Vietnam because it contained "the offending image of the nine-dash line".<ref>{{cite news |last=Nguyen |first=Phuong |date=July 3, 2023 |title=Vietnam bans 'Barbie' movie over South China Sea map |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/vietnam-bans-barbie-movie-over-south-china-sea-map-2023-07-03/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703090106/https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/vietnam-bans-barbie-movie-over-south-china-sea-map-2023-07-03/ |archive-date=July 3, 2023 |access-date=July 3, 2023 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Ly |first=Mi |date=July 3, 2023 |title=Phim Barbie bị cấm chiếu ở Việt Nam vì có hình ảnh 'đường lưỡi bò' |url=https://tuoitre.vn/phim-barbie-bi-cam-chieu-o-viet-nam-vi-co-hinh-anh-duong-luoi-bo-20230703120307715.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230706174600/https://tuoitre.vn/phim-barbie-bi-cam-chieu-o-viet-nam-vi-co-hinh-anh-duong-luoi-bo-20230703120307715.htm |archive-date=July 6, 2023 |access-date=July 6, 2023 |newspaper=[[Tuổi Trẻ]] |language=vi}}</ref> The ''[[Tiền Phong (newspaper)|Tiền Phong]]'' newspaper reported that the nine-dash line "appears multiple times in the film".<ref>{{cite news |title=Bye bye 'Barbie': Vietnam bans new movie over South China Sea map |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230703-bye-bye-barbie-vietnam-bans-new-movie-over-south-china-sea-map |access-date=July 7, 2023 |agency=[[Agence France-Presse]] |date=July 3, 2023 |via=[[France 24]] |archive-date=July 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230707123245/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230703-bye-bye-barbie-vietnam-bans-new-movie-over-south-china-sea-map |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Việt Nam cấm chiếu phim 'Barbie' vì có đường lưỡi bò |url=https://tienphong.vn/viet-nam-cam-chieu-phim-barbie-vi-co-duong-luoi-bo-post1548187.tpo scheduled to be released in Vietnam on July 21.<ref>{{cite web |last=Shackleton|first=Liz|date=July 3, 2023|title='Barbie' Banned In Vietnam Over Map Showing China's Claims In South China Sea|url=https://deadline.com/2023/07/barbie-banned-vietnam-china-nine-dash-line-1235429197/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=July 4, 2023|archive-date=July 4, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704155742/https://deadline.com/2023/07/barbie-banned-vietnam-china-nine-dash-line-1235429197/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Speaking to [[Voice of America]], Trịnh Hữu Long (founder of the research group Legal Initiatives for Vietnam) said, "The censors will even be praised for overreacting to the unclear map, by both their superiors and the public, because anti-China sentiment runs deep into the country's political culture", and that "the government is surely using legitimate nationalist reasoning to strengthen its entire censorship system", while Michael Caster at the free expression group [[Article 19]] said, "Maps are political, and borders often bear historical wounds, but rather than ensuring free and open discussion, the knee jerk response to censor seldom supports historical or transitional justice".<ref>{{cite news |last=Scott |first=Liam |title=No Barbie Girl in Vietnam's World |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/no-barbie-girl-in-vietnam-s-world-/7171971.html |access-date=July 14, 2023 |agency=[[Voice of America]] |date=July 8, 2023 |archive-date=July 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710031444/https://www.voanews.com/a/no-barbie-girl-in-vietnam-s-world-/7171971.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Speaking to ''[[Vox (website)|Vox]]'', [[University of California, Berkeley]] professor Peter Zinoman said, "To the Chinese, the nine-dash line signifies their legitimate claims to the South China Sea", and "to the Vietnamese, it symbolizes a brazen act of imperialist bullying that elevates Chinese national interest over an older shared set of interests of socialist brotherhood". [[Harvard University]] professor {{Interlanguage link|Huệ-Tâm Hồ Tài|vi|Hồ Tài Huệ Tâm}} said since the producers of the film were aiming for the [[Mainland China|mainland Chinese]] market in the hopes that it would be a blockbuster, "they are ready to accept [mainland China's] view of geography. Disinformation works by repetition". [[New York University]] professor Kevin Li said, "In my view, banning [''Barbie''] was a no-brainer."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Brinkhof |first1=Tim |title=How Hollywood appeases China, explained by the Barbie movie |url=https://www.vox.com/culture/2023/7/13/23791805/barbie-map-nine-dash-line-vietnam-china |access-date=July 20, 2023 |website=[[Vox (website)|Vox]] |date=July 13, 2023 |archive-date=July 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720064228/https://www.vox.com/culture/2023/7/13/23791805/barbie-map-nine-dash-line-vietnam-china |url-status=live}}</ref> In response to Vietnam's ban, [[Chinese Foreign Ministry]] spokesperson [[Mao Ning (diplomat)|Mao Ning]] stated at a press briefing on July 4 that the "South China Sea issue" should not be linked with "normal cultural exchange".<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng/xwfw_665399/s2510_665401/202307/t20230704_11107557.html |title=Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning's Regular Press Conference on July 4, 2023 |publisher=[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China]] |date=July 4, 2023 |access-date=August 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230812131146/https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng/xwfw_665399/s2510_665401/202307/t20230704_11107557.html |archive-date=August 12, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=====Philippines=====<!--Do NOT change to 'level 4' (four equal signs on both sides). Not all users use the "Vector (2022)" skin, which does not distinguish levels 4 and 5.-->
When news of Vietnam's ban reached the Philippines, Senator [[Francis Tolentino]], vice chairman of the [[Philippine Senate Committee on Foreign Relations]], told [[CNN Philippines]] that ''Barbie'' may also be banned in the country because it "denigrates" Filipino sovereignty.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Brzeski |first=Patrick |title=The Philippines Threatens to Join Vietnam in Banning 'Barbie' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/philippines-barbie-ban-vietnam-1235529421/ |access-date=July 7, 2023 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=July 5, 2023 |archive-date=July 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711011044/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/philippines-barbie-ban-vietnam-1235529421/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Senator [[Jinggoy Estrada]] called the film to be banned over the alleged inclusion of the nine-dash line; opposition senator [[Risa Hontiveros]] quipped "the movie is fiction, and so is the nine-dash line", and suggested adding a disclaimer to the film instead of banning its release.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cayabyab |first=Marc Jayson |title=Senators want 'Barbie' film banned over 9-dash-line scenes |url=https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2023/07/05/2278720/senators-want-barbie-film-banned-over-9-dash-line-scenes |access-date=July 5, 2023 |newspaper=[[The Philippine Star]] |date=July 5, 2023 |archive-date=July 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230706174627/https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2023/07/05/2278720/senators-want-barbie-film-banned-over-9-dash-line-scenes |url-status=live}}</ref> Senator [[Robin Padilla]], chairman of the [[Philippine Senate Committee on Public Information and Mass Media|Senate mass media committee]], suggested that the film producers must edit out references to the nine-dash line or risk the film being banned.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1797622/padilla-suggests-cutting-out-of-chinas-9-dash-line-claim-from-barbie-film/amp |title=Padilla suggests cutting China's 9-dash line scene from 'Barbie' film |first=Beatrice |last=Pinlac |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |date=July 5, 2023 |access-date=July 5, 2023 |archive-date=July 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230706174607/https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1797622/padilla-suggests-cutting-out-of-chinas-9-dash-line-claim-from-barbie-film/amp |url-status=live}}</ref>

and that there was no clear nor outright depiction of the nine-dash line, as the line in the film was "not U-Shaped" and had "eight dots or dashes" instead of nine.<ref>{{cite news |last=Abarca |first=Charie Mae |title=MTRCB allows screening of controversial 'Barbie' film in PH cinemas |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Tan |first=Clement |date=July 13, 2023 |title=Philippines allows 'Barbie' movie to be screened, calls China map 'cartoonish' gave the film a PG rating, as well as allowing it to be screened in the country, however they requested Warner Bros. to "blur the controversial lines in order to avoid further misinterpretations".<ref>{{cite news |last=Garner |first=Jom |title=MTRCB greenlights showing of 'Barbie' in Phl Tribune]] |date=July 11, 2023 |archive-date=July 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713044854/https://tribune.net.ph/2023/07/11/mtrcb-rejects-calls-to-prohibit-the-distribution-and-showing-of-the-barbie-movie/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Bacelonia |first=Wilnard |title=MTRCB to solon: No basis to ban 'Barbie' movie |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1205413 |access-date=July 12, 2023 =====World map drawing and Warner Bros.' statement=====<!--Do NOT change to 'level 4' (four equal signs on both sides). Not all users use the "Vector (2022)" skin, which does not distinguish levels 4 and 5.-->
[[File:Barbie Land Real World Map.png|thumb|Following the news of Vietnam's ban of the film, some media outlets pointed to a scene in the film's trailer featuring a drawing of a world map with a curved line of dashes alongside "Asia" which they said represented China's nine dash line claim to the South China Sea. Warner Bros. stated that it was "not intended to make any type of statement".]]
With the rising concerns over the alleged appearance of the nine-dash line, several media outlets pointed to a drawing of a world map which appears in a trailer for the film.<ref ====Religious interpretation and LGBTQ+ themes====
In some [[Muslim-majority countries]], there were attempts to ban the film on moral grounds or for allegedly showing LGBTQ+ themes. Some of them were successful.<ref>{{cite news |last=Brown |first=Anna |title=Barbie in the Middle East |url=https://www.washingtoninstitute.org/policy-analysis/barbie-middle-east |access-date=March 17, 2024 |newspaper=[[The Washington Institute for Near East Policy]] |date=September 8, 2023 |url-status=live |archive-date=March 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240317141453/https://www.washingtoninstitute.org/policy-analysis/barbie-middle-east}}</ref>

=====Pakistan=====<!--Do NOT change to 'level 4' (four equal signs on both sides). Not all users use the "Vector (2022)" skin, which does not distinguish levels 4 and 5.-->
In [[Pakistan]], the film was released nationwide on July 21, 2023.<ref name="GeoNews-23JUL25-BarbieInPunjab">{{cite news |last1=Khalid |first1=Nadia |title=Punjab censor board cleared Barbie. In the [[Middle East]], the film was initially scheduled to be released on July 19, 2023, before being delayed to August 31.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Rubin |first1=Rebecca |title='Barbie' Sets Release in Saudi Arabia and More Territories After Potential Ban in Middle East |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/barbie-theatrical-release-middle-east-potential-ban-1235690791/ |access-date=August 10, 2023 |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=August 8, 2023 |archive-date=August 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810110340/https://variety.com/2023/film/news/barbie-theatrical-release-middle-east-potential-ban-1235690791/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Later, [[Majid Al Futtaim Group#Cinemas|Vox Cinemas]], the distributor of Warner Bros. films in the region, announced that the film would be released in the region on August 10.<ref name="AP-23AUG04-BarbieMiddleEast">{{cite news |title=Initially delayed, the 'Barbie' movie is now set to be released in the United Arab Emirates |url=https://apnews.com/article/barbie-movie-release-united-arab-emirates-ea69e4ee144be1c1d8d53cd2920fb1db |access-date=August 10, 2023 |work=[[Associated Press News]] |date=August 4, 2023 |archive-date=August 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230804110604/https://apnews.com/article/barbie-movie-release-united-arab-emirates-ea69e4ee144be1c1d8d53cd2920fb1db |url-status=live}}</ref> Although the film censorship authorities in the region initially did not specify any reason, it was suggested that the inclusion of a [[transgender]] actress in one of the Barbie roles, and the narrations and dialogs related to LGBTQ+ matters might have been the issues with the film.<ref name="AP-23AUG04-BarbieMiddleEast"/>

scope of Interior Ministry's [[General Directorate of General Security|General Security]]) to review the film and give its recommendation.<ref name="Reuters-23AUG09-BarbieLebanonKuwait"/><ref ==Reception==
===Box office===
''Barbie'' grossed $636.8&nbsp;million in the United States and Canada, and $810.9&nbsp;million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $1.448&nbsp;billion.<ref name="BOM"/><ref name="NUM"/> This was described by [[Warner Bros.]] as "reaching a Barbillion".<ref>{{cite news |date=August 7, 2023 |title=Barbie film hits $1 billion at global box office |work=[[Newsround]] |url=https://www.bbc.com/newsround/66426228 |access-date=October 19, 2023 |archive-date=October 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231027150118/https://www.bbc.co.uk/newsround/66426228 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' calculated the film's net profit as $421{{nbsp}}million, accounting for production budgets, marketing, talent participations, and other costs; box office grosses, television and streaming, and home media revenues placed it second on their list of 2023's "Most Valuable Blockbusters".<ref>{{cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=May 6, 2024 |title='Barbie' Struts To No. 2 In ''Deadline''{{'s}} 2023 Most Valuable Blockbuster Tournament |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/barbie-movie-profits-1235902885/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240506195447/https://deadline.com/2024/05/barbie-movie-profits-1235902885/ |archive-date=May 6, 2024 |access-date=May 6, 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

It was described as a "record-breaking" box office success during its opening weekend,<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=July 23, 2023 |title=Box Office: 'Barbie' Opens to Record-Setting $155 Million, 'Oppenheimer' Shatters Expectations With $80 Million Debut |access-date=July 23, 2023 |magazine=Variety}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Barker |first1=Stephen |last2=Walters |first2=Jack |date=June 19, 2023 |title=Barbie 2: Sequel Set-Up, If It's Greenlit & Everything We Know |url=https://screenrant.com/barbie-2-cast-story-details-updates/ |url-status=live ====Other territories====

Outside of the United States and Canada, ''Barbie'' earned $194.3&nbsp;million from 69 offshore markets in its opening weekend. Of the 69 markets, it was the number one film for the weekend in 58, scored the largest opening weekend for a Warner Bros. film in 26 and marked the largest opening for a 2023 film in 24. In the United Kingdom, the film opened with $24.2&nbsp;million, which was the year's largest opening. In France, it opened with $10.2&nbsp;million, marking the largest debut for a Warner Bros. film since ''[[Joker (2019 film)|Joker]]'' (2019).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Tartaglione |first1=Nancy |title='Barbie' An Even Bigger Knockout With $356M+ Global Bow, 'Oppenheimer' Increases Genius To $180M+ WW Launch – International Box Office Actuals Update |url=https://deadline.com/2023/07/barbie-oppenheimer-barbenheimer-christopher-nolan-cillian-murphy-margot-robbie-ryan-gosling-gloabl-international-box-office-1235443180/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |date=July 24, 2023 |access-date=July 24, 2023 |archive-date=July 26, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726083458/https://deadline.com/2023/07/barbie-oppenheimer-barbenheimer-christopher-nolan-cillian-murphy-margot-robbie-ryan-gosling-gloabl-international-box-office-1235443180/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The following weekend, ''Barbie'' earned $127&nbsp;million, dropping by just 31%. It remained the number one film of the weekend in 57 markets. In Australia, the film scored the largest second week ever, for a running total of $30.6&nbsp;million after two weekends. In the UK, ''Barbie'' began outpacing the ten-day total of ''Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2'', Warner Bros.' highest-grossing film in the country, in its second weekend.<ref>{{cite news |last=Tartaglione |first=Nancy |date=July 30, 2023 |title='Barbie' Pirouettes To Powerhouse $775M Global; In Japan, ''Barbie'' ranked at no. 16.<ref>{{cite news |first=Suzanne | last=Kuwata |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/commentary/2023/08/23/japan/barbie-japan/ |title=Why is the 'Barbie' movie bombing in Japanese theaters? |newspaper=[[The Japan Times]] |date=August 23, 2023 |access-date=August 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829194245/https://www.japantimes.co.jp/commentary/2023/08/23/japan/barbie-japan/ |archive-date=August 29, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> Prior to the release date, public opinion of ''Barbie'' had soured after the official Twitter account for the ''Barbie'' film had responded positively to several Barbenheimer memes, all of which depicted atomic bombing mushroom clouds comically. This was seen as an endorsement of such jokes, and, in turn, was met with disapproval from the Japanese public, who criticized their ignorance, particularly due to their negligence towards the history of the [[atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki]]. [[Mitsuki Takahata]], who provided Barbie's voice in the Japanese dub of the film, stated on her [[Instagram]] account that she was disappointed and had considered dropping out of one of the film's promotional events.<ref>{{cite news | first=Rocky | last=Swift | url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-opening-barbie-marred-by-controversy-ahead-nuclear-memorials-2023-08-03/ | title=Japan opening of 'Barbie' marred by controversy ahead of nuclear memorials | work=[[Reuters]] | date=August 3, 2023 | access-date=August 28, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230803133850/https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japan-opening-barbie-marred-by-controversy-ahead-nuclear-memorials-2023-08-03/ |archive-date=August 3, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In China, ''Barbie'' earned more than $32 million as of August 2023.<ref>{{cite news | first=Larissa | last=Gao | url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/barbie-movie-china-patriarchy-feminism-backlash-government-crackdown-rcna99172 | title='Barbie' triggers heated discussions over patriarchy and feminism in China | agency=[[NBC News]] | date=August 13, 2023 | access-date=December 28, 2023 | archive-date=December 28, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231228154942/https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/barbie-movie-china-patriarchy-feminism-backlash-government-crackdown-rcna99172 | url-status=live}}</ref>

===Critical response===
''Barbie'' attained widespread critical acclaim.{{efn|Attributed to multiple references:<ref>{{cite web |last=Coyle |first=Jake |date=July 25, 2023 |title='Barbenheimer' box office shows audiences want more movies without a Jedi or superhero |url=https://fortune.com/2023/07/25/barbenheimer-box-office-audiences-want-more-movies-without-jedi-superhero/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230802165125/https://fortune.com/2023/07/25/barbenheimer-box-office-audiences-want-more-movies-without-jedi-superhero/ |archive-date=August 2, 2023 |access-date=August 14, 2023 |website=Fortune}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Stern |first=Marlow |date=August 9, 2023 |title=Bill Maher's 'Barbie' Movie Review Is a Total Embarrassment |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/bill-maher-barbie-movie-review-twitter-patriarchy-lame-1234803114/ |access-date=August 16, 2023 |magazine=Rolling Stone |quote=The movie was released to near-universal critical acclaim and has grossed over $1 billion worldwide, making Gerwig the first solo female director with a billion-dollar movie. |archive-date=August 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230816220607/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/bill-maher-barbie-movie-review-twitter-patriarchy-lame-1234803114/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=July 22, 2023 |title=Barbie vs Oppenheimer at Box Office: Who won at the preview and what else now? The website's consensus reads, "''Barbie'' is a visually dazzling comedy whose meta humor is smartly complemented by subversive storytelling."<ref>{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes |id=barbie |type=movie |accessdate=August 13, 2026}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 80 out of 100, based on 67 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{Cite Metacritic |id=barbie |type=movie |access-date=August 13, 2026}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "A" on an A+ to F scale, while those polled by [[PostTrak]] gave it an 89% overall positive score, with 79% saying they would definitely recommend the film.<ref name="Deadline-Previews"/>

In his review for the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', [[Michael Phillips (critic)|Michael Phillips]] called ''Barbie'' "a lovely, eccentrically imaginative example of brand extension and raw, untrammeled commercialism", applauded the production design, and summed: "The crucial partnership here is the one between director and performer, Gerwig and Robbie; anything Gerwig and Baumbach's verbally dexterous script requires, from Barbie's first teardrop to the final punchline, Robbie handles with unerring precision."<ref>{{cite news |date=July 18, 2023 |title="Barbie" review: A doll's life is richly imagined |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/movies/sc-ent-barbie-movie-review-0719-20230718-skedihtmx5ctbgm5psx72kwhqi-story.html |access-date=July 19, 2023 |newspaper=Chicago Tribune |archive-date=July 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230718225946/https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/movies/sc-ent-barbie-movie-review-0719-20230718-skedihtmx5ctbgm5psx72kwhqi-story.html |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Richard Brody]] of ''[[The New Yorker]]'' called it "brilliant, beautiful and fun as hell", claiming the "giddily stylized vision of a doll coming to life makes a serious case for the art of adapting even the most sanitized [[Intellectual property|I.P.]]" and commended the "free and wild" direction as well as the "profuse and exquisite" visual aesthetics.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Brody |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Brody |date=July 21, 2023 |title="Barbie" Is Brilliant, Beautiful, and Fun as Hell |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] the ''[[Evening Standard]]'' hailed the film as "easily the comedy of the year" with a large amount of fun, where "star and producer Margot Robbie, and writer-director Greta Gerwig, have done themselves proud" with a "breezily outrageous" film "about a woman's right to be 'weird, dark and crazy'".<ref>{{cite news |last=O'Sullivan |first=Charlotte |date=July 20, 2023 |title=Barbie review: |url-status=live}}</ref> Eileen Jones of ''[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]]'' said that the film "manages to overcome cumbersome plotting and feminist pieties to provide a delightful spectacle of funny moments that add up to something pretty good".<ref>{{cite web |last=Jones |first=Eileen |date=July 24, 2023 |title=It's Kind of Amazing That Barbie Manages to Be as Good as It Is |magazine=[[Jacobin (magazine)|Jacobin]]}}</ref>

In ''[[The Guardian]]'', [[Peter Bradshaw]] awarded ''Barbie'' a three out of five stars, describing it as "beamingly affectionate and deliriously pink-themed" but "perhaps a giant two-hour commercial for a product" and highlighted Gosling as a scene-stealer, being given "all the best lines".<ref>{{cite news |title=Barbie review – Ryan Gosling is plastic fantastic in ragged doll comedy |url=https://theguardian.com/film/2023/jul/19/barbie-review-greta-gerwig-delirious-bubblegum-fantasy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720064227/https://theguardian.com/film/2023/jul/19/barbie-review-greta-gerwig-delirious-bubblegum-fantasy |archive-date=July 20, 2023 |access-date=July 19, 2023 |newspaper=The Guardian|date=July 19, 2023 |last1=Bradshaw |first1=Peter}}</ref>

Lovia Gyarke of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' called the film a "tricky balancing act of corporate fealty and subversion" lauding Gerwig's direction, the set design, costumes, soundtrack and lead performances, but criticizing the "muddled politics and flat emotional landing".<ref name="thrreview"/> [[Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] critic Peter Debruge praised the humor for giving "permission to challenge what Barbie represents" and lauded Gosling's physical performance, but concluded that the film is "an intellectual experience, not an emotional one, grounded largely in audience nostalgia".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Debruge |first=Peter |date=July 18, 2023 |title='Barbie' Review: Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling Compete for Control of High-Concept Living Doll Comedy |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230719033819/https://variety.com/2023/film/reviews/barbie-review-margot-robbie-ryan-gosling-1235672349/ |archive-date=July 19, 2023 |access-date=July 19, 2023 |magazine=Variety}}</ref> In the ''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]'' component of ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'', Alison Willmore commended the lead performances, particularly that of Robbie, whom she characterized "as capable of heartbreaking earnestness as humor, and who sometimes effortlessly achieved both at once", but lamented the themes of the film, opining that it "doesn't ultimately want to do much more than talk itself in circles about these themes".<ref>{{cite web |last=Willmore |first=Alison |date=July 18, 2023 |title=We Shouldn't Have to Grade Barbie on a Curve |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/barbie-review-we-shouldnt-have-to-grade-this-on-a-curve.html |url-access=limited |url-status=live 2023 |website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]}}</ref> On a similar note, [[Stephanie Zacharek]] of [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']] praised Robbie's "buoyant, charming performance", Gosling's "go-for-broke" effort, and the "inventive production design", but criticized the "self aware" nature of the film especially following the first half-hour, concluding that it is a feminist film "only in the most scattershot way", and that it is not "subversive".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Zacharek |first=Stephanie |author-link=Stephanie Zacharek |date=July 18, 2023 |title=''Barbie'' Is Very Pretty But Not Very Deep |url=https://time.com/6295639/barbie-movie-review/ |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721171633/https://time.com/6295639/barbie-movie-review/ found that the "doll drowned herself in kitsch derision" while ''[[GQ]]''-France, regretting that the film did not prove as radical as might have been expected, found it was somehow a continuation of ''[[Little Women (2019 film)|Little Women]]''.<ref>{{cite web |date=2023-07-19 |title=Le monde est sauvé : Barbie est un bon film |url=https://www.gqmagazine.fr/article/barbie-critique-film-margot-robbie-ryan-gosling-greta-gerwig |access-date=2024-03-10 |website=GQ France |language=fr-FR |archive-date=March 10, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240310002220/https://www.gqmagazine.fr/article/barbie-critique-film-margot-robbie-ryan-gosling-greta-gerwig |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Camilla Long]] of ''[[The Times]]'' wrote that the film featured Mattel's "pink, squealing, corporate grasping", trying to be "ahead of the [[sexism]] curve", but "ended up feeling sexist itself" for its portrayal that "men are stupid, go to the gym, run everything and don't care about women, while women are sensible, striving but ultimately conflicted victims".<ref>{{cite news |last=Long |first=Camilla |date=July 24, 2023 |title=Barbie is a hot pink, sexist mess of a film |newspaper=[[The Times]] |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/barbie-is-a-hot-pink-sexist-mess-of-a-film-n6gm8b6p6 |access-date=July 25, 2023 |issn=0140-0460 |archive-date=October 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007194748/https://www.thetimes.com/culture/film/article/barbie-is-a-hot-pink-sexist-mess-of-a-film-n6gm8b6p6 |url-status=live}}</ref> In the review by [[Kyle Smith (critic)|Kyle Smith]] in ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', he stated: "As bubbly as the film appears, its script is like a grumpier-than-average women's studies seminar", exemplified by the Mattel employee character's "long monologue on how miserable it is to be female".<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Kyle |title='Barbie' Review: Beyond Her Ken |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/barbie-review-margot-robbie-greta-gerwig-ryan-gosling-mattel-256b6688 |access-date=July 26, 2023 |newspaper=Wall Street Journal |date=July 18, 2023 |archive-date=July 26, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726232101/https://www.wsj.com/articles/barbie-review-margot-robbie-greta-gerwig-ryan-gosling-mattel-256b6688 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[MovieWeb]] ranked it number 1 on its list of the "Best Comedy Movies of the 2020s (So Far)", writing that "Gerwig's ode to the Barbie girl and her Barbie world&nbsp;... is as surprisingly modern and introspective as audiences have come to expect from her work. Scrunching 60 plus years of history into a two-hour time frame aside, this film gets straight at the heart of what it's like being a woman today while providing more than a laugh or two in the process."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://movieweb.com/comedy-movies-2020s/#barbie-2023|title=Best Comedy Movies of the 2020s (So Far), Ranked|publisher=MovieWeb|date=August 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230830125206/https://movieweb.com/comedy-movies-2020s/#barbie-2023|archive-date=August 30, 2023|url-status=live|access-date=August 19, 2023}}</ref> Chinese film critic Li Jingfei ({{Lang|zh-HANS|李竞菲}}) praised the film's humor and criticism of patriarchy, qualifying that its themes were too often advanced by slogans rather than the experiences of its characters.<ref name="Vistopia2023">{{cite web |last=Li |first=Jingfei |script-title=zh:《芭比》，我们超爱 |trans-title=Barbie, we love it |script-work=zh:去电影院的路上 |publisher=Vistopia ({{Lang|zh-HANS|看理想}}) |via=[[The Paper (newspaper)|The Paper]] |date=July 28, 2023 |url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_23994020 |language=zh-CN |access-date=August 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230803185318/https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_23994020 |archive-date=August 3, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Filmmakers such as [[Allison Anders]], [[Joe Dante]], [[Drew Goddard]], [[Chad Hartigan]], [[Rachel Morrison]] and [[Paul Schrader]] also cited the film as among their favorites of 2023.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 31, 2023 |title=38 Directors Pick Their Favorite Films of 2023 |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-best-movies-tv-2023|website=IndieWire}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Flat |first1=Chris |title=65 Directors Pick Their Favorite Films of 2024 |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/directors-pick-best-films-2024/ |access-date=30 December 2024 |work=IndieWire |date=30 December 2024}}</ref>

In June 2025, ''[[IndieWire]]'' ranked the film at number 46 on its list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far)."<ref>{{cite web |date=June 16, 2025 |title=The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far)|url=https://www.indiewire.com/lists/best-movies-2020s/ |access-date=2025-06-23}}</ref> In July 2025, it ranked number 84 on the "Readers' Choice" edition of ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century."<ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |date=July 2, 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref>

==Future==
===Sequel===
On July 25, 2023, following ''Barbie''{{'}}s premiere, Gerwig stated she had no plans for a sequel.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Thomas |first=Carly |date=2023-07-26 |title=Greta Gerwig on a Potential 'Barbie' Sequel, Film's Criticism |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/greta-gerwig-barbie-potential-sequel-film-criticism-1235545212/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |magazine=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> On August 4, it was reported that Gerwig, co-writer Baumbach, and stars Robbie and Gosling had been contracted for only one film.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Kit |first=Borys |date=2023-08-04 |title='Barbie' Is About to Be a $1 Billion Movie, But Has No Sequel in Sight |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/barbie-margot-robbie-ryan-gosling-sequel-1235550788/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |magazine=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> On December 13, 2024, ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' reported that a sequel had entered early development, with Gerwig and Baumbach set to return. Representatives for Warner Bros., Gerwig, and Baumbach denied the claim.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Gardner |first=Chris |date=2024-12-13 |title='Barbie' Sequel in "Early Stages" as Greta Gerwig and Noah Baumbach Settle on Story Idea (Exclusive) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/barbie-sequel-status-greta-grewig-noah-baumbach-warner-bros-1236083434/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |magazine=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> On July 31, 2026, ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that a sequel had entered early talks, with Robbie, Gosling, and Gerwig in negotiations to return; however, talks were stalled as [[David Zaslav]] was reportedly unwilling to pay the salaries being negotiated for their return. Additionally, Warner Bros. is reportedly scrambling to reach a deal for the potential sequel by December 2026, before the ''Barbie'' rights revert to Mattel.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sperling |first=Nicole |date=2026-07-31 |title=Will 'Barbie' Get a Sequel? Warner Bros. Is Scrambling to Reach a Deal. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/31/business/media/barbie-sequel-warner-bros-mattel.html |access-date=2026-07-31 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> On August 12, 2026, ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' reported that Gerwig, Robbie, and Gosling had all rejected at least six offers from Warner Bros. for the sequel, and it was unlikely a deal would be reached before Mattel regained the ''Barbie'' rights.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Donnelly |first=Matt |date=2026-08-12 |title='Barbie 2' in Crisis: Sequel Could Be Shelved Amid Pay Battle and Crumbling Deal Talks |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/barbie-2-paused-gerwig-robbie-failed-deals-sequel-1236833075/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> On September 13, 2026, Mattel Studios head Robbie Brenner expressed interest in a sequel but stated that the studio was currently more focused on developing the animated adaptation, stating, “We all want to see the ''Barbie'' sequel; I want to see it too. I’m sure at some point, one day, there will be one.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarke |first=Stewart |date=2026-09-13 |title=Mattel Studios Boss Says "We All Want To See The Barbie Sequel" |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/mattel-studios-boss-wants-to-see-a-barbie-sequel-1237100871/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> On October 2, 2026, ''Variety'' reported that [[David Ellison]] was moving forward with plans to revive the sequel following [[Paramount Skydance]]'s [[Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance|acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Angelique |date=2026-10-02 |title=Skydance Shuffle: David Ellison Addresses Troops About New Name, Says Adieu to Mike and Pam and Sets Table for ‘Barbie 2’ |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/david-ellison-skydance-name-mike-pam-barbie-2-1236897929/ |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Animated adaptation===
In July 2025, it was reported that [[Illumination (company)|Illumination]] and [[Mattel Studios]] finalized a deal to develop a theatrical animated Barbie film with [[Universal Pictures]] set to distribute. The project is not intended to be connected to the live-action film.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2025/07/barbie-animated-feature-illumination-mattel-studios-close-deal-1236461077/|title='Barbie' Animated Feature In Works From Illumination & Mattel Studios |first=Matt|last=Grobar|date=July 17, 2025|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

'''''Boys Don't Cry''''' is a 1999 American biographical [[drama film]] directed by [[Kimberly Peirce]], and co-written by Peirce and Andy Bienen. The film is a dramatization of the real-life story of [[Brandon Teena]] (played by [[Hilary Swank]]), an American [[trans man]] who attempts to find himself and love in [[Nebraska]] but falls victim to a brutal [[hate crime]] perpetrated by two male acquaintances. The film co-stars [[Chloë Sevigny]] as Brandon's girlfriend, Lana Tisdel.

After reading about the case while in college, Peirce conducted extensive research for a screenplay, which she worked on for almost five years. The film focuses on the relationship between Brandon and Lana. The script took dialogue directly from archive footage in the 1998 documentary ''[[The Brandon Teena Story]]''.<ref>[http://filmmakermagazine.com/archives/issues/fall1999/boys.php Kimberly Peirce profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150922094632/http://filmmakermagazine.com/archives/issues/fall1999/boys.php |date=September 22, 2015 }}</ref> Many actresses sought the lead role during a three-year casting process before Swank was cast. Swank was chosen because her personality seemed similar to Brandon's. Most of the film's characters were based on real-life people; others were [[composite character|composites]].

Filming occurred during October and November 1998 in the [[Dallas]], Texas area. The producers initially wanted to film in [[Falls City, Nebraska]], where the real-life events had taken place; however, budget constraints meant that [[principal photography]] had to occur in Texas. The film's cinematography uses dim and artificial lighting throughout and was influenced by a variety of styles, including [[Neorealism (art)|neorealism]] and the films of [[Martin Scorsese]], while the soundtrack consisted primarily of [[country music|country]], [[blues music|blues]], and [[rock music|rock]] music. The film's themes include the nature of [[Romance (love)|romantic]] and [[Platonic love|platonic]] relationships, the causes of [[violence against LGBTQ people]], especially [[transgender]] people, and the relationship among [[social class]], [[race (human categorization)|race]], and [[gender]].

The film premiered at the [[New York Film Festival]] on October 8, 1999, before appearing at various other film festivals. Distributed by [[Fox Searchlight Pictures]], the film received a [[limited release]] in the United States on October 22, 1999, and it performed well at the North American box office, gaining three times its production budget by May 2000. The film was acclaimed by critics, with many ranking it as one of the best films of the year; praise focused on the lead performances by Swank and Sevigny as well as the film's depiction of its subject matter. However, some people who had been involved with Brandon in real life criticized the film for not portraying the events accurately.

''Boys Don't Cry'' was nominated for multiple awards; at the [[72nd Academy Awards]] in 2000, Swank was awarded the [[Academy Award for Best Actress]] and Sevigny was nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]]. The pair were also nominated at the [[57th Golden Globe Awards]], with Swank winning the [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama|Best Actress – Drama]] award. ''Boys Don't Cry'', which dealt with controversial issues,<ref name="Levy">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/1999/film/reviews/boys-don-t-cry-1117752076/ |title=Review: Boys Don't Cry |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |last=Levy |first=Emanuel |date=September 2, 1999 |access-date=April 25, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505022149/http://variety.com/1999/film/reviews/boys-don-t-cry-1117752076/ |archive-date=May 5, 2015}}</ref> was initially assigned an [[Motion Picture Association of America film rating system#NC-17|NC-17]] [[Motion Picture Association of America film rating system#MPAA film ratings|rating]] but was later reclassified to an R rating. It was released on [[home video]] in September 2000. In 2019, the film was selected for preservation in the United States [[National Film Registry]] by the [[Library of Congress]] as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant."<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Tartaglione|first=Nancy|title=National Film Registry Adds 'Purple Rain', 'Clerks', 'Gaslight' & More; 'Boys Don't Cry' One Of Record 7 Pics From Female Helmers|url=https://deadline.com/2019/12/national-film-registry-2019-record-female-directors-boys-dont-cry-purple-rain-clerks-gaslight-platoon-full-list-1202806279/|magazine=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=December 11, 2019|access-date=December 11, 2019|archive-date=July 20, 2020|archive-url=https://archive.today/20200720165858/https://deadline.com/2019/12/national-film-registry-2019-record-female-directors-boys-dont-cry-purple-rain-clerks-gaslight-platoon-full-list-1202806279/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Women Rule 2019 National Film Registry|url=https://www.loc.gov/item/prn-19-116/women-rule-2019-national-film-registry/2019-12-11/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=Library of Congress|archive-date=December 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211155249/https://www.loc.gov/item/prn-19-116/women-rule-2019-national-film-registry/2019-12-11/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Complete National Film Registry Listing|url=https://www.loc.gov/programs/national-film-preservation-board/film-registry/complete-national-film-registry-listing/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=Library of Congress|archive-date=May 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160507094100/https://www.loc.gov/programs/national-film-preservation-board/film-registry/complete-national-film-registry-listing/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Plot==
In 1993, [[Brandon Teena]] is a young [[trans man]] living in rural Nebraska.<ref>{{cite web|last=D'Erasmo |first=Stacey |title=Boy Interrupted |work=[[Out Magazine]] |date=October 1999 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gWIEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA65 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518164629/https://books.google.com/books?id=gWIEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA65 |archive-date=May 18, 2015}}</ref> When Brandon is discovered to be [[transgender]] by a former girlfriend's brother, he receives death threats. Soon after, he is involved in a [[street fighting#Bar fights|bar fight]] and is evicted from his cousin's trailer. Brandon moves to [[Falls City, Nebraska]], where he befriends ex-convicts John Lotter and Tom Nissen, <!-- EDITORS NOTE: Nissen is the correct spelling of this name; see sources for confirmation. --> and their friends Candace and Lana Tisdel. Brandon becomes romantically involved with Lana, who is initially unaware both of his anatomy and his troubled past. The two make plans to move to [[Memphis, Tennessee]], where Brandon will manage Lana's karaoke singing career. Eventually, they kiss during a date night which ends with them having sex.

The police detain Brandon on charges that arose before his relocation; they place him in the women's section of the Falls City jail.<!--Please note in American English, "jail" is used for a short-term incarceration facility, and Brandon is in jail and not a long term prison--> Lana bails Brandon out and asks why he was placed in a women's jail. Brandon attempts to lie to her, saying he's a [[hermaphrodite]] born with [[intersex]] organs, and will soon receive genital reconstruction surgery, but Lana stops him, declaring her love for him regardless of his gender. However, while Brandon is in jail, Candace finds a number of documents listing Brandon's birth name, and she and her friends react to this news with shock and disgust. They enter Brandon's room, search among Brandon's things, and discover transgender [[pamphlets]] that confirm their suspicions. When Brandon and Lana return, Tom and John violently confront Brandon and take him into the bathroom, forcibly removing his pants and his white briefs, revealing his female genitals. They try to make Lana look, but she shields her eyes and turns away. After this confrontation, Tom and John drag Brandon into John's car and drive to an isolated location, where they brutally beat and take turns raping him.

Afterward, they take Brandon to Tom's house, but Brandon escapes by climbing through a bathroom window. Although his assailants threaten Brandon and warn him not to report the attack to the police, Lana convinces him to do so. However, the police chief proves to be less concerned with the crime and interrogates Brandon about his sexual identity.

Later, John and Tom get drunk and drive to Candace's house. Lana attempts to stop them, but they find Brandon and kill him along with Candace before fleeing the scene, while Lana lies with Brandon's body. The next morning, Lana awakens next to Brandon's corpse. Her mother arrives and takes her away from the scene. As Lana leaves Falls City, a letter to her from Brandon that she found on his body, is heard in a voiceover, saying that in Memphis "I'll be waiting for you, love always and forever".
