'''''Deliverance''''' is a 1972 American [[thriller film]] directed and produced by [[John Boorman]] from a screenplay by [[James Dickey]], who adapted it from his [[Deliverance (novel)|1970 novel]]. It follows four businessmen from [[Atlanta]] who venture into the remote [[Appalachia|northern Georgia wilderness]] to go [[whitewater canoe|whitewater canoeing]] down the [[Cahulawassee River]] before it is dammed, only to find themselves in danger from the area's inhabitants and nature. It stars [[Jon Voight]], [[Burt Reynolds]], [[Ned Beatty]], and [[Ronny Cox]], with the latter two making their feature film debuts.

''Deliverance'' was a critical and commercial success. It earned three [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations and five [[Golden Globe Award]] nominations, and grossed [[US dollar|$]]46.1 million on a budget of $2 million. It became a popular culture landmark for a scene featuring Cox's character playing "[[Dueling Banjos]]" on guitar with a banjo-picking country boy, and garnered notoriety for a scene in which Beatty's character is brutally raped by a [[mountain man]]. In 2008, it was selected for preservation in the United States [[National Film Registry]] by the [[Library of Congress]] as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cinematic Classics, Legendary Stars, Comedic Legends and Novice Filmmakers Showcase the 2008 Film Registry|url=https://www.loc.gov/item/prn-08-237/2008-entries-to-national-film-registry-announced/2008-12-30/|access-date=2020-09-25|website=Library of Congress}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Complete National Film Registry Listing |url=https://www.loc.gov/programs/national-film-preservation-board/film-registry/complete-national-film-registry-listing/|access-date=2020-09-25|website=Library of Congress}}</ref>

In retrospective analysis, the film has since garnered criticism from journalists, historians, and citizens of [[Rabun County, Georgia]], where the film was shot,<ref name="welles12">{{cite news |last1=Welles |first1=Cory |title=40 years later, 'Deliverance' causes mixed feelings in Georgia |url=https://www.marketplace.org/story/2012/08/22/40-years-later-deliverance-causes-mixed-feelings-georgia |access-date=November 13, 2025 |work=Marketplace |date=August 22, 2012}}</ref><ref name="phillips12">{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Rich |title=40 years later, 'Deliverance' still draws tourists, stereotypes |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2012/06/22/us/deliverance-40-years/index.html |access-date=November 13, 2025 |work=[[CNN]] |date=June 22, 2012}}</ref> for its portrayal of the people and culture of [[Appalachia]],<ref name="adams2021">{{cite news |last1=Adams |first1=Ella |title=Through Ella's Eyes: The hillbilly stereotype is outdated and lazy |url=https://theappalachianonline.com/through-ellas-eyes-appalachian-stereotypes/ |access-date=November 13, 2025 |work=The Appalachian |date=October 7, 2021}}</ref><ref name="Price100">{{cite web |date=2018}}</ref><ref name="mancini"/> its promotion of [[Appalachian stereotypes]] in film and television,<ref name="scovell22">{{cite news |last1=Scovell |first1=Adam |title=How masterly horror |access-date=November 13, 2025 |date=November 29, 2020}}</ref><ref name="humphries">{{cite news |last1=Humphries |first1=Steven |title=What do 'Elegy' and 'Nomadland' say about Hollywood's view of Science Monitor]] |date=December 17, 2020}}</ref>

==Plot==
Four [[Atlanta]] businessmen decide to go whitewater canoeing down the [[Cahulawassee River]] in the remote northern Georgia wilderness before it becomes dammed. Lewis Medlock is an avid outdoorsman and survivalist who leads the group, and Ed Gentry has been on several trips, but lacks Lewis's self-confidence, while Bobby Trippe and Drew Ballinger are novices.

En route to their launch site, the men, in particular Bobby, are rude toward the locals, who in turn become hostile to the "city boys". At a local gas station, Drew engages a young banjo-playing boy in a musical duel with his guitar. The duel is mutually enjoyable, and some of the locals break into dance at the sound of it. However, the boy does not acknowledge Drew when offered a friendly handshake.

The four friends travel down the river in two canoes, which briefly become separated. Ed and Bobby encounter a pair of mountain men emerging from the woods, one carrying a shotgun and missing his two front teeth. Following a disagreement, the men force Bobby to undress and the unarmed man rapes him, demanding that he "squeal like a pig".  

Ed tries to help, despite being tied to a tree, and held at gunpoint. After raping Bobby, one of the mountain men begins to threaten Ed, claiming "he had a purty mouth". Before the mountain man can force himself on Ed, Lewis sneaks up and kills the rapist with his bow and arrow while Ed snatches the shotgun from the other mountain man, who flees into the woods. After a heated debate between Lewis and Drew, Ed and Bobby side with Lewis' plan to bury the body and continue on as if nothing had happened. The four continue downriver, but the canoes reach a dangerous stretch of rapids. As Drew and Ed reach the rapids in the lead canoe, Drew falls into the water without his life jacket.

The canoes collide on the rocks, throwing the three remaining men into the river and smashing one of the canoes. Lewis breaks his thigh bone and the other two are washed ashore alongside him in a gorge. Lewis, who believes Drew fell out of the boat because he was shot, encourages Ed to climb to the top of the gorge and ambush the other mountain man, who they believe is stalking them from above. Ed reaches an overhang and hides out until morning. He wakes up and sees a distant shotgun-wielding man resembling one of the rapists. Ed nocks his arrow and draws, but begins to shake with panic. The man spots him, and aims his weapon at Ed; Ed clumsily shoots, misses, and falls backwards onto one of his own arrows. Ed then manages to shoot true and kills the man, who falls down the cliff only to be caught and suspended by his braces. Ed then abseils partway down the face to dislodge the body, but his rope breaks, and he and the corpse fall entangled into the river below; Ed is unharmed and Bobby reels him in. They then inspect the body and confirm it is the toothless man from before, though he is now wearing dentures. Ed and Bobby weigh down the body in the river to ensure it will never be found once the river is dammed, then do the same to Drew's broken body when they encounter it downriver. The three men carefully fabricate a cover story for local authorities to explain Drew's death.

Finally reaching the small town of Aintry, a critically injured Lewis is taken by ambulance to the hospital. Ed and Bobby lie about their adventure to Sheriff Bullard in order to escape a possible triple murder charge. Their cover up is almost blown when Ed thinks he has overheard Bobby secretly telling the sheriff the truth, but Bobby convinces him otherwise. Ed and Bobby visit Lewis in the hospital, where the doctor is contemplating [[amputation|amputating]] his broken leg. While being closely observed by a police officer, a worried Ed whispers to Lewis that they need to change their cover story. A coy Lewis relaxes him by pretending that the head trauma has wiped his memory clear of everything after the canoe collision. Sheriff Bullard does not believe the men and reveals that Deputy Queen is suspicious of them because his brother-in-law went hunting a few days earlier and has not yet returned. However, with no evidence to hold them, he lets them leave, warning them never to return. The three men part, vowing to keep their story of death and survival a secret for the rest of their lives.

Ed reunites with his wife and son, but remains traumatized, having a nightmare about a bloated hand rising from the lake.

==Production==
=== Casting ===
Casting was by [[Lynn Stalmaster]]. Dickey had initially wanted [[Sam Peckinpah]] to direct the film, but [[Warner Bros.]] was not so keen on Peckinpah; so they settled on [[John Boorman]] to direct.<ref name=iw/><ref>https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/john-boorman-burt-reynolds-jon-voight-ned-beatty-talk-deliverance-casting-marlon-brando-more-98214/</ref> Dickey also wanted [[Gene Hackman]] to portray Ed Gentry, whereas Boorman wanted [[Lee Marvin]] to play the role.<ref name=iw/>  Boorman also wanted [[Marlon Brando]] to play Lewis Medlock, who turned it down because he believed he couldn't fit into the canoes.<ref name=iw/><ref>https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/john-boorman-burt-reynolds-jon-voight-ned-beatty-talk-deliverance-casting-marlon-brando-more-98214/</ref> [[Jack Nicholson]] was considered for the role of Ed,<ref name=iw/> while both [[Donald Sutherland]] and [[Charlton Heston]] turned down the role of Lewis.<ref name=iw/>  Other actors who were considered for the film included [[Robert Redford]], [[Henry Fonda]], [[George C. Scott]] and [[Warren Beatty]].<ref name=iw/> Boorman denied that Fonda was considered for a role in the film.<ref>https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/john-boorman-burt-reynolds-jon-voight-ned-beatty-talk-deliverance-casting-marlon-brando-more-98214/</ref>

===Filming===
''Deliverance'' was shot primarily in [[Rabun County, Georgia|Rabun County]] in northeastern Georgia. The canoe scenes were filmed in the [[Tallulah Gorge]] southeast of [[Clayton, Georgia|Clayton]] on the [[Chattooga River]], which divides the northeastern corner of [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] from the northwestern corner of [[South Carolina]]. Additional scenes were shot in [[Salem, South Carolina]]. Filming took place from May to August 1971.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068473/locations/?ref_=tttr_ql_dt_5 | title=Deliverance (1972) - Filming & production - IMDb | website=[[IMDb]] }}</ref>

A scene was also shot at the Mount Carmel Baptist Church cemetery. This site has since been flooded and lies {{convert|130|feet}} under the surface of [[Lake Jocassee]], on the border between [[Oconee County, South Carolina|Oconee]] and [[Pickens County, South Carolina|Pickens]] counties in South Carolina.<ref name="jocassee">{{cite news | url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/greenvilleonline/access/1688999131.html?FMT=ABS&date=Feb+20,+2009 | title=Cable network to detail history of Lake Jocassee | access-date=2009-02-25 | work=The Greenville News | first=Anna | last=Simon | date=2009-02-20 | archive-date=June 4, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604115051/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/greenvilleonline/access/1688999131.html?FMT=ABS&date=Feb+20,+2009 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ohio.com/entertainment/mailbag/69264542.html|title=Body double plays banjo|first=Rich|last=Heldenfels|work=[[Akron Beacon Journal]]|date=2009-11-05|access-date=2009-11-06}}</ref> The dam shown under construction is [[Jocassee Dam]] near Salem, South Carolina.

During the filming of the canoe scene, author [[James Dickey]] showed up inebriated and entered into a bitter argument with producer-director [[John Boorman]], who had rewritten Dickey's script. They allegedly had a brief fistfight in which Boorman, a much smaller man than Dickey, suffered a broken nose and four shattered teeth.<ref name=iw>{{cite news|last=Lyttleton|first=Oliver|title=5 Things You Might Not Know About 'Deliverance,' Released 40 Years Ago Today|date=30 July 2012|work=[[IndieWire]]|url=http://www.indiewire.com/2012/07/5-things-you-might-not-know-about-deliverance-released-40-years-ago-today-251460/|access-date=28 September 2017|archive-date=September 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928150843/http://www.indiewire.com/2012/07/5-things-you-might-not-know-about-deliverance-released-40-years-ago-today-251460/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Dickey was thrown off the set, but no charges were filed against him. The two reconciled and became good friends, and Boorman gave Dickey a cameo role as the sheriff at the end of the film.

The inspiration for the Cahulawassee River was the [[Coosawattee River]], which was dammed in the 1970s and contained several dangerous whitewater rapids before being flooded by [[Carters Lake (Blue Ridge Mountains)|Carters Lake]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Roper|first1=Daniel M.|title=The Story of the Coosawattee River Gorge|journal=North Georgia Journal|issue=Summer 1995|url=http://www.brownsguides.com/blog/coosawattee-river-gorge|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101222063750/http://www.brownsguides.com/blog/coosawattee-river-gorge |archive-date=2010-12-22 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Stunts ===
The studio cut the film's budget after becoming concerned about its content,<ref>{{cite news |date=27 July 2022 |author=Adam Scovell |publisher=[[BBC]] |title=How masterly horror Deliverance set a controversial trend |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20220727-how-rural-horror-deliverance-set-a-controversial-trend }}</ref> and the actors performed their own stunts, such as Jon Voight climbing the cliff himself.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pratt |first=Sean |title=Deliverance {{!}} SBIFF |url=https://sbiff.org/deliverance/ |access-date=2023-05-29 |language=en-US}}</ref> Reynolds requested to have one scene re-shot with himself in a canoe rather than a dummy as it tumbled over a real waterfall.<ref name=":0" /> Reynolds recalled his shoulder and head hitting rocks and floating downstream with all of his clothes torn off, then waking up with director Boorman at his bedside.<ref name=":0" /> Reynolds asked "How'd it look?" and Boorman said, "It looked like a dummy falling over a waterfall."<ref name=":0">{{cite web |date=20 September 2016 |title=That Time Burt Reynolds Tried To Go Down A Waterfall For A Movie Stunt |website=Cinemablend|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/news/1557830/that-time-burt-reynolds-tried-to-go-down-a-waterfall-for-a-movie-stunt }}</ref> Beatty almost drowned and Reynolds cracked his tailbone.<ref>{{cite news |date=17 June 2012 |author=Geoff Boucher |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |title='Deliverance' crew returns to the river |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/la-xpm-2012-jun-17-la-ca-deliverance-20120617-story.html }}</ref>

Regarding the courage of the four main actors in the movie performing their own stunts without insurance protection, Dickey said that all of them "had more guts than a burglar".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Culture |first=Center for the Study of Southern |title=Revisiting Deliverance |url=https://southernstudies.olemiss.edu/study-the-south/revisiting-deliverance/ |access-date=2023-05-29 |website=southernstudies.olemiss.edu |language=en}}</ref> In a nod to their stunt-performing audacity, early in the movie Lewis says, "Insurance? I've never been insured in my life. I don't believe in insurance. There's no risk".{{fact|date=June 2026}}

==="Squeal like a pig"===
Several people have been credited with the phrase "squeal like a pig", spoken during the graphic rape scene. Ned Beatty said he thought of it while he and actor Bill McKinney (who played Beatty's rapist) were improvising the scene.<ref>Burger, Mark. (March 19, 2006). "[https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/journalnow/access/1005939731.html?dids=1005939731:1005939731&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Mar+19%2C+2006&author=Mark+Burger+JOURNAL+ARTS+REPORTER&pub=Winston+-+Salem+Journal&edition=&startpage=1&desc=BEATTY+GIVEN+MASTER+OF+CINEMA+AWARD+%3B+CHARACTER+ACTOR+IS+A+VETERAN+OF+MORE+THAN+200+FILM+AND+TELEVISION+PRODUCTIONS Beatty Given Master of Cinema Award; Character Actor Is a Veteran of More than 200 Film and Television Productions] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090323002208/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/journalnow/access/1005939731.html?dids=1005939731:1005939731&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Mar+19%2C+2006&author=Mark+Burger+JOURNAL+ARTS+REPORTER&pub=Winston+-+Salem+Journal&edition=&startpage=1&desc=BEATTY+GIVEN+MASTER+OF+CINEMA+AWARD+%3B+CHARACTER+ACTOR+IS+A+VETERAN+OF+MORE+THAN+200+FILM+AND+TELEVISION+PRODUCTIONS |date=March 23, 2009 }}", ''[[Winston-Salem Journal]]'', Page B1<br />"Regarding his debut film, ''Deliverance'' (1972), in which his character undergoes an unforgettably vivid sexual assault, Beatty said: 'The whole "squeal like a pig" thing ... came from guess who.' As the audience laughed, he theatrically put his head in his hands and silently pointed to himself, before elaborating how director Boorman encouraged him to improvise the scene with his onscreen tormentor, Bill McKinney."</ref> James Dickey's son, [[Christopher Dickey]], wrote in his memoir about the film production, ''Summer of Deliverance'', that because Boorman had rewritten so much dialogue for the scene, one of the crewmen suggested that Beatty's character should just "squeal like a pig".<ref>{{cite book|title=Summer of Deliverance: A Memoir of Father and Son |first=Christopher |last=Dickey |author-link=Christopher Dickey |publisher=Simon and Schuster|year= 2010|isbn=978-1439129593|page=186}}</ref> Boorman, in a [[Audio commentary|DVD commentary]] he made for the film, said the line was used because the studio wanted the male rape scene to be filmed in two ways: one for cinematic release, and one that would be acceptable for television. As Boorman did not want to do that, he decided that the phrase "squeal like a pig", suggested by Rabun County liaison Frank Rickman, was a good replacement for the original dialogue in the script.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rabunhistory.org/history-sketches/frank-rickman-red-clay-michelangelo/|title=Rabun County Historical Society|publisher=www.rabunhistory.org|access-date=September 10, 2018|archive-date=July 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715181240/https://www.rabunhistory.org/history-sketches/frank-rickman-red-clay-michelangelo/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Reynolds later recalled the scene as so uncomfortable cameramen avoided watching, and he opted to interrupt the filming. He said, "I asked John Boorman, the director, 'Why did you let it go that long?' He said, 'I wanted to take it as far as I could with the audience, and I figured you'd run in when it got too far.'"<ref name="ContactMusic2008"/>

==Soundtrack==
The [[Dueling Banjos (album)|film's soundtrack]] brought new attention to the musical work "[[Dueling Banjos]]", which had been recorded numerous times since 1955. Only [[Eric Weissberg]] and Steve Mandel were originally credited for the piece. The onscreen credits state that the song is an arrangement of the song "Feudin' Banjos", showing Combine Music Corp as the copyright owner. Songwriter and producer [[Arthur "Guitar Boogie" Smith]], who had written "Feudin' Banjos" in 1955, and recorded it with five-string banjo player [[Don Reno]], filed a lawsuit for songwriting credit and a percentage of royalties. He was awarded both in a landmark copyright infringement case.<ref>{{cite news |title=Country guitarist Arthur Smith dies |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-26885910 |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=15 April 2015}}</ref> Smith asked Warner Bros. to include his name on the official soundtrack listing, but reportedly asked to be omitted from the film credits because he found the film offensive.<ref>{{cite news |first=Terence |last=McArdle |title=Arthur Smith, guitarist who wrote 'Guitar Boogie' and 'Duelin' Banjos,' dies at 93 |url=http://wapo.st/1ihceud |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=15 April 2015 |date=6 April 2014 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

[[Joe Boyd]], who was producing the music for the movie, offered "Duelling Banjos" to [[Bill Keith (musician)|Bill Keith]], who turned it down and suggested Eric Weissberg instead.<ref name=Boyd>Boyd, Joe, White Bicycles – Making Music in the 1960s, Serpent's Tail, 2006. Page 238. ISBN 1-85242-910-0</ref>

No credit was given for the film score. The film has a number of sparse, brooding passages of music scattered throughout, including several played on a synthesizer. Some prints of the movie omit much of this extra music.{{fact|date=June 2026}}

Boorman was given a gold record for the "Dueling Banjos" hit single; this was later stolen from his house by the Dublin gangster [[Martin Cahill]]. Boorman recreated this scene in ''[[The General (1998 film)|The General]]'' (1998), his biographical film about Cahill.<ref>{{cite news|title=Artistic reunion brings Martin Cahill to life|url=https://irishecho.com/2011/02/artistic-reunion-bringsmartin-cahill-to-life-4/|access-date=2 April 2017|work=[[The Irish Echo]]|date=May 27 – June 2, 1998}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Commercial===
''Deliverance'' was a box office success in the United States, becoming the [[1972 in film#Top grossing films (U.S.)|fourth-highest grossing film of 1972]], with a domestic take of over $46 million.<ref name="TN">{{cite web|url=https://www.the-numbers.com/movies/1972/0DLVR.php|publisher=The Numbers|title=Deliverance, Box Office Information|access-date=January 21, 2012}}</ref> The film's financial success continued the following year, when it went on to earn $18 million in North American "[[Gross rental|distributor rentals]]" (receipts).<ref>"Big Rental Films of 1973", ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', 9 January 1974 p 19</ref>

===Critical===
''Deliverance'' received generally positive reviews by critics, and is widely regarded as one of the best films of 1972.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.filmsite.org/1972.html |title=Greatest Films of 1972 |publisher=Filmsite.org |access-date=2012-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.films101.com/y1972r.htm |title=The Best Movies of 1972 by Rank |publisher=Films101.com |access-date=2012-05-05 |archive-date=November 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106000954/http://www.films101.com/y1972r.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://cinepad.com/awards/best_70s.htm |title=Best Films of the 1970s |publisher=Cinepad.com |access-date=2012-05-05 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120510120236/http://cinepad.com/awards/best_70s.htm |archive-date=2012-05-10 }}</ref>

Contemporary critic [[Gene Siskel]] of the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' gave the film four stars out of four and wrote, "It is a gripping horror story that at times may force you to look away from the screen, but it is so beautifully filmed that your eyes will eagerly return."<ref name="Siskel">{{cite news |last1=Siskel |first1=Gene |title=The Movies: Deliverance |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/77346990/ |work=Chicago Tribune |date=October 5, 1972 |page=Section 2, Page 5|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> [[Charles Champlin]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' called it "an engrossing adventure, a demonstrable labor of love" carried by Voight and Reynolds.<ref>Champlin, Charles (August 13, 1972). "Men Against River—of Life?—in 'Deliverance'". ''[[Los Angeles Times]]''. Calendar, p. 17.</ref> Gary Arnold of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' wrote that the film was "certainly a distinctive and gripping piece of work, with a deliberately brooding, ominous tone and visual style that put you in a grave, fearful frame of mind, almost in spite of yourself."<ref>Arnold, Gary (October 5, 1972). "' Deliverance': A Gripping Piece of Work". ''[[The Washington Post]]''. B1.</ref>

Not all reviews were positive. [[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' gave the film a mixed 2.5 stars out of a possible 4. He declared the film was "admittedly effective on the level of simple adventure" and had good performances, particularly from Voight and Reynolds. However, Ebert also wrote ''Deliverance'' "totally fails [in] its attempt to make some kind of significant statement about its action [...] It's possible to consider civilized men in a confrontation with the wilderness without throwing in rapes, cowboy-and-Indian stunts and pure exploitative sensationalism."<ref>[https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/deliverance-1972 "Deliverance"]. ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]''.</ref>

Arthur D. Murphy of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' wrote that the setting was "majestic" but it was "in the fleshing out that the script fumbles, and with it the direction and acting."<ref>Murphy, Arthur D. (July 19, 1972). "[https://variety.com/review/VE1117790346 Film Reviews: Deliverance]". ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]''. 14.</ref> 

[[Vincent Canby]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' was also generally negative, calling the film "a disappointment" because "so many of Dickey's lumpy narrative ideas remain in his screenplay that John Boorman's screen version becomes a lot less interesting than it has any right to be."<ref>{{cite news|last=Canby|first=Vincent|date=July 31, 1972|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1972/07/31/archives/the-screen-james-dickeys-deliverance-arrives-weekend-canoe-trip-of.html|title=The Screen: James Dickey's 'Deliverance' Arrives|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|page=21}}</ref>

[[Pauline Kael]] writing for ''[[The New Yorker]]'' was critical of the film and wrote that the movie demonstrated that it could be effective "even if you are always aware of the actors' acting and don't really believe in a single character."<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kael |first=Pauline |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tkShTL84MrcC&q=the+age+of+movies+selected+writings+of+pauline+kael |title=The Age of Movies: Selected Writings of Pauline Kael: A Library of America Special Publication |date=2011-10-27 |publisher=Library of America |isbn=978-1-59853-171-8 |pages=373 |language=en}}</ref>

On review aggregation website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the film holds a 90% rating based on reviews from 68 critics, with an average rating of 8.40/10. The site's consensus states: "Given primal verve by John Boorman's unflinching direction and Burt Reynolds' star-making performance, ''Deliverance'' is a terrifying adventure."<ref>{{cite web |title=Deliverance |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/deliverance/ |access-date=June 12, 2025 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media]]}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the {{#switch:  | episode = episode | series = series | season = season | film }} a score of 80 out of 100, based on 15 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Deliverance'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/deliverance |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=May 6, 2022 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref>

==Legacy==
Following the film's release, Georgia Governor [[Jimmy Carter]] established a state film commission to encourage television and movie production there. By 2012 the state had "become one of the top five production destinations in the U.S".<ref name="welles">{{cite web|url= http://www.marketplace.org/topics/life/40-years-later-deliverance-causes-mixed-feelings-georgia |last=Welles |first= Cory |title=40 years later, 'Deliverance' causes mixed feelings in Georgia|website=Marketplace|date= August 22, 2012|access-date= August 27, 2014}}</ref> Tourism increased to Rabun County by the tens of thousands after the film's release. By 2012, tourism was the largest source of revenue in the county, and rafting had developed as a $20 million industry in the region.<ref name="welles"/> Jon Voight's stunt double for this film, Claude Terry, later purchased equipment used in the movie from Warner Brothers. He founded a whitewater rafting adventure company on the Chattooga River, Southeastern Expeditions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.southeasternexpeditions.com/about-us/ |website=Southeastern Expeditions|title=About us|date=8 April 2013 |access-date= August 19, 2013}}</ref> Payson Kennedy, the stunt double for Ned Beatty, established the Nantahala Outdoor Center with his wife and Horace Holden along the [[Nantahala River]] in [[Swain County]], North Carolina, in 1972, the same year that ''Deliverance'' was released.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Knoepp |first1=Lilly |title=Exploring Southern Appalachia: 'Deliverance' And Beyond |url=https://www.bpr.org/post/exploring-southern-appalachia-deliverance-and-beyond#stream/0 |website=Blue Ridge Public Radio |date=2 September 2019 |access-date=1 November 2020}}</ref>

"Dueling Banjos" won the 1974 [[Grammy Award for Best Country Instrumental Performance]]. The film was selected by ''The New York Times'' as one of ''The Best 1,000 Movies Ever Made'', while the viewers of [[Channel 4]] in the United Kingdom voted it #45 on a list of ''The 100 Greatest Films''.  Reynolds later called it "the best film I've ever been in".<ref>{{cite news|title=Workaholic Burt Reynolds sets up his next task: Light comedy |last=Siskel |first=Gene |author-link=Gene Siskel |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=Nov 28, 1976|page=e2}}</ref> However, he stated that the rape scene went "too far".<ref name="ContactMusic2008">{{cite magazine|title=Reynolds: 'Deliverance Rape Scene Went Too Far'|date=21 January 2008|magazine=[[Contactmusic.com]]|url=http://www.contactmusic.com/burt-reynolds/news/reynolds-deliverance-rape-scene-went-too-far_1056945|access-date=28 September 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315233006/http://www.contactmusic.com/burt-reynolds/news/reynolds-deliverance-rape-scene-went-too-far_1056945| archive-date=March 15 2018}}</ref>

Filmmaker [[Bong Joon Ho]] has cited ''Deliverance'' as one of his top four favorite films.<ref>{{YouTube|id=MM5ckjUOnT4|title=Four Favorites with Bong Joon Ho and Sharon Choi}}</ref>

In 2025, ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' listed ''Deliverance'' as having the best stunts of 1972.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Doherty |first=Thomas |date=June 7, 2025 |title=The Best Stunts of All Time, Over Nearly 100 Years of the Oscars |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/best-stunts-all-time-movies-oscars-stunt-design-100-years/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250720043450/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/best-stunts-all-time-movies-oscars-stunt-design-100-years/ |archive-date=July 20, 2025}}</ref>

The line "Where you goin' city boy?" at the beginning of the film is sampled in [[Primus (band)|Primus]]'s 1993 single "[[My Name Is Mud]]". The line "Now let's you just drop them pants" and adjacent dialogue from the same scene of the film is sampled in the "Drop Yer Britches" mix of [[Revolting Cocks]] single "[[Beers, Steers, and Queers]]".

'''''Dhurandhar'''''{{efn|{{Translation|Stalwart}}}} is a 2025 Indian [[Hindi]]-language [[Spy film|spy action thriller]] film written and directed by [[Aditya Dhar]]. Produced by Dhar, Lokesh Dhar and [[Jyoti Deshpande]] under [[Jyoti Deshpande|Jio Studios]] and [[B62 Studios]], the film features an [[ensemble cast]] consisting of [[Ranveer Singh]], [[Akshaye Khanna]], [[Sanjay Dutt]], [[Arjun Rampal]], [[R. Madhavan]], [[Sara Arjun]], [[Rakesh Bedi]], [[Gaurav Gera]], and [[Danish Pandor (actor)|Danish Pandor]] alongside several supporting actors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dhurandhar release date, cast, characters, true story and everything else you need to know |url=https://www.gqindia.com/content/dhurandhar-release-date-cast-characters-true-story-and-everything-else-you-need-to-know |website=GQ India |date=19 November 2025 |access-date=29 November 2025 |language=en-IN |first=Sanjana |last=Ray |archive-date=30 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251130052925/https://www.gqindia.com/content/dhurandhar-release-date-cast-characters-true-story-and-everything-else-you-need-to-know |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Britannica">{{Cite news |last=Roy |first=Gitanjali |title=Why Is Bollywood Film Series Dhurandhar Controversial? |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Why-Is-Dhurandhar-Controversial |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260101232704/https://www.britannica.com/topic/Why-Is-Dhurandhar-Controversial |archive-date=1 January 2026 |access-date=13 January 2026 |work=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> The first instalment of a [[Dhurandhar Duology|duology]], it centres on a high-stakes [[List of Indian intelligence agencies|covert counter-terrorism operation]].<ref name="Britannica" /> The film follows an undercover Indian intelligence agent who infiltrates [[Karachi]]'s criminal syndicates and political power structures in Pakistan in an effort to dismantle a terror network targeting India.

The film's storyline draws loose inspiration from multiple real-life geopolitical events and conflicts in [[South Asia]], including the [[Indian Airlines Flight 814|1999 IC-814 hijacking]], the [[2001 Indian Parliament attack]], the [[2008 Mumbai attacks]], and developments linked to Pakistan's [[Operation Lyari]].<ref name="Britannica"/><ref>{{Cite news |date=20 November 2025 |title=Inside Operation Lyari, Pakistan's crackdown on gangs, which inspired Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' |url=https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/dhurandhar-movie-operation-lyari-pakistan-crackdown-gangs-13952441.html |access-date=29 November 2025 |work=[[Firstpost]] |archive-date=26 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251126055043/https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/dhurandhar-movie-operation-lyari-pakistan-crackdown-gangs-13952441.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="NDTV story">{{Cite web |date=9 December 2025 |title=The Dhurandhar Story: How a tip-off about Kandahar hijacker became a Ranveer Singh blockbuster |url=https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/the-dhurandhar-story-how-a-tip-off-about-kandahar-hijacker-became-a-ranveer-singh-blockbuster-9776603/ |website=NDTV |access-date=27 December 2025 |archive-date=5 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105063152/https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/the-dhurandhar-story-how-a-tip-off-about-kandahar-hijacker-became-a-ranveer-singh-blockbuster-9776603 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Principal photography]] for ''Dhurandhar'' took place from July 2024 to October 2025 across multiple locations in India and abroad, including the states and union territories of [[Punjab, India|Punjab]], [[Maharashtra]], [[Chandigarh]], [[Ladakh]] and [[Himachal Pradesh]], as well as Thailand. The film features music composed by [[Shashwat Sachdev]], cinematography by [[Vikash Nowlakha]], and editing by Shivkumar V. Panicker. With a runtime of 214 minutes, ''Dhurandhar'' ranks as one of the [[List of longest films in India|longest Indian films]] ever produced.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/dhurandhar-becomes-the-longest-hindi-film-in-17-years-since-jodha-akbar-with-a-runtime-of-214-minutes-joins-the-list-of-movies-like-loc-kargil-lagaan/articleshow/125727722.cms|title=Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' becomes the LONGEST Hindi film in 17 years since 'Jodha Akbar', with a runtime of 214 minutes, joins the list of movies like 'LOC Kargil', 'Lagaan'|work=The Times of India|date=3 December 2025|via=The Economic Times – The Times of India|access-date=24 December 2025|archive-date=3 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260103022349/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/dhurandhar-becomes-the-longest-hindi-film-in-17-years-since-jodha-akbar-with-a-runtime-of-214-minutes-joins-the-list-of-movies-like-loc-kargil-lagaan/articleshow/125727722.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Dhurandhar'' was released theatrically on 5 December 2025 and received mixed reviews from critics, with praise for its cast performances, direction, cinematography, action sequences, [[Dhurandhar (soundtrack)|musical score]], and [[Dhurandhar Duology|production design]], with criticism directed towards its extended runtime. The film also attracted controversy for its blending of fictional elements with real historical events, with some commentators describing it as [[Propaganda|propagandistic]].<ref name="Hindu government-embedded" /><ref name="Wire troll" /><ref name="IE bigoted">{{Cite news |date=12 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar pushes a bigoted vision, gaslighting the audience into accepting it as entertainment |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]] |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-pushes-a-bigoted-vision-gaslighting-audience-into-accepting-it-as-entertainment-10406515/ |archive-date=31 December 2025 |access-date=27 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251231164752/https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-pushes-a-bigoted-vision-gaslighting-audience-into-accepting-it-as-entertainment-10406515/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Commercially, the film achieved [[Dhurandhar#Box office|significant box-office success]], grossing over {{INR}}[[1000 Crore Club|1,000 crore]] worldwide within three weeks of release, having beat multiple records, including being the [[List of highest-grossing Indian films#Highest-grossing films|fifth-highest-grossing Indian film]], second highest-grossing [[A certificate|A-rated]] Indian film, and the second [[List of highest-grossing Hindi films|highest-grossing Hindi film worldwide]] at the time of its release.<ref>{{citation |first=Naman |last=Ramachandran |title=Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' Propels India Box Office to Record $1.48 Billion in 2025 |newspaper=Variety |date=15 January 2026 |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/ranveer-singh-dhurandhar-india-box-office-2025-1236631963/ |access-date=18 January 2026 |archive-date=16 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116120000/https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/ranveer-singh-dhurandhar-india-box-office-2025-1236631963/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

The film was banned from theatrical release in several [[Gulf Cooperation Council]] countries.<ref name="DC"/><ref name="IT GCC" /> A direct sequel, ''[[Dhurandhar: The Revenge]]'', was released on 19 March 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dhurandhar hits theatres: Second part of Ranveer's film to release on this date |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/bollywood/story/dhurandhar-part-two-film-release-date-ranveer-singh-aditya-dhar-sanjay-dutt-arjun-rampal-akshaye-khanna-r-madhavan-rakesh-bedi-2831185-2025-12-05 |work=India Today |date=5 December 2025 |access-date=5 December 2025 |archive-date=12 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251212080202/https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/bollywood/story/dhurandhar-part-two-film-release-date-ranveer-singh-aditya-dhar-sanjay-dutt-arjun-rampal-akshaye-khanna-r-madhavan-rakesh-bedi-2831185-2025-12-05 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Plot==
{{Hatnote|The film is divided into eight chapters: "The Price of Peace", "Stranger in the Land of Shadows", "The Bastard King of Lyari", "Bullets and Roses", "The Jinn", "The Devil's Guardian", "The Butterfly Effect" and "Et tu Brutus".}}

On 30 December 1999, [[Minister of External Affairs (India)|Minister of External Affairs]] Devavrat Kapoor and Ajay Sanyal, [[Director of the Intelligence Bureau|Director]] of [[Intelligence Bureau (India)|the Intelligence Bureau]] negotiate with terrorist [[Indian Airlines Flight 814#Hijackers|Zahoor Mistry]] to release three terrorists and pay a US$10 million ransom in exchange for the lives of [[Indian Airlines Flight 814|airline passengers held captive]] in [[Kandahar]]. Though [[Research & Analysis Wing#Secretary (Research)|R&AW Special Secretary]] K. S. Bhullar rejects Sanyal's proposal to infiltrate terrorist networks in Pakistan, Kapoor later authorises Sanyal's covert "Operation Dhurandhar" following the [[2001 Indian Parliament attack]].

Three years later, in 2004, Hamza Ali Mazari is an Indian agent who reaches Pakistan via the [[Torkham border crossing]] in [[Afghanistan]], landing up in the [[Lyari]] suburb of [[Karachi]]. He meets Mohammed Aalam, a juice-shop owner, moves in with him, and works as a waiter while studying local gang politics. As a [[Baloch people|Baloch]], Hamza can align only with the gang led by gangster [[Rehman Dakait]] and his cousin and deputy [[Uzair Baloch]].

Hamza learns that a rival [[Pashtuns|Pathan]] gang, led by Rehman's estranged father Babu Dakait and Arshad Pappu, plan to kill Rehman's eldest son Naieem Baloch. Babu's men attack a wedding attended by Naieem and his younger brother Faizal; Hamza saves Faizal, but Naieem is killed. At the hospital, Rehman and Uzair note Hamza's firearm skills and recruit him. Jameel Jamali of the Pakistan Awami Party (PAP) urges Uzair not to retaliate before the [[2008 Pakistani general election|general elections]], but Hamza encourages revenge. Rehman's gang massacres Babu's men, and Rehman brutally murders Babu with a weighing stone, proclaiming Baloch dominance over Lyari.

At a PAP rally, Hamza meets Jameel's young daughter Yalina and begins a relationship with her. Rehman is introduced to [[Major (rank)|Major]] Iqbal of the [[Inter-Services Intelligence|ISI]] by the Khanani brothers, businessmen who are nudging Rehman into politics; Iqbal requests weapons and ammunition for a terror attack on India and in return, he will get Rehman a place in politics. Hamza learns about Iqbal and Khanani’s [[Fake Indian currency note|counterfeit-currency operation]], and relays the information to Aalam, in reality an Indian field agent, who informs Sanyal; the IB suspects Pakistan possesses Indian currency plates. Rehman and his men get the requested weapons from [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]].

However, because of a threat given by Rehman to Khanani, he informs Jameel that Rehman is entering politics. Jameel’s career is threatened by this. Backed by Major Iqbal, Rehman enters politics and declares an alliance between his party the [[People's Aman Committee]], and the PAP of Aquib Ali Zarwari. Jameel responds by recruiting suspended [[Superintendent of police|Superintendent of Police]] [[Aslam Khan (police officer)|Chaudhary Aslam]] to eliminate Rehman, an old nemesis to Aslam, leading to the formation of the [[Operation Lyari|Lyari Task Force]]. On the day of the delivery of the weapons, Rehman’s son suddenly falls sick and is rushed to the hospital while Hamza and Uzair go to deliver weapons. There, Hamza learns that the attack has been postponed as an Indian agent had told the IB of their arrival and sees Iqbal torture that Indian spy. During the way to the hospital, Rehman is arrested by Aslam and Hamza interrogates the chef of the house who admits to Jameel, Aslam and Pappu plotting to kill Rehman in a staged encounter; the meeting between the three was recorded by Yalina. Hamza threatens Jameel that if Rehman isn’t released, he will leak the video and torture LTF officers at their secret office. Aslam is forced to release Rehman.

Despite Hamza's intelligence, the [[2008 Mumbai attacks|26/11 Mumbai terror attack]] occurs and Rehman, Iqbal, Khanani watch it live from the KKI factory in his attendance. Traumatized, Hamza meets Aalam and resolves to dismantle Pakistan's terror infrastructure. He secretly proposes to Jameel that by marrying Yalina, he will rule Lyari while granting Jameel lasting influence. He then conspires with Jameel and Aslam to eliminate Rehman. At Hamza and Yalina's wedding, Major Iqbal requests another weapons shipment for an attack on Amritsar. Exploiting Rehman's drunkenness, Hamza schedules the delivery to coincide with another engagement, creating an ambush opportunity. On the day of delivery, Hamza sends Uzair to the shipment site while driving Rehman to Aslam's trap. Rehman realises the betrayal mid-journey; a violent struggle follows, ending in a crash. Hamza escapes, kills two of Rehman's henchmen, and helps Aslam subdue Rehman, who later dies from his injuries in the hospital.

Hamza's real identity is revealed to be Jaskirat Singh Rangi, an Indian death-row inmate turned covert operative for Ajay Sanyal. With Rehman eliminated, he consolidates power in Lyari and [[Dhurandhar: The Revenge|prepares to target "Bade Sahab", the architect of multiple Pakistani terror attacks]].

==Production==
{{Main|Dhurandhar Duology}}

==Music==
{{Main|Dhurandhar (soundtrack)|l1 = Dhurandhar (soundtrack)}}

<!--Do not remove the italics from the hatnote-->The soundtrack was composed by [[Shashwat Sachdev]], in his second collaboration with Dhar after ''[[Uri: The Surgical Strike]]'' (2019). The songs featured lyrics written by [[Irshad Kamil]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Ba***ds of Bollywood, Dhurandhar composer Shashwat Sachdev collaborates with Oscar-winning Hans Zimmer |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/music/the-bads-of-bollywood-dhurandhar-composer-shashwat-sachdev-collaborates-with-oscar-winner-hans-zimmer-101761273843333.html |website=Hindustan Times |date=24 October 2025 |access-date=29 November 2025 |language=en |archive-date=19 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251119084853/https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/music/the-bads-of-bollywood-dhurandhar-composer-shashwat-sachdev-collaborates-with-oscar-winner-hans-zimmer-101761273843333.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Justin Jose]] served as the [[re-recording mixer]] for the film. The music rights were acquired by [[Saregama]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dhurandhar – Title Track – Dhurandhar – 15 October 2025 |url=https://www.saregama.com/album/dhurandhar-title-track-dhurandhar_178643 |website=[[Saregama]] |access-date=29 November 2025 |archive-date=15 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251115190126/https://www.saregama.com/album/dhurandhar-title-track-dhurandhar_178643 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 31 December 2025, the distributors replaced the film's Digital Cinema Package (DCP) across India with an altered version.<ref>{{cite web |title=Revised version of Akshaye Khanna's Dhurandhar hits cinemas today |website=[[India Today]] |date=1 January 2026 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/bollywood/story/dhurandhar-crosses-rs-1100-crore-box-office-with-revised-version-after-ministry-edits-2845186-2026-01-01 |access-date=2 January 2026 |archive-date=1 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260101171042/https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/bollywood/story/dhurandhar-crosses-rs-1100-crore-box-office-with-revised-version-after-ministry-edits-2845186-2026-01-01 |url-status=live }}</ref> The changes included muting words like 'Baloch' and 'intelligence' after they were 'found to be offensive to certain communities'.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dhurandhar makers mute words like 'Baloch' in Ranveer Singh film, officials deny it was on I&B Ministry directive |website=[[Hindustan Times]] |date=3 January 2026 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-makers-mute-words-like-baloch-in-ranveer-singh-film-officials-deny-it-was-on-i-b-ministry-directive-101767408149517.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Fenil |last=Seta |access-date=31 December 2025 |title=EXCLUSIVE: I&B Ministry asks Dhurandhar makers to remove 'Baloch'; revised version of Ranveer Singh-starrer to play in cinemas from January 1, 2026 |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/bollywood/exclusive-revised-version-ranveer-singh-starrer-play-cinemas-january-1-2026/ |work=Bollywood Hungama |date=31 December 2025 |archive-date=31 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251231152844/https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/bollywood/exclusive-revised-version-ranveer-singh-starrer-play-cinemas-january-1-2026/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Previously, the filmmakers received a legal notice from members of the Baloch community, which accused them of defaming the Baloch. The film was re-released again in India on 12 March 2026 while in the overseas it was released on 13 March 2026.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=12 March 2026 |title=Ranveer Singh's 'Dhurandhar' returns to theatres worldwide ahead of its much-awaited sequel |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/ranveer-singhs-dhurandhar-returns-to-theatres-worldwide-ahead-of-its-much-awaited-sequel/articleshow/129498898.cms |website=Times of India}}</ref> The re-release happened in more than 1,000 screens worldwide, ahead of the release of the sequel.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=13 March 2026 |title=Dhurandhar's first part a RARE film in post-Covid era to complete 100 days in cinemas; becomes the ONLY film ever to run in cinemas until its sequel's release |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/bollywood/dhurandhars-first-part-rare-film-post-covid-era-complete-100-days-cinemas-becomes-film-ever-run-cinemas-sequels-release/ |website=Bollywood Hungama}}</ref>

===Distribution===
The film was distributed by [[PVR Inox Pictures]] in areas of [[Central India]], [[Tamil Nadu]] and [[Kerala]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Fenil |last=Seta |access-date=2 December 2025 |title=EXCLUSIVE: PVR INOX's Nayana Bijli bets big on Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar: "It's an IDEAL film for the big screen"; adds, "2025 has proved that ANYTHING can work, be it Saiyaara, Mahavatar Narsimha, Laalo" |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/features/exclusive-pvr-inoxs-nayana-bijli-bets-big-ranveer-singhs-dhurandhar-ideal-film-big-screen-adds-2025-proved-anything/ |website=Bollywood Hungama}}</ref>

===Home media===
The digital streaming rights for the first part were acquired by [[Netflix]] for ₹85 crore.<ref>{{cite web |title=SCOOP: Dhurandhar 2 OTT rights EXPLODE to Rs. 150 cr; Ranveer Singh creates yet another RECORD as Jio Hotstar wins big! |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/bollywood/scoop-dhurandhar-2-ott-rights-explode-to-rs-150-cr-ranveer-singh-creates-yet-another-record-as-jio-hotstar-wins-big/ |work=Bollywood Hungama |date=4 February 2026}}</ref> The film began streaming on Netflix from 30 January 2026 in [[Hindi]] along with dubbed versions in [[Tamil language|Tamil]] and [[Telugu language|Telugu]] languages. The streaming release had 9 minutes cut from the film's original theatrical version, making this version's runtime 205 minutes (3 hours and 25 minutes).<ref>{{cite web |date=23 January 2026 |title='Dhurandhar' OTT release: When and where to stream the Ranveer Singh–Akshaye Khanna starrer |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/features/dhurandhar-ott-release-stream-ranveer-singh-akshaye-khanna-starrer/ |access-date=23 January 2026 |work=Bollywood Hungama}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Rawal |first=Sugandha |date=30 January 2026 |title=Dhurandhar on OTT {{!}} Netflix leaves viewers upset over edits, muted dialogues: 'Censoring an A rated film is a joke' |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/dhurandhar-release-on-netflix-leaves-viewers-upset-over-edits-muted-dialogues-ranveer-singh-akshaye-khanna-aditya-dhar-101769744906222.html |access-date=30 January 2026 |website=Hindustan Times}}</ref> However, mostly statutory disclaimers regarding smoking were removed from the digital version to streamline the pace of the film.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=31 January 2026 |title=Dhurandhar OTT cut explained: Netflix addresses row over 9-minute trim from digital release |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/entertainment/ott/dhurandhar-ott-cut-explained-netflix-addresses-row-over-9-minute-trim-from-digital-release-of-ranveer-singh-akshaye-khanna-release-2026-01-31-1028247 |website=India TV News}}</ref> 

Later, Netflix reported the film trended at number one in 22 nations globally, most notably in [[Middle East]]ern and [[Asian countries]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bohra |first=Anurag |date=6 February 2026 |title=Dhurandhar tops Netflix in 22 nations including Pak, Bangladesh, Saudi Arabia, UAE |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/celebrities/story/dhurandhar-tops-netflix-in-22-nations-including-pak-bangladesh-saudi-arabia-uae-2864136-2026-02-06 |access-date=10 February 2026 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref> The film, with 7.6 million views, also became the first Indian film to cross 7 million views on Netflix within its first weekend, surpassing films like [[Animal (2023 Indian film)|''Animal'']], [[Fighter (2024 film)|''Fighter'']] and ''[[Pushpa 2: The Rule]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Riya |date=5 February 2026 |title=Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar sets all time record with 7.6 million views on Netflix debut; beats Animal, Pushpa 2, Jawan |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/ranveer-singh-dhurandhar-beats-animal-pushpa-2-jawan-sets-all-time-record-7-6-million-views-netflix-debut-aditya-dhar-101770256121888.html |access-date=26 February 2026 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> It was also the number one non-English film on Netflix in its first week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramachandran |first=Naman |date=7 February 2026 |title='Dhurandhar,' Indian Spy Thriller Set in Pakistan, Hits No. 1 on Netflix's Global Non-English Film Chart – and Tops India, Pakistan |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/dhurandhar-netflix-charts-global-india-pakistan-1236655619/ |access-date=26 February 2026 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Critical reception===
''Dhurandhar'' received mixed reviews from critics. {{Rotten Tomatoes prose|35|5.80|20|access-date={{RT data|access date}}|archive-url=}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dhurandhar (2025) |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/dhurandhar |access-date=23 December 2025 |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |language=en |archive-date=17 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251217072249/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/dhurandhar |url-status=live }}</ref>

Trade analyst [[Taran Adarsh]] gave 4.5/5 stars and described the film as a "brilliant" and "power-packed" action spectacle, citing its strong storytelling  and box-office appeal.<ref>{{Cite tweet|user=taran_adarsh|last=Adarsh|first=Taran|number=1997358248366834093|title=#OneWordReview... #Dhurandhar: BRILLIANT.|date=6 December 2025|access-date=6 December 2025}}</ref> Gayatri Nirmal of ''[[Pinkvilla]]'' gave 4/5 stars and praised the second-half, screenplay, and background score but criticised the runtime.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Movie Review: Don't let runtime fool you, Aditya Dhar fires up a crackling Ranveer-Akshaye showdown |url=https://www.pinkvilla.com/entertainment/reviews/dhurandhar-movie-review-dont-let-runtime-fool-you-aditya-dhar-fires-up-a-crackling-ranveer-akshaye-showdown-1398944 |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=PINKVILLA |language=en |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205142236/https://www.pinkvilla.com/entertainment/reviews/dhurandhar-movie-review-dont-let-runtime-fool-you-aditya-dhar-fires-up-a-crackling-ranveer-akshaye-showdown-1398944 |url-status=live }}</ref> Siddhant Adlakha of ''[[IGN]]'' rated the film 8/10 stars and wrote "Bollywood gangster saga ''Dhurandhar'' walks a fine line between raucous entertainment and hateful propaganda."<ref name="IGN">{{Cite web |last=Adlakha |first=Siddhant |date=9 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Review |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/dhurandhar-review |access-date=19 December 2025 |website=IGN |language=en |archive-date=15 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215122730/https://www.ign.com/articles/dhurandhar-review |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Renuka Vyavahare of ''[[The Times of India]]'' gave 3.5/5 stars and calling the film a "power-packed Karachi mafia thriller" where lead actor Ranveer Singh delivers a "subdued yet scorching" performance that largely anchors the film's impact. She highlighted the film's immersive world-building, the gritty, violent underworld of Karachi's Lyari mafia through a narrative structured in multiple chapters, with a runtime of nearly three-and-a-half hours that nevertheless "rarely feels overbearing", owing to what is described as "stylish, tight storytelling."<ref>{{cite web |last=Vyavahare |first=Renuka |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Movie Review: Ranveer Singh's subdued yet scorching screen presence fuels this power-packed Karachi mafia thriller |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/movie-reviews/dhurandhar/movie-review/125786542.cms |access-date=5 December 2025 |work=[[The Times of India]] |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205104113/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/movie-reviews/dhurandhar/movie-review/125786542.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

Devesh Sharma of ''[[Filmfare]]'' gave 3.5/5 stars and wrote "Aditya Dhar's ''Dhurandhar'' is a film that refuses to be contained by the grammar of a conventional spy thriller."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Devesh |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Movie Review: Sprawling Spy Film Buoyed By Performances |url=https://www.filmfare.com/reviews/bollywood-movies/dhurandhar-movie-review-sprawling-spy-film-buoyed-by-performances-79781.html |access-date=19 December 2025 |website=Filmfare |language=en}}</ref> ''[[Bollywood Hungama]]'' gave 3/5 stars and called it a well-made, ambitious big-screen experience with top-notch craft, memorable moments and some truly outstanding performances.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Movie Review: DHURANDHAR is a big-screen experience |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/dhurandhar/critic-review/dhurandhar-movie-review/dhurandhar-is-a-big-screen-experience/ |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=[[Bollywood Hungama]] |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205105026/https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/dhurandhar/critic-review/dhurandhar-movie-review/dhurandhar-is-a-big-screen-experience/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Rishabh Suri of ''[[Hindustan Times]]'' gave 3/5 stars and described it as a "lengthy yet loaded spy drama", highlighting the performances of Ranveer Singh and Akshaye Khanna as well Aditya Dhar's direction. He also noted the film occasionally feels too long and dense with too many sub-plots.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suri |first=Rishabh |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar review: Aditya Dhar's lengthy yet loaded spy drama is anchored by Ranveer Singh and Akshaye Khanna's brilliance |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-review-aditya-dhar-lengthy-loaded-spy-drama-anchored-by-ranveer-singh-akshaye-khanna-r-madhavan-sanjay-dutt-101764926015126.html |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=[[Hindustan Times]] |archive-date=14 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251214204833/https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-review-aditya-dhar-lengthy-loaded-spy-drama-anchored-by-ranveer-singh-akshaye-khanna-r-madhavan-sanjay-dutt-101764926015126.html |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Radhika Sharma of ''[[NDTV]]'' gave 3/5 stars and praised the cast performances and soundtrack, but criticised the second half calling it "a completely different film altogether."<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Review: Feral Ranveer Singh, Stellar Akshaye Khanna Drive An Indulgent Spy Thriller Home |url=https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/dhurandhar-review-feral-ranveer-singh-stellar-akshaye-khanna-drive-an-indulgent-spy-thriller-home-3-stars-9756586 |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=[[NDTV]] |archive-date=6 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251206024005/https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/dhurandhar-review-feral-ranveer-singh-stellar-akshaye-khanna-drive-an-indulgent-spy-thriller-home-3-stars-9756586 |url-status=live }}</ref> Taher Ahmed of ''[[Deccan Herald]]'' gave 3/5 stars and praised the performances, cinematography, and soundtrack, but criticised the runtime, pacing, and climax.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ahmed |first=Taher |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Review: Ranveer Singh Shines in Spy Thriller |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/entertainment/dhurandhar-movie-review-a-long-winding-game-of-chess-3821133 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205144346/https://www.deccanherald.com/entertainment/dhurandhar-movie-review-a-long-winding-game-of-chess-3821133 |archive-date=5 December 2025 |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref>

Simran Khan of ''[[Times Now]]'' gave 3/5 stars and wrote "The Aditya Dhar actioner's ending doesn't quite justify its lengthy runtime. However the adrenaline-pumping set pieces and relentless high-voltage action, paired with a background score that amplifies the drama and keeps the tension from ever dipping, make the ride worth it."<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Movie Review: Ranveer Singh Delivers Knockout Punch In Aditya Dhar's High-Voltage Actioner |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/entertainment-news/reviews/dhurandhar-movie-review-ranveer-singh-starrer-action-movie-imdb-ratings-public-reaction-review-153248351 |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=Times Now |language=en |archive-date=24 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251224160801/https://www.timesnownews.com/entertainment-news/reviews/dhurandhar-movie-review-ranveer-singh-starrer-action-movie-imdb-ratings-public-reaction-review-153248351 |url-status=live }}</ref> Karthik Ravindranath of ''[[The Week (Indian magazine)|The Week]]'' gave 3/5 stars and wrote "The film's powerful core is diluted by overt jingoism, unnecessary elements, and a tendency to dumb down its message for the audience. Despite these irritants, it remains a largely engaging, albeit flawed, tribute to India's heroes."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ravindranath |first=Karthik |date=5 December 2025 |title='Dhurandhar' review: Aditya Dhar made a brilliant movie, and then dumbed it down |url=https://www.theweek.in/review/movies/2025/12/05/dhurandhar-review-aditya-dhar-made-a-brilliant-movie-and-then-dumbed-it-down.html |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=The Week |language=en |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205120955/https://www.theweek.in/review/movies/2025/12/05/dhurandhar-review-aditya-dhar-made-a-brilliant-movie-and-then-dumbed-it-down.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Vineeta Kumar of ''[[India Today]]'' gave 3/5 stars and wrote "''Dhurandhar'' is a sprawling, muscular, politically sharp thriller that bites off a lot, and thanks to Khanna's explosive brilliance, chews most of it successfully."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Vineeta |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar review: Ranveer leads, but Akshaye rules this labyrinth of war, politics |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/reviews/story/dhurandhar-review-ranveer-singh-leads-but-akshaye-khanna-rules-this-labyrinth-of-war-politics-2831261-2025-12-05 |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

Kartik Bhardwaj of ''[[The New Indian Express]]'' gave 2.5/5 stars and wrote "The Aditya Dhar directorial seems like a film which is asking for your time, so that it can lay down its cards. But then two hours have passed and the ace seems to be still far up its sleeves."<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 December 2025|first=Kartik|last=Bhardwaj|title=Dhurandhar Movie Review: Ranveer Singh's spy/gangster drama crackles, ignites but never takes off|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/entertainment/review/2025/Dec/05/hindireview2025dec05dhurandhar-movie-review-ranveer-singhs-spygangster-drama-crackles-ignites-but-never-takes-off|access-date=6 December 2025 |website=The New Indian Express|language=en}}</ref> [[Deepa Gahlot]] of ''[[Rediff.com]]'' gave 2.5/5 stars and wrote "''Dhurandhar'' may not have the dark realism of a spy story, which a web show can manage. But it does not have the flamboyance either that has come to be associated with espionage movies."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gahlot |first=Deepa |author-link=Deepa Gahlot |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Review: Excessively Violent |url=https://www.rediff.com/movies/review/dhurandhar-review/20251205.htm |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=Rediff.com |language=en |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205223839/https://www.rediff.com/movies/review/dhurandhar-review/20251205.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Shalini Langer of ''[[The Indian Express]]'' gave 2.5/5 stars, and described the film as an "ambitious spy thriller" that ultimately works only "in flashes". She praised the film's scale, production values, and the attempt to depict the many layers of Lyari's criminal, political, and familial dynamics. However, she argued that despite its large cast and multiple narrative strands, the film only intermittently comes together, with its storytelling lacking consistency.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Langer |first=Shalini |date=5 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar movie review: Ranveer Singh's ambitious spy thriller works only in flashes |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/movie-review/dhurandhar-movie-review-ranveer-singhs-ambitious-spy-thriller-works-only-in-flashes-10403537/ |access-date=5 December 2025 |website=The Indian Express |archive-date=5 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205105011/https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/movie-review/dhurandhar-movie-review-ranveer-singhs-ambitious-spy-thriller-works-only-in-flashes-10403537/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Sakhi Thirani of ''[[Common Sense Media]]'' gave 1/5 stars and wrote "Despite dealing with sensitive issues like terrorism and war, ''Dhurandhar'' lacks a sincere or thoughtful storyline. Instead, it's more concerned with romanticizing torture, aggression, and machismo without examining the consequences of such violence."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thirani |first=Sakhi |date=18 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Movie Review |url=https://www.commonsensemedia.org/movie-reviews/dhurandhar |access-date=9 January 2026 |website=Common Sense Media |language=en}}</ref> [[Sadanand Dhume]] of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' wrote "Dhurandhar is the first major Bollywood movie to realistically portray the terrorist threat India faces."<ref name=DhumeWSJ>{{Cite web |last=Dhume |first=Sadanand |author-link=Sadanand Dhume |date=17 December 2025 |title=Opinion: 'Dhurandhar,' India's New Movie About Islamic Terrorism, Is a Hit |url=https://www.wsj.com/opinion/dhurandhar-indias-new-movie-about-islamic-terrorism-is-a-hit-a8f99b28 |url-access=subscription |access-date=19 December 2025 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> Columnist [[Shobhaa De]] wrote "It's not about politics. Yes, three and a half hours of it."<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 December 2025 |title=Shobhaa De Reviews Dhurandhar: "Ranveer Singh Chewed Up The Entire Film" |url=https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/shobhaa-de-reviews-dhurandhar-ranveer-singh-chewed-up-the-entire-film-9811920 |work=NDTV |archive-date=16 December 2025 |access-date=19 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251216203935/https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/shobhaa-de-reviews-dhurandhar-ranveer-singh-chewed-up-the-entire-film-9811920 |url-status=live }}</ref> Nandini Ramnath of ''[[Scroll.in]]'' wrote "A considerable stretch of the staggering 214-minute film is no different from gangland chronicles led by swaggering, aphorism-dripping men. ===Box office===
''Dhurandhar'' grossed {{INRConvert|1056.62|c}} in India and {{INRConvert|293.03|c}} in other territories for a worldwide total of {{INRConvert|1350.83|c}}.<ref name="BollyHungama">{{Cite web|date=6 December 2025|title=Dhurandhar Box Office Collection|url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/dhurandhar/box-office/|access-date=17 March 2026|website=[[Bollywood Hungama]]|language=en|archive-date=4 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260404153831/https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/dhurandhar/box-office/|url-status=live}}</ref> It is the [[List of Indian films of 2025|highest grossing Indian film of 2025]], [[List of highest-grossing Hindi films|third highest grossing Hindi film of all-time]], [[List of highest-grossing Indian films|fifth highest grossing Indian film of all-time]] and the highest grossing [[Central Board of Film Certification|A certified]] Indian film of all time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar Box Office Worldwide Collection Day 19: Ranveer's film earns Rs 925 cr globally; Dhurandhar 2 to release pan-India |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-box-office-collection-day-19-update-ranveer-singh-film-earns-over-rs-600-crore-10435460/ |website=The Indian Express |access-date=25 December 2025 |archive-date=24 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251224103221/https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-box-office-collection-day-19-update-ranveer-singh-film-earns-over-rs-600-crore-10435460/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaur |first=Arshdeep |date=21 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar is now the 6th highest earning Bollywood movie of all time – beats Animal, closely behind Pathaan for #5 |url=https://www.livemint.com/entertainment/dhurandhar-box-office-collection-day-16-6th-highest-earning-bollywood-movie-of-all-time-beats-animal-pathaan-11766290907467.html |access-date=21 December 2025 |website=mint |language=en |archive-date=21 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251221075006/https://www.livemint.com/entertainment/dhurandhar-box-office-collection-day-16-6th-highest-earning-bollywood-movie-of-all-time-beats-animal-pathaan-11766290907467.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The film had a worldwide opening of {{INRConvert|86.5|c}}, which drew significant attention within the trade due to its scale and unusual daily trends.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Dhurandhar Opening Weekend NUMBERS – Box Office India|url=https://boxofficeindia.com/report-details.php?articleid=9496#google_vignette|website=boxofficeindia.com|access-date=1 February 2026}}</ref> According to industry tracking, the film posted reported collections of around {{INRConvert|24|c}} on release day,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dhurandhar Opening Day Box Office – Box Office India|url=https://boxofficeindia.com/report-details.php?articleid=9494|website=boxofficeindia.com|access-date=1 February 2026}}</ref> {{INRConvert|27|c}} on the following day, and a sharp jump to {{INRConvert|35.5|c}} the day after. The reported opening weekend figures were described by trade observers as unprecedented.<ref name=":0" /> Trade analysts estimate ''Dhurandhar'' collected approximately ₹276 crore nett within nine days of release, placing it on course for a lifetime total of over ₹500 crore nett, with some projections suggesting it could become the first original Hindi film to cross ₹600 crore nett.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Dhurandhar Nine Days COLLECTIONS – UPADTED – Box Office India|url=https://boxofficeindia.com/report-details.php?articleid=9508|website=boxofficeindia.com|access-date=1 February 2026}}</ref>

Industry reports noted that, despite early adjustments to reported figures, the film's sustained second-week performance was driven largely by organic word of mouth and audience demand.<ref name=":1" /> ''Dhurandhar'''s second weekend and overall week performed better than first week.<ref>{{Cite news |title= Day-wise Dhurandhar Box Office |url= https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/dhurandhar/box-office/|access-date= |website= Bollywood Hungama
|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Dhurandhar box office collection day 35: Ranveer Singh film slows down, manages to cross ₹790 crore |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-box-office-collection-day-35-ranveer-singh-film-slows-down-manages-to-cross-790-crore-101767885856342.html |access-date= |website= Hindustan Times 
|language=en}}</ref> It earned over {{INR}}30 crore in Hindi net on its second Monday (11th day), the highest for any Indian film.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dhurandhar Goes FULL BEAST MODE: Blasts Rs. 30 cr. on Day 11 (2nd Monday) - Rs. 400 cr. tomorrow CONFIRMED! |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/box-office-special-features/dhurandhar-goes-full-beast-mode-blasts-rs-30-cr-day-11-2nd-monday-rs-400-cr-tomorrow-confirmed/ |access-date= 15 December 2025|website=Bollywood Hungama 
|language=en}}</ref> Trade reports stated ''Dhurandhar'' grossed approximately ₹880 crore worldwide within 19 days of release, placing it among the highest-grossing Hindi films globally.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Dhurandhar Worldwide Box Office (19 Days) – Box Office India|url=https://boxofficeindia.com/report-details.php?articleid=9526|website=boxofficeindia.com|access-date=1 February 2026}}</ref> With only [[Pathaan (film)|''Pathaan'']], [[Jawan (film)|''Jawan'']] (both 2023) and ''[[Pushpa 2: The Rule]]'' (2024) ahead at the time, analysts projected the film was on course to surpass the ₹1,000 crore worldwide mark, with final estimates ranging between ₹1,150–1,200 crore. Strong and sustained overseas performance, particularly in markets such as the United States, Canada and Australia, was cited as a major contributor to its continued growth, alongside dominant returns from key Indian territories.<ref name=":2" />

On 26 December 2025, ''Dhurandhar'' surpassed the ₹[[1000 Crore Club|1,000 crore]] worldwide box-office mark, reaching an estimated ₹1,003 crore in global grosses. The milestone was achieved through ₹668.8 crore in India nett collections and ₹206.91 crore in overseas earnings, becoming the fourth Hindi film to do so, ninth overall to achieve this feat, and marking Ranveer Singh's first ₹1,000 crore global grosser.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=26 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar storms into the Rs. 1,000 crore worldwide club; Ranveer Singh scores his first 1,000 cr. grosser |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/box-office-special-features/dhurandhar-storms-rs-1000-crore-worldwide-club-ranveer-singh-scores-first-1000-cr-grosser/ |work=Bollywood Hungama |date=26 December 2025 |archive-date=26 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226064834/https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/box-office-special-features/dhurandhar-storms-rs-1000-crore-worldwide-club-ranveer-singh-scores-first-1000-cr-grosser/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

On 7 January 2026, the film emerged as the [[List of highest domestic net collection of Hindi films|highest-grossing film in Hindi domestic net collections]] with {{INR}}895 crore Hindi net collections,<ref name="HT highest-grossing">{{Cite web |last=Mathur |first=Abhimanyu |date=7 January 2026 |title=Dhurandhar becomes highest grossing film in Hindi, beats Pushpa 2 with historic ₹831 crore haul |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/dhurandhar-becomes-highest-grossing-film-in-hindi-beats-pushpa-2-with-831-crore-haul-ranveer-singh-aditya-dhar-101767773372917.html |access-date=11 January 2026 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> [[List of highest-grossing films in India|highest grosser in Hindi language alone]], and also the most successful Bollywood film after the [[COVID-19|COVID-pandemic]].<ref name="HT highest-grossing" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Wadhwa |first=Aman |date=26 December 2025 |title=Dhurandhar box office collection: Ranveer Singh film becomes highest-grossing Indian movie in overseas markets in 2025, earns Rs... |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/bollywood/report-dhurandhar-box-office-collection-ranveer-singh-spy-thriller-becomes-first-indian-film-to-earn-rs-200-crore-overseas-in-2025-aditya-dhar-akshaye-khanna-sanjay-dutt-arjun-rampal-r-madhavan-3195015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226113748/https://www.dnaindia.com/bollywood/report-dhurandhar-box-office-collection-ranveer-singh-spy-thriller-becomes-first-indian-film-to-earn-rs-200-crore-overseas-in-2025-aditya-dhar-akshaye-khanna-sanjay-dutt-arjun-rampal-r-madhavan-3195015 |archive-date=26 December 2025 |access-date=26 December 2025 |work=DNA India}}</ref> This record was beaten by its sequel ''[[Dhurandhar: The Revenge]]'' in April 2026, which grossed over {{INR}}1000 crore.<ref>{{Cite news |title= Dhurandhar:The Revenge Box office|url= https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/dhurandhar-the-revenge/box-office/|access-date= |website=
|language=en}}</ref> The film's foreign distributor Pranab Kapadia estimates the film lost out on US$10 million (₹90 crore) in earnings because its release was banned in Gulf countries.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 December 2025 |title=Ranveer Singh's ''Dhurandhar'' Lost Around Rs 90 Crore Due To Ban In Middle East, Reveals Overseas Distributor |url=https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/ranveer-singhs-dhurandhar-lost-around-rs-90-crore-due-to-ban-in-middle-east-reveals-overseas-distributor-10124914 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260104193703/https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/ranveer-singhs-dhurandhar-lost-around-rs-90-crore-due-to-ban-in-middle-east-reveals-overseas-distributor-10124914 |archive-date=4 January 2026 |access-date=8 February 2026 |work=NDTV |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=1 January 2026 |title=Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar loses $10 million (Rs 90 crore) due to Gulf ban, says overseas distributor, 'We have to respect the rules of every country' |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/ranveer-singhs-dhurandhar-loses-10-million-rs-90-crore-due-to-gulf-ban-says-overseas-distributor-we-have-to-respect-the-rules-of-every-country/articleshow/126279027.cms |access-date=8 February 2026 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mazumdar |first=Shreyanka |date=30 December 2025 |title=Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar Could've Earned $10M More If Not For Middle East Ban, Reveals Distributor |url=https://www.news18.com/movies/bollywood/ranveer-singhs-dhurandhar-couldve-earned-10m-more-if-not-for-middle-east-ban-reveals-distributor-9801122.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106065943/https://www.news18.com/movies/bollywood/ranveer-singhs-dhurandhar-couldve-earned-10m-more-if-not-for-middle-east-ban-reveals-distributor-9801122.html |archive-date=6 January 2026 |access-date=8 February 2026 |work=News18 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Factual accuracy and political messaging==
The film begins with a disclaimer stating it represents fiction,<ref name="IE Dhruv Rathee">{{Cite web |date=22 December 2025 |title=Dhruv Rathee slams Dhurandhar as 'false propaganda', switches off comments as actors defend film: 'That was India's situation' |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/youtuber-dhruv-rathee-slams-dhurandhar-propaganda-actors-defend-film-india-26-11-10431751/ |access-date=9 January 2026 |website=The Indian Express |language=en |archive-date=23 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251223105801/https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/youtuber-dhruv-rathee-slams-dhurandhar-propaganda-actors-defend-film-india-26-11-10431751/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="AJ"/> however, it repeatedly tells the audience it is inspired by real events.<ref name="IE Dhruv Rathee"/><ref name="Ishita Sengupta">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eQYtzce3UIo |title=Hindi Critics Vs Pakistani Reporter on Dhurandhar |date=15 December 2025 |last=Sengupta |first=Ishita |type=Video |language=en |publisher=Editor Breakdown |time=0:15 |access-date=11 January 2026 |quote=And then 10 minutes, 15 minutes into it, it says that it's based on incredibly true events.
