Director [[Karan Johar]] initially intended to cast [[Shah Rukh Khan]], [[Kajol]], [[Rani Mukerji]], and [[Ajay Devgn]] in the principal roles of Dev, Maya, Rhea, and Rishi, respectively.<ref name="SRKANK" /> However, both Devgn and [[Saif Ali Khan]] declined the film due to their prior commitments to [[Vishal Bhardwaj]]'s [[Omkara (2006 film)|''Omkara'']] (2006), in which they played leading roles.<ref name=":5" /> Saif had previously collaborated with Johar on ''[[Kal Ho Naa Ho]]'' (2003) after [[Salman Khan]] declined the role of Rohit because he did not wish to "play second fiddle". Johar subsequently cast [[Abhishek Bachchan]] as Rishi after being impressed by his performance in ''[[Yuva]]'' (2004), marking Bachchan's first official collaboration with Dharma Productions after initially shooting for a cameo appearance in ''[[Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham...]]'' (2001) which was edited out of the film.<ref name="SRKANK" />

The role of Maya was initially offered to Kajol, which was intended to mark her return to cinema after a five-year hiatus from full time acting following ''[[Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham...]]'' (2001) and a [[Cameo appearance|cameo]] appearance in ''[[Kal Ho Naa Ho]]'' (2003). She declined the part due to creative disagreements and a prior commitment to [[Yash Raj Films]]' [[Fanaa (2006 film)|''Fanaa'']] (2006), which she found more compelling.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-08-07 |title=THROWBACK: When Kajol revealed why she rejected Rani Mukerji's role in Shah Rukh Khan's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna; 'I just didn't agree…' |url=https://www.pinkvilla.com/entertainment/news/throwback-when-kajol-revealed-why-she-rejected-rani-mukerjis-role-in-shah-rukh-khans-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-i-just-didnt-agree-1336575 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=PINKVILLA }}</ref> In an episode of [[List of Koffee with Karan episodes#Season 2 (2007)|''Koffee with Karan'']], Kajol also expressed discomfort with the film's treatment of extramarital relationships, stating, “Yes, there were some points I disagreed with. As a woman... I feel when you get married, you should want to work on it.”<ref name=":0" /> Despite turning down the role, she made a [[Cameo appearance|cameo]] appearance in the song “Rock 'N' Roll Soniye.”

Following Kajol's departure, Mukerji—who was originally cast as Rhea—was recast in the role of Maya, which she later described as “a turning point” in her life.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rani Mukerji says Karan Johar's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna was a turning point in her life. Here's why |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/bollywood/story/rani-mukerji-says-shah-rukh-khan-and-karan-johars-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-was-a-turning-point-in-her-life-heres-why-exclusive-2347871-2023-03-17 |access-date=15 September 2023 |website=India Today|date=17 March 2023 }}</ref> [[Preity Zinta]]—who had previously collaborated with Johar on ''[[Kal Ho Naa Ho]]'' (2003) after [[Kareena Kapoor]] refused the role of Naina due to a salary dispute with Johar—was subsequently brought in to portray Rhea, describing the role as a deliberate shift from her typically vivacious screen image: “I play this cold woman,” she explained, “which wasn’t easy for a warm person like me to do.”<ref name="bubbly image">{{cite web |date=17 March 2006 |title=I'm sick of my bubbly image: Preity Zinta |url=http://www.sify.com/movies/i-m-sick-of-my-bubbly-image-preity-zinta-news-bollywood-kkfvpnghabj.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120820031203/http://www.sify.com/movies/i-m-sick-of-my-bubbly-image-preity-zinta-news-bollywood-kkfvpnghabj.html |archive-date=20 August 2012 |access-date=5 November 2007 |website=[[Sify]]}}</ref> [[Ameesha Patel]] was also considered for the role but declined due to scheduling conflicts.<ref name=":5" />

[[Amitabh Bachchan]] and [[Kirron Kher]] were cast as Samarjit ("Sam"), Rishi's father, and Kamaljit ("Kamal"), Dev's mother, respectively. [[Arjun Rampal]] was cast as Jai Mehra, Rhea's boss, replacing earlier considerations for [[John Abraham]]. Despite this, Abraham was later featured in a [[Cameo appearance|cameo]] as a DJ in the song “Where’s the Party Tonight?” Director [[Tarun Mansukhani]] also made a cameo appearance as one of Rishi's friends.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Aryan Khan's journey from being a child star to aspiring director: Here's all you need to know about Shah Rukh Khan's son |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/aryan-khans-journey-from-being-a-child-star-to-aspiring-director-heres-all-you-need-to-know-about-shah-rukh-khans-son/articleshow/80478735.cms |access-date=23 October 2021 |work=The Times of India |date=3 October 2021 |archive-date=5 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211005092016/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/aryan-khans-journey-from-being-a-child-star-to-aspiring-director-heres-all-you-need-to-know-about-shah-rukh-khans-son/articleshow/80478735.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

The role of Dev and Rhea's young son, Arjun, was portrayed by [[Ahsaas Channa]], a female child actor known for convincingly playing young boys in earlier projects. The decision was considered unconventional, but her performance was well received.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WUYh8YavveU |title=Ahsaas Channa on playing Shah Rukh Khan's son in 'Kabhi Alvida Na Kehna' #shorts #youtubeshorts |date=2024-12-26 |last=Bollywood Bubble |access-date=2025-04-15 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

[[Riteish Deshmukh]] and Aryan Khan, Shah Rukh Khan's son, filmed cameo appearances that were ultimately removed during editing. Additionally, both Johar and his assistant director [[Ayan Mukerji]] appeared briefly on screen—Johar in the film's final train sequence seated behind Shah Rukh Khan, and Mukerji in the “Tumhi Dekho Naa” montage, where he stepped in as an extra due to a shortage of background performers. He appears wearing a green sweater and carrying gift boxes.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2020-08-28 |title=Fashion Friday: When Rani Mukerji wore six sensuous chiffon sarees in Tumhi Dekho Naa |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/lifestyle/fashion/story/fashion-friday-when-rani-mukerji-wore-six-sensuous-chiffon-sarees-in-tumhi-dekho-naa-1716167-2020-08-28 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=India Today }}</ref>

Notably, the principal cast—excluding [[Abhishek Bachchan]]—had previously worked together in [[Yash Chopra]]'s ''[[Veer-Zaara]]'' (2004).<ref>{{cite web |date=31 May 2023 |title=Amitabh Bachchan was nervous while shooting KANK, embarrassed Shah Rukh Khan questioned Karan Johar: 'What is this nonsense?' |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/shah-rukh-khan-amitabh-bachchan-embarrassed-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-karan-johar-autobiography-8638403/lite/ |access-date=31 May 2023 |website=Indian Express}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=31 May 2023 |title=Karan Johar reveals most actors were awkward on the sets of Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/karan-johar-reveals-most-actors-were-awkward-on-the-sets-of-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna/articleshow/100649531.cms |access-date=12 August 2023 |website=Times of India}}</ref>

=== Filming ===
[[File:Union Station New Haven waiting area.gk.jpg|thumb|A major portion of the film was shot at the [[Union Station (New Haven)|Union Station]] in [[New Haven, Connecticut|New Haven]].|alt=<nowiki>Interior of [[Union Station]] in [[New Haven|New Haven, Connecticut]], showing arched windows, hanging globe lights, digital departure boards, and passengers seated or walking through the concourse.          </nowiki>]]

Although ''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' is set in [[New York City]], a significant portion of the film was shot in the [[United States]], primarily in [[Connecticut]]. Key scenes were filmed in [[East Hartford]] and [[New Haven]], including a [[Association football|soccer]] game sequence at [[Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field|Rentschler Field]], home to the [[UConn Huskies football|UConn Huskies football team]], with the stadium's "UConn" logo visible in several shots. Scenes intended to depict [[Grand Central Terminal]] were filmed at New Haven's [[Union Station (New Haven)|Union Station]] and [[Philadelphia]]’s [[30th Street Station]]. The film was primarily shot over 90 days in the United States, with additional scenes completed on four custom-built sets in [[Mumbai]]. During the U.S. shoot, [[Rani Mukerji]] reportedly suffered from a severe skin allergy due to extreme weather conditions.<ref>{{cite web |title=KANK launch |url=http://www3.dharma-production.com/KANK/launch.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071126060438/http://www3.dharma-production.com/KANK/launch.html |archive-date=26 November 2007 |access-date=31 January 2008 |website=KANI: Official website of Dharma Productions}}</ref>

One of the most challenging sequences to film was the song “Tumhi Dekho Naa,” which was shot across several iconic locations in and around New York City. Each color-themed segment corresponded to a specific location: blue at [[Columbia University]], yellow at [[Wall Street]], orange at [[Bear Mountain State Park]], pink at [[St. Patrick's Cathedral (New York City)|St. Patrick's Cathedral]], red at [[Landmarks of Hoboken, New Jersey#Pier A Park|Pier A Park]] in [[Hoboken, New Jersey]], and green at Union Station in New Haven. The red sequence was originally meant to include [[Rainmaking|artificial rain]], but freezing temperatures caused water droplets to turn into ice mid-air, creating safety risks. Instead, the scene was filmed on a sunny day using two hundred red umbrellas. The green segment faced a shortage of extras, requiring crew members—including [[assistant director]] [[Ayan Mukerji]]—to fill in.<ref name=":2" />

The freezing temperatures during the New York schedule caused further complications. During the same song, temperatures dropped to –14&nbsp;°C (7&nbsp;°F), causing significant discomfort for Mukerji, who was dressed in a [[Chiffon (fabric)|chiffon]] saree. The conditions were so harsh that she was unable to walk unassisted and had to be carried to her vehicle by her cousin Ayan Mukerji.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-01-02 |title=When Karan Johar nearly 'killed' Rani Mukerji during Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna shoot |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/when-karan-johar-nearly-killed-rani-mukerji-during-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-shoot/articleshow/106482569.cms |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> Despite these challenges, director [[Karan Johar]] continued the shoot as planned, making only minor adjustments to ensure safety.

Due to a scheduling conflict, Johar delegated the direction of a key hotel scene to [[Shah Rukh Khan]]. Initially reluctant, Khan completed the sequence with remote guidance from [[Amitabh Bachchan]] over the phone.<ref name=":5" />

== Themes and analysis ==
''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' explores themes of [[Infidelity|marital infidelity]], emotional dissatisfaction, and the complexities of modern relationships. The narrative follows Dev and Maya, both in unfulfilling marriages, who develop a deep emotional connection that leads to an [[Affair#Extramarital affair|extramarital affair]]. The film examines the notion of encountering a [[soulmate]] after marriage and the resulting emotional and familial consequences.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 March 2023 |title=Here's why Karan Johar had big fight with Aditya Chopra over SRK and Rani's sex scene in Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/karan-johar-had-big-fight-with-aditya-chopra-over-sex-scene-in-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-101677930471028-amp.html |access-date=20 July 2023 |website=Hindustan Times}}</ref>

Director [[Karan Johar]] cited a real-life incident he witnessed in [[London]], where a couple amicably ended their marriage, as a key inspiration for the story. This event, combined with thematic elements from [[Richard Linklater]]'s ''[[Before Sunset]]'' (2004), motivated Johar to explore the deeper dynamics of love, commitment, and the consequences of relationship choices.<ref name="SRKANK" />

Johar addressed criticisms suggesting that the film glorifies infidelity, clarifying that his intention was not to endorse extramarital affairs but to portray the emotional turmoil and consequences involved. In interviews, he emphasized that the film reflects the emotional complexity of contemporary relationships and the importance of understanding one's personal needs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Agencies |date=2024-01-14 |title='People said I endorsed infidelity through Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna' |url=https://www.millenniumpost.in/entertainment/people-said-i-endorsed-infidelity-through-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-548158 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=www.millenniumpost.in }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-08-04 |title=ETimes Decoded: Revisiting Karan Johar's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna, that blurred the lines between right and wrong when it came to love... |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/etimes-decoded-revisiting-karan-johars-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-that-blurred-the-lines-between-right-and-wrong-when-it-came-to-love-/articleshow/102401923.cms |access-date=2025-04-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

The film's themes align with earlier works such as [[Yash Chopra]]'s [[Silsila (1981 film)|''Silsila'']] (1981) and [[Mahesh Bhatt]]'s [[Arth (film)|''Arth'']] (1982), both of which tackled similar subject matter. Comparisons have also been drawn with [[Mike Nichols]]' [[Closer (film)|''Closer'']] (2004) and Johar's own production ''[[Gehraiyaan]]'' (2022), directed by [[Shakun Batra]], for their exploration of romantic conflict and moral ambiguity.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 February 2022 |title=Gehraiyaan isn't Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna. It's millennial and love doesn't win |url=https://theprint.in/feature/reel-take/gehraiyaan-isnt-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-its-millennial-and-love-doesnt-win/827147/ |access-date=23 September 2022 |website=The Print}}</ref>

== Soundtrack ==
{{Main|Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna (soundtrack album)}}

The soundtrack of ''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' was composed by [[Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy]], with lyrics by [[Javed Akhtar]].<ref>{{cite web |date=2006-06-14 |title=Karan Johar on KANK's Music |url=http://www.sify.com/movies/karan-johar-on-kank-s-music-news-bollywood-kkfvjMicbgc.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021100229/http://www.sify.com/movies/karan-johar-on-kank-s-music-news-bollywood-kkfvjMicbgc.html |archive-date=2012-10-21 |access-date=2011-08-17 |website=[[Sify]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title='Karan Johar likes his English hooks' |url=http://www.rediff.com/movies/2006/aug/10sel.htm |access-date=2011-08-17 |work=Rediff.com |archive-date=10 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810203409/http://www.rediff.com/movies/2006/aug/10sel.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> It marked their second collaboration with director [[Karan Johar]] after ''[[Kal Ho Naa Ho]]'' (2003). The soundtrack was released in the [[United Kingdom]] on 12 June 2006 and officially launched in India on 16 June 2006 during the [[7th IIFA Awards]] in [[Dubai]].<ref>{{cite web |date=2006-06-09 |title='Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna' music launch at I.I.F.A |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/box-office-special-features/2006-lowest-openers-in-u-k/ |access-date=2011-08-17 |website=[[Bollywood Hungama]] |archive-date=15 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090915223447/http://www.bollywoodhungama.com/news/2006/02/11/6675/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The album received widespread acclaim for its melodies, modern arrangements, and thematic resonance, particularly the songs "Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna", "Mitwa", and "Tumhi Dekho Naa", which became chart-topping hits.<ref name="rediff22">{{cite web |date=2006-06-21 |title=Great tunes from KANK |url=http://in.rediff.com/movies/2006/jun/16kank.htm |access-date=2011-08-17 |work=Rediff.com |archive-date=8 July 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060708140920/http://in.rediff.com/movies/2006/jun/16kank.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The soundtrack achieved strong commercial performance upon release. It debuted at number one on Indian music charts and remained at the top position for ten consecutive weeks. Competing with other popular soundtracks such as ''[[Fanaa (2006 film)|Fanaa]]'', ''[[Krrish]]'', and ''[[Gangster: A Love Story]]'', it sold approximately 1.9 million units, according to ''[[Box Office India]]'', making it the second highest-selling Bollywood soundtrack of 2006, behind only ''[[Dhoom 2]]''.<ref>{{cite web |date=2006-09-01 |title=Top Ten albums of the week |url=http://www.bollywoodhungama.com/features/2006/09/01/1504/index.html |access-date=2011-08-17 |website=[[Bollywood Hungama]]}}{{dead link|date=July 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=2009-01-22 |title=Music Hits 2000-2009 |url=http://www.boxofficeindia.com/showProd.php?itemCat=286&catName=MjAwMC0yMDA5 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090122120910/http://www.boxofficeindia.com/showProd.php?itemCat=286&catName=MjAwMC0yMDA5 |archive-date=22 January 2009 |access-date=2011-08-17 |website=Box Office India}}</ref>

== Release ==
The [[teaser trailer]] for ''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' was unveiled alongside the theatrical release of [[Fanaa (2006 film)|''Fanaa'']] on 26 May 2006, as part of the film's promotional campaign.<ref>{{cite web |date=1 June 2006 |title=Bonus treat with Aamir's Fanaa |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/bonus-treat-with-aamir-s-fanaa/story-yGgiHw6ioJE78njAClwZ2H.html |website=Hindustan Times}}</ref> The film premiered globally on 11 August 2006 and was released across more than 1,200 screens worldwide, marking one of the widest international releases for a Hindi-language film at the time.<ref name="sify.com">{{cite web |title=KANK opens in 1,200 screens |url=http://sify.com/movies/bollywood/fullstory.php?id=14257901 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930205532/http://sify.com/movies/bollywood/fullstory.php?id=14257901 |archive-date=30 September 2007 |access-date=24 August 2007 |work=sify.com}}</ref>

In the United States, the [[Motion Picture Association|Motion Picture Association of America]] (MPAA) initially assigned the film an R rating for strong language and sexual content. Following an appeal by the distributors, the film was reclassified with a PG-13 rating.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

== Reception ==

=== Critical reception ===
''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' received mixed-to-positive reviews in India and internationally. Critics praised its [[Ensemble cast|ensemble]] performances, emotional complexity, and bold narrative treatment of extramarital relationships, though many noted its excessive runtime and melodramatic tone as key drawbacks. On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the film holds an approval rating of 58% based on 12 reviews, with the consensus stating: “Though ambitious in its attempt to explore infidelity and emotional isolation, ''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' is weighed down by its excessive runtime and melodramatic execution.”<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna {{!}} Rotten Tomatoes |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/kabhi_alvida_naa_kehna |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=www.rottentomatoes.com  |archive-date=30 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630120404/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/kabhi_alvida_naa_kehna |url-status=live }}</ref> On [[IMDb]], it has a rating of 6.1/10 based on over 23,000 user votes.<ref>{{Citation |last=Johar |first=Karan |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |date=2006-08-11 |type=Drama, Romance |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0449999/?ref_=nv_sr_srsg_1_tt_4_nm_4_in_0_q_kank |access-date=2025-04-14 |others=Shah Rukh Khan, Rani Mukerji, Amitabh Bachchan |publisher=Dharma Productions, Dillywood}}</ref>

In India, [[Taran Adarsh]] from ''[[Bollywood Hungama]]'' called it [[Karan Johar]]’s "finest work to date," praising the screenplay's contrast between light and emotionally intense moments, and lauding the chemistry among the cast.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hungama |first=Bollywood |date=2006-08-11 |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna Review 4.5/5 {{!}} Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna Movie Review {{!}} Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna 2006 Public Review {{!}} Film Review |website=[[Bollywood Hungama]] |url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna/critic-review/kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-movie-review/ |access-date=2025-04-14 }}</ref> [[Rajeev Masand]] ([[Network18 Group|''IBNLive'']]) awarded the film 4 out of 5 stars, commending Johar's control over narrative structure and his ability to elevate ordinary moments with dialogue and score.<ref>{{cite web |title=Masand's verdict: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |url=http://ibnlive.in.com/news/masands-verdict--kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna/18315-8.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090721012607/http://ibnlive.in.com/news/masands-verdict--kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna/18315-8.html |archive-date=21 July 2009 |website=IBN Live}}</ref> [[Baradwaj Rangan]] noted the film was “too long, too weepy,” but appreciated its thematic depth and subversion of genre tropes. ''Nowrunning'' echoed this sentiment, applauding the film's departure from traditional family-centric storytelling in favor of exploring uncomfortable emotional truths.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-08-13 |title=Review: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |url=https://baradwajrangan.wordpress.com/2006/08/13/review-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna/ |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=Baradwaj Rangan  |archive-date=22 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922002805/https://baradwajrangan.wordpress.com/2006/08/13/review-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

However, not all feedback was positive. [[Kaveree Bamzai]] (''[[India Today]]'') felt Johar lost his usual balance between emotional weight and levity, while Raja Sen (''[[Rediff.com]]'') criticized the film's script, characters, and length, calling it "a mammoth 22-reel experience" with "cardboard characters and glitzy emptiness."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-08-28 |title=Movie review: 'Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna' starring Shah Rukh Khan, Abhishek Bachchan |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/your-week/story/20060828-film-review-of-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-784871-2006-08-27 |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=India Today }}</ref><ref name="Sen">{{cite web |date=25 August 2006 |title=KANK is an exhausting film by Raja Sen |url=http://www.rediff.com/movies/2006/aug/11kank.htm |access-date=30 January 2008 |work=Rediff.com |archive-date=20 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171020124431/http://www.rediff.com/movies/2006/aug/11kank.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Internationally, the film received a warmer reception. [[Neil Genzlinger]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' praised the film's visual excesses and comic timing, noting its larger-than-life appeal.<ref name="Genzlinger">{{cite news |last=Genzlinger |first=Neil |date=26 August 2006 |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna, a Bollywood Divorce Tale |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/08/12/movies/12kabh.html?ex=1313035200&en=44270ed672924be2&ei=5088&partner=rssnyt&emc=rss |access-date=30 January 2008 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> Derek Elley of [[Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] highlighted the film's emotional volatility and credited the performances of [[Amitabh Bachchan]] and [[Preity Zinta]].<ref name="Elley">{{cite web |last=Elley |first=Derek |date=30 August 2006 |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |url=https://www.variety.com/review/VE1117931316.html?categoryid=31&cs=1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061230002241/https://variety.com/review/VE1117931316.html?categoryid=31&cs=1 |archive-date=30 December 2006 |access-date=31 January 2008 |work=Variety}}</ref> ''[[The Austin Chronicle]]'' lauded its restraint and internalized emotional tone, calling it a “slow and elegant descent into emotional tumult rarely explored in mainstream cinema.”<ref>{{Cite web |title=Movie Review: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |url=https://www.austinchronicle.com/events/film/2006-08-11/kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna/ |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=www.austinchronicle.com }}</ref>

=== Box office ===
''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' was released on 11 August 2006 across more than 1,200 screens worldwide.<ref name="sify.com" /> The film opened to strong box office results, recording a then-record opening in several Indian cities and grossing approximately ₹27.85 [[crore]] (equivalent to US$6.2 million at the time) in its first week in India. Although it remains [[Karan Johar]]’s lowest-grossing film in India in terms of net domestic collections (unadjusted for inflation), it ranked as the [[List of Hindi films of 2006|fourth highest-grossing Hindi film of 2006]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kabhi Alvida Na Kehna - Movie - Box Office India |url=https://www.boxofficeindia.com/movie.php?movieid=364 |access-date=2025-04-15 |website=www.boxofficeindia.com |archive-date=22 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230822195953/https://www.boxofficeindia.com/movie.php?movieid=364 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Internationally, the film performed exceptionally well. It grossed $10.56 million overseas, becoming the third-highest overseas grosser for a Bollywood film as of 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=KANK |url=http://www.boxofficeindia.com/showProd.php?itemCat=308&catName=TGlmZXRpbWU= |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131006052405/http://www.boxofficeindia.com/showProd.php?itemCat=308&catName=TGlmZXRpbWU%3D |archive-date=6 October 2013 |access-date=10 August 2007 |work=Box Office India |df=dmy-all}}</ref> During its opening weekend, it collected $1.35 million in the United States and $1.4 million (£750,000) in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web |title=KANK declared a hit in India |url=http://www.boxofficeindia.com/2006.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070808100831/http://www.boxofficeindia.com/2006.htm <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date=8 August 2007 |access-date=10 August 2007 |work=Box Office India}}</ref> Its total box office reached $3.27 million in the U.S. and over £5.07 million in the UK. One factor contributing to its American success was its release across 64 theatres, including non-traditional markets such as [[Miami]], [[Tampa]], and [[Raleigh, North Carolina|Raleigh]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=kabhialvidanaakehna.htm |access-date=10 August 2007 |work=Box Office Mojo}}</ref>

Upon release, the film surpassed ''[[Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham...]]'' (2001) to become the highest-grossing Indian film worldwide.<ref name="sify.com" /> Its total global gross amounted to ₹113 crore (equivalent to US$37 million at the time),<ref name="BOI gross" /><ref name="currency" /><ref name="Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna" /> making it the top-grossing Indian film of the decade in overseas markets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Top Worldwide Grossers 2006 |url=https://boxofficeindia.com/worldwide-total-gross.php?year=2006 |website=boxofficeindia.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Box Office India overseas earners |url=http://www.boxofficeindia.com/cpages.php?pageName=overseas_earners |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080207070143/http://www.boxofficeindia.com/cpages.php?pageName=overseas_earners |archive-date=7 February 2008 |access-date=19 May 2010 |work=Box Office India}}</ref> When adjusted for inflation, it remains one of the highest-grossing Indian films globally.<ref>{{cite web |title=Top Lifetime Inflation Adjusted Grossers Worldwide |url=http://www.boxofficeindia.com/showProd.php?itemCat=313&catName=TGlmZXRpbWUgQWRqdXN0ZWQ= |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204140124/http://www.boxofficeindia.com/showProd.php?itemCat=313&catName=TGlmZXRpbWUgQWRqdXN0ZWQ%3D |archive-date=4 December 2013 |access-date=1 June 2011 |website=Box Office India}}</ref>

== Accolades ==
{{Main|List of accolades received by Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna}}A recipient of several accolades, ''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' led the [[52nd Filmfare Awards]] with 23 nominations, winning [[Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] for Abhishek Bachchan. The film also received one [[International Indian Film Academy Awards|IIFA Award]], two [[Global Indian Film Awards]], one [[People's Choice Awards India|People's Choice Award India]], one [[Screen Awards|Screen Award]], one [[Stardust Awards|Stardust Award]], and five [[Zee Cine Awards]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite web |author=IndiaFM News Bureau |date=10 June 2007 |title=IIFA Awards 2007 winners |url=http://www.indiafm.com/features/2007/06/10/2750/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071228080201/http://www.indiafm.com/features/2007/06/10/2750/index.html |archive-date=28 December 2007 |access-date=12 July 2021 |website=[[Bollywood Hungama]]}}</ref>

It was also among the films considered for India's official submission to the [[79th Academy Awards|2007]] [[Academy Award for Best International Feature Film]], alongside ''[[Rang De Basanti]]'', ''[[Krrish]]'', ''[[Omkara (2006 film)|Omkara]]'', and ''[[Lage Raho Munna Bhai]]''.<ref>{{cite web |date=28 August 2006 |title=Final cut: Which one will be our be our best bet at Oscars? |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/final-cut-which-one-will-be-our-best-bet-at-oscars/articleshow/1930939.cms?from=mdr |access-date=16 July 2021 |website=The Times of India}}</ref> Ultimately, ''Rang De Basanti'' was selected as the country's entry.<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 September 2006 |title=Rang De Basanti is India's entry for the Oscars |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/rang-de-basanti-is-india-s-entry-for-the-oscars-106092500053_1.html |access-date=16 July 2021 |newspaper=Business Standard India |agency=Press Trust of India}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' has gained recognition over time for its thematic boldness and unconventional portrayal of romantic relationships in Hindi cinema. The film has been retrospectively described as a [[Cult film|cult classic]] and ahead of its time, particularly for its exploration of marital infidelity and emotional dissatisfaction within urban relationships.<ref name="KANK1">{{Cite web |last=Sasi |first=Tusshar |date=2016-08-10 |title='Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna': Mainstream Bollywood At Its Bravest Best |url=https://filmysasi.com/kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna-10-years-review/ |access-date=2023-08-11 |website=Filmy Sasi }}</ref><ref name="KANK2">{{Cite web |date=2022-02-21 |title='Silsila,' 'KANK,' 'Gehraiyaan': Reflects Time And Cultural Attitude Towards Relationships And Infidelity |url-status=dead|archive-date=18 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230118214227/http://reelisticviews.com/silsila-kank-gehraiyaan-reflects-time-and-cultural-attitude-towards-relationships-and-infidelity/ }}</ref> It has also been cited by ''[[Filmfare]]'' as one of the best ensemble cast films in Hindi cinema, and was featured by critic [[Shubhra Gupta]] in her book ''50 Films That Changed Bollywood'', noting its impact on the narrative boundaries of mainstream Hindi cinema.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 April 2023 |title=10 Bollywood Family Dramas Movies Featuring An Ensemble Cast |work=Pickle}}</ref>

In a retrospective feature, ''[[Filmfare]]'' observed that "''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' was made ahead of its time. The subject and the treatment forced people to sit up and think out of their comfort zone."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Paul |first1=Ushnota |date=11 August 2016 |title=10 reasons why we still love Kabhi |url=https://www.vervemagazine.in/arts-and-culture/a-nostaligic-re-living-of-kabhi-alvida-naa-kehna |url-status=live |access-date=2023-08-20 |website=Times of India }}</ref> ''[[Firstpost]]'' referred to the film as [[Karan Johar]]'s "most polarized work" as a filmmaker,<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 August 2022 |website=Film Companion }}</ref>

The film is often cited among the notable works of Johar, [[Shah Rukh Khan]], [[Rani Mukerji]], [[Abhishek Bachchan]], and [[Preity Zinta]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna at 10: Shah == Home media and streaming ==
''Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna'' was released on [[DVD]] on 26 October 2006 by [[Yash Raj Films]]. The two-disc set featured [[Dolby Digital|Dolby Digital 5.1]] audio, optional subtitles in English, Arabic, Malay, Tamil, and Telugu, and included bonus content such as [[deleted scene]]s and behind-the-scenes featurettes.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.blu-ray.com/dvd/Kabhi-Alvida-Naa-Kehna-DVD/126420/ |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna DVD |access-date=2025-04-15 |via=www.blu-ray.com}}</ref> The film was subsequently released on [[Blu-ray]] on 18 May 2010. The Blu-ray edition featured a [[1080p]] high-definition transfer, [[DTS-HD Master Audio|DTS-HD Master Audio 5.1]], and was issued as a region-free release with English and Arabic subtitles.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Kabhi-Alvida-Naa-Kehna-Blu-ray/11845/ |title=Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna Blu-ray (India) |access-date=2025-04-15 |via=www.blu-ray.com}}</ref>

As of 2025, the film is available for streaming on platforms including [[Netflix]] and [[Amazon Prime Video]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=WATCH! Shahrukh Khan and Rani Mukerji's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna on Netflix |url=https://www.netflix.com/in/title/70057651?preventIntent=true |access-date=2021-12-28 |website=Netflix }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=WATCH! Shahrukh Khan and Rani Mukerji's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna on Amazon Prime |url=https://www.primevideo.com/detail/Kabhi-Alvida-Naa-Kehna/0P53I0VNZ3ZG8GY68CGHDNVSO7 |access-date=2021-11-29 |website=Amazon Prime Video }}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: List of 20th-century films considered the worst
======================================================================

{{Short description|none}}
{{about|films considered the worst from the 20th century|21st-century films considered the worst|List of 21st-century films considered the worst|other uses|Lists of films considered the worst}}
{{protection padlock|reason=Persistent [[WP:Disruptive editing|disruptive editing]]|small=yes}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2022}}
{{Use American English|date=March 2023}}
{{Dynamic list}}
[[File:Reefer Madness (1936).jpg|220px|thumb|''[[Reefer Madness]]'' (1936), one of the earliest films to garner particularly negative reviews<ref name="psmag">{{cite magazine|last=Lincoln|first=Kevin|title=The Benefits of Being the Worst Movie Ever Made|url=https://psmag.com/economics/benefits-worst-movie-ever-made-84813|access-date=October 23, 2017|magazine=[[Pacific Standard]]|date=July 2, 2014|archive-date=October 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023115728/https://psmag.com/economics/benefits-worst-movie-ever-made-84813|url-status=live}}</ref>]]

The [[film]]s listed below have been ranked by a number of critics in varying media sources as being among the worst films ever made in the 20th century. Examples of such sources include [[Metacritic]], [[Roger Ebert]]'s list of most-hated films, ''[[The Golden Turkey Awards]]'', ''[[Leonard Maltin's Movie Guide]]'', [[Rotten Tomatoes]], [[pop culture]] writer [[Nathan Rabin]]'s ''[[My Year of Flops|My World of Flops]]'', the [[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]], the cult TV series ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'' (alongside spinoffs ''[[Cinematic Titanic]]'', ''[[The Film Crew]]'' and ''[[RiffTrax]]''), and the [[Golden Raspberry Awards]] (aka the "Razzies"). Films on these lists are generally [[feature film|feature-length films]] that are [[commerce|commercial]]/[[art film|artistic]] in nature (intended to turn a profit, express personal statements or both), professionally or independently produced (as opposed to [[amateur]] productions, such as [[home movie]]s), and released in theaters, then on home video. There are 57 films listed below, with 103 across both lists.

== 1930s ==

=== ''Maniac'' (1934) ===
{{Main|Maniac (1934 film){{!}}''Maniac'' (1934 film)}}
[[File:Maniac5.jpg|thumb|''[[Maniac (1934 film)|Maniac]]'' (1934) is one of the many [[pre-Code]] exploitation films from the 1930s featuring sex, violence and drugs.]]
''Maniac'', also known as ''Sex Maniac'', is a [[pre-Code]] [[exploitation film|exploitation]]-[[horror film]] directed by [[Dwain Esper]]. The story is a loose adaptation of the [[Edgar Allan Poe]] story "[[The Black Cat (short story)|The Black Cat]]" and follows a [[vaudeville]] impersonator who becomes an assistant to a [[mad scientist]]. Promoted as a documentary on [[mental illness]], ''Maniac'' was criticized for its gratuitous footage of women undressing and for plagiarizing horror sequences from the 1922 silent film ''[[Häxan]]''. [[Danny Peary]] believes that ''Maniac'' is the worst film ever made, and [[Charlie Jane Anders]] of [[Gawker Media]]{{'}}s ''[[io9]]'' described it as "possibly the worst movie in history."<ref>{{Cite book|last=Peary|first=Danny|author-link=Danny Peary|title=Cult Midnight Movies: Discover the 37 Best Weird, Sleazy, Sexy, and Crazy Good Cinema Classics|publisher=[[Workman Publishing Company]]|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TTsPBAAAQBAJ&q=Maniac+%281934%29+Dwain+Esper|year=2014|isbn=9780761181699|access-date=October 2, 2020|archive-date=October 25, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231025172439/https://books.google.com/books?id=TTsPBAAAQBAJ&q=Maniac+%281934%29+Dwain+Esper#v=snippet&q=Maniac%20(1934)%20Dwain%20Esper&f=false|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/did-the-worst-movie-of-all-time-come-out-75-years-ago-5161275 |title=Did The Worst Movie Of All Time Come Out 75 Years Ago? |publisher=[[io9]] |last=Anders |first=Charlie Jane |date=February 26, 2009 |access-date=February 18, 2019 |archive-date=February 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190218201930/https://io9.gizmodo.com/did-the-worst-movie-of-all-time-come-out-75-years-ago-5161275 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Rotten Tomatoes]] placed ''Maniac'' on its list of movies "So Bad They're Unmissable",<ref name="sobad">{{cite web |url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/25-movies-so-bad-theyre-unmissable/|title=25 Movies So Bad They're Unmissable |last=Adams |first=Michael |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |date=January 30, 2010 |access-date=January 25, 2015 }}</ref> ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' included the film on its list of the 20 worst movies ever and it is featured in [[John J. B. Wilson]]'s book ''[[The Official Razzie Movie Guide: Enjoying the Best of Hollywood's Worst]]''.<ref name="italianvanity">{{cite news|url=https://www.vanityfair.it/show/cinema/2018/02/25/20-film-piu-brutti-di-sempre|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108083603/https://www.vanityfair.it/show/cinema/2018/02/25/20-film-piu-brutti-di-sempre |work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|title=I 20 film più brutti di sempre|last=Pellegrini|first=Francesca|language=it|date=February 25, 2018|access-date=February 18, 2019|archive-date=January 8, 2022}}</ref>

=== ''Reefer Madness'' (1936) ===
{{Main|Reefer Madness{{!}}''Reefer Madness''}}
[[File:ReeferMadness_13.jpg|thumb|Originally titled ''Tell Your Children'', the anti-[[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] film ''[[Reefer Madness]]'' was called "the grand-daddy of all 'Worst' movies" by [[Leonard Maltin]].]]
''Reefer Madness'' (originally released as ''Tell Your Children'' and sometimes titled or subtitled as ''The Burning Question'', ''Dope Addict'', ''Doped Youth'', and ''Love Madness'') is a 1936 American [[exploitation film]] and [[propaganda|propaganda work]] revolving around the melodramatic events that ensue when high school students are lured by pushers to smoke [[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] and consequently become addicted and involved in various crimes such as a [[Hit and run (vehicular)|hit and run accident]], [[manslaughter]], [[murder]], attempted rape, descent into madness, association with organized crime, and suicide.

''[[Pacific Standard]]'' wrote that ''Reefer Madness'' was "one of the first films ever to be considered transcendentally bad"<ref name="psmag"/> and [[Leonard Maltin]] has called it "the grand-daddy of all 'Worst' movies".<ref name="Maltin01211">{{cite book |last=Maltin |first=Leonard |author-link=Leonard Maltin |title=Leonard Maltin's Movie and Video Guide 2004 |publisher=Signet |year=2003 |isbn=0-451-20940-0 |url=https://archive.org/details/leonardmaltinsmo00leon }}</ref> <!--Dead source, no archive available except the deprecated archive.today, thus [[WP:V|unverifiable]]: ''[[Las Vegas CityLife]]'' named it the "worst ever" runner-up to ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'',<ref>{{cite news |url=http://archives.lasvegascitylife.com/articles/2009/09/24/ae/stage/iq_31362594.txt |date=September 24, 2009 |last=McKee |first=David |work=Las Vegas CityLife |access-date=November 17, 2013 |title=What's the Worst Movie Ever? }}</ref> and--> [[News.com.au]] considered it a "disastrous flop turned cult classic" due to its "terrible acting and exaggerated drug-addicted stereotypes".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news.com.au/national/nsw-act/when-hollywoods-worst-films-become-cult-classics/news-story/792f3f09aba66809245d65328c73921c|title=When Hollywood's worst films become cult classics|work=[[News.com.au]]|first=Troy|last=Lennon|date=December 7, 2017|access-date=January 20, 2019|archive-date=January 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121064145/https://www.news.com.au/national/nsw-act/when-hollywoods-worst-films-become-cult-classics/news-story/792f3f09aba66809245d65328c73921c|url-status=live}}</ref> Natalli Amato of ''[[The Daily Dot]]'' included ''Reefer Madness'' on her list of the best worst movies, writing that it "may be one of the worst movies of all time for the fact that it accomplished the exact opposite of its intended goal" by becoming a cult classic among stoners.<ref>{{cite web |last=St-Amand |first=Vanessa |title=Ranked: The best worst movies you need to watch |url=https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/best-worst-movies/ |website=[[The Daily Dot]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |date=March 29, 2022 |archive-date=June 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619224037/https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/best-worst-movies/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Leafly]]''{{'}}s Danté Jordan also wrote that it may be "the worst movie of all time", criticizing its many inaccuracies regarding marijuana use and calling it "easily one of the most uncreative and [[tone-deaf]] pieces of anti-cannabis propaganda".<ref>{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Danté |title=We watched 'Reefer Madness' to confirm it's still complete garbage |url=https://www.leafly.com/news/lifestyle/reasons-why-reefer-madness-is-complete-garbage |website=[[Leafly]] |access-date=July 8, 2022 |language=en |date=January 27, 2020 |archive-date=July 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708065233/https://www.leafly.com/news/lifestyle/reasons-why-reefer-madness-is-complete-garbage |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''The Terror of Tiny Town'' (1938) ===
{{Main|The Terror of Tiny Town{{!}}''The Terror of Tiny Town''}}
''The Terror of Tiny Town'', directed by [[Sam Newfield]] and produced by [[Jed Buell]], remains the only [[musical film|musical]] [[Western (genre)|Western]] with an all-[[Dwarfism|dwarf]] cast.<ref name="tinyterror"/> The film was pulled from obscurity as a [[camp (style)|camp classic]] after appearing in college and [[midnight film|midnight screenings]] in the early 1970s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Terror of Tiny Town (1938)|url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92598/the-terror-of-tiny-town|access-date=December 16, 2020|website=Turner Classic Movies|language=en|archive-date=June 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614012516/https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/92598/the-terror-of-tiny-town|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1978, it was included in [[Michael Medved]]'s book ''[[The Fifty Worst Films of All Time]]'',<ref name="tinyterror">{{cite web|url=https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-terror-of-tiny-town-dvd/|title=The Terror of Tiny Town (DVD)|work=Film Threat|date=June 17, 2005|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=March 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324034956/https://filmthreat.com/uncategorized/the-terror-of-tiny-town-dvd/|url-status=live}}</ref> and it has since been listed as one of the worst films ever made by ''[[Flavorwire]]'',<ref name="Flavorwire"/> Rotten Tomatoes,<ref name="sobad"/> and ''[[The Golden Turkey Awards]]''.<ref name="tinyterror"/> [[Melvin Defleur]] referred to it as "Perhaps the worst film of all time",<ref>{{Cite book|last=Defleur|first=Melvin|author-link=Melvin Defleur|title=Understanding Mass Communication: A Liberal Arts Perspective|publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt]]|edition=6|year=1998|page=160}}</ref> and critic Gabriel Ricard listed it as the worst film ever made; stating, "not only is it pretty terrible, but ''Tiny Town'' is also pretty endearing."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://culturedvultures.com/best-worst-movies/|title=20 Best Worst Movies Of All Time|work=Cultured Vultures|last=Richard|first=Gabriel|date=June 5, 2019|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=December 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209080410/https://culturedvultures.com/best-worst-movies/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1986, ''The Terror of Tiny Town'' was the first film featured on ''[[Canned Film Festival]]'', a [[late night television]] show featuring the worst movies ever made.<ref name="cannedfilm">{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-06-20-8602140300-story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220507001443/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-06-20-8602140300-story.html|title=A 'Terror' Kicks Off World's Worst Film Festival|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|last=Terry|first=Clifford|date=June 20, 1989|access-date=March 23, 2020|archive-date=May 7, 2022}}</ref>

== 1940s ==

=== ''The Babe Ruth Story'' (1948) ===
{{Main|The Babe Ruth Story{{!}}''The Babe Ruth Story''}}
[[File:William_Bendix_1960.JPG|thumb|left|upright|Actor [[William Bendix]], who played The Great Bambino in ''[[The Babe Ruth Story]]'' (1948), cited as one of the worst [[biopics]] ever made]]
''The Babe Ruth Story'' is a 1948 [[baseball film]] biography of [[Babe Ruth]], starring [[William Bendix]], [[Claire Trevor]] and [[Sam Levene]].<ref>{{Citation|last1=Del Ruth|first1=Roy|title=The Babe Ruth story|date=2010|publisher=Warner Home Video|language=en|oclc=694103117|last2=Considine|first2=Bob|last3=Callahan|first3=George|last4=Bendix|first4=William|last5=Trevor|first5=Claire|last6=Bickford|first6=Charles|last7=Frawley|first7=William|last8=Levene|first8=Sam|last9=Allied Artists Productions}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' describes it as "the ''[[Plan 9 from Outer Space]]'' of baseball biopics".<ref>{{cite news |title=The Babe Ruth Story (1948)|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/3535/The-Babe-Ruth-Story/overview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219200719/http://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/3535/The-Babe-Ruth-Story/overview |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 19, 2013 |department=Movies & TV Dept.|work=[[The New York Times]]|first=Hal|last=Erickson|author-link=Hal Erickson (author)|date=2013|access-date=November 30, 2013}}</ref> It was rushed into release while Ruth was still alive. One infamous scene features Ruth promising a dying child that he will hit two [[home run]]s; the child is subsequently cured of his ailments after Ruth delivers on the promise.<ref name="homerun"/>

[[Baseball Hall of Fame]]r [[Ted Williams]] believed it to be the worst movie he had ever seen. ''[[The Washington Times]]'' stated that it "stands as possibly the worst movie ever made".<ref>{{cite news |title=Duke as Williams? A Prince of an Idea |first=Dan |last=Shaughnessy |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=XscSAAAAIBAJ&pg=7230,788739&dq=babe+ruth+story+worst+film |newspaper=Spokane Chronicle |date=April 3, 1986 |last=Heller |first=Dick |title=Clinic and reception in the works to honor NBA pioneer Lloyd |newspaper=The Washington Times |date=July 23, 2000 |url-access=subscription "nearly every list of the worst movies ever made" was "with good reason".<ref>{{cite web |last=Apple |first=Charles |title=Some of the worst movies of all-time |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/sep/22/some-worst-movies-all-time/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=September 22, 2020 |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710190457/https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/sep/22/some-worst-movies-all-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Newberry |first=Paul |title=Counting down baseball's worst movie locales |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/counting-down-baseballs-worst-movie-locales/4492519007/ |website=[[The |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625165504/https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/counting-down-baseballs-worst-movie-locales/4492519007/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Newsday]]''{{'}}s Jack Mathews similarly wrote that ''The Babe Ruth Story'' was "what many people consider to be the worst sports movie of all time".<ref>{{cite journal |last=Dunne |first=Michael |title=Post-War Cultural Construction in "The Babe Ruth Story" |journal=Studies in Popular Culture |date=October 1996 |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=1–7 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23413739
