=== ''Ishtar'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Ishtar (film){{!}}''Ishtar'' (film)}}
[[File:Elaine May - publicity1.jpg|thumb|upright|''[[Ishtar (film)|Ishtar]]'' director [[Elaine May]]<ref name="2024lineup"/> defended her 1987 box office flop, stating, "If all of the people who hate ''Ishtar'' had seen it, I would be a rich woman today."<ref name="elainemay">{{Cite web|url=https://forward.com/culture/434193/elaine-may-mounting-a-comeback-at-87-is-directing-a-new-film/|title=Elaine May, Mounting A Comeback At 87, Is Directing A New Film|last=Grisar|first=PJ|work=[[The Forward]]|access-date=April 28, 2020|date=November 4, 2019|archive-date=November 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191105155049/https://forward.com/culture/434193/elaine-may-mounting-a-comeback-at-87-is-directing-a-new-film/|url-status=live}}</ref>]]
''Ishtar'' was written and directed by [[Elaine May]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mubi.com/notebook/posts/the-not-so-savage-messiahs|title=The Not-So-Savage Messiahs|date=August 5, 2013|website=MUBI|access-date=August 2, 2022|archive-date=August 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817111104/https://mubi.com/notebook/posts/the-not-so-savage-messiahs|url-status=live}}</ref> and starred [[Academy Award|Oscar]]-winning duo [[Warren Beatty]] and [[Dustin Hoffman]] as an ode to the ''[[Road to...]]'' film series featuring [[Bing Crosby]] and [[Bob Hope]]. Beatty and Hoffman star as Rogers and Clarke, two untalented lounge singers who travel to [[Morocco]] in hopes of finding a gig.<ref name="brody">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/movie-of-the-week-ishtar|title=Movie of the Week: "Ishtar"|last=Brody|first=Richard|author-link=Richard Brody|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]|access-date=February 11, 2019|date=August 6, 2015|archive-date=January 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190109004100/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/movie-of-the-week-ishtar|url-status=live}}</ref> Due to unanticipated problems with filming in the desert—which resulted in numerous reshoots—the film ran over budget by $30 million. While its final budget cost was $55 million, ''Ishtar'' earned only $14,375,181 at the North American box office, leading ''Ishtar'' to become synonymous with "[[Box office bomb|box-office flop]]". It was also subject to harsh reviews from critics. The film was nominated for Worst Picture and Worst Screenplay in the [[8th Golden Raspberry Awards]], winning one for Worst Director. ''The [[San Jose Mercury News]]'' claimed that "Time has not improved this film's reputation as being one of the worst ever made."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/movies-dvd/ci_17017300 |title=Review: 'Dinner for Schmucks' a savory comedy |newspaper=[[San Jose Mercury News]] |date=May 1, 2011 |access-date=September 20, 2013 |archive-date=September 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921061311/http://www.mercurynews.com/movies-dvd/ci_17017300 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]]'' suggested it was "so bad it could have been deliberate", and called it "one of the worst films ever made",<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.timeout.com/london/film/ishtar |title=Ishtar |magazine=[[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]] |access-date=February 20, 2020 |archive-date=November 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181115225621/https://www.timeout.com/london/film/ishtar |url-status=live }}</ref> while [[Ed Morrissey]] referred to it as "The ''[[Citizen Kane]]'' of big-budget, A-list vehicular homicides."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hotair.com/archives/2009/02/22/what-were-the-worst-movies-of-all-time/ |title=What were the worst movies of all time? |first=Ed |last=Morrissey |work=Hot Air |author-link=Ed Morrissey |date=February 22, 2009 |publisher=[[Hot Air (news site)|Hot Air]] |access-date=September 20, 2013 |archive-date=September 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921060444/http://hotair.com/archives/2009/02/22/what-were-the-worst-movies-of-all-time/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was included in Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Movies of All Time'' book, Rotten Tomatoes placed it amongst "25 Movies So Bad They're Unmissable" and [[Richard Roeper]] included it on his list of the 40 worst films he had ever seen.{{sfn|Sauter|page=213–216}}<ref name="RichardRoeper">{{cite book|first=Richard|last=Roeper|authorlink=Richard Roeper|title=10 Sure Signs a Movie Character is Doomed and Other Surprising Movie Lists|location=New York City|publisher=[[Hachette Books|Hyperion Books]]|date=2003|ISBN=978-0786888306|pages=66–67}}</ref><ref name="sobad"/> In 1999, ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' placed the film on a list of the 100 worst ideas of the 20th century.<ref name="worstideas">{{cite magazine |url=http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,991230,00.html |title=The 100 Worst Ideas Of The Century |date=June 14, 1999 |access-date=April 8, 2018 |url-access=subscription |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |first1=Melissa |last1=August |first2=Harriet |last2=Barovick |first3=Michelle |last3=Derrow |first4=Tam |last4=Gray |first5=Daniel S. |last5=Levy |first6=Lina |last6=Lofaro |first7=David |last7=Spitz |first8=Joel |last8=Stein |first9=Chris |last9=Taylor |archive-date=October 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021051659/http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,991230,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The film has since become a cult classic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.filminquiry.com/10-movies-low-ratings-actually-good/|title=10 Movies With Low Ratings That Are Actually Good|first=Alistair|last=Ryder|date=August 6, 2015|website=Film Inquiry|access-date=January 11, 2019|archive-date=January 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190112044239/https://www.filminquiry.com/10-movies-low-ratings-actually-good/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Ishtar'' has seen a minor critical re-evaluation from some critics like [[Richard Brody]],<ref name="brody"/> and directors [[Quentin Tarantino]], [[Edgar Wright]], and [[Martin Scorsese]] have praised it in interviews.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2020/05/ishtar-box-office-flop-game-changer-setback-female-directors-1202231739/|title='Ishtar': How Hollywood Decided That One Box-Office Flop Spoke for All Female Directors|last=Brueggemann|first=Tom|date=May 17, 2020|website=[[IndieWire]]|language=en|access-date=December 9, 2022|archive-date=July 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705130534/https://www.indiewire.com/2020/05/ishtar-box-office-flop-game-changer-setback-female-directors-1202231739/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Gary Larson]], who initially lampooned the movie in ''[[The Far Side]]'', said he regrets writing that cartoon because he based it solely on ''Ishtar''{{'}}s reputation, and that he enjoyed the film when he later watched it. As of December 2022, it is the only cartoon he has publicly admitted to regretting.<ref>{{cite web|last=McGuire|first=Liam|title=Gary Larson Names the One Far Side Comic He Wants to Apologize For|website=[[ScreenRant]]|date=December 1, 2022|access-date=December 9, 2022|url=https://screenrant.com/far-side-gary-larson-apologize-ishtar-mistake/|archive-date=December 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209004631/https://screenrant.com/far-side-gary-larson-apologize-ishtar-mistake/|url-status=live}}</ref> Defenders argue that the studio did not back May, resulting in a [[public relations]] disaster before it was released in theaters.<ref name="elainemay"/> [[Joe Queenan (author)|Joe Queenan]] compared the film to another comedy film considered the worst, ''[[Gigli]]'', and wrote that although it was considered one of the worst films ever made at the time of its release, it "has several comic moments" and does not get worse on subsequent viewings, unlike ''Gigli''.<ref name="queenan"/>

=== ''Leonard Part 6'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Leonard Part 6{{!}}''Leonard Part 6''}}
[[File:Bill cosby 1969.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Bill Cosby]] became the first person to [[List of people who have accepted Golden Raspberry Awards|accept a Golden Raspberry Award]] for ''[[Leonard Part 6]]'', which he admitted was the worst movie ever made.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://siskelebert.org/?p=2512|title=Worst of 1987 – Siskel and Ebert Movie Reviews|website=siskelebert.org|access-date=January 9, 2022|archive-date=January 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220109145300/https://siskelebert.org/?p=2512|url-status=live}}</ref>]]
''Leonard Part 6'', starring (as well as written and produced by) [[Bill Cosby]], was intended as a parody of spy movies. Leonard Parker, a former [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]] spy, is brought out of retirement to save the world from an evil vegetarian who brainwashes animals to kill people. Rita Kempley at ''[[The Washington Post]]'' noted the large number of Coca-Cola product placements and said "The only good thing about Bill Cosby's ''Leonard Part 6'' is that we didn't have to see Parts 1 through 5."<ref name="wprk">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/leonardpart6pgkempley_a0ca2f.htm|title=Leonard Part 6 (PG)|last=Kempley|first=Rita|date=December 19, 1987|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=June 27, 2012|archive-date=September 21, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921220949/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/leonardpart6pgkempley_a0ca2f.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> Scott Weinberg at DVD Talk noted the film as "truly one of the worst movies you'll ever see ... movies this bad should be handled with Teflon gloves and a pair of tongs".<ref name="weinberglp6">{{cite web|url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/15632/leonard-part-6/|title=Leonard Part 6|last=Weinberg|first=Scott|date=April 26, 2005|work=DVD Talk|access-date=June 27, 2012|archive-date=November 6, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106000452/http://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/15632/leonard-part-6/|url-status=live}}</ref> By 1990, Dennis King of the ''[[Tulsa World]]'' wrote that the film had "become synonymous with 'bomb{{'"}}.<ref>{{cite news|last=King|first=Dennis|title=Ghost Dad|date=July 6, 1990|newspaper=[[Tulsa World]]|url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/archives/ghost-dad/article_5b0372e5-e91b-5570-b2c7-c9edabbfae0a.html|access-date=January 27, 2019|archive-date=May 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507042016/https://www.tulsaworld.com/archives/ghost-dad/article_5b0372e5-e91b-5570-b2c7-c9edabbfae0a.html|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Total Film'' and ''Vanity Fair'' subsequently included ''Leonard Part 6'' on their respective worst film lists.<ref name=TotalFilm/><ref name="italianvanity"/> Cosby himself disowned the film, and when it was released to theaters he publicly advised people not to see it. It earned [[Golden Raspberry]]s for Worst Actor (Cosby), Worst Picture, and Worst Screenplay. It was also nominated for two more Razzie Awards, for Worst Supporting Actress and Worst Director.<ref name=LATimes>{{cite news|title=Leonard RIP?|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=December 20, 1987|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1987-12-20-ca-29856-story.html|access-date=December 26, 2010|first=Pat H.|last=Broeske|archive-date=January 19, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119151239/http://articles.latimes.com/1987-12-20/entertainment/ca-29856_1_leonard-part|url-status=live}}</ref> Cosby became the first person to [[List of people who have accepted Golden Raspberry Awards|accept a Golden Raspberry Award]],<ref name="feran">{{Cite news |last= Feran |first= Tim |title = Section: Features – Accent & Arts – Intermission | newspaper = [[Columbus Dispatch]] |location = [[Columbus, Ohio]] |page = 01F |date = April 26, 1992}}</ref> and said "It was the worst movie I ever made – the worst movie anyone ever made".<ref>{{cite news |title=Stars take critics with a grain of salt |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=waFEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1013,2816922&dq=leonard+part+6+worst+ever&hl=en |newspaper=[[The Daily Union]] |date=May 12, 1991 |access-date=April 1, 2020 |archive-date=August 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816054117/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=waFEAAAAIBAJ&pg=1013,2816922&dq=leonard+part+6+worst+ever&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''Nukie'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Nukie{{!}}''Nukie''}}
''Nukie'' is a 1987 South African film directed by Sias Odendaal (credited as Sias Odendal) and Michael Pakleppa, and starring [[Steve Railsback]], Ronald France, and [[Glynis Johns]]. The plot concerns an alien, Nukie, who crash lands on Earth and seeks help from two children to reunite with his brother, Miko, who has been captured by the United States government. The film is considered to be a knock-off of [[Steven Spielberg]]'s 1982 film ''[[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial]]''. Witney Seibold of ''[[/Film]]'' writes that "''Nukie'' is only remarkable for how undeniably terrible it is", noting that it appears on lists of the worst films ever made.<ref name="slash">{{cite web |last=Seibold |first=Witney |title=The Nukie Controversy Explained: Destroying Crappy Movies For Charity |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1167319/the-nukie-controversy-explained-destroying-crappy-movies-for-charity/ |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=January 16, 2023 |date=January 13, 2023 |archive-date=January 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230114222128/https://www.slashfilm.com/1167319/the-nukie-controversy-explained-destroying-crappy-movies-for-charity/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' note that it is "regarded as one of the worst movies ever made",<ref>{{cite web |last=Trinos |first=Angelo Delos |title=10 Copycat Films That Are Worse Than What They're Ripping Off |url=https://www.cbr.com/copycat-films-worse-than-original/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |date=15 August 2022 |access-date=11 January 2023 |archive-date=January 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111233339/https://www.cbr.com/copycat-films-worse-than-original/ |url-status=live }}</ref> with critic [[The Cinema Snob|Brad Jones]] selecting ''Nukie'' as the worst film he has ever seen,<ref>{{cite web |last=Phalin |first=Mike |title=Schlock and the Snob: An Interview With Brad Jones |url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/185215/schlock-snob-interview-brad-jones/ |website=[[Dread Central]] |access-date=11 January 2023 |date=26 August 2016 |archive-date=January 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230101080206/https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/185215/schlock-snob-interview-brad-jones/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Red Letter Media]] calling it "Possibly one of the worst films ever made."<ref>{{cite web |last=Newgent |first=Sean |title=VHS copy of forgotten 'E.T.' knock-off 'Nukie' sells for $80,600 |url=https://www.kgun9.com/entertainment/vhs-copy-of-forgotten-e-t-knock-off-nukie-sells-for-80-600 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111230814/https://www.kgun9.com/entertainment/vhs-copy-of-forgotten-e-t-knock-off-nukie-sells-for-80-600 |publisher=[[KGUN-TV]] |access-date=11 January 2023 |language=en |date=10 January 2023 |archive-date=11 January 2023}}</ref> ''Total Film'' write that it is considered by some to be the "most painful movie ever made";<ref name="kidsmovie">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/50-worst-kids-movies/|title=50 Worst Kids Movies|last=Winning|first=Joshua|work=[[Total Film]]|publisher=[[GamesRadar]]|date=November 8, 2011|access-date=July 8, 2017 }}</ref> they listed ''Nukie'' the worst kids' movie ever made and one of the worst science-fiction films ever made.<ref name="kidsmovie"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/25-worst-science-fiction-films/|title=25 Worst Science-Fiction Films|last=Winning|first=Joshua|work=[[Total Film]]|publisher=[[GamesRadar]]|date=June 30, film's co-director, Michael Pakleppa, referred to ''Nukie'' as "the most wrong-gone thing [he had] ever done in [his] life" and feared that the final product was "the worst film on Earth".<ref>{{cite web |last=Balmont |first=James |title=Nukie: the strange story behind the forgotten ET knock-off |archive-date=January 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230130102008/https://www.dazeddigital.com/film-tv/article/58061/1/nukie-the-et-knock-off-film-awful-alien-vhs-interview |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== ''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie'' (1987) ===
{{Main|The Garbage Pail Kids Movie{{!}}''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie''}}
''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie'' is a 1987 [[live-action]] adaptation of the then-popular [[Garbage Pail Kids|trading card series of the same name]], itself a gross-out parody of the then-popular [[Cabbage Patch Kids]] dolls co-created by [[Pulitzer Prize]]-winning cartoonist [[Art Spiegelman]]. The film is often criticized for its [[gross-out humor]], nonsensical plot, poor explanations, bad acting, and the unsettling appearance of the Garbage Pail Kids (the title characters are depicted by dwarf actors in low-budget costumes, with poorly functioning mouths and expressionless faces). It has a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.<ref>{{Rotten Tomatoes|qid=Q7735810|title=The Garbage Pail Kids Movie}}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film holds a score of 1, making it tied for the lowest scoring film on the site.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/browse/movies/score/metascore/all?sort=asc |title=Best Movies of All Time |work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=April 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215194915/https://www.metacritic.com/browse/movies/score/metascore/all?sort=asc |archive-date=February 15, 2023 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Caryn James of ''[[The New York Times]]'' said the movie is "too repulsive for children or adults of any age" and is "enough to make you believe in strict and faraway boarding schools".<ref>{{cite news |first=Caryn |last=James |url=https://movies.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9B0DE1D81030F931A1575BC0A961948260 |title=Movie Review – The Garbage Pail Kids Movie |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=June 6, 2010 |date=August 28, 1987 |archive-date=February 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120210083257/http://movies.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9B0DE1D81030F931A1575BC0A961948260 |url-status=live }}</ref> Carlos Coto of the ''[[Sun-Sentinel]]'' called it "one of the worst ever made".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1987-09-05/features/8703110946_1_garbage-pail-kids-cabbage-patch-kids-kids-show |title=Trashy 'Garbage Pail Kids' Has No Value |newspaper=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=September 29, 2010 |date=September 5, 1987 |archive-date=January 13, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120113001340/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1987-09-05/features/8703110946_1_garbage-pail-kids-cabbage-patch-kids-kids-show |url-status=dead }}</ref> Internet critic [[Doug Walker (comedian)|Doug Walker]], best known for the series ''[[Nostalgia Critic]]'', stated in a 2012 video that it was not only the worst film he had ever reviewed as the Nostalgia Critic, but the worst movie he had ever seen overall, deeming that the film served to undermine its own moral. His mother had forbidden him from seeing it as a child, stating, "I, by all the heavenly blessings, thank my mother for stopping me from seeing this movie, because I'm very convinced that this movie would've taken away half my brain."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=4-mps8wKdhD8nWDu&v=_8Ik0xbSjSY |work=Zachary Matthew James |title=Doug Walker on The Garbage Pail Kids Movie |via=[[YouTube]] |date=December 16, 2012 |access-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517170607/https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=4-mps8wKdhD8nWDu&v=_8Ik0xbSjSY |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2025, Walker released an updated list of the worst films he had reviewed, with ''The Garbage Pail Kids Movie'' once again taking the top spot.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=N5s747W621s |title=Doug's Top 10 Worst Movies |work=Channel Awesome |via=[[YouTube]] |date=May 9, 2025 |access-date=June 25, 2025 }}</ref>

Much of the film's content is said to be inappropriate for children, its intended audience. Throughout the movie, the Garbage Pail Kids steal, get in fights, bite people's toes off, flatulate in people's faces, threaten others with [[switchblade]]s, urinate upon themselves, and run over cars. In addition to scatological behavior, the movie has several scenes that feature sexual images, violence, and drinking. Offended parents launched a nationwide protest of the movie that successfully resulted in the movie being withdrawn from circulation.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://allmovie.com/work/the-garbage-pail-kids-movie-19217 |title=The Garbage Pail Kids Movie > Overview |website=[[AllMovie]] |access-date=June 6, 2010 |archive-date=June 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200601082028/https://www.allmovie.com/movie/the-garbage-pail-kids-movie-v19217 |url-status=live }}</ref> The shortened release contributed to the movie's poor gross of only $1,576,615.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=garbagepailkids.htm |title=The Garbage Pail Kids Movie (1987) |work=Box Office Mojo |access-date=March 7, 2011 |archive-date=March 23, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110323072054/http://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=garbagepailkids.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> It was nominated for three Razzies at the [[8th Golden Raspberry Awards]]: Worst Visual Effects, Worst New Star for the Garbage Pail Kids collectively, and Worst Original Song.

=== ''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2'' (1987) ===
{{Main|Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2{{!}}''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2''}}
''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2'' is the sequel to the 1984 Christmas-themed [[slasher film]] ''[[Silent Night, Deadly Night]]'', which faced protests from parent groups and sharp criticism from ''[[At the Movies (1986 TV program)|At the Movies]]'' hosts Roger Ebert and Gene Siskel due to its promotional campaign featuring an ax-wielding [[Santa Claus]].<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2">{{cite web |last1=Bailey |first1=Jason |title=So Bad It's Good: It's Christmas Time (and Garbage Day) in 'Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2' |url=https://www.flavorwire.com/493459/so-bad-its-good-its-christmas-time-and-garbage-day-in-silent-night-deadly-night-part-2 |website=[[Flavorwire]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date=December 12, 2014}}</ref> The film was a financial success despite the controversy, leading producers to enlist [[Lee Harry]] to repurpose its footage for a new project; however, $100,000 was eventually allocated to shoot additional original material.<ref name="sndnp2sr">{{cite web |last1=Kennedy |first1=Michael |title=Why Silent Night, Deadly Night 2 Was So Legendarily Bad |url=https://screenrant.com/silent-deadly-night-2-problems-production-bad/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date=3 August 2022}}</ref> Nearly half of the ''Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2''{{'}}s runtime consists of flashbacks to the first film, narrated by Ricky Caldwell (Eric Freeman), the brother of the original film's protagonist, as he recounts events before embarking on his own murderous rampage.<ref name="sndnp2sr"/>

Much of the film's reception and legacy centers on Freeman's performance, which ''Flavorwire'' states "may very well be the single worst performance ever committed to celluloid".<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2" /> A scene in which Ricky shouts "garbage day!" before shooting and killing a bystander taking out his trash became an [[Internet meme]] after being uploaded to [[YouTube]] in its early years.<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2" /> ''Screen Rant'' has since deemed the film to be "a masterpiece of the so bad it's good variety",<ref name="sndnp2sr" /> and "one of the worst movies ever made"<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gunning |first1=Cathal |title=Every Killer Santa Horror Movie Ranked |url=https://screenrant.com/killer-santa-horror-movies-ranked-worst-best/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date=25 December 2022}}</ref> Emmett O'Regan of ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' also selected it as the worst movie ever made,<ref>{{cite web |last1=O'Regan |first1=Emmett |title=Why Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2 Is the Worst Movie of All Time |url=https://www.cbr.com/silent-night-deadly-night-worst-movie-all-time/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |access-date=December 14, 2024 |language=en |date= December 11, 2022}}</ref> and an article in ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' asserted that: "in terms of filmmaking quality—it's hard to believe that in terms of pure, unadulterated crap, anything could ever surpass it."<ref name="20pastechristmas"/> Additionally, ''Flavorwire'', ''[[/Film]]'', and ''Paste'' have all listed it as the worst Christmas film ever made.<ref name="flavorwiresndnp2" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Donato |first1=Matt |title='Silent Night, Deadly Night Part 2' Is The Best Worst Christmas Horror Movie And You Must Watch It |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/555210/silent-night-deadly-night-part-2/ |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=December 15, 2024 |date=December 22, 2017}}</ref><ref name="20pastechristmas">{{cite web |last1=Vorel |first1=Jim |title=The 20 Worst Christmas Movies of All Time |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/movies/christmas/the-20-worst-christmas-movies-of-all-time |website=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]] |access-date=December 14, 2024}}</ref> ''Time Out'' and ''Flavorwire'' later included it on their respective lists of the worst films ever made.<ref name="timeoutlist"/><ref name="Flavorwire"/>

=== ''Hobgoblins'' (1988) ===
{{Main|Hobgoblins (film){{!}}''Hobgoblins'' (film)}}
''Hobgoblins'', by [[Rick Sloane]], is widely considered a low-budget [[Mockbuster|knock-off]] that capitalizes on the popularity of the 1984 film ''[[Gremlins]].''<ref name="hobstandard"/> It gained popularity in 1998 after being featured on an episode of ''Mystery Science Theater 3000''. ''MST3K'' writer [[Paul Chaplin]] later commented on ''Hobgoblins'', saying, "Oh, man. You have no idea the torture it was to watch this movie several times in the space of a week. It shoots right to the top of the list of the worst movies we've ever done." Specific points of the film that were lampooned were the extreme misogyny and atrocious treatment of women; the film's technical incompetence and repetitive scenes; its asinine, poorly conceived plot; its dreadful acting; and its ugly look and gratuitous vulgarity, particularly in regards to its characters and subject matter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.castleforrester.com/media/guide/0907.htm |title=Episode Guide|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013042500/http://www.castleforrester.com/media/guide/0907.htm |archive-date=October 13, 2008 }}</ref> David Cornelius of ''DVD Talk'' stated, "There's not one aspect of this movie that isn't the Worst Thing Ever."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/38236/mad-monster-rally/ |title=Mad Monster Rally : DVD Talk Review of the DVD Video |website=[[DVD Talk]]|access-date=March 5, 2014|last=Cornelius |first=David|date=August 18, 2009 |archive-date=February 24, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224044732/http://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/38236/mad-monster-rally/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Evening Standard|The Standard]]''{{'}}s ''Bad Horror Club'' noted its status as one of the worst films of all time, commenting: "it's so preposterously badly made, terribly acted and ineptly constructed that it makes for some of the most fun you can ever have watching a movie."<ref name="hobstandard">{{cite web |last1=Embley |first1=Jochan |last2=Fletcher |first2=Harry |title=Remembering 80s disaster Hobgoblins in all its chaotic glory |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/film/bad-horror-club-hobgoblins-80s-disaster-a4422426.html |website=[[Evening Standard|The Standard]] |access-date=December 8, 2024 |language=en |date=April 23, 2020}}</ref>

Sloane has embraced ''Hobgoblins''{{'}} status as one of the worst films of all time, stating that he fears that it will be forgotten if it is removed from IMDb's user-generated bottom 100 list.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/12169/rick-sloane-talks-hobgoblins/|title=Rick Sloane Talks Hobgoblins|author=Foywonder|date=June 23, 2009|website=[[Dread Central]]|language=en|access-date=December 8, 2024}}</ref> After seeing the ''MST3K'' episode himself, Sloane was inspired to direct [[Hobgoblins 2|a sequel]], which was released in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mubi.com/films/hobgoblins-2|title=Hobgoblins 2|via=[[Mubi (streaming service)|MUBI]]|access-date=May 10, 2020|archive-date=September 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210927043012/https://mubi.com/films/hobgoblins-2|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to IMDb,<ref name="hobstandard"/> it has been featured on lists from ''Flavorwire'' and ''Total Film'',<ref name="Flavorwire"/><ref name=TotalFilm/> and ''[[ComicBook.com]]'' placed it at the top of their list of "Terrible Movies That Are So Bad They're A Must-Watch".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hathaway |first1=Ben |title=5 Terrible Movies That Are So Bad They're A Must-Watch |url=https://comicbook.com/movies/list/5-terrible-movies-that-are-so-bad-theyre-a-must-watch/ |website=[[ComicBook.com]] |access-date=February 28, 2026 |date=October 15, 2025}}</ref>

=== ''Mac and Me'' (1988) ===
{{Main|Mac and Me{{!}}''Mac and Me''}}
''Mac and Me'' is about a young boy in a wheelchair who meets and befriends an alien who has crash-landed on Earth. A box-office failure,<ref>{{cite news|title=Advertising is so much a part of life that it's understandable to find familiar products in films. But sometimes it goes too far.|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=August 29, 1999|url=https://articles.latimes.com/1999/aug/29/entertainment/ca-4591/3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204041237/http://articles.latimes.com/1999/aug/29/entertainment/ca-4591/3|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 4, 2013|access-date=May 17, 2012}}</ref> the film grossed $6,424,112 in the United States<ref>{{mojo title|macandme|Mac and Me}}</ref> on a $13 million budget.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/MovieDetails/58827|title=Mac and Me|website=[[AFI Catalog of Feature Films]]|access-date=April 27, 2018|archive-date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093913/https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/MovieDetails/58827|url-status=live}}</ref> It used to have a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose critical consensus notes that it is "duly<!--sic: should be "dually"--> infamous" as both an imitation of ''[[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial]]'' (1982), and a marketing vehicle for [[McDonald's]] and [[Coca-Cola]]<ref name="rottentomatoes1">{{Rotten Tomatoes|qid=Q1761515|title=Mac and Me}}</ref> (the filmmakers had admitted a profit-sharing arrangement with the former).<ref>{{cite news|title= Movie Review Mac and Me Takes a Big McBite Out of E.T.|newspaper= [[Los Angeles Times]]|url= https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-08-15-ca-300-story.html|access-date= December 5, 2010|archive-date= March 7, 2011|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110307085307/http://articles.latimes.com/1988-08-15/entertainment/ca-300_1_big-mac|url-status= live}}</ref> [[Leonard Maltin]] described the film as being "more like a TV commercial than a movie",<ref name="Maltin01211"/> and Marjorie Baumgarten of the ''[[Austin Chronicle]]'' called it a "shameless ''E.T.'' knockoff".<ref name="rottentomatoes1"/> ''Mac and Me'' is widely regarded as one of the worst films ever made,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/movies-with-bizarre-weird-source-material/|title=15 Movies With Bizarre Source Material|last=McGranaghan|first=Mike|date=March 21, 2017|website=[[Screen Rant]]|access-date=June 23, 2018|archive-date=June 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624035654/https://screenrant.com/movies-with-bizarre-weird-source-material/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://movieweb.com/mac-and-me-movie-alternate-ending-video/|title=Alternate Mac and Me Ending Unearthed and It's Insane|last=Millican|first=Josh|date=August 8, 2018|work=[[MovieWeb]]|access-date=December 15, 2018|archive-date=September 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911081746/https://movieweb.com/mac-and-me-movie-alternate-ending-video/|url-status=live}}</ref> with ''[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]'' reporting that it is "frequently pulled out in 'worst film of all time' arguments".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/2016/07/18/top-aliens-in-the-movies/mac-and-me/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/2016/07/18/top-aliens-in-the-movies/mac-and-me/ |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Top 20 aliens in the movies|date=December 19, 2017|website=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|access-date=April 27, 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Filmmaker [[Morgan Spurlock]] (responsible for the 2004 Oscar-nominated ''[[Super Size Me]]'') declared it the "worst thing you'll ever see in your entire life", as well as the most egregious example of [[product placement]] in cinema history.<ref name="crow">{{cite news|url=https://movies.yahoo.com/blogs/movie-talk/morgan-spurlock-dubs-mac-worst-movie-ever-sold-060910653.html|date=April 22, 2011|last=Crow|first=Jonathan|work=[[Yahoo! Movies]]|access-date=August 29, 2013|title=Morgan Spurlock Dubs 'Mac and Me' the Worst Film Ever Sold|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120405070102/http://movies.yahoo.com/blogs/movie-talk/morgan-spurlock-dubs-mac-worst-movie-ever-sold-060910653.html|archive-date=April 5, 2012}}</ref> The film was also named the worst ever in the ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'',<ref>{{cite news|date=January 22, 2017|title=Mac and Me|newspaper=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|quote=McDonald's created an 'E.T.' rip-off called 'Mac and Me' in 1988&nbsp;... It's the worst movie ever made.}}</ref> as well as by broadcaster [[Simon Mayo]]<ref name="mayo">{{cite episode|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p03slrls|title=Paul Rudd and Chris Evans interviewed by Simon Mayo|series=Kermode and Mayo's Film Review |date=April 29, 2016|station=[[BBC Radio 5 Live]]|access-date=April 27, 2018|time=10 minutes|quote=''Mac and Me''... we're talking about the worst film ever made.|archive-date=May 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180510202715/https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p03slrls|url-status=live}}</ref> and writer/producer [[Damon Lindelof]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gq.com/story/damon-lindelof-paul-alien-comedy|title=Damon Lindelof's Open Letter to Paul the Alien|last=Lindelof|first=Damon|author-link=Damon Lindelof|date=March 14, 2011|magazine=[[GQ]]|access-date=April 27, 2018|archive-date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093747/https://www.gq.com/story/damon-lindelof-paul-alien-comedy|url-status=live}}</ref> Michael Hayden of ''[[GQ (Indian edition)|GQ India]]'' referred to it as "hands down the worst family movie in Hollywood history".<ref name="gqindia">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.gqindia.com/content/6-best-bad-films/#s-cust0|title=The 6 best bad films|last=Hayden|first=Michael|date=November 10, 2011|magazine=[[GQ (Indian edition)|GQ India]]|access-date=May 11, 2018|archive-date=May 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512044317/https://www.gqindia.com/content/6-best-bad-films/#s-cust0|url-status=live}}</ref> The film was nominated for four Razzie Awards including Worst Picture and Worst Screenplay, and won two trophies: Worst Director for [[Stewart Raffill]] (tied with [[Blake Edwards]] for ''[[Sunset (1988 film)|Sunset]]'') and Worst New Star for [[Ronald McDonald]] in a cameo. ''Mac and Me'' has however [[Mac and Me#In popular culture|gained a cult following]] and was featured on the second season of the ''[[Mystery Science Theater 3000]]'' revival (the only Razzie-winning film ever to be riffed in the history of the show).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thrillist.com/entertainment/nation/mcdonalds-mac-and-me-paul-rudd-movie-et-spinoff|title=How McDonald's Bizarre 'E.T.' Knockoff Got Made|last=Patches|first=Matt|date=April 3, 2017|website=[[Thrillist]]|access-date=December 11, 2017|archive-date=December 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211213637/https://www.thrillist.com/entertainment/nation/mcdonalds-mac-and-me-paul-rudd-movie-et-spinoff|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.nerdist.com/mac-and-me-bottleneck-gallery-figure-pins/|title=Mac and Me Finally (?) Gets Figure and Pin Collection|last=McNally|first=Victoria|date=April 24, 2017|website=[[Nerdist Industries|Nerdist]]|access-date=May 11, 2018|archive-date=May 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512044315/https://nerdist.com/mac-and-me-bottleneck-gallery-figure-pins/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uproxx.com/tv/mystery-science-theater-3000-mac-and-me-season-2/|title='Mystery Science Theater 3000' Will Tackle 'Mac And Me' In Season 2|website=Uproxx|date=November 12, 2018|access-date=January 3, 2020|archive-date=January 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200103134816/https://uproxx.com/tv/mystery-science-theater-3000-mac-and-me-season-2/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbr.com/mst3k-movies-good-without-the-riffing/|title=10 MST3K Movies You Should Watch Without The Riffing|first=Derek|last=Faraci|date=June 12, 2022|website=CBR|access-date=February 12, 2023|archive-date=February 12, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230212014327/https://www.cbr.com/mst3k-movies-good-without-the-riffing/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== ''Things'' (1989) ===
{{Main|Things (film){{!}}''Things'' (film)}}
''Things'', a 1989 Canadian [[low budget]], [[independent film|independent]], [[shot-on-video film|shot on video]] horror [[exploitation film]], was written and produced by Andrew Jordan and Barry J. Gillis. It cost approximately $35,000 in total to make<ref name="CANUX">{{cite web|url=http://www.canuxploitation.com/review/things.html|title=''Things'' review|website=Canuxploitation|access-date=December 28, 2013|archive-date=September 29, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130929234728/http://www.canuxploitation.com/review/things.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and marked the mainstream film debut of porn star [[Amber Lynn]]. It was ostensibly made as [[Homage (arts)|homage]] to horror icons and films, such as [[George A. Romero]] and his ''[[Night of the Living Dead]]'' franchise.<ref name="CO1">{{cite web|url=http://www.critcononline.com/films_on_the_fringe.htm|title=Films on the Fringe: Things (1989)|website=Critic Online|access-date=June 7, 2009|archive-date=April 15, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090415201758/http://www.critcononline.com/films_on_the_fringe.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> Adam Symchuk of ''Screen Rant'' wrote: "While films like ''[[The Room]]'' and ''[[Birdemic: Shock and Terror|Birdemic]]'' seem to be constant contenders for the best 'so bad it's good' movie, [''Things''] is the true unheralded champion among many [[Cinephilia|cinephiles]]."<ref>{{cite web |title=It Came From The North: 10 Great Monster Movies From Canada |url=https://screenrant.com/great-monster-movies-from-canada/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |last=Symchuk |first=Adam |access-date=July 26, 2022 |date=September 30, 2020 |archive-date=July 26, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220726091201/https://screenrant.com/great-monster-movies-from-canada/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Likewise, Jeff Kirschner of ''[[Dread Central]]'' nominated it as the worst movie ever made and [[Will Pfeifer]] opined that "It's so terrible I can't think of another movie that even comes close."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/142337/things-worst-movie-ever-made/|title=Things: The Worst Movie Ever Made|date=December 10, 2015|website=[[Dread Central]]|last=Kirschner|first=Jeff|access-date=July 26, 2022|archive-date=December 4, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204173115/https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/142337/things-worst-movie-ever-made/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pfeifer |first=Will |author-link=Will Pfeifer |title=Monsters, mullets meet for snoozefest |url=https://www.jacksonnewspapers.com/x1348677046/Will-Pfeifer-Monsters-mullets-meet-for-snoozefest |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210902063835/https://www.jacksonnewspapers.com/x1348677046/Will-Pfeifer-Monsters-mullets-meet-for-snoozefest |newspaper=[[Jackson Herald|Jackson Newspapers]] |access-date=July 26, 2022 |date=October 17, 2008 |archive-date=September 2, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, ''RiffTrax'' concluded that ''Things'' was the worst movie that they had ever spoofed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nelson |first1=Mike J. |author-link1=Michael J. Nelson |last2=Murphy |first2=Kevin |author-link2=Kevin Murphy (actor) |last3=Corbett |first3=Bill |author-link3=Bill Corbett |title=Things |url=https://www.rifftrax.com/things |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220305141159/https://www.rifftrax.com/things |website=[[Rifftrax]] |archive-date=March 5, 2022 |access-date=July 26, 2022 |language=en |date=March 4, 2022}}</ref>

== 1990s ==

=== ''Troll 2'' (1990) ===
{{Main|Troll 2{{!}}''Troll 2''}}
Despite its title, ''Troll 2'' does not feature any trolls (the antagonists are actually [[goblin]]s) and has no relation to the [[Troll (1986 film)|original 1986 film]]. ''Troll 2'' was produced under the title ''"Goblins"'', but the title was changed by American distributors.<ref name="GriggsTroll" /> In the film, an American family vacations to the town of Nilbog (goblin spelled backwards), where vegetarian goblins attempt to turn the family into edible plants.<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/> It was shot in [[Utah]] and the cast was composed of local amateur actors. A [[language barrier]] developed between the cast and the Italian crew, led by director [[Claudio Fragasso]], who had translated the script to English.<ref name="GriggsTroll">{{cite web |last1=Griggs |first1=Brandon |title=Troll 2: As camp as it gets |url=https://archive.sltrib.com/story.php?ref=/arts/ci_5457861 |website=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] |date=March 17, 2007 |access-date=December 30, 2024}}</ref> The bad acting and dialogue have become notorious for their [[Camp (style)|camp]] value,<ref name="GriggsTroll" /> with individual scenes having become Internet memes.<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/><ref name="collidertroll">{{cite web |last1=Berchtold |first1=Trent |title=The 10 Most Rewatchable Bad Horror Movies, Ranked |url=https://collider.com/bad-horror-movies-rewatchable-ranked/ |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=December 30, 2024 |language=en |date=September 29, 2024}}</ref> In 2009, [[Michael Stephenson (filmmaker)|Michael Stephenson]], the child star of ''Troll 2'', released ''[[Best Worst Movie]]'', a documentary exploring the film's tumultuous production and its unexpected cult following.<ref name="trollbestworst"/>

[[NPR]] reports that it is "known as the worst movie of all time"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=105420828 |title=The Beauty Of The 'Best Worst Movie' |work=NPR |date=June 15, 2009 |publisher=[[NPR]] |access-date=June 15, 2009 |archive-date=June 20, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090620200356/http://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=105420828 |url-status=live }}</ref> while ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' calls it "a popular candidate for the worst film ever made".<ref name="trollbestworst">{{cite web |url=https://avclub.com/article/ibest-worst-movie-iuncovers-the-heartbreaking-psyc-95807 |title=Best Worst Movie uncovers the heartbreaking psychodrama in a memorably insane B-movie |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |last=Rabin |first=Nathan |author-link=Nathan Rabin |date=March 29, 2013 |access-date=March 29, 2013 |archive-date=May 16, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140516063721/http://www.avclub.com/article/ibest-worst-movie-iuncovers-the-heartbreaking-psyc-95807 |url-status=live }}</ref> Likewise, ''[[TV Guide]]'' proclaimed that "''Troll 2'' is really as bad as they come",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/movies/troll-2/review/129231 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170426044557/http://www.tvguide.com/movies/troll-2/review/129231/ |title=Troll 2 Review |work=[[TV Guide]] |archive-date=April 26, 2017 |access-date=March 5, 2014}}</ref> and Ken Hanke of ''[[Mountain Xpress]]'' stated in his review that: "There are movies that are bad. There are movies that are so-bad-they're-good. And then there's ''Troll 2''—a movie that's so bad that it defies comprehension."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mountainx.com/movies/review/troll_2 |title=Movie Review: Troll 2 |work=[[Mountain Xpress]] |last=Hanke |first=Ken |date=July 23, 2008 |access-date=March 5, 2014 |archive-date=October 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019171306/http://www.mountainx.com/movies/review/troll_2 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Troll 2'' regularly appears on lists of films considered the worst, including: ''Flavorwire'',<ref name="Flavorwire"/> ''[[Fotogramas]]'',<ref name="fotogramas">{{cite web |last=Rosado |first=Ricardo |title=Las 20 peores películas de la historia del cine: un homenaje |url=https://www.fotogramas.es/noticias-cine/g19447838/20-peores-peliculas-historia/?slide=19 |website=[[Fotogramas]] |access-date=January 26, 2022 |language=es-ES |date=October 1, 2020}}</ref> ''IGN'',<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/> Rotten Tomatoes,<ref name="sobad"/> ''Screen Rant'',<ref name="Screen Rant"/> and ''Time Out''.<ref name="timeoutlist"/> Furthermore, ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' named it the most rewatchable bad movie of all time.<ref name="collidertroll" />

=== ''Highlander II: The Quickening'' (theatrical version, 1991) ===
{{Main|Highlander II: The Quickening{{!}}''Highlander II: The Quickening''}}
The French-British film ''Highlander II: The Quickening'' is a sequel to the 1986 cult film ''[[Highlander (film)|Highlander]]'', which transitions the [[fantasy]] of the original film into [[science fiction]], and [[retcons]] the mystical warriors of the first film into [[Extraterrestrial life|aliens]]. It received a harsh reception from both critics and audiences, as it has a 0% score on Rotten Tomatoes and appears on its 100 Worst Movies of All Time.<ref name="rt100worst">{{cite web |title=Bad Movies: The 100 Worst Movies of All Time |url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/guide/worst-movies-of-all-time/ |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date=March 10, 2024}}</ref> Common criticisms included the lack of motivation for the characters, blatant disregard for backstory from the first film (such as the new and seemingly incongruent origin for the Immortals and the unexplained resurrection of Ramírez), glaring plot holes, a messy and nonsensical story structure, the filmmaker's inability to balance unrelated plots and subplots, and obvious contradictions in the film's internal logic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2000/06/16/highlander-2-renegade-version|title=Highlander 2: Renegade Version|author=I. G. N. Staff|date=June 16, 2000|website=IGN}}</ref> In selecting it as the worst movie sequel of all time, ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' also wrote that "it is typically considered one of the worst films of all time'.<ref>{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Isaac |title=The 10 Worst Movie Sequels Ever, Ranked |url=https://www.cbr.com/worst-movie-sequels-ever/ |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]] |access-date=January 11, 2022 |date=January 5, 2022}}</ref> Roger Ebert named it the worst film of 1991, stating: "If there is a planet somewhere whose civilization is based on the worst movies of all time, ''Highlander 2: The Quickening'' deserves a sacred place among their most treasured artifacts."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/highlander-2-the-quickening-1991 |title=Highlander 2: The Quickening movie review (1991) |first=Roger |last=Ebert |author-link=Roger Ebert |work=Chicago Sun-Times |date=November 1, 1991 |access-date=October 10, 2020}}</ref> An ''[[IGN]]'' review said: "How bad is this movie? Well, imagine if [[Ed Wood]] were alive today, and someone gave him a multi-million dollar budget. See his imagination running rampant, bringing in aliens from outer space with immensely powerful firearms, immortals who bring each other back to life by calling out their names, epic duels on flying skateboards, and a blatant disregard for anything logical or previously established—now you are starting to get closer to the vision of ''Highlander II''."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2000/06/16/highlander-2-renegade-version |title=Highlander 2: Renegade Version Review |work=IGN |date=June 16, 2000}}</ref> ''Screen Rant'' has since included it on its list of the 25 worst films of all time.<ref name="Screen Rant"/>

In 1995, the film's director [[Russell Mulcahy]] made a [[director's cut]] version known as ''Highlander 2: Renegade Version'' and then later released another version simply known as ''Highlander 2: The Special Edition'' for its 2004 DVD release. The film was reconstructed on both occasions largely from existing material, with certain scenes removed and others added back in, and the entire sequence of events changed. The reconstructed film's reception was far better than the original's; it was elevated to a mixed reception.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://joblo.com/horror-movies/news/highlander-ii-there-can-be-only-four-cuts---part-2|title = Highlander II: There can be only four cuts!| work = JoBlo Movie Network|date = November 24, 2010|access-date = March 16, 2013}}</ref>

=== ''Super Mario Bros.'' (1993) ===
{{main|Super Mario Bros. (film){{!}}''Super Mario Bros.'' (film)}}
[[File:Bob hoskins filming ruby blue cropped (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Oscar-nominated actor [[Bob Hoskins]] (pictured in 2006) described ''Super Mario Bros.'' as "the worst thing I ever did" later in his life.]]
The first [[feature-length]] live-action film based on a video game, ''Super Mario Bros.'' was directed by the husband-and-wife team of [[Rocky Morton]] and [[Annabel Jankel]] (known for their work on ''[[Max Headroom (TV series)|Max Headroom]]''). It follows the brothers [[Mario]] ([[Bob Hoskins]]) and [[Luigi (character)|Luigi]] ([[John Leguizamo]]), plumbers who venture into a parallel universe to rescue [[Princess Daisy]] ([[Samantha Mathis]]) from the villainous [[Bowser|King Koopa]] ([[Dennis Hopper]]). The ''[[Super Mario]]'' series' publisher, [[Nintendo]], believed the [[Mario (franchise)|''Mario'' franchise]] was strong enough for experimentation and gave the filmmakers free creative license.<ref name="Wired: MarioSucked">{{cite magazine |last=Russell |first=Jamie |title=Why the Super Mario Movie Sucked |url=https://www.wired.com/2012/04/generation-xbox-super-mario-movie/ |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=April 23, 2012}}</ref> The finished film bears little resemblance to the games,<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies">{{cite web |last=Bibbiani |first=William |title=The Best Worst Movies Ever Made: The Room, Super Mario Bros. and More |url=https://sea.ign.com/breakin-2-electric-boogaloo/180321/feature/the-best-worst-movies-ever-made-the-room-super-mario-bros-and-more |website=[[IGN]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=December 27, 2021}}</ref> trading their colorful [[Mushroom Kingdom]] for a [[Dystopia|dystopic]] world populated by humanoid dinosaurs.<ref name="Wired: MarioSucked"/><ref name="RiffTrax: Mario"/> ''[[SyFy Wire]]'' wrote: "Some movies are so bad that they're secretly good. ''Super Mario Bros.'' is so bad it crushes your spirit. It's unfathomably terrible."<ref name="SyFy: Mario">{{cite web |last=Grierson |first=Tim |title=This week in genre history: Super Mario Bros. the movie gets an instant 'game over' |url=https://www.syfy.com/syfy-wire/super-mario-bros-movie-genre-history |website=[[SyFy Wire]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=May 26, 2020}}</ref> The film was criticized for its inconsistent tone, complex narrative, and lack of faithfulness to the source material.<ref>{{Cite AV media |last1=Siskel |first1=Gene |last2=Ebert |first2=Roger |date=August 18, 2008 |title=Siskel & Ebert Review 'Super Mario Bros.' |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QbEH66qiwrY |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810150516/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QbEH66qiwrY |archive-date=August 10, 2016 |access-date=November 28, 2016 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Walsh |first=Michael |title=8 Things Fans Want To See In The Super Mario Movie |url=https://collider.com/things-fans-want-super-mario-movie/ |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=June 22, 2022}}</ref> According to ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', ''Super Mario Bros.'' is a mainstay on lists compiling the worst films of all time.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shanfield |first1=Ethan  |title=Mario Powers Up: How Nintendo Visionary Shigeru Miyamoto and Illumination's Chris Meledandri Plan to Super Smash Hollywood |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/features/super-mario-bros-movie-shigeru-miyamoto-interview-1235572488/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=March 21, 2024 |date=April 4, 2023}}</ref> It was voted the sixth worst film of all time by [[RiffTrax]] in 2012,<ref name="RiffTrax: Mario">{{cite web |title=Worst Movies of All Time Top 10 |url=https://www.rifftrax.com/worst-movies-of-all-time-top-10 |publisher=[[RiffTrax]] |access-date=July 9, 2022 |date=2012}}</ref> and ''[[IGN]]'' ranked it among the "best worst movies ever made" in 2021.<ref name="IGN: BestWorstMovies"/> Author [[David Bodanis]], in his 2020 book ''The Art of Fairness'', called ''Super Mario Bros.'' "the worst movie ever made".<ref>{{cite book |last=Bodanis |first=David |title=The Art of Fairness: The Power of Decency in a World Turned Mean |date=November 2020 |publisher=[[Abrams Books]] |isbn=9781647003869 |chapter=Directors |quote=The result was ''1941'', and while it's not the worst movie ever made—not when ''Super Mario Bros.'' is still available—it's definitely a contender.}}</ref>

In addition to scathing reviews, ''Super Mario Bros.'' was a [[box-office bomb]], and Morton and Jankel were "[[Blacklisting|blacklisted]]" as directors in Hollywood.<ref name="SyFy: Mario"/> In a 2007 interview, Hoskins said: "The worst thing I ever did? ''Super Mario Bros.'' It was a fuckin' nightmare. The whole experience was a nightmare. It had a husband-and-wife team directing, whose arrogance had been mistaken for talent. After so many weeks their own agent told them to get off the set! Fuckin' nightmare. Fuckin' idiots."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hattenstone |first=Simon |date=August 3, 2007 |title=The Method? Living it out? Cobblers! |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/aug/03/2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161216193111/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2007/aug/03/2 |archive-date=December 16, 2016 |access-date=December 13, 2016 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> In a 2011 interview, he was asked, "What is the worst job you've done?", "What has been your biggest disappointment?", and "If you could edit your past, what would you change?" His answer to all three was ''Super Mario Bros.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenstreet |first=Rosanna |date=June 17, 2011 |title=Q&A: Bob Hoskins |url=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2011/jun/18/bob-hoskins-interview-neverland |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110021801/http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2011/jun/18/bob-hoskins-interview-neverland |archive-date=November 10, 2013 |access-date=December 13, 2016 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> The film made Nintendo wary of licensing its works to film studios,<ref name="Sony">{{cite news|last=Vary|first=Adam|title=Sony Pictures Lands 'Mario Bros.' Movie Rights From Nintendo, Leaked Emails Show|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/adambvary/sony-nintendo-mario-bros-movie#.duwkpjZgV|access-date=December 11, 2014|website=[[BuzzFeed News]]|date=December 11, 2014|archive-date=December 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141212093710/http://www.buzzfeed.com/adambvary/sony-nintendo-mario-bros-movie#.duwkpjZgV|url-status=live}}</ref> and it did not license ''Mario'' again until it collaborated with [[Illumination (company)|Illumination]] for ''[[The Super Mario Bros. Movie]]'' (2023) three decades later.<ref name="SyFy: Mario"/><ref name="terrible10"/> [[Seth Rogen]], who voiced [[Donkey Kong (character)|Donkey Kong]] in the 2023 film, called ''Super Mario Bros.'' one of the worst films ever made and what "made me realize that movies, like, could be bad. That never occurred to me until that moment."<ref>{{cite web |last=Malkin |first=Marc |title='Super Mario Bros. Movie' Star Seth Rogen Calls Original 1993 Adaptation 'One of the Worst Films Ever Made' |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/columns/super-mario-bros-seth-rogen-slams-original-movie-1235574029/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=March 21, 2024 |date=April 5, 2023}}</ref>

=== ''North'' (1994) ===
{{Main|North (1994 film){{!}}''North'' (1994 film)}}
[[File:Rob_Reiner_LBJ_Library_2016_-_DIG13955_105.jpg|thumb|Actor/director [[Rob Reiner]] (pictured in 2016) made the [[family film]] ''[[North (1994 film)|North]]'' (1994), which was panned by critics to the point that [[Roger Ebert]] famously declared he "hated, hated, hated this movie" on the [[film review]] show ''[[At the Movies (1986 TV program)|Siskel and Ebert at the Movies]]''.]]
The [[Rob Reiner]] film ''[[North (1994 film)|North]]'' is an adaptation of the novel ''North: The Tale of a 9-Year-Old Boy Who Becomes a Free Agent and Travels the World in Search of the Perfect Parents'' by [[Alan Zweibel]], who also wrote the screenplay and has a minor role in the film. ''North'', which stars [[Elijah Wood]] in the title role and also marked [[Scarlett Johansson]]'s film debut, was a critical and commercial failure, earning only $7,138,449 worldwide despite its budget of over $40 million. It was widely criticized for its plot, its cast of insensitive characters, lack of humor and portrayal of numerous ethnic stereotypes (especially Alaskan Inuit). It has a 14% approval rating at [[Rotten Tomatoes]].<ref>{{cite web |title=North Movie Reviews, Pictures – Rotten Tomatoes |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |url=https://rottentomatoes.com/m/north/ |access-date=March 7, 2011}}</ref> [[Roger Ebert]] gave it zero stars and wrote, "I hated this movie. Hated hated hated hated hated this movie. Hated it. Hated every simpering stupid vacant audience-insulting moment of it. Hated the sensibility that thought anyone would like it. Hated the implied insult to the audience by its belief that anyone would be entertained by it."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://siskelebert.org/?p=493|title=Worst of 1994 – Siskel and Ebert Movie Reviews|website=siskelebert.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://siskelebert.org/?p=5388|title=The Client, Lassie, It Could Happen to You, North, Barcelona, 1994 – Siskel and Ebert Movie Reviews|website=siskelebert.org}}</ref> He continued saying "''North'' is a bad film – one of the worst movies ever made",<ref name="northebert">{{cite web |last=Ebert |first=Roger |author-link=Roger Ebert|title=North movie review & film summary (1994) |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/north-1994 |website=[[RogerEbert.com]] |date=July 22, 1994 |access-date=April 8, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> and it is also on his list of most hated films.<ref name="eberthated"/> Both Ebert and [[Gene Siskel]] named ''North'' as the worst film of 1994.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Official Site of Gene Siskel |work=Cmgww.com |url=http://www.cmgww.com/stars/siskel/screening_room/thumbs_down.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090226070236/http://www.cmgww.com/stars/siskel/screening_room/thumbs_down.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 26, 2009 |access-date=March 7, 2011}}</ref> [[Mick LaSalle]] of the ''San Francisco Chronicle'' said in his review that "''North'' is director Rob Reiner's first flat-out failure, a sincerely wrought, energetically made picture that all the same crashes on takeoff. It's strange and oddly distasteful, at its best managing to be bad in some original and unexpected ways."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/1995/01/06/dd59113.dtl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031113141403/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fc%2Fa%2F1995%2F01%2F06%2Fdd59113.dtl |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 13, 2003 |work=[[The San Francisco Chronicle]] |title=Rob Reiner's 'North' Is Distastefully Bad |last=LaSalle |first=Mick |author-link=Mick LaSalle |date=January 8, 2011}}</ref> [[Richard Roeper]] named ''North'' as one of the 40 worst movies he has ever seen, saying that, "Of all the films on this list, ''North'' may be the most difficult to watch from start to finish."<ref name="RichardRoeper"/> The film was nominated for the following awards at the [[15th Golden Raspberry Awards]]: Worst Picture, Worst Actor ([[Bruce Willis]], also for ''[[Color of Night]]''), Worst Supporting Actress ([[Kathy Bates]]), Worst Supporting Actor ([[Dan Aykroyd]], also for ''[[Exit to Eden (film)|Exit to Eden]]''), Worst Director, and Worst Screenplay ([[Andrew Scheinman]] and [[Alan Zweibel]]).

=== ''Dis – en historie om kjærlighet'' (''A Story About Love'') (1995) ===
{{Main|A Story About Love{{!}}''A Story About Love''}}
The Norwegian [[romantic film]] ''Dis – en historie om kjærlighet'' was directed by Aune Sand. The film follows different couples and their love stories around the world, in [[Cairo]], [[Normandy]], [[Oslo]] and [[New York City]]. ''Dis'' received universally poor reviews by critics, and has been called the most poorly reviewed Norwegian film in history.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Kristoffersen|first=Marius Vartdal|title=Hva Var I Veien Med Dis?|url=http://znett.com/2011/05/hva-var-i-veien-med-dis/|date=May 3, 2011|access-date=July 14, 2014|magazine=[[Z Filmtidsskrift]]|language=no}}</ref><ref name="osloby.no"/> Critic Harald Kolstad of ''[[Dagsavisen]]'' gave it a score of zero, refused to acknowledge ''Dis'' as a film, and claimed to have never seen anything worse.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pedersen |first=Brent Erik |title=Hedrer Dagsavisens kritiker |url=http://www.dagsavisen.no/kultur/hedrer-dagsavisens-kritiker/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140617125554/http://www.dagsavisen.no/kultur/hedrer-dagsavisens-kritiker/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 17, 2014 |access-date=July 14, 2014 |newspaper=Dagsavisen|language=no }}</ref> ''[[Aftenposten]]'' referred to the film as "the largest turkey" and "the most reviled film",<ref name="osloby.no">{{cite news|title=Norges største kalkun flyr igjen|url=http://www.osloby.no/article199599_2.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120814005215/http://www.osloby.no/article199599_2.ece|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2012|date=June 28, 2012|access-date=July 14, 2014|newspaper=Aftenposten|language=no}}</ref> and ''Total Film'' included it on its list of the 66 worst films ever made.<ref name="TotalFilm"/> Despite being a critical disaster it became a commercial success, gaining [[cult film]] status with a following akin to ''[[The Rocky Horror Picture Show]]'', with fans embracing its "so bad it's good" qualities.<ref name="osloby.no"/> Director Aune Sand insists that ''Dis'' is a masterpiece.<ref>{{cite news|title= Slakter norsk film|url=http://www.dagbladet.no/kultur/2005/07/20/437937.html|access-date=July 14, 2014|newspaper=Dagbladet|language=no}}</ref>

=== ''Showgirls'' (1995) ===
{{Main|Showgirls{{!}}''Showgirls''}}
[[File:Paul Verhoeven.jpg|thumb|Director [[Paul Verhoeven]], whose ''[[Showgirls]]''<ref name="2024lineup"/> earned a record 13 [[Golden Raspberry Award]] nominations, was the first person to attend the ceremony and [[List of people who have accepted Golden Raspberry Awards|accept the awards in person]].<ref>{{Cite news |last= Persall |first= Steve |title = 'Showgirls' gets razzed | newspaper = [[St. Petersburg Times]] |page = 2B |date = March 25, 1996}}</ref>]]
Hype for [[Paul Verhoeven]]'s [[erotic]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama]] ''Showgirls'' focused on the sex and nudity in this [[NC-17]] French-American film with a $45 million budget, but the final result was critically derided. Much hype revolved around the film's star, [[Elizabeth Berkley]], who only two years before had starred in the lighthearted and chaste teen [[situation comedy|sitcom]] ''[[Saved by the Bell]]''. The film won seven [[Golden Raspberry Award|Razzie Awards]], a record at that time, and received 13 nominations, a record that still stands. It received an additional award at the [[20th Golden Raspberry Awards]], where it was awarded Worst Picture of the Decade. Kenneth Turan of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' called it, "a film of thunderous oafishness that gives adult subject matter the kind of bad name it does not need or deserve".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rottentomatoes.com/m/showgirls/reviews/#page=2&sort=source |title=Showgirls – Movie Reviews |website=Rotten Tomatoes |access-date=March 5, 2014}}</ref> Michael Dequina of TheMovieReport.com also criticized the film, claiming that it was "the best bad filmmaking Hollywood has to offer".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://themoviereport.com/movierpt1.html#showgirls |title=The Movie Report Archive, Volume 1 |work=TheMovieReport.com |access-date=November 18, 2013}}</ref> Adam White wrote in ''[[The Independent]]'' that it was "the worst movie ever made" but also a masterpiece.<ref name="showgirlsindy">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/showgirls-elizabeth-berkley-paul-verhoeven-you-dont-nomi-documentary-a9407086.html |title=Showgirls: The remarkable resurrection of the worst movie ever made |work=[[The Independent]]|last=White|first=Adam|date=March 18, 2020|access-date=April 17, 2020}}</ref> Stephen Lynch of the ''[[Knight Ridder|Knight Ridder/Tribune]]'' similarly named it the worst movie ever made, calling it "so bad it may be brilliant".<ref>{{cite news |title=Critic picks worst movies of all time |first=Stephen|last=Lynch|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=398&dat=20011003&id=oGhOAAAAIBAJ&pg=6912,5443994|newspaper=Bartow Press |date=October 3, 2001 |access-date=June 12, 2014}}</ref> Various sources have since included ''Showgirls'' in their respective lists of the worst films ever made, including: Rotten Tomatoes, ''Empire'', ''Screen Rant'', ''Vanity Fair'', and ''Flavorwire''.<ref name="Flavorwire"/><ref name="Screen Rant"/><ref name="italianvanity"/><ref name="sobad"/><ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/> ''Showgirls'' was also featured in Michael Sauter's ''The Worst Movies of All Time'' as well as ''The Official Razzie Movie Guide''. Despite being a critical failure and failing at the box office initially, ''Showgirls'' found success as a [[Camp (style)|camp]] [[cult film]], particularly among the [[LGBT community]], but whether the film was intended to be satirical remains subject to debate.<ref name="showgirlsindy"/> On the [[home video]] market, the film was [[MGM]]'s most profitable release for years.<ref name="showgirlsindy"/>

=== ''The Scarlet Letter'' (1995) ===
{{Main|The Scarlet Letter (1995 film){{!}}''The Scarlet Letter'' (1995 film)}}
A "freely adapted" version of the [[The Scarlet Letter|1850 romantic novel]] by [[Nathaniel Hawthorne]], directed by [[Roland Joffé]] and starring [[Demi Moore]] and [[Gary Oldman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/os-xpm-1995-10-13-9510110375-story.html|title='Scarlet Letter' is Untrue to the Hawthorne Tale|last=Boyar|first=Jay|date=October 13, 1995|website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> The film met with universally negative reviews<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deseretnews.com/top/705/7/The-Scarlet-Letter-20-best-selling-books-that-werent-as-acclaimed-as-film-adaptations.html|title=20 best-selling books that weren't as acclaimed as film adaptations|last=Purdy|first=Alicia|date=May 26, 2012|website=[[Deseret News]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213092221/https://www.deseretnews.com/top/705/7/The-Scarlet-Letter-20-best-selling-books-that-werent-as-acclaimed-as-film-adaptations.html|access-date=September 26, 2018|archive-date=December 13, 2013}}</ref> and was a [[box-office bomb]], grossing $10.4 million against a production budget of $46 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Scarlet Letter (1995)|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=scarletletter.htm|website=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=November 12, 2020}}</ref> Multiple critics named the film the worst of 1995.<ref name="hicks">{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/1995/12/22/19211366/best-worst-movies-of-1995|title=Best & Worst Movies of 1995|last=Hicks|first=Chris|date=December 22, 1995|website=[[Deseret News]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/entertainment/article/So-Bad-You-Can-t-Hate-Them-Demi-Moore-s-3017177.php|title=So Bad You Can't Hate Them|last=LaSalle|first=Mick|author-link=Mick LaSalle|date=December 30, 1995|website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|access-date=November 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thecoast.ca/halifax/worst-film/BestOf?oid=10515293|title=Worst Film 1995|website=[[The Coast (newspaper)|The Coast]]|access-date=November 6, 2020}}</ref>

Chris Hicks of the ''[[Deseret News]]'' argued that its deviation from the source material represents "Hollywood's arrogance in its purest form".<ref name="hicks"/> ''[[The Washington Post]]''{{'}}s Amy E. Schwartz reported that the "nutty" film was described by numerous reviewers as the worst they had ever seen.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/opinions/1995/10/24/even-hawthorne-would-have-laughed/765e3169-7ffb-4b1f-934d-5b2c3c1468f5/|title=Even Hawthorne Would Have Laughed|last=Schwartz|first=Amy E|date=October 24, 1995|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> Kevin Williamson of ''[[National Review]]'' observed a "combination of awfulness and inexplicability", and claimed that "any objective and authoritative analysis will reveal that the worst film ever made is Demi Moore's version of ''The Scarlet Letter''".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nationalreview.com/media-blog/i-hate-disagree-my-betters-kevin-d-williamson/|title=I Hate to Disagree with My Betters...|last=Williamson|first=Kevin|date=February 19, 2009|website=[[National Review]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> Sadie Trombetta of ''[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]'' wrote that it "has earned an almost permanent spot on every 'Worst Movie of All Time' list",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bustle.com/articles/121305-9-books-that-should-never-have-been-made-into-movies|title=9 Books That Should Never Have Been Movies|last=Trombetta|first=Sadie|date=November 5, 2015|website=[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> while author [[Libby Fischer Hellmann]] noted that it is "widely cited as the worst film adaptation ever made".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.libbyhellmann.com/5-great-books-movie-stinkers/|title=5 Great Books That Were Movie Stinkers|last=Hellmann|first=Libby Fischer|author-link=Libby Fischer Hellmann|date=August 7, 2016|website=LibbyHellmann.com|access-date=November 6, 2020|archive-date=May 20, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520165056/http://libbyhellmann.com/5-great-books-movie-stinkers/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The film was nominated for seven [[Golden Raspberry Awards]], winning "Worst Remake or Sequel". Furthermore, Roger Ebert placed the film on his "most hated" list.<ref name="eberthated"/>

===''Bio-Dome'' (1996)===
{{Main|Bio-Dome{{!}}''Bio-Dome''}}
The 1996 comedy film ''Bio-Dome'' focuses on two moronic stoner best friends, played by [[Pauly Shore]] and [[Stephen Baldwin]], who accidentally get trapped inside of the Bio-Dome, a hermetically sealed ecological system whose owner is played by [[Henry Gibson]], after mistaking it for a mall while looking for a bathroom.

For [[MTV News]], Eric Snider wrote in 2008 that "nothing can account for...the movie ''Bio-Dome'', which is–and I do not make this assertion lightly–the worst crime ever perpetrated against humanity throughout all of recorded history". Snider went on to call it "quite bad" and "certainly one of the worst comedies" he had ever seen, criticizing Pauly Shore's performance as unfunny and the film's writing as stupid.<ref>{{cite web |last=Snider |first=Eric |title=Eric's Bad Movies: Bio-Dome (1996) |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/2759537/erics-bad-movies-bio-dome-1996/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220710185442/http://www.mtv.com/news/2759537/erics-bad-movies-bio-dome-1996/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 10, 2022 |website=[[MTV News]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=June 19, 2008}}</ref> [[Syfy|Syfy Wire]]{{'}}s Cassidy Ward described ''Bio-Dome'' as "one of the best-worst movies of all time", stating that its plot "strains credulity", while Jon O'Brien of ''[[Inverse (website)|Inverse]]'' called it "one of the worst movies ever made" and wrote that it "has nothing to offer but unconvincing pratfalls...tumbleweed one-liners...and some unashamed sexism, too".<ref>{{cite web |last=Ward |first=Cassidy |title=Bio-Dome was a stoner movie flop, but Biosphere 2 was a real experiment |url=https://www.syfy.com/syfy-wire/bio-dome-biosphere-2-real-science-movie |website=[[Syfy|Syfy Wire]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=January 13, 2021}}</ref><ref name="inversekylie">{{cite web |last=O'Brien |first=Jon |title=How a '90s sci-fi comedy became one of the worst movies ever made |url=https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/bio-dome-movie-science-fiction-anniversary |website=[[Inverse (website)|Inverse]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=January 17, 2021}}</ref> It was described as "almost unwatchably awful" and "a baffling piece of work" by Charles Bramesco of ''[[Uproxx]]'', who wrote that it was a "perennial contender in the battle for the title of Worst Movie Ever".<ref>{{cite web |last=Bramesco |first=Charles |title=20 Years Later, The Pure Stupidity Of 'Bio-Dome' Remains Unmatched |url=https://uproxx.com/movies/bio-dome-20th-anniversary/ |website=[[Uproxx]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=January 12, 2016}}</ref> ''[[The A.V. Club]]''{{'}}s Nathan Rabin wrote, "Critics and audiences alike found the ''Bio-Dome'' to be an abomination unto the Lord, an affront to the gods of cinema, and also a very bad movie, bad enough to be considered the gold standard of crapitude in Shore's oeuvre", noting that it had the lowest Metacritic score of any movie, with 1 out of 100.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Rabin, Nathan|author1-link=Nathan Rabin |title=I Watched This On Purpose: Bio-Dome |url=https://www.avclub.com/i-watched-this-on-purpose-bio-dome-1798214668 |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en-us |date=August 27, 2008}}</ref> ''Bio-Dome'' was named one of the worst movies of the 1990s in a poll conducted by [[RiffTrax]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Jodi |title=Rifftrax Compiles The 20 Worst Movies Of The 90s: Disagree With Them, Won't You? |url=https://www.pajiba.com/seriously_random_lists/rifftrax-compiles-the-20-worst-movies-of-the-90s.php |website=Pajiba |access-date=July 10, 2022 |date=January 21, 2015}}</ref>

[[Kylie Minogue]], who starred in the film as oceanographer Petra von Kant, called appearing in the film the worst decision of her career.<ref name="inversekylie"/> For his performance in the movie, Shore won the [[Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Actor]] at the [[17th Golden Raspberry Awards]], tying with [[Tom Arnold (actor)|Tom Arnold]] for his performance in ''[[Big Bully (film)|Big Bully]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=In film, these were worst of 1996 |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/1997/03/25/in-film-these-were-worst-of-1996/ |website=[[Tampa Bay Times]] |access-date=July 10, 2022 |language=en |date=March 25, 1997}}</ref>

=== ''Batman & Robin'' (1997) ===
{{Main|Batman & Robin (film){{!}}''Batman & Robin'' (film)}}
[[File:Btrjpg.jpg|thumb|The [[comic book]] [[superhero]] sequel ''[[Batman & Robin (film)|Batman & Robin]]'' (1997) was named the worst movie ever made by ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]''.]]
''Batman & Robin'' is a [[superhero film]] based on the [[DC Comics]] character [[Batman]], the sequel to the 1995 film ''[[Batman Forever]]'', and the fourth and final installment of [[Warner Bros.]]' [[Batman in film#Tim Burton and Joel Schumacher series (1989–1997)|initial ''Batman'' film series]]. It was directed by [[Joel Schumacher]] and stars [[George Clooney]] as [[Bruce Wayne (1989 film series character)|Bruce Wayne / Batman]], [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]] as [[Mr. Freeze]], [[Uma Thurman]] as [[Poison Ivy (character)|Poison Ivy]], [[Chris O'Donnell]] as [[Dick Grayson]] / [[Robin (character)|Robin]], [[Alicia Silverstone]] as [[Barbara Gordon|Barbara Wilson]] / [[Batgirl]], and [[Michael Gough]] as [[Alfred Pennyworth]]. The film was largely criticized for its [[toyetic]] and [[camp (style)|camp]] approach, and Mr. Freeze's approach and [[one-line joke]]s.

{{as of|2017|June}}, [[review aggregator]] Rotten Tomatoes reports that 11% of critics have given the film a positive review based on 89 reviews, certifying it "Rotten" with an average rating of 3.7/10, and the critics' consensus: "Joel Schumacher's tongue-in-cheek attitude hits an unbearable limit in ''Batman & Robin'', resulting in a frantic and mindless movie that's too jokey to care much for."<ref>{{cite web |url = https://rottentomatoes.com/m/1077027-batman_and_robin/ |title = Batman & Robin | website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date = July 6, 2019}}</ref> By comparison [[Metacritic]] collected an average score of 28/100, based on 21 reviews.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://metacritic.com/movie/batman-robin |title = Batman & Robin (1997): Reviews | work=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |access-date=April 17, 2010}}</ref> [[Michael J. Nelson]], of ''Mystery Science Theater 3000'' fame, wrote of the movie in his book, ''Movie Megacheese'', "''Batman & Robin'' is not the worst movie ever. No, indeed. It's the worst thing ever.
