Yes, it's the single worst thing that we as human beings have ever produced in recorded history."<ref>{{Cite book |url = https://archive.org/details/mikenelsonsmovie00nels |url-access = registration |page = [https://archive.org/details/mikenelsonsmovie00nels/page/79 79] |title = Mike Nelson's Movie Megacheese |publisher = Harper Collins |isbn = 978-0-380-81467-1 |last1 = Nelson |first1 = Michael J |date = June 20, 2000}}</ref> ''Batman & Robin'' also came in first in an ''Empire'' poll of the 50 worst films ever.<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/> Joel Schumacher apologized to disappointed fans on the 2005 DVD release of ''Batman & Robin''.<ref>{{cite AV media |people = Joel Schmacher |title = "Making of" Introduction | medium = DVD |publisher = Warner Bros. |year = 2005 }}</ref> In 2021, Clooney stated that he refused to let his wife, [[Amal Clooney|Amal]], watch the film, saying, "There are certain films I just go, 'I want my wife to have some respect for me{{'"}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=2021-10-05 |title=George Clooney Refuses to Show 'Batman & Robin' to His Wife: 'I Want Her to Have Respect for Me' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/george-clooney-refuses-show-wife-batman-robin-1234669477/ |access-date=2023-07-13 |website=IndieWire |language=en-US}}</ref> Clooney later made a [[cameo appearance]] as Bruce Wayne in the [[DC Extended Universe]] film ''[[The Flash (film)|The Flash]]'' (2023).<ref>[https://variety.com/2023/film/news/george-clooney-refuses-batman-movies-the-flash-cameo-1235844045/ George Clooney Says There's 'Not Enough Drugs in the World' to Get Him to Play Batman Again, Even After 'The Flash' Cameo - Variety]</ref>

=== ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' (''The Day and the Night'') (1997) ===
{{Main|Day and Night (1997 film){{!}}''Day and Night'' (1997 film)}}
The French [[romance film]] ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was directed by philosopher [[Bernard-Henri Lévy]]. It follows a French author who fled to Mexico for a quiet life and an actress who is willing to seduce him to get a part in a film adapted from one of his books. Before its release, ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was heavily promoted in many French newspapers and magazines.<ref name="ti">Jade Lindgaard and Xavier De La Porte, ''The Imposter: BHL in Wonderland'' (Translated by John Howe) London; Verso, 2012. {{ISBN|978-1-84467-748-1}} (p. 48-9).</ref> When the film premiered at the [[Berlin International Film Festival]] in 1997, hundreds of journalists walked out of the screening and those that stayed ridiculed it.<ref name="Plato">{{cite news |last=Dahlburg |first=John-Thor |title=The Film That Plato Didn't Make |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=March 28, 1997 |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-03-28-ca-42798-story.html |access-date=October 14, 2013}}</ref> Following its release, ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was harshly criticized by the French media, with overwhelmingly negative reviews appearing in publications such as ''[[Libération]]'', ''[[Le Monde]]'' and ''[[Le Nouvel Observateur]]''.<ref name="ti"/> The film also did poorly commercially, with only 73,147 seats for ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' having been sold two months after its release.<ref name="ti"/> ''[[L'Humanité]]'' called it an "Absolute debacle" and [[Michel Houellebecq]] referred to it as the "most preposterous film in history".<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Tim |title=Public Enemies by Michel Houellebecq and Bernard-Henri Lévy – review |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2011/dec/08/public-enemies-houellebecq-levy-review |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=May 10, 2023 |date=December 8, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=The volcano a molehill |newspaper=[[L'Humanité]] |date=February 19, 1997 |url=https://www.humanite.fr/node/154931 |access-date=October 14, 2013}}</ref> ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' was considered the worst French film since 1945 by film magazine ''[[Cahiers du cinéma]]'', and its status as the "worst film in history" was discussed by the French version of ''[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slate.fr/story/27925/pire-film-du-monde-bhl-concurrence |title='Le Jour et la Nuit', pire film de l'histoire ... Vraiment? |date=October 3, 2010 |work=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]|access-date=December 19, 2013}}</ref> Likewise, English-language film site ''[[/Film]]'' described its status as "one of the worst foreign language movies ever made", and filmmaker [[Claude Chabrol]] selected it as one of the worst movies ever made.<ref>{{cite web |last=Thiellement |first=Pacome |title=Le film que BHL n'a pas compris (pourtant c'est son préféré !) |url=https://www.blast-info.fr/emissions/2023/le-film-que-bhl-na-pas-compris-pourtant-cest-son-prefere-6fAP-oVYSFuCqF6zPuXNlA |website=[[:fr:Blast (web TV)|Blast le souffle de l'info]] |access-date=May 10, 2023 |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pearson |first=Ben |title=BBC Polls Critics, Releases 100 Greatest Foreign Films List |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/562029/bbc-polls-critics-releases-100-greatest-foreign-films-list/ |website=[[/Film]] |access-date=May 10, 2023 |date=October 30, 2018}}</ref> An original documentary, ''Anatomy of a Massacre'', was released with the ''Le Jour et la Nuit'' DVD, and focused on its intense negative reception and failure.<ref>{{cite news |title=BHL et la critique ciné, c'était le jour et la nuit |newspaper=[[20 minutes (France)|20 Minutes]] |date=October 11, 2010 |url=http://www.20minutes.fr/medias/607145-media-bhl-critique-cine-jour-nuit |access-date=October 14, 2013}}</ref>

=== ''The Avengers'' (1998) ===
{{Main|The Avengers (1998 film){{!}}''The Avengers'' (1998 film)}}
An adaptation of the popular 1960s [[The Avengers (TV series)|British TV series]] of the same name, ''The Avengers'' starred [[Ralph Fiennes]] as John Steed and [[Uma Thurman]] as [[Emma Peel]], with [[Sean Connery]] as their antagonist, Sir August de Wynter. It was directed by [[Jeremiah S. Chechik]]. ''The Avengers'' began to receive negative publicity after [[Warner Bros.]], the film's distributor, refused to allow any early press-screenings for movie reviewers.<ref>{{cite news |author-link=Godfrey Cheshire |first=Godfrey |last=Cheshire |url=https://variety.com/1998/film/reviews/the-avengers-sputtering-spies-steed-and-peel-lack-appeal-1200454676/ |title=The Avengers – Sputtering Spies: Steed and Peel Lack Appeal |work=Variety |date=August 17, 1998 |access-date=June 27, 2022}}</ref> After early test screenings, ''The Avengers'' was heavily edited by the studio.<ref name="NYTreview2">{{cite news |first=Janet |last=Maslin |author-link=Janet Maslin |url=https://www.nytimes.com/library/film/081598avengers-film-review.html |title='The Avengers': Shh! They're Trying Not to Be Noticed |newspaper=The New York Times |date=August 15, 1998 |access-date=January 27, 2015 }}</ref> On its release, ''The Avengers'' was savaged by film critics, with the ''[[Birmingham Post]]'' stating "''The Avengers'' is being slated by critics as the worst film ever made" and adding that one reviewer had joked the film was such a "turkey" that the makers should have handed distribution to the poultry chain [[Bernard Matthews Farms|Bernard Matthews]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Film-''The Avengers'' |newspaper=The Birmingham Post |date=August 19, 1998 }}</ref> Several reviewers disparaged ''The Avengers'' for lacking the wit and excitement of its source material.<ref name="rt2">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.radiotimes.com/film/cjykx/the-avengers |title=Review: The Avengers |first=Alan |last=Jones |magazine=Radio Times |access-date=January 27, 2015 }}</ref><ref name="db">{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/entertainment/not-so-excellent-avengers-insults-old-series-awful-film-debases-tv-inspiration-article-1.807212 |title=Not So Excellent Avengers |first=David |last=Bianculli |newspaper=[[New York Daily News]] |date=August 18, 1998 |access-date=January 27, 2015 }}</ref> [[Janet Maslin]] strongly criticized ''The Avengers'': "With pseudo-suave repartee that would make [[Austin Powers (character)|Austin Powers]] blush and with so many shades of ''[[Howard the Duck (film)|Howard the Duck]]'' that one scene depicts man-size pastel teddy bears sitting around a conference table, it's a film to gall fans of the old TV series and perplex anyone else. I can't remember another Friday morning show where I heard actual cries of "Ugh!" on the way out the door" and finished her review with, "At a pared-down, barely rational 100 minutes, ''The Avengers'' is short but not short enough."<ref name="NYTreview2"/>

David Bianculli said, "This ''Avengers'' film is so horrendously, painfully and thoroughly awful, it gives other cinematic clunkers like ''[[#Ishtar (1987)|Ishtar]]'' and ''Howard the Duck'' a good name."<ref name="db"/> Alan Jones in ''[[The Radio Times]]'' stated "The cult 1960s TV series gets royally shafted by Hollywood in this stunningly designed blockbuster that's stunningly awful in every other department ... Terrible special effects and zero chemistry between Fiennes and Thurman make this notorious disaster a total waste of everyone's time and energy."<ref name="rt2"/> ''The Avengers'' also shared a [[Razzie Award]] for "Worst Remake or Sequel" with the 1998 adaptations of ''[[Psycho (1998 film)|Psycho]]'' and ''[[Godzilla (1998 film)|Godzilla]]'' at the [[19th Golden Raspberry Awards]]. ''Total Film'' magazine later voted Fiennes and Thurman in ''The Avengers'' as "The Worst Movie Double Act Of All Time".<ref>{{cite news |title=Double disasters make it to top of the flops |newspaper=[[Western Mail (Wales)|The Western Mail]] |location=Cardiff |date=December 1, 2003 }}</ref> The film also appeared on Metacritic's list of the all-time lowest-scoring films.<ref name="Metacritic"/>

=== ''Fatal Deviation'' (1998) ===
{{Main|Fatal Deviation{{!}}''Fatal Deviation''}}
''Fatal Deviation'' is often credited as being the first [[martial arts film]] to be filmed in Ireland. It stars martial artist James Bennett and [[Michael Graham (singer)|Michael Graham]], who is best known for being a member of the boy band [[Boyzone]]. ''[[The Irish Post]]'' and ''[[Den of Geek]]'' write that it is a mainstay of worst film lists.<ref name="irishpost"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/fatal-deviation/looking-back-at-fatal-deviation-irelands-only-martial-arts-film|title=Meet Fatal Deviation, Ireland's only martial arts film|last=Lines|first=Craig|date=November 4, 2015|access-date=June 7, 2019|work=[[Den of Geek]]|archive-date=June 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607211617/https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/fatal-deviation/looking-back-at-fatal-deviation-irelands-only-martial-arts-film|url-status=dead}}</ref> Luke McKinney of [[Cracked.com]] called it the worst film ever made, writing: "There are so many things about making a movie that Jimmy doesn't know, that you could replace film school with this movie alone—just screening it once for students and asking them to list all the things it did wrong. Anyone who doesn't write 'everything' instantly fails."<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.cracked.com/article_18632_irelands-only-kung-fu-movie-is-worst-film-ever-made.html|title=Ireland's Only Kung Fu Movie (Is The Worst Film Ever Made)|last=McKinney|first=Luke|date=July 3, 2010|access-date=March 9, 2019|work=[[Cracked.com]]}}</ref> ''[[The Irish Post]]'' named it the worst Irish film of all time,<ref name="irishpost">{{cite web |url= https://www.irishpost.com/entertainment/definitive-ranking-7-worst-irish-films-time-158594|title= A definitive ranking of the 7 worst Irish films of all-time|first=Aidan|last=Lonergan|date= August 16, 2018|access-date= March 9, 2019|work= [[The Irish Post]]}}</ref> the ''[[Irish Independent]]'' wrote that it is "regarded as one of the worst films ever made" and ''[[Comic Book Resources]]'' called it "one of the worst commercial movies ever made".<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.independent.ie/lifestyle/westlife-what-next-26785226.html|title=Westlife: what next?|date= October 22, 2011|access-date=March 9, 2019|work=[[Irish Independent]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Boehm |first=Simon |title=Ireland's First Martial Arts Movie Is Gloriously Bad |url=https://www.cbr.com/fatal-deviation-ireland-martial-arts-movie-cult-classic/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |access-date=July 13, 2022 |date=March 15, 2021}}</ref> ''[[Entertainment.ie]]'' placed it on its list of "10 So Bad They're Good Movies You Need To See Before You Die" and it was covered in ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]''{{'}}s ''Bad Movie Diaries'' column.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://entertainment.ie/cinema/movie-news/10-so-bad-theyre-good-movies-you-need-to-see-before-you-die-227463/|title=10 So Bad They're Good Movies You Need To See Before You Die|last=Lloyd|first=Bryan|access-date=March 9, 2019|work=[[entertainment.ie]]|date=March 12, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2018/07/bad-movie-diaries-fatal-deviation-1998.html |title=Bad Movie Diaries: Fatal Deviation (1998)|last1=Vorel|first1=Jim|last2=Lowe|first2=Kenneth|access-date=June 7, 2019|work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]|date=July 31, 2018}}</ref>

=== ''Parting Shots'' (1999) ===
{{Main|Parting Shots{{!}}''Parting Shots''}}
The British [[black comedy]] ''Parting Shots'' was the last film directed by [[Michael Winner]]. It starred rock musician [[Chris Rea]] as a man who, after being told he has only six months to live, begins murdering people who have wronged him. [[Andrew Collins (broadcaster)|Andrew Collins]] took a very negative view of the film: "''Parting Shots'' ... is going to set the course of British film-making back 20 years. It is not only the worst British film produced in this country since ''[[Carry On Emmannuelle]]'' (quite a feat in itself), it is a thoroughbred contender for the crown of Worst Film Ever Made."<ref>Andrew Collins, "How to Shoot a Real Turkey" ''[[The Observer]]'', March 28, 1999. ''Observer Screen'', p.6.</ref> In an interview about the film, Charlotte O'Sullivan, the [[The Independent|''Independent'']]{{'}}s film editor, claimed ''Parting Shots'' was "the worst film I've ever seen". O'Sullivan also criticized it for glorifying vigilantism: "It's Michael Winner and you know, he doesn't have any sense of irony. He seems to be saying it is okay to go and kill people."<ref>"Winner's Turkey has a bad aftertaste". ''[[The Sunday Herald]]'', May 2, 1999 (p.7)</ref> The journalist [[Miles Kington]] later claimed "''Parting Shots'' ... was directed by Michael Winner and despite the glittering cast, was possibly the worst film ever made."<ref>Miles Kingston, "One or two plots to occupy my declining years". ''[[The Independent]]'', May 3, 2005, (p.30).</ref> I. Q. Hunter listed ''Parting Shots'' as one of the candidates for "the Worst British film ever made".<ref name="iqh"/> ''Parting Shots'' was also featured in a poll of ''Empire'' magazine readers' "50 Worst Movies Ever" poll.<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/>

=== ''The Underground Comedy Movie'' (1999) ===
{{Main|The Underground Comedy Movie{{!}}''The Underground Comedy Movie''}}
''The Underground Comedy Movie'' is based on a [[cable access]] show from 1988. Director and lead actor [[Vince Offer]] constructed the film out of a series of tasteless, [[low culture|lowbrow skits]]<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eXCwEb1qfcA The Bizarre Scandals of TV Commercial Stars - wavywebstuff on YouTube]</ref> (including [[Gena Lee Nolin]] loudly using the restroom and a superhero named ''Dickman'' who dresses in a giant [[human penis|penis]] costume and defeats his enemies by squirting them with [[semen]]). In 1999, Offer filed a suit against [[20th Century Fox]] and the co-directors of ''[[There's Something About Mary]]'' (1998), [[Farrelly brothers|Bobby and Peter Farrelly]], claiming that 14 scenes in ''Mary'' were stolen from his film.<ref name="ewol">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/article/1999/06/11/underground-comedy-movie-2/|title=Movie Review Underground Comedy Movie|date=June 11, 1999|access-date=December 3, 2019|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Gleiberman|first=Owen|archive-date=November 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105184521/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,273701,00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Farrellys released this statement: "We've never heard of him, we've never heard of his movie, and it's all a bunch of baloney."<ref name="ewx">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/article/1998/10/16/monitor-269/|title=Monitor: Celebrity news for October 16, 1998|last1=Karger|first1=Dave|first2=Suna|last2=Chang|date=October 16, 1998|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=December 3, 2019|archive-date=November 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105184053/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,285287,00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Lawrence Van Gelder]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' referred to it as a "wretched film" and stated that "''The Underground Comedy Movie'' stands as a monument to ineptitude and self-delusion."<ref name="nytvangelder">{{cite news|url=https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/film/052899comedy-film-review.html|title=Lawrence Van Gelder's review of ''The Underground Comedy Movie'' |last=Van Gelder |first=Lawrence |author-link=Lawrence Van Gelder |work=[[The New York Times]]|date=May 28, 1999 |access-date=December 19, 2013}}</ref> [[Rod Dreher]] of the ''[[New York Post]]'' said it "may be the least amusing comedy ever made".<ref>{{cite news|last=Dreher|first=Rod|author-link=Rod Dreher|title='Comedy' is Really Buried by Its Trash|work=[[New York Post]]|date=May 28, 1999}}</ref> Dave Shulman of ''[[L.A. Weekly]]'' described it as a "serious contender for the single worst movie ever made",<ref>{{cite web |title=Critic's Corner S-Z |url=http://thestinkers.com/critics3.html#Underground%20Comedy%20Movie |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010412233933/http://thestinkers.com/critics3.html#Underground%20Comedy%20Movie |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 12, 2001 |website=[[Stinkers Bad Movie Awards]] |access-date=July 9, 2022}}</ref> while Stinkers Bad Movie Awards co-founder Mike Lancaster said that it was the worst film that he had ever paid to see.<ref name="Lancaster"/> [[Nathan Rabin]] covered the film in his column detailing terrible films and stated that: "nothing I've covered for this column was quite as soul-crushingly, brain-meltingly terrible as ... ''The Underground Comedy Movie'''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nathanrabin.com/happy-place/2018/9/4/this-looks-terrible-the-underground-comedy-movie-1999|title=This Looks Terrible! The Underground Comedy Movie (1999)|last=Rabin|first=Nathan|author-link=Nathan Rabin|work=nathanrabin.com|date=September 4, 2018|access-date=February 23, 2019}}</ref> Thom Bennett at ''[[Film Journal International]]'', wrote "Anyone offended by unbearably bad films, jokes that are not funny and wasting 90 minutes of their lives is, as promised, guaranteed to be offended. In fact, to even call this mess a comedy is giving it far too much credit", and "''The Underground Comedy Movie'' may well be the worst film I have ever seen."<ref name="fji">{{cite web|url=http://www.filmjournal.com/filmjournal/esearch/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000697847|title=Underground Comedy Movie, The|last=Bennett|first=Thom|work=[[Film Journal International]]|access-date=March 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105184223/http://www.filmjournal.com/filmjournal/esearch/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1000697847|archive-date=November 5, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Writing in ''[[Central Western Daily]]'', Peter Young said, "I am pretty sure that I can declare this The Worst Film I Have Ever Seen."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.centralwesterndaily.com.au/story/1386763/comedy-film-best-kept-underground/|title=Comedy film best kept underground|last=Young|first=Peter|work=[[Central Western Daily]]|date=March 26, 2013|access-date=March 6, 2018}}</ref>

==2000==
=== ''Battlefield Earth'' (2000) ===
{{Main|Battlefield Earth (film){{!}}''Battlefield Earth'' (film)}}
[[File:John Travolta Battlefield Earth signing.jpg|thumb|[[John Travolta]] during ''[[Battlefield Earth (film)|Battlefield Earth]]''{{'s}} promotional tour]]

''Battlefield Earth'' is based on the first half of [[L. Ron Hubbard]]'s 1982 [[Battlefield Earth (novel)|novel of the same name]], and stars [[John Travolta]], [[Barry Pepper]] and [[Forest Whitaker]]. It was criticized for its script, acting, overuse of [[Dutch angle]]s, dialogue, several inconsistencies, and plot holes. The film has a 3% rating at Rotten Tomatoes,<ref>{{Rotten Tomatoes|qid=Q811023|title=Battlefield Earth}}</ref> where it is included in the top 100 worst-reviewed movies of all time.<ref name="rt100worst"/><ref name="rottenworst">{{cite web |url=https://rottentomatoes.com/guides/worst_of_the_worst/ |title=The worst of the worst pictures |website=Rotten Tomatoes |date=September 21, 2009 |access-date=January 17, 2011 |archive-date=November 23, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101123212257/http://www.rottentomatoes.com/guides/worst_of_the_worst/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Roger Ebert predicted that the film, "for decades to come will be the punch line of jokes about bad movies",<ref name="BEarth">{{cite news |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/battlefield-earth-2000 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |title=Battlefield Earth movie review (2000) |date=May 12, 2000 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |last=Ebert |first=Roger |author-link=Roger Ebert}}</ref> and placed it on his "most hated" list.<ref name="eberthated"/> Nathan Rabin covered the film as part of his ''My World of Flops'' column for ''[[The A.V. Club]]'', calling it "a fiasco that occupies a distinguished place high atop the pantheon of widely reviled crap" and said, "A legendary disaster well before it finished completion, ''Battlefield Earth'' hit theaters with a 'Kick Me' sign on it so massive it could be detected from outer space."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.avclub.com/my-year-of-flops-case-file-66-battlefield-earth-1798212540 |title=My Year OF Flops Case File #66: Battlefield Earth |last=Rabin |first=Nathan |author-link=Nathan Rabin |website=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=September 11, 2007 |language=en-US |access-date=January 27, 2019}}</ref>

The film ultimately won nine [[Golden Raspberry Awards]], including Worst Picture, Worst Screen Couple (John Travolta and "anyone on the screen with him"), and a special award in 2010 as the Worst Picture of the Decade.<ref name="30thRazzies">{{cite web |title=Razzie Noms for Worst Picture of the Decade |work=Razzies.com |url=http://www.razzies.com/history/09NomPOD.asp |access-date=February 2, 2010}}</ref> This was the most Razzies won by any film in the history of the awards at the time,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.razzies.com/history/07release.asp |title=Golden Raspberry Award Foundation |work=Razzies.com |access-date=November 18, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130321103846/http://www.razzies.com/history/07release.asp |archive-date=March 21, 2013}}</ref> a record it held until ''[[Jack and Jill (2011 film)|Jack and Jill]]'' surpassed it with 10 wins in 2012.<ref name=RazzieWin>{{cite news |title=Adam Sandler movie Jack and Jill sweeps Razzie awards |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-17582458 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=April 2, 2012 |access-date=May 17, 2012}}</ref> Listing the film as one of the worst decisions in movie history, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' quipped that, "If Earth sticks around long enough for the Golden Raspberry Awards to hand out a 'worst movie of the century' at their 2100 ceremony, it'll probably win that, too."<ref name="50decisions"/> The movie appeared on Metacritic's list of the all-time lowest-scoring films,<ref name="Metacritic"/> and is on the [[Movie Review Query Engine]]'s (MRQE) 50 Worst Movies list,<ref name="MRQE50">{{cite web |url=https://www.mrqe.com/lists/50_worst_movies |title=50 Worst Movies |work=[[Movie Review Query Engine]] |access-date=April 17, 2019}}</ref> as well as worst film lists from ''Screen Rant'', ''Vanity Fair'', ''Flavorwire'', ''[[Digital Trends]]'' and the ''New York Daily News''.<ref name="Flavorwire">{{cite web|url=http://flavorwire.com/477608/the-50-worst-movies-ever-made/view-all |title=The 50 Worst Movies Ever Made|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330132846/https://www.flavorwire.com/477608/the-50-worst-movies-ever-made/view-all |first=Jason |last=Bailey |date= September 17, 2014|access-date=November 19, 2025|archive-date=March 30, 2019 |work=[[Flavorwire]]}}</ref><ref name="Screen Rant"/><ref name="italianvanity"/><ref name="digitaltrends">{{cite web|url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/movies/worst-movies-ever-made/|title=10 Worst Movies You Can Watch|work=[[Digital Trends]]|last=Nicol|first=Will|date=May 10, 2017|access-date=July 28, 2017}}</ref><ref name="NYDN">{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/worst-movies-made-gallery-1.3678697|title=The worst movies ever made|last=Lisi|first=Brian|work=[[New York Daily News]]|date=December 5, 2017 |access-date=March 14, 2018}}</ref> ''Empire'' named it the second worst movie ever made after ''[[Batman & Robin (film)|Batman & Robin]]'' and ''[[The Register]]'' listed it as the worst movie ever made.<ref name="The 50 Worst Movies Ever"/><ref name="battlefieldregister">{{cite web |title=Battlefield Earth ruled worst film Ever |work=[[The Register]]|last=Haines |first=Lester |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2012/04/20/worst_movie/ |access-date=April 5, 2018 |date=April 20, 2012}}</ref> Pepper and Whitaker both expressed regret for their involvement in ''Battlefield Earth'', while film screenwriter [[J. David Shapiro]] later apologized for making "the suckiest movie ever".<ref>{{cite web |last=Dembrow |first=Dylan |title=15 Things You Didn't Know About The Disastrous Battlefield Earth |url=https://screenrant.com/battlefield-earth-movie-worst-trivia-facts-secrets/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |date=January 28, 2018 |access-date=December 5, 2020}}</ref><ref name="battlefieldregister"/>

===''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' (2000)===
{{main|Titanic: The Legend Goes On{{!}}''Titanic: The Legend Goes On''}}
''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' (also known as ''Titanic, mille e una storia'', ''Titanic: La leggenda continua'' and ''Titanic: The Animated Movie'') is an Italian animated [[mockbuster]] about [[Sinking of the Titanic|the sinking]] of the {{RMS|Titanic}}. It features a similar romantic storyline to [[Titanic (1997 film)|James Cameron's 1997 film]], but also has a number of talking animals (most notably, a [[rapping]] dog).<ref name="screenrantanimated">{{cite web|date=January 15, 2017|title=12 Worst Animated Movies of All Time|url=http://screenrant.com/worst-animated-movies-all-time/|access-date=January 7, 2022|work=[[Screen Rant]]|archive-date=January 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108225848/https://screenrant.com/worst-animated-movies-all-time/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Reviews condemned the quality of the animation and criticized the plot for being insensitive to the memory of the victims of the ''Titanic''.<ref name="screenrantanimated"/>

''[[Total Film]]'' named ''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' as "officially the worst film ever made", after it topped a list of the 66 worst films ever.<ref name=TotalFilm/> An article from ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]'' also described it as one of the worst films ever made, but notes that it "[lacks] the cult following that other bad films often acquire", stating: "''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' is too heinous for such fond pleasures."<ref>{{cite web |last=Mattson |first=Kelcie |title=I Watched the Animated Titanic Musical So You Don't Have To |url=https://collider.com/titanic-animated-movie/ |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=May 3, 2024 |language=en |date=September 11, 2023}}</ref> Critic Tim Brayton said that "It is one of the most surreally bad films I have ever encountered", adding: "For sheer mesmerising grotesqueness, there's almost nothing I can name that beats it, and no fan of bad movies can say that their life is complete till they've been exposed to it."<ref>{{cite web |title=Titanic: The Animated Movie |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/titanic_the_animated_movie |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |access-date=January 28, 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Brayton |first=Tim |title=Titanic: The Legend Goes On... (2000) – Movie Review |url=https://www.alternateending.com/2020/05/titanic-the-legend-goes-on-2000.html |website=Alternate Ending |access-date=January 28, 2022 |date=May 20, 2020}}</ref> ''Total Film'' also included the film on a list of the worst kids' movies, describing it as being "widely considered one of the worst animated films ever made",<ref name="kidsmovie"/> while Spanish film magazine ''[[Fotogramas]]'' selected it as one of the 20 worst films ever made.<ref name="fotogramas"/> ''[[Screen Rant]]'' included it on a list of the 12 worst animated films of all time, and it topped a ''Showbiz Cheat Sheet'' list of the top 10 worst animated films ever, with author Will Roberts commenting that "[any] list of the worst animated films of all time begins with ... ''Titanic: The Legend Goes On''".<ref name="screenrantanimated"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cheatsheet.com/entertainment/worst-animated-movies.html/|title=10 Worst Animated Movies of All Time|work=Showbiz Cheat Sheet|last=Roberts|first=Will|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=January 28, 2022|archive-date=January 22, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122103918/https://www.cheatsheet.com/entertainment/worst-animated-movies.html/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, ''Titanic: The Legend Goes On'' became the lowest-rated film on [[IMDb]]'s Bottom 100 list.<ref>{{cite web |last=Renzetti |first=Jackie |title=Not Your Cameron's 'Titanic' |url=https://mndaily.com/223181/arts-entertainment/not-your-camerons-titanic/ |newspaper=[[The Minnesota Daily]] |date= April 16, 2014|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>

'''''Man of Steel''''' is a 2013 [[superhero film]] based on the [[DC Comics]] character [[Superman]]. Directed by [[Zack Snyder]] and written by [[David S. Goyer]], who developed the story with producer [[Christopher Nolan]], it is the first film in the [[DC Extended Universe]] (DCEU),<ref name="DCEU" /><ref name="DCMarvelForbes" /> and a [[Reboot (fiction)|reboot]] of the [[Superman in film|''Superman'' film series]], depicting the character's [[Origin of Superman|origin story]]. [[Henry Cavill]] stars as [[Superman (DC Extended Universe)|Superman]], alongside [[Amy Adams]], [[Michael Shannon]], [[Kevin Costner]], [[Diane Lane]], [[Laurence Fishburne]], and [[Russell Crowe]]. In the film, Clark Kent learns that he is a superpowered alien from the planet [[Krypton (comics)|Krypton]] and assumes the role of mankind's protector as Superman, making the choice to face [[Zod (DC Extended Universe)|General Zod]] and stop him from destroying humanity.

Development began in 2008 when [[Warner Bros. Pictures]] took pitches from comic book writers, screenwriters, and directors, opting to reboot the franchise. In 2009, a court ruling resulted in [[Jerry Siegel]]'s family recapturing the rights to Superman's origins and Siegel's copyright. The decision stated that Warner Bros. did not owe the families additional royalties from previous films, but if they did not begin production on a Superman film by 2011, then the Shuster and Siegel estates would be able to sue for lost revenue on an unproduced film. Nolan pitched Goyer's idea after a story discussion on ''[[The Dark Knight Rises]]'', and Snyder was hired as the film's director in October 2010. [[Principal photography]] began in August 2011 in [[West Chicago, Illinois]], before moving to [[Vancouver]] and [[Plano, Illinois]].

''Man of Steel'' premiered in the [[Alice Tully Hall]] in New York City on June 10, 2013, and was released by Warner Bros. Pictures in the United States on June 14. The film received mixed reviews from critics,<!--Per WP:FILMLEAD, any summary statement "should reflect an overall consensus explicitly summarized by one or more reliable sources"--><ref name="VultureRoundup" /> and was a commercial success, grossing $670{{nbsp}}million worldwide on a budget of $225–258{{nbsp}}million, becoming the [[2013 in film#Highest-grossing films|ninth-highest-grossing film of 2013]]. Critics praised its visuals, music, casting, performances, and action sequences, but criticized its dark tone and some plot elements, as well as the portrayal of Superman. A sequel, ''[[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice]],'' was released in 2016. A further reboot, ''[[Superman (2025 film)|Superman]]'', the first film in the [[DC Universe (franchise)|DC Universe]] (DCU), was released in 2025, and stars [[David Corenswet]] as the title character.

{{TOC limit|3}}

==Plot==
<!-- Per WP:FILMPLOT, plot summaries for feature films should be between 400 and 700 words only. -->
The planet [[Krypton (comics)|Krypton]] is destabilizing due to reckless mining of the [[planetary core]]. The Kryptonian Council ignores the warnings of renowned scientist [[Jor-El]], who then steals and infuses the Kryptonian genetics codex into his new-born son, [[Clark Kent|Kal-El]], the first naturally-born Kryptonian in centuries. Jor-El and his wife Lara manage to evacuate Kal-El in a spacecraft toward Earth before Jor-El is killed by [[Zod (DC Extended Universe)|General Zod]] during a coup d'état. Zod's insurrection is stopped by the Kryptonian Council; he and his followers are sent into the [[Phantom Zone]] as punishment. Krypton is destroyed, along with all its remaining inhabitants.

Kal-El lands in [[Kansas]], where he is adopted by [[Jonathan and Martha Kent]] and named [[Superman (DC Extended Universe)|Clark]]. As he grows older, due to his Kryptonian physiology and Earth's [[G-type main-sequence star|yellow sun]], he develops superhuman powers that Jonathan urges him to keep hidden until he is mature enough to handle the global consequences, even refusing Clark's help years later, leading to his death in a storm. Burdened with guilt, Clark travels the globe hiding under various aliases, seeking his purpose, and discreetly helping those in need.

''[[Daily Planet]]'' reporter [[Lois Lane (DC Extended Universe)|Lois Lane]] investigates the discovery of a Kryptonian scout ship in the Arctic. Disguised as a worker, Clark enters the ship. He learns from its artificial intelligence, modeled after Jor-El, about his origins, and that Clark was sent to Earth with the hope he would guide its people. While following Clark, Lois inadvertently triggers the ship's security system. Clark uses his powers to rescue her. Wearing a uniform provided by the ship, he begins testing his abilities. Unable to convince her editor-in-chief, [[Perry White]], to publish an article on the incident, Lois leaks the story to a popular [[blogger]]. She tracks down Clark in [[Smallville (comics)|Smallville]] intent on exposing him. However, upon hearing of Jonathan Kent's sacrifice, Lois decides to keep Clark's identity safe, while fueling Perry's suspicions.

Zod and his followers are revealed to have been released from the Phantom Zone when Krypton was destroyed. They retrofitted their prison vessel into a functioning ship and salvaged several [[Terraforming#In popular culture|xenoforming]] devices from abandoned Kryptonian outposts. Waiting thirty-three years for a sign of Kryptonian survival, they are drawn to Earth when Clark accessed the ancient scout ship. Zod threatens Earth unless Clark surrenders to him; Clark reveals himself to [[U.S. military]] personnel and surrenders to their custody. Lois is also captured by the military due to her leaked story. 

Clark negotiates a meeting with Zod, who demands Clark and Lois join him on his ship. Onboard, Zod infiltrates their minds, revealing his intention to xenoform Earth into a new Krypton once he is in possession of the codex, which will result in humanity's [[extinction]]. Clark refuses to join Zod. Using the Jor-El AI to temporarily take over the ship, he and Lois escape. Intending to use the codex to repopulate his species, Zod investigates Clark's pod in Smallville. However, the codex cannot be found and Zod angrily threatens Martha. Clark fights off Zod's followers across Smallville, convincing the military of his allegiance to Earth.

Zod's science officer, [[Jax-Ur]], discovers Jor-El hid the codex's information within Clark's genes, the extraction of which would be fatal. Zod nevertheless deploys his xenoforming device, the World Engine to the [[Indian Ocean]], while descending his ship over Metropolis. The two work in concert to xenoform Earth, severely damaging [[Metropolis (comics)|Metropolis]]. Clark, now dubbed "[[Superman]]" by Lois, destroys the World Engine while the military launches an attack on Zod's primary vessel, utilizing Clark's pod to create a [[gravitational singularity|singularity]]. The attack is successful, sending Zod's troops back to the Phantom Zone. With his ship destroyed and Krypton's only hope of revival gone, a vengeful Zod vows to destroy Earth and its inhabitants. He and Clark engage in a cataclysmic battle across Metropolis, which concludes when Clark is [[trolley problem|forced to kill]] Zod as he attacks a family trapped in a train station.

Sometime later, Clark, as Superman, persuades the government to let him act independently, promising not to turn against humanity. To gain covert access to dangerous situations, Clark takes a job reporting for the ''Daily Planet'' alongside Lois.

==Cast==

* [[Henry Cavill]] as [[Superman (DC Extended Universe)|Kal-El / Clark Kent]]:<!--STOP! He is not credited as "Superman". This is based on film crediting.!--> <br /> A [[Kryptonian]] with superhuman powers and abilities, sent by his parents to Earth as an infant to escape the destruction of his homeworld, Krypton, and raised under the mental guidance of farmers in [[Smallville (comics)|Smallville]], [[Kansas]], until he is inspired by the [[holographic]] message from his late father to become Earth's greatest protector. Cavill is the first non-American actor to play the character.<ref name="CavillCast" /><ref name="CavillCast2" /> He was previously cast in ''[[Superman: Flyby]]'', which was ultimately shelved,<ref name="CavillFlyby" /> and was considered for the role in the 2006 film ''[[Superman Returns]]'', but lost to [[Brandon Routh]].<ref name="CavillRouth" /><ref name="SnyderCollider" /> Cavill stated, "There's a very real story behind the Superman character." He explained that everyone's goal has been to explore the difficulties his character faces as a result of having multiple identities—including his birth name, Kal-El, and his alter ego, Clark Kent. Cavill also stated that "He's alone and there's no one like him," referring to Superman's vulnerabilities. "That must be incredibly scary and lonely, not to know who you are or what you are, and trying to find out what makes sense. Where's your [[Reference|baseline]]? What do you draw from? Where do you draw a limit with the power you have? In itself, that's an incredible weakness."<ref name="CavillYahoo" /> In an interview with ''[[Total Film]]'' magazine, Cavill stated he had been consuming nearly 5,000 calories a day, training for over two hours daily and plowing [[protein]] to pack on the [[muscle]] mass.<ref name="CavillTotalFilm" /> [[Tyler Hoechlin]] (who would later [[Clark Kent (Superman & Lois)|play the character]] in the [[Arrowverse]] and ''[[Superman & Lois]]''), [[Matthew Goode]], [[Armie Hammer]], [[Jamie Dornan]], [[Joe Manganiello]] and [[Colin O'Donoghue]] were also considered for the role. Manganiello was subsequently cast as [[Deathstroke]] in [[Justice League (film)|''Justice League'']].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 23, 2021 |title=Superman & Lois Star Tyler Hoechlin Auditioned for Zack Snyder's Man of Steel |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/superman-lois-star-tyler-hoechlin-auditioned-for-zack-snyders-man-of-steel/ |access-date=February 12, 2022 |publisher=[[Den of Geek]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kit |first=Borys |date=January 30, 2011 |title=How Henry Cavill Beat Matthew Goode and Others to Land 'Superman' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/henry-cavill-beat-matthew-goode-94438/ |access-date=May 26, 2022 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Buchanan |first=Kyle |date=November 18, 2021 |title=Jamie Dornan Goes Back to 'Belfast,' but Not Without Worry |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/18/movies/jamie-dornan-belfast.html |work=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 7, 2017 |title=Before Joe Manganiello Was Deathstroke, He Nearly Played Superman |url=https://uproxx.com/movies/joe-manganiello-almost-played-superman/}}</ref> Manganiello was Snyder's second choice behind Cavill.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1660275/henry-cavill-superman/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011234856/http://www.mtv.com/news/1660275/henry-cavill-superman/ | archive-date=October 11, 2016 | title=MTV &#124; as he wanted his interpretation be from the source material.<ref>{{Cite magazine |title='Man of Steel': The four 'Superman' comics that inspired Henry Cavill |url=https://ew.com/article/2013/04/21/man-of-steel-four-superman-comic-books-inspired-henry-cavill/ |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/film/henry-cavill | title=Henry Cavill | date=May 31, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://directconversations.com/2021/03/21/interview-flashback-henry-cavill-talks-man-of-steel/ | title=Interview flashback: Tim talks with Henry Cavill about 'Man of Steel' | date=March 21, 2021 }}</ref> Cooper Timberline was cast as the 9-year-old Clark Kent, and [[Dylan Sprayberry]] was cast as the 13-year-old Clark Kent.<ref name="SprayberryCast" />
* [[Amy Adams]] as [[Lois Lane (DC Extended Universe)|Lois Lane]]:<ref name="AdamsCast" /><ref name="AdamsCast2" /> <br /> A reporter for the ''[[Daily Planet]]'' newspaper and the love interest of Clark Kent. Adams was selected from a list of actresses that included [[Kristen Stewart]], [[Zoe Saldaña]], [[Olivia Wilde]], and [[Mila Kunis]].<ref name="Zaldana" /><ref name="Stewart" /><ref name="WildeKunis" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2011 |title=Director Zack Snyder feels 'slighted' after Kristen Stewart turns down role in 'Superman' reboot |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/gossip/director-zack-snyder-feels-slighted-kristen-stewart-turns-role-superman-reboot-article-1.133043 |website=[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]] |location=New York}}</ref> "There was a big, giant search for Lois," Snyder said. "For us, it was a big thing and obviously a really important role. We did a lot of auditioning, but we had this meeting with Amy Adams and after that I just felt she was perfect for it."<ref name="AdamsCast3" /> Adams auditioned for the role three times: once for the unproduced ''Superman: Flyby'', and the second time for ''Superman Returns'' before landing the current role.<ref name="AdamsFlyby" /> Adams was confirmed to play Lois Lane in March 2011. While announcing the role, Snyder said in a statement, "We are excited to announce the casting of Amy Adams, one of the most versatile and respected actresses in films today. Amy has the talent to capture all of the qualities we love about Lois: smart, tough, funny, warm, ambitious and, of course, beautiful."<ref name="AdamsCast4" /> On portraying Lois Lane, Adams stated that the film would feature a Lois Lane who is an "independent, feisty woman ... but set in a more identifiable world." Adams said that "She has become more of a free-ranging journalist, someone who likes to be hands-on. The nature of the newspaper business has changed so much. There is so much more pressure."<ref name="AdamsGeekTyrant" />
* [[Michael Shannon]] as [[Zod (DC Extended Universe)|General Zod]]:<ref name="ShannonCast" /> <br /> A Kryptonian general with the same [[Superpower (ability)|superpowers]] as Superman, bent on transforming Earth into a new Krypton under his reign. [[Viggo Mortensen]] and [[Daniel Day-Lewis]] were also considered for the role.<ref name="Mortensen" /><ref name="Day-Lewis" /> Snyder stated, "Zod is not only one of Superman's most formidable enemies, but one of the most significant because he has insights into Superman that others don't. Michael is a powerful actor who can project both the intelligence and the malice of the character, making him perfect for the role."<ref name="ShannonCast" /> When Goyer was asked about why Zod was chosen as the villain, he stated, "The way (Christopher) Nolan and I have always approached movies as well is you never say, 'Hey, which villain would be cool for this movie?' You start with the story first. What kind of story? What kind of theme do you want to tell? So we worked that out. Then, usually the villain becomes obvious in terms of who's going to be the appropriate [[antagonist]] for that. When you guys see the movie, the only villain we could've used was Zod and the Kryptonians. I mean, when you see what the whole story is, nothing else would have even made sense."<ref name="GoyerSHH" />
* [[Kevin Costner]] as [[Jonathan Kent (DC Extended Universe)|Jonathan Kent]]:  <br /> Clark's adoptive father.<ref name="CostnerCast" /> Snyder explained his reason for casting the on-screen couple is solely for the realism: "I think the thing you realize when you look at Diane and Kevin, in our decision to cast them so far, you sort of get a sense of how tonally we're looking at the movie, and what you realize is that those guys are serious actors, and we're taking this movie very seriously in terms of the tone of having those guys. You're talking about having a situation where whatever the action is or whatever the drama of the movie is, our first priority is to make sure it's rendered in the most realistic way we can get at."<ref name="Snyderio9" /> After taking on the role, Costner was disappointed when he read the script.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cinemablend.com/interviews/kevin-costner-zack-snyder-man-of-steel-script-hot-take-tornado-scene-superman | title='I Can't Fly?' Kevin Costner Remembers Reading Zack Snyder's Man of Steel Script, and His Hot Take on the Tornado Scene | date=June 29, 2024 }}</ref>

"This was a very important piece of casting for me because Martha Kent is the woman whose values helped shape the man we know as Superman," Snyder said in the release. "We are thrilled to have Diane in the role because she can convey the wisdom and the wonder of a woman whose son has powers beyond her imagination."<ref name="LaneCast" />

And so he was my inspiration for Perry."<ref name="FishburneBradley" />

[[Gal Gadot]] was offered the role but declined because she was pregnant at that time; this allowed her to be later cast as [[Diana Prince (DC Extended Universe)|Wonder Woman]] in [[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice|the film's sequel]].<ref name="Gadot" /> [[Alice Eve]], [[Diane Kruger]] and [[Rosamund Pike]] were also considered for the role.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kroll |first=Justin |date=February 4, 2011 |title=3 considered for 'Superman' female lead |url=https://variety.com/2011/film/news/3-considered-for-superman-female-lead-1118031515/ |access-date=May 26, 2022 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 5, 2011 |title=News: Exclusive: Superman's Undisclosed Character Revealed {{!}} Latino Review |url=http://www.latinoreview.com/news/exclusive-superman-s-undisclosed-character-revealed-12492 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110205215510/http://www.latinoreview.com/news/exclusive-superman-s-undisclosed-character-revealed-12492 |archive-date=February 5, 2011 |access-date=May 26, 2022}}</ref> About the role of Faora, Traue said in an interview: "What I liked about her was that as a woman, we have certain doubts and we think too much sometimes about ourselves and all these things, they're not there for Faora. She's a bred warrior. So to really focus on that aspect, that fear is a chemical reaction and that it was bred out of her and she doesn't have it. It's liberating when you actually think about it. That you're just a one-track mind, there's no filter, there's no double meaning. She gets orders and she answers those orders without a question."<ref name="TraueTribute" />
* [[Ayelet Zurer]] as [[Lara Lor-Van (DC Extended Universe)|Lara Lor-Van]]: <br /> Kal-El's biological mother and loyal wife to Jor-El. * [[Christopher Meloni]] as Col. Nathan Hardy:<ref name="ColliderImage" /><ref name="MeloniCast" /> <br /> A United States Air Force officer, call sign "[[Guardian (DC Comics)|Guardian]]", assigned to the [[United States Northern Command]].
* [[Russell Crowe]] as [[Jor-El (DC Extended Universe)|Jor-El]]: <br /> A Kryptonian scientist who is Kal-El's biological father. [[Sean Penn]] and [[Clive Owen]] were also considered for the role.<ref name="CroweCast" /> Crowe incorporates how his own fatherhood informed his reading of the script to portray Jor-El, stating that "... it was one of those things where that's how it was connecting me. That's the question that Jor-El faces, that's the situation that he's in."<ref name="CroweYahoo" /> Crowe also comments on his preparation for the film stating that: "When I signed on ... well, one, I didn't realize that I would be wearing [[Spandex]]—'cause you know that's Superman's costume—I didn't realize that I'd have to fit into it as well," Crowe said. "But, I also didn't realize the type of organiser that Zack Snyder is, 'cause this was really old-school prep. This is sort of [[David Lean]]-level preparation, and I really appreciated him. And I was on the movie for three and a half or four months before I even got in front of the camera."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russell Crowe Discusses 'Massive' & 'Intense' Training for Man of Steel | date=June 6, 2013 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J7UMkDboUuQ |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>

[[Carol Ferris|Carrie Ferris]], a United States Air Force officer and the assistant to General Swanwick.<ref name="WrenCast" /> [[Richard Schiff]] plays [[Emil Hamilton (DC Extended Universe)|Dr. Emil Hamilton]], a scientist who works with the United States Armed Forces for DARPA.<ref name="SchiffCast" /><ref name="SchiffCast2" /><ref name="SchiffCast3" /> [[Carla Gugino]] portrays the voice of Kelor, the Kryptonian AI service-robot.<ref name="GuginoCast" /> [[Mackenzie Gray]] plays [[Jax-Ur (DC Extended Universe)|Jax-Ur]], a Kryptonian scientist who is one of General Zod's followers.
