==Production==
===Development===
In June 2008, [[Warner Bros. Pictures|Warner Bros.]] took [[Pitch (filmmaking)|pitches]] from comic book writers, screenwriters and directors on how to successfully [[Reboot (fiction)|reboot]] the [[Superman in film|''Superman'' film series]].<ref name="MillarMTV" /> Comic book writers [[Grant Morrison]], [[Mark Waid]], [[Geoff Johns]] and [[Brad Meltzer]] were among those who pitched their ideas for a reboot: "I told them, it's not that bad. Just treat ''[[Superman Returns]]'' as the [[Ang Lee]] ''[[Hulk (film)|Hulk]]''", Morrison said. Waid said: "''[[The Incredible Hulk (film)|The Incredible Hulk]]'' has proven the audience will forgive you and let you redo the franchise".<ref name="RebootMTV" /> Morrison's idea was similar to his work on ''[[All-Star Superman]]'', while Waid's was akin to ''[[Superman: Birthright]]''.<ref name="RebootMTV" /> [[Mark Millar]], teaming with director [[Matthew Vaughn]], also planned an epic eight-hour ''Superman'' trilogy, each installment released a year apart, similar to ''[[The Lord of the Rings (film series)|The Lord of the Rings]]''.<ref name="MillarDoG" /><ref name="VaughnMTV" /> Millar compared it to [[The Godfather (film series)|''The Godfather'' trilogy]], in which it would chronicle the entire life of Superman, from the early days of Krypton, where little Kal-El witnesses his father's tireless struggle to save the planet, to the finale where Superman loses his powers as the Sun starts to go [[supernova]].<ref name="MillarEmpire" /> According to Millar, Vaughn suggested his ''[[Stardust (2007 film)|Stardust]]'' actor [[Charlie Cox]] as a Golden-Age inspired Superman "when he was a bit more of a regular person".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chang |first=Tom |date=May 14, 2020 |title=Daredevil's Charlie Cox Once Considered for Superman |url=https://bleedingcool.com/movies/daredevils-charlie-cox-once-considered-for-superman/ |access-date=April 5, 2021 |website=[[Bleeding Cool]]}}</ref> Vaughn would later say his pitch for a trilogy film would have been to a similar tone to [[Richard Donner]]'s [[Superman (1978 film)|1978 film]], and would have included villains such as Zod, [[Brainiac]], and [[Lex Luthor]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=October 19, 2023 |title=Matthew Vaughn Details Failed Superman Trilogy Pitch, Says 'Star Wars' Has 'Gone Wrong' and He'd Reboot Luke Skywalker: Everyone Will Go 'Bats— Crazy' |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/matthew-vaughn-superman-trilogy-failed-star-wars-reboot-luke-1235761824/ |access-date=November 23, 2023 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

In August 2008, Warner Bros. suggested that the planned [[sequel]] to ''Superman Returns'', subtitled ''Man of Steel'' by director [[Bryan Singer]], would now be a reboot of the film series. Studio executive Jeff Robinov planned to have the film released either by 2010 or 2011, explaining that "''Superman Returns'' didn't quite work as a film in the way that we wanted it to. It didn't position the character the way he needed to be positioned. Had Superman worked in 2006, we would have had a movie for Christmas of this year or 2009. Now the plan is just to reintroduce Superman without regard to a [[Batman]] and Superman movie at all."<ref name="RobinovWSJ" /> Paul Levitz stated in an interview that Batman holds the key to the Superman reboot. He elaborated: "Everyone is waiting for <nowiki>[</nowiki>[[Christopher Nolan]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> to sign on for another Batman, once that happens, the release date for Superman and all other future projects will follow."<ref name="LevitzMovieWeb" /> In February 2009, [[McG]], who previously planned to direct ''Superman: Flyby'', expressed interest in returning to the Superman franchise.<ref name="LevitzMovieWeb" /><ref name="McGio9" /> August 2009 saw a court ruling in which [[Jerry Siegel]]'s family recaptured 50% of the rights to Superman's origins and Siegel's share of the copyright in [[Action Comics 1|''Action Comics'' #1]].<ref name="SiegelVariety" /> In addition, a judge ruled that Warner Bros. did not owe the families additional royalties from previous films. However, if they did not begin production on a Superman film by 2011, then the Siegel estate would have been able to sue for lost revenue on an unproduced film.<ref name="SiegelVariety2" />

{{quote box|width=35%|align=right|quote=He basically told me, 'I have this thought about how you would approach Superman', I immediately got it, loved it and thought: That is a way of approaching the story I've never seen before that makes it incredibly exciting. I wanted to get [[Emma Thomas]] and I involved in shepherding the project right away and getting it to the studio and getting it going in an exciting way.|source=—[[Christopher Nolan]], recalling the moment when Goyer presented the idea of a modernized Superman.<ref name="GoyerStory" /><ref name="NolanSR" />}}
During story discussions for ''[[The Dark Knight Rises]]'' in 2008, [[David S. Goyer]] told Nolan his idea regarding how to present Superman in a modern context.<ref name="GoyerStory" /> Impressed with Goyer's concept, Nolan pitched the idea to the studio,<ref name="GoyerStory" /> who hired Nolan to produce and Goyer to write based on the financial and critical success of ''[[The Dark Knight]]''.<ref name="NolanDeadline" /><ref name="RobinovWSJ" /> Nolan admired Singer's work on ''Superman Returns'' for its connection to Richard Donner's version, stating that "a lot of people have approached Superman in a lot of different ways. I only know the way that has worked for us that's what I know how to do", emphasizing the idea that Batman exists in a world where he is the only superhero and a similar approach to Superman would assure the integrity needed for the new film. Nolan, however, clarified that the film would not have any relationship with the previous ''Superman'' film series, in which he commented: "Each serves to the internal logic of the story. They have nothing to do with each other".<ref name="NolanLATimes" />

[[Guillermo del Toro]], with whom Goyer worked on ''[[Blade II]]'', turned down the director's position on the reboot because of his commitment on a film adaptation of ''[[At the Mountains of Madness]]'',<ref name="delToroDeadline" /> while [[Robert Zemeckis]] was also approached.<ref name="ZemeckisMTV" /> [[Ben Affleck]], [[Darren Aronofsky]], [[Duncan Jones]], [[Jonathan Liebesman]], [[Matt Reeves]] (who would later direct a [[The Batman (film)|Batman reboot]]), and [[Tony Scott]] were considered as potential directors.<ref name="DirectorsDeadline" />

[[Zack Snyder]] was hired as director in October 2010,<ref name="SnyderHired" /> while casting began the following November.<ref name="CastingBegin" /><ref name="CastingBegin2" /> In the original script Zod was going to be sucked into the [[Phantom Zone]], but Snyder and Goyer felt it was unsatisfying so they asked DC Comics if Superman would kill someone if he didn't have a choice. Nolan was against this approach, leading Goyer to come up with the scene with the heat vision and putting people in imminent danger and this convinced Nolan.<ref name="EmpireOnlineMoS">{{Cite web |last=Plumb |first=Ali |date=June 18, 2013 |title=David S. Goyer And Zack Snyder On Man Of Steel's Secrets |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/features/man-steel-secrets/ |access-date=August 20, 2024 |publisher=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire Online]] }}</ref> Robinov spoke to ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' and allowed a peek over the wall of secrecy surrounding Warner Bros.' DC plans: "It's setting the tone for what the movies are going to be like going forward. In that, it's definitely a first step."<ref name="RobinovEW" /> Plans included for the film to contain references to the existence of other superheroes, alluding to the possibility of a further [[DC Universe]],<ref name="SnyderBatmanNews" /> and setting the tone for a shared fictional universe of DC Comics characters on film.<ref name="RobinovEW" /> Snyder confirmed both [[Booster Gold]] and Batman references in the film. When Zod destroys a satellite, the words "Wayne Enterprises" are scrolled on the satellite.<ref name="EasterEggs" /> Snyder and Nolan considered having ''Man of Steel'' share continuity with [[The Dark Knight trilogy|''The Dark Knight'' trilogy]], but ultimately decided against it.<ref name="MoSTDK" />

The film's storyboard was created by storyboard artist [[Jay Oliva]], in his first live-action feature film project, along with Snyder.<ref name="OliviaVfK" /> Oliva has cited the Japanese [[anime]] shows ''[[Dragon Ball Z]]'' and ''[[Birdy the Mighty]]'' as an inspiration for the film's epic battle scenes. During the film's brainstorming, Oliva pitched the idea as "I could come up with something I've never seen in live-action American cinema and only in anime".<ref name="OlivaCB" />

===Filming===
[[Principal photography]] began on August 1, 2011, at an [[industrial park]] near [[DuPage Airport]] under the codename "Autumn Frost".<ref name="ChicagoBusiness2" /> Zack Snyder expressed reluctance to shoot the film in 3D due to the technical limitations of the format and instead chose to shoot in 2D and [[2D to 3D conversion|convert the film into 3D]] in [[post-production]], for a 2D, 3D, RealD 3D, IMAX 3D and 4DX release.<ref name="Snyder3D" /> Snyder also chose to shoot on [[35 mm movie film|film]] instead of [[digital cinematography|digitally]] because he felt it would make the film "a big movie experience".<ref name="SnyderFilm" /> Cinematographer [[Amir Mokri]] shot the film with [[Panavision]] [[Panavision cameras#Panaflex Millennium|Panaflex Millennium XL2]] cameras and [[Anamorphic format#Origination|C-Series anamorphic lenses]].<ref name="Panavision" /> Filming was expected to last for two to three months.<ref name="ChicagoBusiness" /> Production took place in [[Plano, Illinois]] on August 22 to 29.<ref name="ChicagoBusiness2" /><ref name="FilmingHuffPost" /> According to an interview with Michael Shannon, filming would continue until February 2012.<ref name="FilmingCollider" />

''Man of Steel'' filmed in the [[Chicago]] area, [[California]], and [[Burnaby]]'s Mammoth Studios in [[Vancouver]], which was used as a set for Krypton and the extraterrestrial aircraft portrayed in the film.<ref name="Filming-Vancouver Sun" /><ref name="Vancouver" /> Vancouver's North Shore waterfront area was also used for the oil rig rescue scene where Superman is first introduced.<ref name="Filming-Vancouver Sun">{{Cite news |last=Barrett |first=Jessica |date=June 13, 2013 |title=Why Vancouver was passed over to play Metropolis in Man of Steel |url=https://vancouversun.com/Entertainment/Movies/vancouver-was-passed-over-to-play-metropolis-in-man-of-steel?r |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712092106/https://vancouversun.com/Entertainment/Movies/vancouver-was-passed-over-to-play-metropolis-in-man-of-steel?r |archive-date=July 12, 2021 |access-date=July 12, 2021 |work=[[The Vancouver Sun]]}}</ref> [[Ucluelet]] and [[Nanaimo]], [[British Columbia]], feature prominently in the film's first hour—the trademark winter mist and rough seas are passed off as [[Alaska]] in the film. Filming took place in the [[Chicago Loop]] from September 7 to 17.<ref name="ChicagoBusiness2" /> The Chicago shoot was a unit project, meaning that filming would partake numerous establishing shots as well as [[Cutaway (filmmaking)|cutaways]] and might not necessarily include principal cast members.<ref name="ChicagoSR" />

===Design===
''Man of Steel'' features a redesigned Superman costume by [[James Acheson]] and [[Michael Wilkinson (costume designer)|Michael Wilkinson]]. The costume preserves the color scheme and "S" logo, but adopts darker tones and notably does not feature the red [[Swim trunks|trunks]] usually worn by Superman. Zack Snyder said the costume is "a modern aesthetic". He and the producers attempted to devise a suit featuring the red trunks, but could not design one that fit into the tone of the film, leading to their removal from the suit.<ref name="DesignNYDaily" /> Because of Wilkinson's unavailability, Snyder chose Acheson to design the suit; however, he only started developing it, and Wilkinson finished the development when he returned, and designed the other character's costumes as well.<ref name="DesignEsquire" /> Due to the substantial weight a practical suit would yield, the [[Kryptonian]] armor for General Zod was constructed through CGI to allow Shannon "freedom of movement".<ref name="DesignTotalFilm" /> In a March 2014 interview with ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]'', Wilkinson explained the reason for the look of Superman's redesigned suit:
{{blockquote|A lot of the efforts we took in the film were to explain why the suit looks the way it does. We didn't want it to be a random, ornamental decision. We start the film on the planet of Krypton, which is where the suit comes from, and we go to great pains to show the suit fitting into the culture. All of the people you see on Krypton are wearing this chainmail-like suit, with the same detailing as the Superman suit. Everyone has their family crests on their chests. The cuff and the boot details are shared through all of the different characters we meet on Krypton. So by the time we see Superman in his suit we understand why it looks the way it looks.<ref name="DesignEsquire" />}}

===Visual effects===
John "DJ" Desjardin served as the visual supervisor for ''Man of Steel'', with [[Weta Digital]], [[Moving Picture Company]] (MPC) and [[DNEG|Double Negative]] providing the [[visual effects]] for the film.<ref name="LetteriIndieWire" /><ref name="DNeg" /> Zack Snyder wanted the film to "appear very natural because there's some very fantastical things in there and he wanted people to suspend their disbelief, and we the visual effects team had to make it as easy as possible for them to do so." Desjardin noted that the intent in shooting the film was to use handheld devices to make the film feel like a "[[Cinéma vérité|documentary-style]]" film. Desjardin said: "We had to think about what that would mean, since we also had to photograph some crazy action. So for a lot of the [[Previsualization|previs]] we did, we'd start to think where our cameras were and where our cameraman was. A lot of the rules are the ''[[Battlestar Galactica]]'' rules for the space cams that [[Gary Hutzel|Gary Hurtzel]]{{sic}} developed for that [[miniseries]], where we want to make sure if we're translating the camera at all it makes sense unless the action is so over the top, like in the end where Superman is beating up Zod, we had to break it a bit."<ref name="FXGuide" />

[[File:KryptonMOS.jpg|thumb|320px|left|Alien-like planet landscapes, creatures, and architecture were created by Weta Digital to further enhance the worldbuilding process of planet Krypton.]]
For the first act of the film taking place on the planet Krypton, Weta Digital placed alien-like planet environments, creatures, and the principal means of display—a technology the filmmakers called "liquid geometry". Weta Digital visual effects supervisor [[Dan Lemmon]] explained that "it's a bunch of silver beads that are suspended through a magnetic field, and the machine is able to control that magnetic field so that the collection of beads behave almost like three-dimensional [[pixel]]s, and they can create a surface that floats in the air and describes whatever the thing is you're supposed to be seeing." The beads of the display, which up close would appear to be pyramids with a slight [[bevel]], were designed to create a surface of the object to depict inside a "console-like" figure.<ref name="FXGuide" />

In the [[3D modeling|modeling]] and [[animation]] aspect of the liquid geometry, Brian Goodwin, the lead effects technical director of Weta Digital, explained: "We had to develop a pipeline to bring in assets, so instead of going through the route of reducing the [[polygon]] count to something usable what we would then do—you would take the model in whatever way it was made and just scatter discrete points onto it, and extract the matrix onto the animation and copy these points onto the matrix and have these sparse points behaving in a way that the model would."<ref name="FXGuide" /> After the animation, artists duplicated the beads onto the animated geometry for a pre-simulated lighting version to get approval on how the object would read. [[Simulation|Sims]] were then run "on all the targets which would be discrete beads floating around on top of the surface which would have its own set of parameters", in which Goodwin further explained: "The bead size or the turbulence that would crawl along the surface constantly updating the orientation was based on the [[Normal (geometry)|normal]] provided by the surface. That was then saved to disk and we would use that sim as the final target for the simulation." After the simulation process, Weta Digital ran every bead through a temporal filter to remove jitter to control the noise. Lighting solutions directly worked on the set. Weta used [[Pixar RenderMan|RenderMan]] to take advantage of improved [[Ray tracing (graphics)|ray tracing]] and [[Geometry instancing|instancing]] objects.<ref name="FXGuide" />

The sequences where Superman uses close-combat fight scenes with the other Kryptonians proved to be a major challenge for the filmmakers and the visual effects crew.<ref name="FXGuide" /> Desjardin explained: "When we do these fights and these hyper-real things, we don't want to do the traditional, 'OK I'm a cameraman, I'm shooting a clean plate, I'm going to pan over here to follow the action that's not really there yet but we'll put the action in later. Because that's us animating the characters to the camera. So we would do that animation with the characters—grappling, punching, or flying away—and we would take the real guys up until the point until they were supposed to do that and we'd cut. Then we'd put an environment camera there and take the environment. And then a camera for reference of the actors and get each moment. So then we had a set of [[Image resolution|high-res]] stills for the environment and the characters. Then, in post, we take the digi-doubles and animate them according to the speeds we want them to move in our digital environment."<ref name="FXGuide" />

MPC handled the visual effects for the "Smallville encounter" sequence. Before providing the visual effects, the shots were previsualized for the fight choreography. After the previsualizations, live action portions of the scene would be filmed in small pieces: "If say Superman was being punched and would land 50 meters away, we would shoot our start position and end position, and then bridge that gap with the CGI takeovers", says [[Guillaume Rocheron]], the MPC visual effects supervisor. A camera rig would then obtain [[key frame]]s of the choreographed actor; Desjardin said "it's a six-still camera rig that's built on a pipe rig so that you can run it in at the end of a setup and get stills of key frames of a performance or an expression, and then we could use those hi-res stills to project onto the CGI double and get really accurate transition lighting and color—right from the set."<ref name="FXGuide" />

On set, a camera rig was used to capture the environment of the sequence. Dubbed "enviro-cam", the visual effects crew would mount a [[Canon EOS 5D]] and a motorized nodal head, allowing the crew to capture the environment at a 360-degree angle with 55K resolution for every shot, the process would take approximately two to four minutes. The set capture resulted in lighting and textures that could be reprojected onto geometry.<ref name="FXGuide" /> Full-screen digital doubles were a major component for the fighting sequences. Digital armor was also added, along with the energy-based Kryptonian helmets. Cyberscan and FACS were conducted with the actors, and [[Polarization (waves)|polarized]] and non-polarized reference photos were taken. Superman's cape and costume were scanned in high detail—the cape in particular became a direct extension of Superman's actions.<ref name="FXGuide" />

For the sequences involving the xenoforming of the city Metropolis, Double Negative handled the visual effects for the sequence. To construct a Metropolis that seemed convincing and realistic, Double Negative used [[Esri]]'s [[CityEngine]] to help procedurally deliver the city. According to [[Ged Wright]], a Double Negative visual effects supervisor, it was a much more sci-fi based role, "so we took what they had done and extended it a great deal. The work we were doing was based around the Downtowns for New York City, L.A. and Chicago, and that gave us the building volumes for heights. We'd skin those volumes with kit parts, but most of it then had to fall down! So we had to rig it for destruction and use it for other aspects of the work as well."<ref name="FXGuide" />

For the destruction of the buildings, the studio rewrote its own asset system to focus towards its dynamic events. The [[Bullet (software)|Bullet]] physics software was a heavily impacted component for the use of the destruction. Wright said that "we wanted to be able to run an RBD event and trigger all these secondary events, whether it was glass or dust simulations—all of those things needed to be chained up and handled in a procedural way. One of the advantages of this was that, because it was all based around a limited number of input components, you can make sure they're modeled in a way they're usable in effects—you can model something but they'll be another stage to rig it for destruction." Fire, smoke, and water stimulation tools were developed at the Double Negative studio. The studio transitioned between the existing proprietary volume [[Rendering (computer graphics)|rendering]] software to rendering in Mantra for elements such as fireball sims. Double Negative also used the in-house fluids tool "Squirt" to handle larger-scale sims and interaction for more tightly coupled volumes and particles. Regarding the battle between Superman and Zod, Double Negative implemented real photography onto its digital doubles.<ref name="FXGuide" />

== Music ==
{{main|Man of Steel (soundtrack)}}

[[Hans Zimmer]] initially denied popular rumors that he would be composing the [[Film score|film's score]],<ref name="ZimmerRumor" /> but in June 2012, it was confirmed that Zimmer would, in fact, be doing so after all.<ref name="ZimmerConfirm" /> To completely distinguish ''Man of Steel'' from the previous films, the iconic "[[Superman music|Superman March]]" by [[John Williams]] was not used.<ref name="WilliamsMarch" /> Hans Zimmer's soundtrack for ''Man of Steel'' was released publicly on June 11, 2013.<ref name="SoundtrackRelease" /> An unofficial rip of the musical score from the third [[Trailer (promotion)|trailer]], entitled "An Ideal of Hope", confirmed to be a cut-down version of the track "What Are You Going to Do When You Are Not Saving the World?", was released on April 19.<ref name="IdealOfHope" /> In late April, the official track listing of the two-[[CD]] deluxe edition was revealed.<ref name="SoundtrackRelease2" />

==Themes==
Many reviewers interpreted ''Man of Steel'' as a religious [[allegory]], especially since Warner Bros. set up a website that contains "a nine-page pamphlet entitled ''Jesus: The Original Superhero''".<ref name="SupermanJesusGuardian" /><ref name="SupermanJesusCNN" /> Justin Craig compares Kal-El's struggle to the [[Passion of Christ]], stating that "Kal-El is more than willing to sacrifice himself to save the people of Earth. Originally reluctant to reveal his identity and powers to the world, Superman decides to turn himself over to Zod to save humanity from annihilation."<ref name="CraigFox" /> Craig also states that there is an allegory to the [[Trinity]] within ''Man of Steel'': "Jor-El returns to Kal-El on Earth as a ghost, guiding his budding superhero son on his journey to salvation. Before Jor-El sends his son off to Earth baby Moses-style, he tells his wife that, like Jesus, 'He'll be a god to them.'"<ref name="CraigFox" /> Paul Asay of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' writes that "Superman floats in space with his arms splayed out as if nailed to an invisible cross," a fact that Craig also mentioned in his assessment of the film.<ref name="AsayWashingtonPost" /><ref name="CraigFox" /> The protagonist of the film is also 33 years old and seeks "counsel at a church."<ref name="LangYahoo" />

Writing for ''The Huffington Post'', Colin Liotta compared Zod to [[Adolf Hitler]], citing: "He feels his vision for a pure Krypton (i.e. a society like the one Hitler envisioned with his [[Nazi eugenics|eugenics program]]) is the only answer for survival."<ref name="LiottaHuffPost" />
The sequence where a young Clark's powers overwhelm him in grade school, leading to him shutting himself in a closet, has led many to speculate that DC Extended Universe Superman is either [[Autism|autistic]] or meant to represent the struggles of autism.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 16, 2020 |title=What does Superman mean to me as a man on the Autism Spectrum |url=https://medium.com/@adweber1991/what-does-superman-mean-to-me-as-a-man-on-the-autism-spectrum-609a8a9be0d6}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 5, 2018 |title=Does Superman Help Explain the Experience of Autism? |url=https://brainworldmagazine.com/does-superman-help-explain-the-experience-of-autism/}}</ref>

==Marketing==
<!--PER THE GUIDELINES, WE DO NOT SIMPLY ADD TRAILERS THAT ARE RELEASED. PLEASE REVIEW WP:MOSFILM#MARKETING BEFORE YOU ADD ANYTHING. THANK YOU.!-->
Warner Bros. and DC Comics won the rights to the domain name manofsteel.com, in use by a member of the public, for use for the film's official website.<ref name="DomainDispute" /> On November 20, 2012, for the release of ''[[The Dark Knight Rises]]'' [[DVD-Video|DVD]] and [[Blu-ray]], Warner Bros. launched a countdown on the film's website where fans could share the countdown on websites like Facebook or Twitter to unlock an "exclusive reward". On December 3, 2012, the "exclusive reward" was revealed to be an official ''Man of Steel'' [[Teaser campaign|teaser]] poster.<ref name="Countdown" /> The poster, which depicts Superman being arrested, generated a positive response and much speculation about the film's story.<ref name="Poster" /> On December 10, 2012, a website appeared at dsrwproject.com that provided audio signals to be decoded by viewers. It was discovered to be related to the film due to the copyright on the website.<ref name="ViralMashable" /> By December 11, 2012, the decoded message led readers to another website with a countdown that led to the public release of the trailer.<ref name="ViralDigitalSpy" /><ref name="TrailerEW" /> In anticipation of the film, [[Mattel]] unveiled a toy line which includes [[Movie Masters]] action figures. In addition, [[Lego]] released three ''Man of Steel'' sets, inspired by scenes from the film; Rubie's Costume Co. also released a new line of ''Man of Steel''-inspired costumes and accessories for both kids and adults.<ref name="MattelLego" /> The film has reportedly earned over $160{{nbsp}}million from promotional [[tie-in]]s.<ref name="TieInsEarnings" />

[[Viral marketing]] campaigns for the film began when the official website was replaced by "deep space radio waves". The message was decoded to reveal a voice that said "You Are Not Alone". The official site continued to be updated with new static files that slowly revealed the symbol for the film's villain, General Zod. Shortly after, the website was replaced with a "message" from Zod, who requested that Earth must return Kal-El to his custody and told Kal-El to surrender within 24 hours or the world would suffer the consequences.<ref name="ViralComingSoon" /> A viral site called "IWillFindHim.com" was released that showed a countdown to the third trailer for the film.<ref name="ViralComingSoon2" />

Warner Bros. enlisted [[Christianity|Christian]]-based marketing firm Grace Hill Media to help spread the [[Christian values|Christian themes]] of the film to the religious [[demographics]]. Special trailers were created outlining the religious tones, due to Hollywood studios frequently marketing movies to specific religious and cultural groups. Warner Bros. previously marketed films such as ''[[The Blind Side (film)|The Blind Side]]'', ''[[The Notebook]]'', ''[[The Book of Eli]]'' and the ''[[Harry Potter (film series)|Harry Potter]]'' series to faith-based groups.<ref name="LangYahoo" /><ref name="FoxPulpit" /> Warner Bros. also asked Professor [[Craig Detweiler]] of [[Pepperdine University]] to "create a Superman-centric sermon outline for pastors titled ''Jesus: The Original Superhero''."<ref name="LangYahoo" /> Regarding this, Paul Asay of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' wrote that "the religious themes keep coming: Free will. Sacrifice. God-given purpose. ''Man of Steel'' isn't just a movie. It's a Bible study in a cape. The messages are so strong that its marketers been{{sic}} explicitly pushing the film to Christian audiences."<ref name="AsayWashingtonPost" />

==Release==
''Man of Steel'' held a [[red carpet]] premiere at the [[Lincoln Center]]'s [[Alice Tully Hall]] in [[New York City]] on June 10, 2013,<ref name="Premiere" /> which featured the attendance of the principal cast members.<ref name="PremiereCast" /> The film received a [[wide release]] on June 14, 2013.<ref name="3DRelease" /><ref name="IMAXRelease" /> The film was originally slated for release in December 2012, but it was pushed to the June 14, 2013, date to avoid competition with Warner Bros.' other film ''[[The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey]]'', which was released on December 14, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 21, 2011 |title='Superman' movie 'Man of Steel' pushed back to avoid 'Hobbit' clash |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a331081/superman-movie-man-of-steel-pushed-back-to-avoid-hobbit-clash/ |access-date=November 23, 2023 |website=Digital Spy |language=en-GB}}</ref> It was released as a single-disc [[DVD-Video|DVD]] (feature film only), on two-disc DVD with bonus features, and respective [[Blu-ray]] and Blu-ray 3D combo packs on November 12, 2013,<ref name="BluRay" /> and in the United Kingdom on December 2, 2013.<ref name="BluRayUK" /> As of January 2019, ''Man of Steel'' has sold more than 2.3{{nbsp}}million DVDs along with an estimated 3.3{{nbsp}}million Blu-ray Discs totaling $44.4{{nbsp}}million and $76.2{{nbsp}}million, respectively, for a total of $120.7{{nbsp}}million in sales.<ref name="DVDSales" /> The film was later released in [[4K resolution|4K]] [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]] format on July 19, 2016.<ref name="4KRelease" />

==Reception==
===Box office===
''Man of Steel'' grossed $291{{nbsp}}million in the United States and Canada, and $379.1{{nbsp}}million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $670.1{{nbsp}}million,<ref name="BOM" /> making it the highest-grossing solo Superman film of all time and the second-highest when adjusting for inflation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Rose |date=August 2, 2016 |title=The Highest Grossing DC Comics Movies Of All Time (Adjusted For Inflation) |url=https://screenrant.com/highest-grossing-dc-comics-movies-ever-all-time-adjusted-for-inflation/ |access-date=May 19, 2021 |website=[[Screen Rant]]}}</ref> It is also the second-highest-grossing reboot of all time behind ''[[The Amazing Spider-Man (2012 film)|The Amazing Spider-Man]]''. ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' calculated the film's net profit as $42.7{{nbsp}}million, when factoring together all expenses and revenues, making it the ninth most profitable release of 2013.<ref name="Profit" /> The film earned $128.7{{nbsp}}million on its opening weekend, including $17.5{{nbsp}}million from IMAX theaters, making it the biggest of such openings for a standalone ''Superman'' film.<ref name="OpeningBO" /> ''Man of Steel'' earned an additional $120{{nbsp}}million from [[DVD-Video|DVD]] and [[Blu-ray]] sales.<ref name="DVDSales" />

''Man of Steel'' made $12{{nbsp}}million from a Thursday night [[Walmart]] screening program, and an additional $9{{nbsp}}million from midnight shows.<ref name="JuneRecord" /> This marked Warner Bros.' third-highest advance night/midnight opening, and the biggest advance night/midnight debut for a non-sequel.<ref name="ForbesMidnight" /> The film eventually earned $44{{nbsp}}million during its opening Friday (including midnight grosses) and $56.1{{nbsp}}million when the Thursday night showings are included. The opening-day gross was the second-highest for a non-sequel, and the 20th-largest overall.<ref name="BOM" /> Its opening weekend gross of $116.6{{nbsp}}million was the third-highest of 2013, behind ''[[Iron Man 3]]'' ($174.1{{nbsp}}million) and ''[[The Hunger Games: Catching Fire]]'' ($158.1{{nbsp}}million), and the third-highest among non-sequels, behind ''[[The Avengers (2012 film)|Marvel's The Avengers]]'' ($207.4{{nbsp}}million) and ''[[The Hunger Games (film)|The Hunger Games]]'' ($152.5{{nbsp}}million). It also broke ''[[Toy Story 3]]''{{'}}s record ($110.3{{nbsp}}million) for the highest weekend debut in June (the record was again broken two years later by ''[[Jurassic World]]''{{'}}s opening gross of $208.8{{nbsp}}million).<ref name="JuneRecord2" /><ref name="JurassicWorld" /> However, on its second weekend, ''Man of Steel''{{'}}s box office fell almost 65%–68% if the Thursday night gross is included—putting it in third place, behind ''[[Monsters University]]'' and ''[[World War Z (film)|World War Z]]''. [[Box Office Mojo]] called it an "abnormally large drop," close to the second-weekend decline for ''[[Green Lantern (film)|Green Lantern]]''.<ref name="2ndWkndDrop" />

''Man of Steel'' earned $73.3{{nbsp}}million on its opening weekend from 24 countries, which includes $4.2{{nbsp}}million from 79 IMAX theaters, setting a June opening-weekend record for IMAX.<ref name="OpeningBO" /> The film set an opening-day record in the [[Philippines]] with $1.66{{nbsp}}million.<ref name="OpeningBO" /> In the United Kingdom, Ireland and Malta, the film earned $5.6{{nbsp}}million on its opening day and £11.2{{nbsp}}million ($17.47{{nbsp}}million) on its opening weekend.<ref name="DeadlineOpening" /><ref name="UKBO" /> Its biggest opener outside the United States was in China, with $25.9{{nbsp}}million in four days (Thursday to Sunday).<ref name="ChinaBO" /> In total earnings, its three largest countries after North America are China ($63.4{{nbsp}}million), the United Kingdom, Ireland and Malta ($46.2{{nbsp}}million) and Australia ($22.3{{nbsp}}million).<ref name="InternationalBOM" />

===Critical response===
On review aggregator [[Rotten Tomatoes]] the film has an approval rating of 56% based on {{RT data|count}} reviews and an average rating of {{RT data|average}}. The site's consensus reads, "''Man of Steel''{{'}}s exhilarating action and spectacle can't fully overcome its detours into generic blockbuster territory."<ref name="RottenTomatoes" /> On [[Metacritic]], the film received a weighted score of 55 out of 100 based on 47 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic" /> Audience polls in North America from [[CinemaScore]] for the film tallied an average grade of an "A−" on an A+ to F scale, with those under the age of 18 and older than 50 giving it an "A".<ref name="DeadlineOpening" />

[[Richard Roeper]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' said that ''Man of Steel'' covered no new ground with regard to Superman films, and instead, "we're plunged back into a mostly-underwhelming film, with underdeveloped characters and supercharged-fight scenes that drag on and offer nothing new in the way of special-effects creativity".<ref name="AspenTimesReview" /> ''[[The Boston Globe]]''{{'}}s [[Ty Burr]] wrote, "What's missing from this Superman saga is a sense of lightness, of pop joy".<ref name="BostonGlobeReview" /> ''[[The Washington Post]]''{{'}}s [[Ann Hornaday]] stated that with "Hans Zimmer's turgid, over-produced score", the film "is an exceptionally unpleasant viewing experience".<ref name="WashingtonPostReview" /> For ''[[The Denver Post]]''{{'}}s Lisa Kennedy, the chief problem with ''Man of Steel'' is the "rhythm and balance in the storytelling and directing" which resulted in a film that swings "between destructive overstatement and flat-footed homilies."<ref name="DenverPostReview" />

Kofi Outlaw, Editor-in-Chief at ''[[Screen Rant]]'', gave ''Man of Steel'' a 4-out-of-5-star review, stating that "''Man of Steel'' has more than earned its keep, and deserves to be THE iconic Superman movie for a whole new generation".<ref name="ScreenRantReview" /> He would go on to name ''Man of Steel'' the best superhero movie of 2013.<ref name="ScreenRantBest" /> Jim Vejvoda of ''[[IGN]]'' gave ''Man of Steel'' a 9 out of 10 while praising the action sequences and the performances of Kevin Costner, Russell Crowe and Michael Shannon.<ref name="IGNReview" /> The performance of Antje Traue as Superman's adversary Faora-Ul, particularly in the Smallville battle scenes, has also been lauded.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ali |first=Azhan |date=May 18, 2018 |title=9 DC Extended Universe Moments That Blew Our Minds! |url=https://www.animatedtimes.com/top-9-dc-extended-universe-moments/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180705033042/https://www.animatedtimes.com/top-9-dc-extended-universe-moments/ |archive-date=July 5, 2018 |access-date=July 4, 2018 |website=Animated Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2013 |title=Ten moments that mattered: Antje Traue as Faora in Man of Steel |url=https://www.dccomics.com/blog/2013/12/23/ten-moments-that-mattered-faora-in-man-of-steel |access-date=July 10, 2018 |website=dccomics.com}}</ref> [[Peter Travers]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' gave it 3 stars out of 4, saying, "Caught in the slipstream between action and angst, ''Man of Steel'' is a bumpy ride for sure. But there's no way to stay blind to its wonders."<ref name="RollingStoneReview" /> [[Todd McCarthy]] of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' said rebooting the franchise was unnecessary, but that the film was confident enough and Snyder's attention to detail careful enough that audiences could overlook another reboot.<ref name="THRReview" /> ''[[PopMatters]]'' journalist J.C. Maçek III, wrote, "The path of this flawed savior isn't quite the one that we have been led to expect and many fans will love that and many fans will decry its comic book-divergent choices. On the other hand, barring Lois Lane's own knowledge of the dual nature of Clark and Superman (thus depriving one of fiction's greatest reveals), the hero we see in the final moments of ''Man of Steel'' is nothing if not the character Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster created ... with just a bit more in the 'imperfections' column."<ref name="PopMattersReview" /> Steve Persall of the ''[[Tampa Bay Times]]'' stated that, "''Man of Steel'' is more than just ''Avengers''-sized [[escapism]]; it's an artistic introduction to a movie superhero we only thought we knew."<ref name="TampaBayReview" /> ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine's [[Richard Corliss]] said, "The movie finds its true, lofty footing not when it displays Kal-El's extraordinary powers, but when it dramatizes Clark Kent's roiling humanity. The super part of ''Man of Steel'' is just okay, but the man part is super."<ref name="TimeReview" /> In a review on [[Roger Ebert]]'s website, [[Matt Zoller Seitz]] awarded the film three out of four stars, calling it an "astonishing movie" and praising the conflict between Clark and Zod. But he criticized the film for not having more personal and intimate moments between Clark and Lois.<ref name="EbertReview" /> In 2014, ''[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]'' ranked ''Man of Steel'' the 286th-greatest film ever made on their list of "The 301 Greatest Movies Of All Time" as voted by the magazine's readers.<ref name="EmpireRank" />

Speaking to [[Fox Business Channel]], [[Grae Drake]], senior editor of Rotten Tomatoes, expressed dismay over the critical reception, stating, "As much as I love and respect our critics at Rotten Tomatoes, I've got to say I am shocked. Listen, the movie's not perfect but ... I just cannot fathom it. It was a good movie, you guys."<ref name="GraeDrake" />

Reaction to the film among comics creators was mixed.<ref name="ComicsDivideMTV" /> Those who enjoyed it include [[Jeff Parker (comics)|Jeff Parker]], [[Heidi MacDonald]], [[Ethan Van Sciver]], [[Christos Gage]] and former Superman writer [[Dan Jurgens]]. Among its detractors were [[Joe Keatinge]], [[Sean McKeever]], Gabriel Hardman and [[Mark Waid]]. MacDonald praised the film's action, drama and leads Henry Cavill and Amy Adams. Van Sciver singled out Cavill in particular for praise. Gage called it the best ''Superman'' film since 1980's ''[[Superman II]]''. Hardman said that he liked a lot of the mechanics but did not connect with the characters, which robbed the story of tension. Waid, who wrote the origin miniseries ''[[Superman: Birthright]]'', criticized the film for its overall "joyless" tone, and for Superman's decision to kill Zod,<ref name="ComicsDivideMTV" /><ref name="WaidReview" /> a criticism echoed by other creators. Writer [[Grant Morrison]], who wrote the critically acclaimed miniseries ''[[All-Star Superman]]'', expressed mixed reaction to the film, saying that while they "kinda liked it and kinda didn't", it did not present anything new, as they would have preferred a "second act" type story with Lex Luthor instead of re-establishing the character by presenting information Morrison is already familiar with. Morrison also questioned the need for a superhero to kill,<ref name="MorrisonUSAToday" /> as did artist [[Neal Adams]]. Adams suggested that other alternatives were open to Superman when Zod threatened innocent people with his heat vision, such as covering his eyes. He also criticized Superman for not moving the battle away from [[Metropolis (comics)|Metropolis]] as the character did at the end of ''Superman II''.<ref name="AdamsCBN" /> [[Jim Lee]] had a positive opinion: "It's epic. It's got a lot of heart, but one of the things that was kind of missing from the last Superman movie I think was the action, and this movie has it in spades. I mean it is a visual thrill ride. It is amazing. You get to see all the powers of Superman, and in all its glory, and I think people are going to be blown away."<ref name="JimLeeComicBook" />

==Future==
===DC Extended Universe===
{{main|DC Extended Universe}}

Warner Bros. began planning a cinematic universe featuring other DC Comics characters following the release of ''Man of Steel''. In June 2013, Goyer was hired to write the film's sequel, along with the script for ''[[Justice League (film)|Justice League]]''.<ref name="GoyerSequel" /> [[Zack Snyder]] revealed at [[San Diego Comic-Con]] the following month that Superman and [[Batman]] would appear in the sequel to ''Man of Steel'', with Cavill, Adams, Lane and Fishburne set to reprise their roles.<ref name="SnyderBatmanTHR" /><ref name="LATimesCC2013" /><ref name="DarkKnightReturns" /> The film's title, ''[[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice]]'', was revealed in May 2014,<ref name="DawnOfJustice" /> and it was theatrically released on March 25, 2016.<ref name="BvSrelease" />

===Cancelled sequel===
{{Further|Superman in film#Man of Steel sequel}}
A full slate of upcoming DC Comics-based films was announced by Warner Bros. Pictures in October 2014. The company also confirmed that a Superman film was in development, with Henry Cavill set to reprise his lead role.<ref name="Oct2014Slate" /> Zack Snyder contemplated the inclusion of [[Brainiac]], the [[Kryptonian]]s, and even [[Metallo]] as possible antagonists for the sequel, but they were ultimately scrapped by April 2013 in favor of a plot with Batman as the antagonist. The film, ''[[Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice]]'', was released in 2016.<ref name="SnyderMoS22021" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jagernauth |first=Kevin |date=July 6, 2015 |title=Metallo Would've Been The 'Man Of Steel 2' Villain |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2015/07/metallo-wouldve-been-the-man-of-steel-2-villain-262309/ |access-date=March 4, 2023 |website=IndieWire |language=en |archive-date=March 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304055916/https://www.indiewire.com/2015/07/metallo-wouldve-been-the-man-of-steel-2-villain-262309/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=987930376965210113 |user=jayoliva1 |title=Okay school is in session... Back in April 2013 (before MoS released in June) I was tasked with doing the Superman 75 short. I met with Zack who was the exec producer on it and he showed me storyboards of BvS with Batman already in it. AND it was a Batman from DKR. |author=Jay Oliva |date=April 22, 2018 |access-date=March 4, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hughes |first=Mark |title=Exclusive Interview With Zack Snyder, Director Of 'Batman Vs. Superman' |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/markhughes/2014/04/17/exclusive-interview-with-zack-snyder-director-of-batman-vs-superman/ |access-date=March 4, 2023 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2016, ''[[TheWrap]]'' reported that a sequel to ''Man of Steel'' had entered active development.<ref name="SequelDevelopment" /> Cavill's manager, [[Dany Garcia]], confirmed that the actor would be involved.<ref name="GarciaSep2016" /> The screenplay was still being developed that November according to Amy Adams.<ref name="AdamsNov2016" /> [[Matthew Vaughn]] was Warner Bros.' top choice to direct the film as of March 2017.<ref name="VaughnMar2017" /> Vaughn previously [[Pitch (filmmaking)|pitched]] an idea for a new Superman trilogy with comic book writer [[Mark Millar]] prior to the development of ''Man of Steel'', in which the destruction of [[Krypton (comics)|Krypton]] would take place after Superman had already grown-up on the planet.<ref name="VaughnMay2019" /> The [[Production of Justice League (film)|troubled production]] and lackluster box office earnings of ''[[Justice League (film)|Justice League]]'' (2017) led to a shake-up at Warner Bros., as the studio chose to rethink its approach to future DC projects.<ref name="VarietyDec2017" /> By late 2017, the script for a ''Man of Steel'' sequel was still incomplete according to ''Justice League'' producer [[Charles Roven]].<ref name="CastChangesNov2017AP" />

In July 2018, prior to the release of ''[[Mission: Impossible – Fallout]]'', director [[Christopher McQuarrie]] and co-star Cavill pitched their take on a new Superman film, but Warner Bros. did not pursue the idea.<ref name="McQuarriePitch" /> [[James Gunn]] was approached later that year to write and direct a Superman film, but he chose instead to move forward with ''[[The Suicide Squad (film)|The Suicide Squad]]'' (2021).<ref name="DoGGunnApr2021" /><ref name="GunnSupermanOffer" /> Following contract issues with Cavill's scheduled cameo appearance in ''[[Shazam! (film)|Shazam!]]'' (2019), as well as scheduling conflicts with his ''Fallout'' commitment,<ref name="CavillSep2018" /><ref name="CavillNov2019" /> it was reported that the actor may be parting ways with the studio.<ref name="CavillSep2018" /> In November 2019, however, Cavill maintained that he still had interest in reprising his role.<ref name="CavillNov2019" /> Warner Bros. remained unsure of the direction the character was heading and was in contact with "high-profile talent", including [[J. J. Abrams]] and [[Michael B. Jordan]], with the latter pitching a Black version of the character.<ref name="VarietyNov2019" /> Development on a ''Man of Steel'' sequel was abandoned by May 2020,<ref name="CavillMay2020Deadline" /> though Cavill remained in talks to appear in a future DC film.<ref name="CavillMay2020Variety" />

===Reboot===
{{main|Superman (2025 film){{!}}''Superman'' (2025 film)}}

Warner Bros. revealed in October 2022 that a sequel to ''Man of Steel'' was being revisited, with Roven serving as a producer and Cavill reprising his role. The studio was still searching for writers, and McQuarrie was still on a list of possible directors.<ref name="RovenCavillSequelOct2022" /> Cavill then appeared in the [[post-credits scene]] of the DCEU film ''[[Black Adam (film)|Black Adam]]'' (2022), and the potential for his return in future projects became more favorable.<ref name="CavillOneOff" /><ref name="BehindCavillFall" /> Shortly after, Cavill's return as Superman in a future film was officially confirmed.<ref name="BehindCavillFall" /><ref name="CavillReturn" /> [[Steven Knight]] had written a script treatment around that time,<ref name="KnightDevelopmentStall" /> which reportedly included Brainiac as the antagonist.<ref name="BehindCavillFall" /> However, there was a lack of interest in the script by Warner Bros. executives.<ref name="KnightDevelopmentStall" /> The following month, ''TheWrap'' reported that newly-appointed co-chairmen and co-CEOs of [[DC Studios]] James Gunn and [[Peter Safran]] were developing new plans for the DC Universe.<ref name="TheWrapSetbacks" /><ref name="THRDec2022" /><ref name="KnightDevelopmentStall" /> Gunn later revealed in December 2022 that the next Superman film would not include Cavill and would instead focus on a younger Superman.<ref name="GunnWriterTHR" /> In early 2023, James Gunn provided details about ''[[Superman (2025 film)|Superman: Legacy]]'', which will be the cornerstone of his new DC Universe. The film, released on July 11, 2025, is not an origin story for the character. Gunn emphasized that the movie would focus on Superman balancing his Kryptonian heritage with his human upbringing, portraying him as the embodiment of "truth, justice, and the American way" in a world that sometimes sees kindness as outdated. Gunn described Superman as a symbol of hope, embodying optimism and compassion in contrast to the darker tones that have sometimes defined superhero films.<ref name="DCSlate" /> Cavill's cameo in ''Black Adam'' was his final appearance as Superman.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Jodee |date=2024-04-17 |title=Henry Cavill Pokes Fun at Short-Lived Superman Return in Black Adam |url=https://www.cbr.com/henry-cavill-short-lived-superman-return-black-adam/ |access-date=2025-05-13 |website=CBR |language=en}}</ref> Gunn later clarified he had never intended to cast Cavill in his new film and referred to the previous one-off cameo, that came to before he and Safran took over DC Studios, as "the end of his story".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gonzalez |first=Umberto |date=2023-01-31 |title=Henry Cavill Was 'Dicked Around by a Lot of People,' James Gunn Says of Superman Actor's DC Limbo |url=https://www.thewrap.com/henry-cavill-james-gunn-comments-superman/ |access-date=2026-01-03 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2025, in an interview promoting ''[[Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning]]'', McQuarrie, who had previously partnered with Cavill to pitch a sequel to ''Man of Steel'' in July 2018,<ref name="McQuarriePitch" /> revealed brief details of his script and take on the movie. He hailed it as a good script and an excellent story that Warner Bros rejected. Despite this, he revealed the door was still open for projects that didn't come to fruition and that he was open to reuniting with Cavill to pitch the movie again if the opportunity was presented in the future.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valenzuela |first=Ernesto |date=2025-05-27 |title='Mission: Impossible' Director Reveals Details of Planned 'Man of Steel 2' With Henry Cavill |url=https://movieweb.com/christopher-mcquarrie-man-of-steel-2-sequel-henry-cavill/ |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=MovieWeb |language=en}}</ref>

======================================================================

{{short description|1929 Soviet silent documentary film}}
{{Other uses}}
{{distinguish|Man with a Camera {{!}} ''Man with a Camera''}}
