supporting roles in ''True Detective''{{'s}} first season include [[Kevin Dunn]] as Major Ken Quesada, Alexandra Daddario as Lisa Tragnetti, and Brad Carter as Charlie Lange.<ref name=td2 />

Pizzolatto narrowed his search for a suitable director to [[Cary Joji Fukunaga]], whom he knew from Anonymous Content, and [[Alejandro González Iñárritu]]. Fukunaga was formally appointed as director after Iñárritu pulled out of the project due to film commitments.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/ct-true-detective-pizzolatto-borrelli-20140122-column.html#page=1 |title=True voice brings 'True Detective' to life |last=Borrelli |first=Christopher |date=January 22, 2014 |website=[[Chicago Tribune]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105134635/http://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/ct-true-detective-pizzolatto-borrelli-20140122-column.html |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref><ref name="beast2">{{Cite web |url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2014/02/26/true-detective-director-cary-fukunaga-s-journey-from-pro-snowboarder-to-hollywood-s-most-wanted.html |title=True Detective Director Cary Fukunaga's Journey from Pro Snowboarder to Hollywood's Most Wanted |last=Stern |first=Marlow |date=February 26, 2014 |website=The Daily Beast  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105135043/http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2014/02/26/true-detective-director-cary-fukunaga-s-journey-from-pro-snowboarder-to-hollywood-s-most-wanted.html |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> In preparation for his work on the series, Fukunaga spent time with a homicide detective of the [[Louisiana State Police]]'s Criminal Investigations Division to develop an accurate depiction of a 1990s homicide detective's work.<ref name="interviewmag">{{Cite web |url=http://www.interviewmagazine.com/culture/cary-fukunaga-true-detective/#_ |title=True Director |last=Brown |first=Emma |website=[[Interview (magazine)|Interview]]  |date=January 9, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105135421/http://www.interviewmagazine.com/culture/cary-fukunaga-true-detective/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Fukunaga recruited [[Adam Arkapaw]], director of photography of ''[[Top of the Lake]]'', as project cinematographer. Arkapaw came to the director's attention for his work in ''[[Animal Kingdom (film)|Animal Kingdom]]'' (2010) and ''[[Snowtown (film)|Snowtown]]'' (2011), and was hired after the two negotiated a deal at a meeting in [[San Francisco]].<ref name="kodak">{{Cite web |url=http://motion.kodak.com/motion/Publications/InCamera/HBO_s_True_Detective_Elevates_the_Television_Drama.htm |title=HBO's True Detective Elevates the Television Drama |date=November 20, 2013 |website=InCamera |publisher=[[Kodak]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105140408/http://motion.kodak.com/motion/Publications/InCamera/HBO_s_True_Detective_Elevates_the_Television_Drama.htm |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Alex DiGerlando, whom Fukunaga had worked with on [[Benh Zeitlin]]{{'s}} ''Glory at Sea'' in 2008, was appointed as the production designer. Fukunaga said in an interview, "I knew what Alex accomplished in the swamps of Louisiana and given some money, how much more amazing he could be in building sets that would just be used for one or two days and be abandoned again."<ref name="fc">{{Cite web|last=Hart|first=Hugh|date=January 6, 2014|title=Director Cary Fukunaga on Conjuring the Louisiana Noir of 'True Detective'|url=http://www.fastcocreate.com/3024587/director-cary-fukunaga-on-conjuring-the-louisiana-noir-of-true-detective|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105190013/http://www.fastcocreate.com/3024587/director-cary-fukunaga-on-conjuring-the-louisiana-noir-of-true-detective|archive-date=November 5, 2015|website=[[Fast Company (magazine)|Fast Company]]}}</ref>

=== Filming ===
[[File:Fort Macomb 2016.jpg|thumb|alt=Shot of the defensive wall ruins of a nineteenth-century brick fort|Ruins of Fort Macomb (pictured in 2016), one of the filming locations in ''True Detective'' season one.]]

HBO chose to film in [[Louisiana]] over Pizzolatto's original preference for [[Arkansas]], as the state offered [[Film industry in Louisiana|transferrable tax credits]] to subsidize the cost of production for all eligible shoots.<ref name=cenlam>{{Cite web |url=http://cenlamar.com/2014/01/16/exclusive-nic-pizzolattos-louisiana/ |title=Exclusive: Nic Pizzolatto's Louisiana | last=White | first=Lamar Jr. |date=January 16, 2014 |publisher=CenLamar |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105181855/http://cenlamar.com/2014/01/16/exclusive-nic-pizzolattos-louisiana/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Pizzolatto was also compelled by the industrial setting as a storytelling device: "There's a contradictory nature to the place and a sort of sinister quality underneath it all&nbsp;...&nbsp;everything lives under layers of concealment. The woods are thick and dark and impenetrable. On the other hand you have the beauty of it all from a distance."<ref name=lamag /><ref name=cenlam/>

Principal photography took three months (between 100 and 110 days), from January to June 2013, with approximately five minutes of film shot per day.<ref name="kodak" /><ref name="fc" /> Production staff constructed various set pieces, among them a scorched chapel, Joel Theriot's [[tent revival]], and the Louisiana State Criminal Investigations Division offices, the last of which they built inside an abandoned light bulb warehouse near [[Elmwood, Louisiana|Elmwood]].<ref name="art" /> For the Dora Lange crime scene, the crew filmed exterior shots at a remote sugarcane field which, because it was partially burned, inspired what DiGerlando called a "moody and atmospheric" backdrop for the corresponding interior scenes.<ref name="art">{{Cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/03/true-detective-alex-digerlando-set-design-props-interview.html |title=Devil's Nests and Beer-Can Men: The Origins of 13 True Detective Set Pieces |last=Martin |first=Denise |date=March 6, 2014 |website=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105190544/http://www.vulture.com/2014/03/true-detective-alex-digerlando-set-design-props-interview.html |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref>

The scene in which Cohle, taking Ginger hostage, escapes a housing complex amidst gunfire, was captured in [[Bridge City, Louisiana|Bridge City]] as a single six-minute [[tracking shot]], a technique Fukunaga had employed in ''[[Sin Nombre (2009 film)|Sin Nombre]]'' (2009) and ''[[Jane Eyre (2011 film)|Jane Eyre]]'' (2011).<ref name="Mtv" /><ref name="arch">{{Cite web |url=http://www.archdaily.com/493920/interiors-true-detective |title=Interiors: True Detective |last1=Ahi |first1=Mehruss |last2=Karaoghlanian |first2=Armen |date=April 8, 2014 |publisher=[[ArchDaily]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925032321/http://www.archdaily.com/493920/interiors-true-detective |archive-date=September 25, 2016}}</ref> Shot in seven takes, preparation for the scene was extensive and demanding: McConaughey trained with Mark Norby to master a fighting style for his character,<ref name="Mtv">{{Cite web |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1722001/true-detective-long-take/ |title='True Detective': How did they pull off that final shot? |last=Sullivan |first=Kevin |date=February 7, 2014 |publisher=[[MTV News]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925031516/http://www.mtv.com/news/1722001/true-detective-long-take/ |archive-date=September 25, 2016}}</ref> and the nature of the shoot required a team of stunt coordinators, make-up artists, and special effects crew on hand during its entire course.<ref name="arch" /> Elsewhere, shooting took place at an unoccupied high school campus in [[Kenner, Louisiana|Kenner]] and nineteenth-century [[Fort Macomb]], located outside [[New Orleans]].<ref name="art" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/03/true-detective-finale-production-designer-fort-maze.html |title=True Detective's Production Designer on the Fort |last=Martin |first=Denise |date=March 10, 2014 |website=New York  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105190839/http://www.vulture.com/2014/03/true-detective-finale-production-designer-fort-maze.html |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Former [[Louisiana State Police]] Detective Tim Hanks served as technical advisor for the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/08/emmys-tim-hanks-kept-true-detective-police-work-honest-816990/ |title=EMMYS: Tim Hanks Kept 'True Detective' Police Work Honest |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=August 8, 2014 |access-date=August 8, 2014}}</ref>

''True Detective'' season one was shot on [[35mm movie film|35 mm film]],<ref name="td">{{Cite AV media |title="Making True Detective" featurette |last=[[Cary Joji Fukunaga]] (director) |publisher=[[HBO]] |year=2014 |time=7:51–7:53 |medium=[[Blu-ray]]}}</ref> which the production staff chose to achieve an authentic "nostalgic" quality.<ref name="kodak" /> The season was filmed using a [[Panavision]] Millennium XL2 camera, and the choice of lens corresponded to the period when a scene took place. Scenes set in 1995 and 2002 were captured with Panavision PVintage lenses, which produced a softer image because they were made of recycled, low-contrast glass. As these scenes were written as a reflection of Cohle and Hart's memory, production sought to make them as cinematic as possible, to reflect what Arkapaw called "the fragmentation of their lucid imaginations back through their past."<ref name="kodak" /> To achieve this, they relied on wider lenses to exaggerate composition.<ref name="kodak" /> The 2012 scenes were shot with Panavision Primo lenses: the visual palette in comparison was sharper and had much more contrast, lending a "modern, crisp feeling" to the images, and, according to Arkapaw, pulling "characters out from their environments to hopefully help audiences get inside their heads".<ref name="kodak" />

=== Art design ===
[[File:TrueDetectivedigitaldouble.jpg|thumb|left|The design team used an assortment of low poly meshes to develop a 3D landscape for the show's title sequence, which were later meticulously superimposed. Digital doubles (such as this one of Hart shown in the upper left frame) were created in some cases to allow more texture.<ref name=aott />|alt=Collage of True Detective's title sequence in intermediate stages, used to illustrate the process of superimposition.]]

Joshua Walsh was responsible for creating ''True Detective''{{'s}} artwork. His work for the show consists of over 100 individual "devil's nests"—twig figurines created by the killer—along with wall paintings and miniature sculptures of men made of beer cans, among others.<ref name=art /> According to DiGerlando, Walsh's interests in hunting and taxidermy made him "the perfect dude for the job".<ref name=art /> A blueprint for the devil's nests was not well established in the script, other than specifications that the structures be able to stand on their own and feature a spiral motif. DiGerlando and Walsh went with a tripod design that showed a spiral when viewed from the base and contained ladder-like crossing elements that symbolized the killer's desire to ascend to a dark [[Plane (esotericism)|spiritual plane]]. Each design had subtle differences from one another.<ref name=art /> DiGerlando cited [[Vodun art|voodoo art]] and the work of [[Henry Darger]] and [[James Charles Castle]] as strong stylistic influences and sought a primitive look for the figurines, one that revealed the workings of a man with "some deep inner urge to express himself".<ref name=art /> To reflect this, Walsh built devil's nests using mud, secondhand children's clothing, reeds, roots, and other materials he felt the killer would use.<ref name=art />

The season's title sequence was a collaboration between director Patrick Clair, his [[Santa Monica]]-based studio Elastic, his [[Sydney]]-based studio Antibody, and [[Brisbane]]-based company Breeder.<ref name="aott">{{Cite web |url=http://www.artofthetitle.com/title/true-detective/ |title=True Detective (2014) |last=Perkins |first=Will |date=January 14, 2014 |publisher=[[Art of the Title]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105191607/http://www.artofthetitle.com/title/true-detective/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref><ref name="fc2">{{Cite web |url=http://www.fastcodesign.com/3027343/a-behind-the-scenes-look-at-the-chilling-the-opening-credits-of-true-detective |title=A Behind-The-Scenes Look at the Chilling Opening Credits Of 'True Detective' |last=Rhodes |first=Margaret |date=March 7, 2014 |website=Fast Company  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105214628/http://www.fastcodesign.com/3027343/a-behind-the-scenes-look-at-the-chilling-the-opening-credits-of-true-detective |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> The design team emphasized southern Louisiana's industrial landscape because it reflected the characters' traits and moral struggles. Clair stated that from the start he had an "unusually clear" vision of ''True Detective''{{'s}} finished opening sequence.<ref name=aott /> Using [[Richard Misrach]]'s photography book ''Petrochemical America'' (2012) as a template, the production team initially photographed the local scenery, and the resulting images were woven together to form the core of the title sequence.<ref name=fc2 /> By the time production began animating, they faced several problems: the photographic stills were too grainy and the footage was too jagged. As a result, many shots were digitally altered and slowed to about a tenth of their original speed, which, according to Clair, "evoked a surreal and floaty mood that perfectly captured what we were after."<ref name=aott />

Creation of a [[3D computer graphics|3D]] effect required the design team to use an assortment of [[low poly|low-poly meshes]], or 3D geometric models.<ref name=aott /> Using a variety of animation and special effects techniques, these images were later [[superimposed]] "with painstaking care" to avoid a sterile, digitized look.<ref name=fc2 /> Clair said, "The most crucial thing to me was that this didn't feel digital, so we went to great lengths to incorporate as much organic imagery as possible."<ref name=fc2 /> For some stills, the design team created [[digital double]]s to develop more texture. The sequence's final cut was polished using optical glitching and [[motion blur|motion distortion]] techniques.<ref name=aott /> ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]'' included the opening sequence in a list of ten of the best title sequences on television.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/tv-and-radio/how-patrick-clair-won-the-emmy-for-90-seconds-of-true-detective-20140818-104xuz.html |title=How Patrick Clair won the Emmy for 90 seconds of True Detective |last=Kalina |first=Paul |date=August 22, 2014 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105215333/http://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/tv-and-radio/how-patrick-clair-won-the-emmy-for-90-seconds-of-true-detective-20140818-104xuz.html |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref>

=== Music ===

Season one's opening theme is "Far from Any Road", an [[alternative country]] song originally composed by [[The Handsome Family]] for their 2003 album ''[[Singing Bones]]''.<ref name=fc2 /> The ''True Detective'' soundtrack features a compilation of [[gospel music|gospel]] and [[blues]] music, which were selected by Pizzolatto and [[T Bone Burnett]]. The pair opposed the use of [[Cajun music]] and [[swamp blues]] for the season's musical score because they felt it was overdone.<ref name=mj /> Burnett said the score was intended to be character-driven, rather than inspired by other crime fiction drama.<ref name="mj">{{Cite web |url=https://www.motherjones.com/mixed-media/2014/01/t-bone-burnett-true-detective-hbo-music-songs |title=T Bone Burnett on How He Chooses Music for True Detective |last=Suebsaeng |first=Asawin |date=January 24, 2014 |website=[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]] |publisher=Foundation For National Progress |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105220121/https://www.motherjones.com/mixed-media/2014/01/t-bone-burnett-true-detective-hbo-music-songs |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Songs by [[Bo Diddley]], [[Melvins]], [[Primus (band)|Primus]], [[The Staple Singers]], [[Grinderman]], [[Wu-Tang Clan]], [[Vashti Bunyan]], [[Townes Van Zandt]], [[Juice Newton]], and [[Captain Beefheart]] appear in season one.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a27608/true-detective-kurt-vonnegut/ |title=True Detective's Mystifying Kurt Vonnegut Connection |last=O'Neil |first=Luke |date=March 4, 2014 |website=Esquire |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105215854/http://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a27608/true-detective-kurt-vonnegut/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.mic.com/articles/82485/the-secret-sauce-of-true-detective-is-its-awesome-soundtrack |title=The Secret Sauce of 'True Detective' is its Awesome Soundtrack |last=Cills |first=Hazel |date=February 17, 2014 |website=[[Mic (media company)|Mic]] |url-status=live composed original pieces with [[Rhiannon Giddens]], who used a [[Swarmatron]] synthesizer, and [[Cassandra Wilson]].<ref name="mj" /> HBO released an abridged soundtrack album, featuring 14 tracks from ''True Detective''{{'s}} first two seasons, on August 14, 2015, through physical media and [[iTunes]].<ref>{{Cite web == Themes and analysis ==

=== Philosophical pessimism and influences ===
[[File:Robert William Chambers.jpg|alt=A publicity portrait of Chambers, circa 1903|thumb|upright|Pizzolatto used Robert W. Chambers' (pictured) ''[[The King in Yellow]]'' as the backbone for much of the season's story.]]

Critics have offered many readings of the influence of [[weird fiction|weird]] and [[horror fiction]] on ''True Detective''{{'s}} narrative, often examining the influence of [[Robert W. Chambers]]' short story collection ''[[The King in Yellow]]'' (1895) and [[Thomas Ligotti]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2014/02/02/writer-nic-pizzolatto-on-thomas-ligotti-and-the-weird-secrets-of-true-detective/ |title=Writer Nic Pizzolatto on Thomas Ligotti and the Weird Secrets of 'True Detective' |last=Calia |first=Michael |date=February 2, 2014 |website=The Wall Street Journal |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105224449/https://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2014/02/02/writer-nic-pizzolatto-on-thomas-ligotti-and-the-weird-secrets-of-true-detective/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Allusions to ''The King in Yellow'' can be observed in the show's dark philosophy,<ref name="wsj2">{{Cite web |url=https://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2014/01/30/the-most-shocking-thing-about-hbos-true-detective/ |title=The Most Shocking Thing About HBO's 'True Detective' |last=Calia |first=Michael |date=January 30, 2014 |website=The Wall Street Journal |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105235314/https://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2014/01/30/the-most-shocking-thing-about-hbos-true-detective/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> its recurring use of "[[Carcosa]]" and "The Yellow King" as [[motif (narrative)|motifs]] throughout the series, and its symbolic use of yellow as a thematic signature that signifies insanity and decadence.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://io9.com/the-one-literary-reference-you-must-know-to-appreciate-1523076497 |title=The One Literary Reference You Must Know to Appreciate ''True Detective'' |last=Hughes |first=Michael M. |date=February 14, 2014 |publisher=[[io9]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105225049/http://io9.com/the-one-literary-reference-you-must-know-to-appreciate-1523076497 |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Pizzolatto was accused of plagiarizing Ligotti because of close similarities between lines in ''True Detective'' and text from Ligotti's nonfiction book ''[[The Conspiracy Against the Human Race]]'' (2010)—accusations Pizzolatto denied, while acknowledging Ligotti's influence.<ref name="cnn">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2014/08/08/showbiz/tv/true-detective-pizzolatto-plagiarism/ |title='True Detective' writer accused of plagiarism |last=Leopoldo |first=Todd |date=August 8, 2014 |publisher=[[CNN]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160513043118/http://www.cnn.com/2014/08/08/showbiz/tv/true-detective-pizzolatto-plagiarism/ |archive-date=May 13, 2016}}</ref>

Other philosophers and writers identified as influences include [[Arthur Schopenhauer]],<ref name=wsj2 /> [[Friedrich Nietzsche]],<ref name=cnn /> [[Gilles Deleuze]],<ref name="budd" /> [[Ray Brassier]], [[Emil Cioran]], and [[Eugene Thacker]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/lincolnmichel/a-true-detective-reading-list |title=A 'True Detective' Reading List |last=Michel |first=Lincoln |date=February 18, 2014 |publisher=[[BuzzFeed]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105235603/http://www.buzzfeed.com/lincolnmichel/a-true-detective-reading-list |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Mathijs Peters, in a piece for ''[[Film International]]'', argued that ''True Detective'' probes Schopenhauerian philosophy through its approach to individuality, self-denial, and the battle between dark and light.<ref name="Filmint">{{Cite web |url=http://filmint.nu/?p=14036 |title='A Giant Gutter in Outer Space': On the Schopenhauerian Themes of HBO's hit series True Detective |last=Peters |first=Mathijs |date=2014 |website=[[Film International]] |publisher=Intellect Ltd. |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925003024/http://filmint.nu/?p=14036 |archive-date=September 25, 2016}}</ref> Ben Woodard noted the show's evolving philosophy, which examines a setting where culture, religion and society are the consequences of biological weakness. Woodward wrote, "Biological programming gets recuperated and socially redistributed visions, faiths, and acerbic personalities take the reins of uncertain ends creating a world where 'people go away'."<ref name="Shipley110">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=110}}</ref> Even the setting, Fintan Neylan argued, emphasizes a world "where the decrepitude of human ordering cannot be hidden".<ref name="Shipley81">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=81}}</ref> "This is not a place where hope fled; it is a place where hope could never take root. It is with these people and environs that the real horror is sourced".<ref name=Shipley81 /> Neylan observed that Cohle's actions are not motivated by [[misanthropy]], rather a drive to challenge "those who try to either disguise or manipulate this frailty of humans for their own benefit".<ref name="Shipley82">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=82}}</ref> Cohle ultimately confronts "an entire philosophical history which has taken its task as that of sweeping frailty away".<ref name=Shipley82 /> [[Christopher Orr (film critic)|Christopher Orr]] at ''The Atlantic'' said ''True Detective'' was "[[David Fincher|Fincherian]] in the best sense", a fusion of ''[[Seven (1995 film)|Se7en]]'' (1995) and ''[[Zodiac (film)|Zodiac]]'' (2007), because of its subject matter, sleek cinematography and "vivid, unsettling" aura.<ref name="atlantic2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2014/02/-em-true-detective-em-the-best-show-on-tv/283727/ |title=''True Detective'': The Best Show on TV |last=Orr |first=Christopher |date=February 11, 2014 |website=[[The Atlantic]] |publisher=Hayley Romer |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106155900/http://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2014/02/-em-true-detective-em-the-best-show-on-tv/283727/ |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref>

Some commentators noted further influences from comic book literature. Adams likened Cohle to the protagonist of ''[[Alan Moore's The Courtyard]]'' and drew parallels with [[Grant Morrison]]'s ''[[The Invisibles]]'' for the show's brief exploration of [[M-theory]] with one of Cohle's monologues.<ref name="comicindiewire">{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/criticwire/the-comic-books-behind-true-detective |title=The Comic Books Behind 'True Detective' |last=Adams |first=Sam |date=February 21, 2014 |publisher=Indiewire |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105235908/http://blogs.indiewire.com/criticwire/the-comic-books-behind-true-detective |archive-date=November 5, 2015 |access-date=July 13, 2015}}</ref> [[ComicsAlliance]] and ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'' columnist Abraham Riesman cited ''[[Top 10 (comics)|Top 10]]'' as the inspiration for the season finale based on dialogue from the episode's closing scene.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/03/true-detective-finale-comics-alan-moore-homage.html |title=Was There a Hidden Comic Book Homage in the True Detective Finale? |last=Riesman |first=Abraham |date=March 10, 2014 |website=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106000129/http://www.vulture.com/2014/03/true-detective-finale-comics-alan-moore-homage.html |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://comicsalliance.com/true-detective-comic-books-weird-fiction-secrets-influences-alan-moore-grant-morrison-invisibles-hbo |title=The Expert's Guide To HBO's 'True Detective' And Weird Comic Book Fiction |last=Stewart |first=Adam and Mark |date=April 4, 2014 |publisher=[[ComicsAlliance]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106001143/http://comicsalliance.com/true-detective-comic-books-weird-fiction-secrets-influences-alan-moore-grant-morrison-invisibles-hbo/ |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref>

=== Auteurism ===
[[File:Cary Joji Fukunaga "Beast Of No Nation" at Opening Ceremony of the 28th Tokyo International Film Festival (21806112494) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|alt=Photo of a man with short hair and glasses wearing a suit at a film premiere|[[Cary Joji Fukunaga]] (pictured in 2015) [[Film director|directed]] the first season in its entirety, with Pizzolatto as the sole writer. Such an arrangement is extremely uncommon in American television production and prompted [[auteur]]ist readings.]]

Another major topic of discussion concerns ''True Detective''{{'s}} artistic merits under the framework of [[auteur|auteur theory]]. Auteurism (from the French ''[[:wikt:auteur#French|auteur]]'', "author") is a critical framework in which films (or other works of art) are assessed as reflections of the personal vision of individual authors, typically the director or writer.<ref name=time2 /> Authorship of a television series is most commonly ascribed to the [[showrunner]], usually a creator of a series who fills a dual role as [[head writer]] and [[executive producer]]. For example, the crime drama ''[[Twin Peaks]]'' (1990–91) is often interpreted as a product of the contrasting visions of its co-creators, [[David Lynch]] and [[Mark Frost]], each of whom exercised varying degrees of control over the course of its first two seasons and later sequels.<ref name="Hallam 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://sensesofcinema.com/2016/twin-peaks/lynch-televison-auteur/ |title=May the Giant Be with You: ''Twin Peaks'' Season Two, Episode One and the Television Auteur |last=Hallam |first=Lindsay |date=July 2016 |website=[[Senses of Cinema]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111195415/http://sensesofcinema.com/2016/twin-peaks/lynch-televison-auteur/ |archive-date=January 11, 2020}}</ref> Colin Robertson at ''[[The List (magazine)|The List]]'' saw ''Twin Peaks'' as the most notable artistic antecedent to ''True Detective''{{'s}} first season, seeing that both shows challenge [[Genre|generic]] crime drama cliches and "use the genre conventions of a [[Whodunit|whodunnit]]-style mystery as a sublimely subversive diving board, and leap off from there to tell a broader story."<ref name=thelist />

From the perspective of auteur theory, the first season of ''True Detective'' is noteworthy for its reliance on only a single screenwriter and a single director: not only did Pizzolatto serve as showrunner, but he and Fukunaga were at the helm of each episode as sole writer and director, respectively.<ref name="Hallam 2016" /> The partnership of a sole writer and sole director was virtually unique in the traditionally collaborative medium of television production, as most series involve a writing staff and a set of several directors working in tandem over the course of a season.<ref name="time2">{{Cite magazine |url=https://time.com/3990805/true-detective-finale-louie-tv-auteurs/ |title=True Detective, Louie, and the Limits of TV Auteurism |last=Poniewozik |first=James |author-link=James Poniewozik |date=August 10, 2015 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804035430/http://time.com/3990805/true-detective-finale-louie-tv-auteurs/ |archive-date=August 4, 2017}}</ref><ref name="thelist">{{Cite web |url=https://www.list.co.uk/article/60066-mad-men-true-detective-and-the-rise-of-the-tv-auteur/ |title=Mad Men, True Detective and the rise of the TV auteur |last=Robertson |first=Colin |date=April 9, 2014 |website=[[The List (magazine)|The List]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925222238/https://www.list.co.uk/article/60066-mad-men-true-detective-and-the-rise-of-the-tv-auteur/ |archive-date=September 25, 2016}}</ref> [[Scott Timberg]] at ''[[Salon (website)|Salon]]'' noted that Pizzolatto's previous writing experience was not in film or television but [[literary fiction]], a "more purely auteurist form" for which total creative control by an individual author is the norm.<ref name="Timberg 2015">{{Cite web |url=https://www.salon.com/test2/2015/07/26/the_dangers_of_auteur_tv_how_true_detective_went_from_critical_darling_to_laughingstock/ |title=The dangers of auteur TV: How 'True Detective' went from critical darling to laughingstock |last=Timberg |first=Scott |author-link=Scott Timberg |date=July 26, 2015 |website=[[Salon (website)|Salon]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200624024357/https://www.salon.com/test2/2015/07/26/the_dangers_of_auteur_tv_how_true_detective_went_from_critical_darling_to_laughingstock/ |archive-date=June 24, 2020}}</ref>

Fukunaga did not return for the second season, which instead featured six directors across eight episodes, and Pizzolatto retained control of the writing. Met with mixed reviews, season two prompted critics to reevaluate the "auteurist" perspective on the previous season. A critical consensus held that, in hindsight, the response to season one had overestimated the extent of Pizzolatto's individual creative responsibility.<ref name="Hallam 2016" /><ref name="time2" /> Ryan Lattanzio at ''[[IndieWire]]'' posited that Fukunaga's direction of the first season in its entirety had resulted in a consistent vision that counterbalanced "Pizzolatto's tendency to overwrite, and undercook".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2015/08/lynch-fincher-true-detective-and-the-unknowable-future-of-auteur-tv-184757/ |title=Lynch, Fincher, 'True Detective' and the Unknowable Future of Auteur TV |last=Lattanzio |first=Ryan |date=August 11, 2015 |website=[[IndieWire]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120085935/http://www.indiewire.com/2015/08/lynch-fincher-true-detective-and-the-unknowable-future-of-auteur-tv-184757/ |archive-date=January 20, 2018}}</ref> Conversely, Brian Tallerico of ''[[RogerEbert.com]]'' recognized the common view that Fukunaga had provided "balance" to "Pizzolatto's overwriting" but argued "the balance came equally" from Harrelson and McConaughey [[playing against type]] in serious roles, as both actors were "widely-known as 'laid-back [[dude]]s,' often in comedies as much as drama".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/streaming/true-detective-returns-to-style-of-first-season-for-third-outing |title=''True Detective'' Returns to Style of First Season for Third Outing |last=Tallerico |first=Brian |date=January 9, 2019 |website=[[RogerEbert.com]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200411205325/https://www.rogerebert.com/streaming/true-detective-returns-to-style-of-first-season-for-third-outing |archive-date=April 11, 2020}}</ref>

=== Religion ===

''True Detective'' explores Christianity and the dichotomy between religion and rationality. Born into a devout [[Catholic]] household, Pizzolatto said that as a child he saw religion as storytelling that acts "as an escape from the truth".<ref name="beast3">{{Cite web |url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2014/03/06/true-detective-s-godless-universe-is-the-hbo-show-anti-christian.html |title='True Detective's' Godless Universe: is the HBO Show Anti-Christian? |last=Romano |first=Andrew |date=March 6, 2014 |website=The Daily Beast  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105223714/http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2014/03/06/true-detective-s-godless-universe-is-the-hbo-show-anti-christian.html |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> According to Andrew Romano at ''[[The Daily Beast]]'', the season alludes to Pizzolatto's childhood and creates a parallel between Christianity and the supernatural theology of "Carcosa": "Both&nbsp;...&nbsp;are stories. Stories people tell themselves to escape reality. Stories that 'violate every law of the universe.'"<ref name=beast3 /> Romano believed this message is not critical of religion ''per se''; rather it shows how the "power of storytelling" and religious zeal "can wind [you] up in some pretty sick places."<ref name=beast3 /> Jeff Jensen from ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' has opined that the show becomes more self-aware through Cohle's harsh critiques of religion, which he viewed as a vehicle for commentary about pop culture escapism.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2014/01/12/true-detective-premiere |title='True Detective' post-mortem: Unraveling the mysteries |last=Jensen |first=Jeff |date=January 12, 2014 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105223958/http://www.ew.com/article/2014/01/12/true-detective-premiere |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Stapleton observed that the crimes on ''True Detective''—through its victims and the implications of sacrifice and sexual violence—"respond to the conservative Christianity from which they originate, and seek to exploit the opportunities for the pleasure of transgression such a structure offers."<ref name="Shipley169">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=169}}</ref>

Theorist Edia Connole saw connections to [[Philip Marlowe]] and ''[[Le Morte d'Arthur]]''{{'s}} [[Lancelot]] in ''True Detective''{{'s}} presentation of Cohle, all "knights whose duty to their liege lord is tempered with devotion to God."<ref name="Shipley63">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=63}}</ref> Other aspects of ''True Detective'' evoke Christian imagery, including the opening scene, which Connole felt mirrored the [[crucifixion of Jesus]].<ref name="Shipley61">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=61}}</ref> The author and philosopher Finn Janning argued that Cohle's evolution illustrates an affinity between [[Buddhism]] and [[Pessimism#Philosophical pessimism|philosophical pessimism]].<ref name=budd /> A self-proclaimed pessimist, Cohle is, however, changed by a [[near-death experience]] in the season finale, in which he has an epiphany, seeing death as "pure love": this echoes the Buddhist concept of [[rigpa]].<ref name="budd">{{Cite web |url=http://www.philosophyoflife.org/jpl201408.pdf |title=True Detective: Pessimism, Buddhism, or Philosophy? |last=Janning |first=Finn |date=December 2014 |website=Journal of Philosophy of Life |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403024031/http://www.philosophyoflife.org/jpl201408.pdf |archive-date=April 3, 2016}}</ref>

=== Masculinity and depiction of women ===

Commentators have noted [[masculinity]] as a theme in ''True Detective''. Christopher Lirette of ''[[Southern Spaces]]'' said the show was about "men living in a brutally masculine world" and women are depicted as "things-to-be-saved and erotic obstacles" à la ''[[Double Indemnity]]'' (1944) and ''[[Chinatown (1974 film)|Chinatown]]'' (1974).<ref name=sspaces /> ''[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]''{{'s}} Willa Paskin said ''True Detective''{{'s}} depiction of its female characters—as sex workers, the deceased and "a nagging wife"—seemed to reveal an intent to reflect the protagonists' "blinkered worldview and the very masculine, Southern cop culture they inhabited".<ref name="slate2">{{Cite web |url=http://www.slate.com/blogs/browbeat/2014/03/10/true_detective_has_a_woman_problem_yes_and_that_s_partly_why_people_love.html |title=True Detective Does Have a Woman Problem. That's Partly Why People Love It |last=Paskin |first=Willa |date=March 10, 2014 |website=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105220604/http://www.slate.com/blogs/browbeat/2014/03/10/true_detective_has_a_woman_problem_yes_and_that_s_partly_why_people_love.html |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Some commentators saw Hart's characterization as a manifestation of this idea, evident through his conventional view of [[Madonna–whore complex|women as virgins and whores]], as well as his treatment of Maggie and Audrey.<ref name="sspaces">{{Cite web |url=http://www.southernspaces.org/2014/something-true-about-louisiana-hbos-true-detective-and-petrochemical-america-aesthetic |title=Something True about Louisiana: HBO's True Detective and the Petrochemical America Aesthetic |last=Lirette |first=Christopher |date=August 31, 2014 |website=[[Southern Spaces]] |publisher=[[Emory University]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106161348/http://southernspaces.org/2014/something-true-about-louisiana-hbos-true-detective-and-petrochemical-america-aesthetic |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref><ref name="thinkp">{{Cite web |url=http://thinkprogress.org/alyssa/2014/02/24/3322541/true-detective/ |title=Why Men Should Want 'True Detective' To Have Great, Nuanced Female Characters |last=Rosenberg |first=Alyssa |date=February 24, 2014 |publisher=[[Think Progress]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105221356/http://thinkprogress.org/alyssa/2014/02/24/3322541/true-detective/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015 |access-date=October 16, 2015}}</ref><ref name="grant">{{Cite web |url=http://grantland.com/hollywood-prospectus/her-looming-shadow-grows-the-women-of-true-detective/ |title=Her Looming Shadow Grows: The Complex Women of True Detective |last=Lambert |first=Molly |date=February 24, 2014 |publisher=[[Grantland]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105221607/http://grantland.com/hollywood-prospectus/her-looming-shadow-grows-the-women-of-true-detective/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> When Hart confronts the two men who had sex with Audrey, he is in essence "charging other men a price for infringing on the daughter he sees, in a muddled way, as both deserving of protection and badly in need of being controlled".<ref name=thinkp />

In her piece for ''[[Salon (magazine)|Salon]]'', Janet Turley said that the women "become reflections of the men", given that the ''True Detective'' universe is seen through the eyes of the show's male leads.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.salon.com/2014/03/09/true_detective_has_a_women_problem/ |title='True Detective' has a woman problem |last=Turley |first=Janet |date=March 9, 2014 |website=[[Salon (magazine)|Salon]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105222256/http://www.salon.com/2014/03/09/true_detective_has_a_women_problem/ |archive-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref> Sam Adams of ''[[Indiewire]]'' contended that the story was about "the horrible things men do to women", many of which are never reported to or investigated by authorities. Adams wrote, "No one missed Dora Lange. Marie Fontenot disappeared, and the police let a rumor stop them from following up".<ref name=indie2 /> He said the role of women was more profound because Cohle suffers through his ex-wife and deceased daughter and Hart is unable to "deal appropriately with the women who are there".<ref name="indie2">{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/criticwire/true-detective-episode-6-review-haunted-houses-women |title=Female Bodies and the Philbrosophy of 'True Detective' |last=Adams |first=Sam |date=February 24, 2014 |publisher=[[Indiewire]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151105223113/http://blogs.indiewire.com/criticwire/true-detective-episode-6-review-haunted-houses-women |archive-date=November 5, 2015 |access-date=July 13, 2015}}</ref> According to Scott Wilson, a cultural studies lecturer at [[Kingston University]], women are categorized as "the [[superego]]ic, the [[obscene]] and the [[sacred]]".<ref name=Shipley160 /> Maggie, in Wilson's interpretation, is portrayed as the superegoic wife who "constantly makes demands on her guilty husband or partner tying him or her down and deflecting him or her from his symbolic role as police".<ref name="Shipley160">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=160}}</ref>

The philosopher Erin K. Stapleton subscribes to the theory that Dora Lange's corpse serves to "provide the initial territory or orientation through which the communities of ''True Detective'' are formed."<ref name="Shipley170">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=170}}</ref> It is through Dora's corpse that Cohle and Hart's partnership is first clearly articulated and in addition to their own bond, "the intimate knowledge" of her body is the basis of all of the other relationships in their respective lives.<ref name=Shipley170 /><ref name="Shipley164">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=164}}</ref> Her narrative thus, by proxy, influences both men's character development as they delve into the case.<ref name="Shipley173">{{harvnb|Shipley|2014|p=173}}</ref>

== Reception ==

=== Viewership ===
''True Detective'' debuted to 2.3 million U.S. viewers, becoming HBO's highest rated series premiere since the [[Boardwalk Empire (episode)|pilot episode]] of ''[[Boardwalk Empire]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/01/true-detective-girls-hbo-ratings.html |title='True Detective': HBO's Best Premiere Since 2010 |last=Adalian |first=Josef |date=January 13, 2014 |website=New York  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106134441/http://www.vulture.com/2014/01/true-detective-girls-hbo-ratings.html |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> Ratings remained steady and peaked at the finale, which drew 3.5 million viewers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/cotown/la-et-ct-hbo-true-detective-finale-ratings-20140310-story.html |title=HBO's 'True Detective' season finale locks up a ratings high |last=Faughnder |first=Ryan |date=March 10, 2014 |website=Los Angeles Times  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106141123/http://articles.latimes.com/2014/mar/10/entertainment/la-et-ct-hbo-true-detective-finale-ratings-20140310 |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> Overall, season one averaged 2.33 million viewers,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://tvseriesfinale.com/tv-show/true-detective-season-one-ratings-31235/ |title='True Detective': Season One Ratings |date=March 12, 2014 |publisher=TV Series Finale |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141202124329/http://tvseriesfinale.com/tv-show/true-detective-season-one-ratings-31235/ |archive-date=December 2, 2014}}</ref> and its average gross audience (which includes [[digital video recorder|DVR]] recordings, reruns, and [[HBO Go]] streaming) totaled 11.9 million viewers per episode, thus becoming HBO's highest rated freshman show since the first season of ''[[Six Feet Under (TV series)|Six Feet Under]]'' 13 years earlier.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/04/true-detective-now-most-watched-hbo-freshman-series-ever-715055/ |title='True Detective' Now Most Watched HBO Freshman Series Ever |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=April 15, 2014 |website=Deadline Hollywood |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106142115/http://deadline.com/2014/04/true-detective-now-most-watched-hbo-freshman-series-ever-715055/ |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/03/ratings-true-detective-soars-with-finale.html |title=Ratings: True Detective Soars With Finale |last=Adalian |first=Josef |date=March 10, 2014 |website=New York  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106212246/http://www.vulture.com/2014/03/ratings-true-detective-soars-with-finale.html |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref>

|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106155611/http://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2014/01/true-detective-review-hbo |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> were criticized by the ''[[New York Post]]'' as "'70s-era psycho-babble" which slowed down the story.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |url=https://nypost.com/2014/01/07/true-detective-needs-dramatic-jolt/l |title='True Detective' needs dramatic jolt |last=Starr |first=Michael |date=January 7, 2014 |website=[[New York Post]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106174952/http://nypost.com/2014/01/07/true-detective-needs-dramatic-jolt/ |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref>  Several critics viewed the portrayals of women as stereotypical: "either angry or aroused",<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=http://grantland.com/features/matthew-mcconaughey-woody-harrelson-hbo-true-detective/ |title=Resisting Arrest |last=Greenwald |first=Andy |date=January 8, 2014 |website=[[Grantland]] |publisher=[[ESPN]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106214125/http://grantland.com/features/matthew-mcconaughey-woody-harrelson-hbo-true-detective/ |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/arts/critics/television/2014/03/03/140303crte_television_nussbaum |title=The shallow deep talk of 'True Detective' |last=Nussbaum |first=Emily |date=March 3, 2014 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106162401/http://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2014/03/03/cool-story-bro |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> though Michelle Monaghan was praised for her performance in a "thankless role".<ref name=":2" />

Pizzolatto and Fukunaga, as sole writer and director of the entire series, were able to exercise much stronger control over the show than is usual for a TV series, which let the show take risks: the pacing, dialogue, and cinematography all departed at times from the expectations for a television drama.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/features/southern-discomfort--is-true-detective-starring-woody-harrelson-and-matthew-mcconaughey-the-best-us-detective-show-since-the-wire-9136919.html |title=Is True Detective, starring Woody Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey, the best US detective show since The Wire? |last=Hughes |first=Sarah |date=February 18, 2014 |website=[[The Independent]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106160740/http://variety.com/2014/tv/reviews/tv-review-hbos-true-detective-1201024636/ |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref>  Pizzolatto's scripts drew occasional criticism as "self-consciously literary" and overwritten,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://artsfuse.org/98478/fuse-tv-review-hbos-true-detective-a-work-in-progress/ |title=Fuse TV Review: HBO's 'True Detective'—A Work in Progress |last=Peary |first=Gerald |date=January 8, 2014 |website=[[The Arts Fuse]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106175757/http://artsfuse.org/98478/fuse-tv-review-hbos-true-detective-a-work-in-progress/ |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref><ref name=":5" /> and several journalists attributed mistakes in the script to Pizzolatto's inexperience in writing TV drama.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/01/11/arts/television/mcconaughey-and-harrelson-star-in-true-detective-on-hbo.html |title=A Coupling as Bizarre as the Murder |last=Hale |first=Mike |date=January 11, 2014 |website=[[The New York Times]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106161212/http://www.nytimes.com/2014/01/11/arts/television/mcconaughey-and-harrelson-star-in-true-detective-on-hbo.html?_r=0 |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> Despite the criticism, the ''[[Daily Telegraph]]'' and [[Uproxx]] described the season as "ambitious"<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/10654871/True-Detective-Sky-Atlantic-review-a-work-of-depth-and-cinematic-flair.html |title=True Detective, Sky Atlantic, review: a work of depth and cinematic flair |last=Harvey |first=Chris |date=February 22, 2014 |website=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106155244/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/tv-and-radio-reviews/10654871/True-Detective-Sky-Atlantic-review-a-work-of-depth-and-cinematic-flair.html |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> and "dense with event and meaning".<ref name=":3" /> The flashback structure also divided critics: it was described as "impressively seamless",<ref name=":6" /> and "a major asset",<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/tvandradioblog/2014/feb/27/true-detective-season-one-episode-one-long-bright-dark |title=True Detective recap: season one, episode one – The Long Bright Dark |last=Mumford |first=Gwilym |date=February 27, 2014 |website=The Guardian  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106160921/http://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/tvandradioblog/2014/feb/27/true-detective-season-one-episode-one-long-bright-dark |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> but the fragmented approach to storytelling was considered a flaw by others.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=vfreview /> Uproxx praised Fukunaga's atmospheric and "hauntingly beautiful" cinematography,<ref name=":3" /> and ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' complimented the "spare, hollow, percussive" soundtrack,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/arts/television/2014/01/09/mcconaughey-and-harrelson-make-true-detective-arresting/9FuWBQeEZZpfxGqaE3KaeJ/story.html |title=McConaughey, Harrelson make 'True Detective' arresting |last=Rodman |first=Sarah |date=January 9, 2014 |website=[[Boston Globe]]  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106160503/http://www.bostonglobe.com/arts/television/2014/01/09/mcconaughey-and-harrelson-make-true-detective-arresting/9FuWBQeEZZpfxGqaE3KaeJ/story.html |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> with Uproxx crediting the creative control the two men wielded for the quality of the result.<ref name=":3" />

The story of two mismatched detectives working on a case was described by several critics as a cliché,<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2014/01/11/true-detective-review-you-have-to-watch-hbo-s-revolutionary-crime-classic.html |title='True Detective' Review: You Have to Watch HBO's Revolutionary Crime Classic |last=Romano |first=Andrew |date=January 11, 2014 |website=The Daily Beast  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510214925/http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2014/01/11/true-detective-review-you-have-to-watch-hbo-s-revolutionary-crime-classic.html |archive-date=May 10, 2016}}</ref><ref name=":8" /> though many reviewers felt this was made into a strength: ''The Daily Beast'', for example, described the narrative as having "the potential to be revolutionary",<ref name=":7" /> and the [[Grantland]] reviewer felt that "the form is truly radical and forward-thinking", though he added that "the content is anything but".<ref name=":2" />  Emily Nussbaum, writing for ''[[The New Yorker]]'', was also critical, considering the real story to be "a simpler tale: one about heroic male outlines and closeups of female asses"; she described the philosophical monologues as "dorm-room deep talk" and argued that the show had "fallen for its own sales pitch".<ref name=":8" /> Other reviewers were more positive: comments ranged from "as frighteningly nervy and furious in its delivery and intent as prime David Lynch",<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/tv/review/true-detective-season-one |title=True Detective: Season One |last=Cabin |first=Chris |date=January 8, 2014 |website=[[Slant Magazine]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106161230/http://www.slantmagazine.com/tv/review/true-detective-season-one |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> to "one of the most riveting and provocative series I've ever seen".<ref name=":7" />

=== Accolades ===
{{See also|List of awards and nominations received by True Detective}}
[[File:Woody Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey at the 66th Primetime Emmy Awards.jpg|right|thumb|upright|alt=A photograph of Woody Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey at the 66th Primetime Emmy Awards|Harrelson (left) and McConaughey (right) at the 66th Primetime Emmy Awards]]

As the nominations for the [[66th Primetime Emmy Awards]] approached, early media reports named ''True Detective'' among several potential miniseries candidates, due to a revision made by the [[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]] that recognized film and miniseries content as distinct categories.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://variety.com/2014/tv/news/emmy-rules-change-restores-movie-and-miniseries-split-1201114252/ |title=Emmy Rules Change Restores Movie and Miniseries Split |last=Lowry |first=Brian |date=February 20, 2014 |website=Variety  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510201216/http://variety.com/2014/tv/news/emmy-rules-change-restores-movie-and-miniseries-split-1201114252/ |archive-date=May 10, 2016}}</ref> By March 2014, HBO had submitted ''True Detective'' as a drama series contender,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://variety.com/2014/tv/news/true-detective-to-submit-as-drama-series-not-miniseries-for-emmys-1201146631/ |title=True Detective' to Submit as Drama Series, Not Miniseries, for Emmys |last=Littleton |first=Cynthia |date=March 25, 2014 |website=Variety  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510203116/http://variety.com/2014/tv/news/true-detective-to-submit-as-drama-series-not-miniseries-for-emmys-1201146631/ |archive-date=May 10, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/article/television/emmys-shocker-hbo-to-submit-true-detective-as-best-drama-series-not-miniseries |title=Emmys Shocker: HBO to Submit 'True Detective' as Best Drama Series, Not Miniseries |last=Travers |first=Ben |date=March 25, 2014 |publisher=[[Indiewire]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510203303/http://www.indiewire.com/article/television/emmys-shocker-hbo-to-submit-true-detective-as-best-drama-series-not-miniseries |archive-date=May 10, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/tv/la-et-st-en-gold-standard-20140515-story.html |title=Gold Standard Emmy bids by 'True Detective' and 'Fargo' bend categories |last=Whipp |first=Glenn |date=May 15, 2014 |website=Los Angeles Times |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106160336/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/tv/showtracker/la-et-st--true-detective-review-20140110-story.html |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> an unconventional move given the show's anthology format and fierce competition from the likes of ''[[Breaking Bad]]'' and ''[[House of Cards (U.S. series)|House of Cards]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/emmys-hbos-true-detective-compete-684153 |title=Emmys: HBO's 'True Detective' to Compete in Fierce Drama Series Category |last=Hunt |first=Stacey |date=March 25, 2014 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510210136/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/tv/la-et-st-en-gold-standard-20140515-story.html |archive-date=May 10, 2016}}</ref> HBO's decision was censured by [[FX (TV channel)|FX]] president [[John Landgraf]], who remarked to reporters at a press event: "My own personal point of view is that a miniseries is a story that ends, a series is a story that continues. To tell you the truth, I think it's actually unfair for HBO to put ''True Detective'' in the drama series category because essentially you can get certain actors to do a closed-ended series – a la [[Billy Bob Thornton]] in ''[[Fargo (TV series)|Fargo]]'' or Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson in ''True Detective'' – who you can't get to sign on for a seven-year [regular drama series] deal."<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2014/04/09/fx-hbo-true-detective-emmy-unfair |title=Unfair' HBO knocked for 'True Detective' Emmy bid |last=Hibbert |first=James |date=April 9, 2014 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510212024/http://www.ew.com/article/2014/04/09/fx-hbo-true-detective-emmy-unfair |archive-date=May 10, 2016}}</ref> Nevertheless, ''True Detective'' emerged as a frontrunner heading into the Primetime Emmy season, and in July 2014, was nominated for twelve awards; its closest rival, ''Breaking Bad'', received sixteen nominations.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/07/emmys-analysis-true-detective-orange-is-the-new-black-broadcast-decline-801826/ |title=Emmy Noms Analysis: 'True Detective', 'Orange' & 'Shameless' Fare Well Amid Category Brouhaha As Free-TV Slips To New Low |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=July 10, 2014 |website=Deadline Hollywood |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510214501/http://deadline.com/2014/07/emmys-analysis-true-detective-orange-is-the-new-black-broadcast-decline-801826/ |archive-date=May 10, 2016}}</ref> The series ultimately won five Emmy awards: [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series|Outstanding Directing]] (Fukunaga), Outstanding Casting, Outstanding Main Title Design, Outstanding Make-Up, and Outstanding Cinematography.<ref name=Emmys />

''True Detective'' was a candidate for a variety of awards, most of which recognized outstanding achievement in direction, cinematography, writing, and acting. It received four [[Golden Globe Award|Golden Globe]] nominations, among them for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Miniseries or Television Film|Best Miniseries or Television Film]], and a [[TCA Award]] for [[TCA Award for Program of the Year|Program of the Year]].<ref name=gg /><ref name=tca /> Among the show's wins include a [[British Academy Television Award]] (BAFTA) for [[British Academy Television Award for Best International Programme|Best International Programme]], a [[Writers Guild of America Award]] in the [[Writers Guild of America Award for Television: Dramatic Series|Dramatic Series]] category, and a [[Critics' Choice Television Award]] for [[Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Actor in a Drama Series|Best Actor in a Drama Series]] (McConaughey).<ref name=bafta /><ref name=ccta /><ref name=wgaa />

== Home media ==
On June 10, 2014, HBO Home Entertainment released the first season of ''True Detective'' on DVD and [[Blu-ray Disc]] formats. In addition to the eight episodes, both formats contain bonus content including interviews with McConaughey and Harrelson, Pizzolatto, and composer Burnett on the show's development, "Inside the Episode" featurettes, two audio commentaries, and deleted scenes from the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/True-Detective-Season-1-Press-Release/19614 |title=True Detective – HBO Video's Official Press Release for {{'}}''The Complete 1st Season''{{'}} |last=Lambert |first=David |date=March 26, 2014 |publisher=TVShowsODVD.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106161647/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/news/True-Detective-Season-1-Press-Release/19614 |archive-date=November 6, 2015}}</ref> During its first week of sale in the United States, ''True Detective'' was the number two-selling TV series on DVD and Blu-ray Disc, selling 65,208 copies.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.the-numbers.com/home-market/packaged-media-sales-chart/2014/06/15 |title=United States Combined DVD and Blu-ray Sales Chart for Week Ending June 15, 2014 |date=June 15, 2014 |publisher=[[The Numbers (website)|The Numbers]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924021519/http://www.the-numbers.com/home-market/packaged-media-sales-chart/2014/06/15 |archive-date=September 24, 2016}}</ref>

'''''Tár''''' is a 2022 [[psychological drama]] film written and directed by [[Todd Field]]. [[Cate Blanchett]] stars as Lydia Tár, a world-renowned conductor, whose life unravels after she is accused of misconduct. The supporting cast includes [[Nina Hoss]], [[Noémie Merlant]], [[Sophie Kauer]], [[Julian Glover]], [[Allan Corduner]], and [[Mark Strong]].

''Tár'' premiered at the [[79th Venice International Film Festival]] in September 2022, where Blanchett won the [[Volpi Cup for Best Actress]]. Following a three-week [[limited theatrical release]], it received a [[wide release]] on October 28, 2022, through [[Focus Features]]. It received acclaim, especially for Blanchett's performance and Field's screenplay and direction. At the [[95th Academy Awards]], it garnered six nominations, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay|Best Original Screenplay]] and [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for Field, and [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] for Blanchett.

''Tár'' is the fourth film in history to be named Best Film of the Year by the [[New York Film Critics Circle]], the [[Los Angeles Film Critics Association]], the [[London Film Critics' Circle]] and the [[National Society of Film Critics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.worldofreel.com/blog/06hby5f5n6voyct05okz3c6yzh7i1j|access-date=October 14, 2026|title=''Tár'' is Only Fourth Film in History to Win London, New York, L.A. and NSFC|author=Jordan Ruimy|date=February 8, 2023|website=World of Reel|quote=The other three are ''[[L.A. Confidential (film)|L.A. Confidential]]'', ''[[Schindler's List]]'' and ''[[The Social Network]]''.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yearendlists.com/visuals/tar-24bc2fc1-2687-4e75-b314-ec01c026b541 |title=''Tár''|publisher=Year-End Lists |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/feature/film-critics-pick-10-best-movies-of-2022|url-status=dead|title=Best of 2022: Film Critic Top Ten Lists |last=Dietz |first=Jason |publisher=[[Metacritic]] |date=December 6, 2022 |access-date= July 3, 2026 |archive-date=December 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206233352/https://www.metacritic.com/feature/film-critics-pick-10-best-movies-of-2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/50-best-movies-2022-critics-poll/ |title=The 50 Best Movies of 2022, According to 165 Critics from Around the World |last1=Foreman |first1=Alison |last2=Blauvelt |first2=Christian |publisher=[[IndieWire]] |date=February 26, 2023 |access-date= July 3, 2026 |archive-date=December 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221227190022/https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/50-best-movies-2022-critics-poll/ |url-status=live}}</ref> It has appeared in numerous lists of the [[List of films voted the best|greatest films]] of the 21st century.<!-- NOTE: This statement is supported by multiple sources in the Reception section. Per WP:CITELEAD, statements in the lead do not need to be cited if the information is cited in the body of the article.-->

== Plot ==
Lydia Tár, [[chief conductor]] of a Berlin orchestra, heavily relies on Francesca, her personal assistant and confidante. While being interviewed by [[Adam Gopnik]] at [[The New Yorker Festival|''The New Yorker'' Festival]], Lydia promotes her upcoming live recording of [[Symphony No. 5 (Mahler)|Mahler's Fifth Symphony]] and memoir ''Tár on Tár''. She meets with Eliot Kaplan, an investment banker and amateur conductor who co-founded the Accordion Foundation with Lydia to support aspiring female conductors. They discuss technique, replacing Lydia's assistant conductor Sebastian with Francesca, and filling a vacant cello position in Berlin.

As a guest lecturer, Lydia holds a masterclass at [[Juilliard School|Juilliard]]. When a student expresses reluctance to study [[Johann Sebastian Bach|Bach]] due to his social views, she encourages him to focus on composers' music rather than their personal lives. The student leaves in frustration. That night, Lydia anonymously receives a first edition of [[Vita Sackville-West]]'s novel ''[[Vita Sackville-West#Challenge|Challenge]]'' with the title page embellished with a hand-drawn [[kené]] pattern, a personal reminder of her trip to Peru. She tears up the page and throws it away.

Lydia flies back to Berlin, where she lives with her wife Sharon, the [[concertmaster]] of the orchestra, and their daughter Petra. Before a [[blind audition]] for the cello position, Lydia spots a young Russian candidate, Olga Metkina, in the bathroom. Lydia changes her scorecard to ensure Olga a spot in the orchestra and proposes to the orchestra that [[Cello Concerto (Elgar)|Elgar's Cello Concerto]] be the companion piece to the Mahler symphony, virtually guaranteeing Olga the soloist position. Lydia's attraction to Olga strains her relationships with Francesca and Sharon.

Krista Taylor, a promising young musician whom Lydia once mentored, has been [[Blacklisting#Employment|blacklisted]] after a dispute with Lydia. After sending disturbing emails to Francesca, Krista ends her own life. Lydia instructs Francesca to delete the emails and hire a lawyer after learning of Krista's parents' plan to sue her. Lydia informs Sebastian of his imminent replacement. Incensed, he calls her out on her inappropriate favoritism, leading Lydia to decide against promoting Francesca.

Lydia is haunted by an increasing [[Hyperacusis|sensitivity to sound]], surreal nightmares, daytime hallucinations, chronic pain, and enigmatic patterned scribbles resembling those Krista once made. While trying to complete a composition dedicated to Petra, she is disturbed by the sound of a medical device next door, where her neighbor is caring for her dying mother. One day, Lydia falls and hurts herself while attempting to follow Olga home, but tells Sharon she was injured in a mugging.

A manipulatively edited video of Lydia's Juilliard class goes viral, and an article accusing her of sexual predation appears in the ''[[New York Post]]''. Lydia's Wikipedia page is also edited by an unseen person to include the controversial new information about her. Lydia tries to contact Francesca, who resigned after being denied the promotion. She breaks into Francesca's home and finds a draft of ''Tár on Tár'', which Francesca has renamed ''Rat on Rat''. Lydia, accompanied by Olga, returns to New York City to attend a deposition for Krista's parents' lawsuit and to promote her book. The two are met by protestors, and Lydia is confronted with incriminating emails between her and Krista that Francesca provided.

In Berlin, Lydia is removed as conductor due to the controversy. Furious over the allegations and Lydia's lack of transparency, Sharon bars her from seeing their daughter. An increasingly depressed and deranged Lydia retreats to her old studio. She sneaks into the live recording she was supposed to conduct, and runs onto the stage to assault Eliot, who replaced her as conductor. Advised to remain out of the public eye by her management, she returns to her modest childhood home on [[Staten Island]], where she finds certificates of achievement bearing her birth name, Linda Tarr. She cries watching an old [[VHS]] of [[Young People's Concerts]] in which [[Leonard Bernstein]] discusses the meaning of music. Her brother Tony arrives and admonishes her for forgetting her roots.

Sometime in the future, Lydia finds work conducting in the Philippines. Seeking a massage, the hotel concierge sends her to a brothel fronting as a massage parlor; the young women sit in a semicircle with numbers on their robes. Number 5 looks directly at Lydia, who rushes outside to vomit. Later, she conducts a live performance of the score for the video game series ''[[Monster Hunter]]'' in front of an audience of [[cosplay]]ers.
