The Battle of the Black Gate was filmed in April<ref name="Year of Filming">{{cite web |last=Tehanu |title=One Year of Principal Photography |publisher=The One Ring.net |date=11 October 2000 |url=http://www.theonering.net/features/exclusives/oneyear_page03.html |access-date=22 October 2006 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060912120101/http://www.theonering.net/features/exclusives/oneyear_page03.html |archive-date=12 September 2006}}</ref> at the [[Rangipo Desert]], a former minefield.<ref>{{cite web |author=Samantha Sofka |url=https://archive.nerdist.com/peter-jackson-filmed-part-of-return-of-the-king-on-a-mine-field/ |title=Peter Jackson Filmed Part of RETURN OF THE KING on a Mine Field |website=nerdist.com |date=15 March 2015 |access-date=23 March 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151022144559/http://nerdist.com/peter-jackson-filmed-part-of-return-of-the-king-on-a-mine-field/ |archive-date=22 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0167260/locations |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003) Filming Locations |website=imdb.com |access-date=23 March 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115175233/http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0167260/locations |archive-date=15 January 2016}}</ref> New Zealand soldiers were hired as extras while guides were on the lookout for unexploded mines. Also a cause for concern were Monaghan and Boyd's scale doubles during a charge sequence. In the meantime, Wood, Astin and Serkis filmed at [[Mount Ruapehu]] for the Mount Doom exteriors. In particular, they spent two hours shooting Sam lifting Frodo on to his back with cross-[[camera coverage]].<ref name="Cameras in Middle-earth"/>

Scenes shot in June were the Paths of the Dead across various locations, including [[Pūtangirua Pinnacles]].<ref name="Year of Filming"/> In July the crew shot some Shelob scenes, and in August and September time was spent on the scenes in Isengard. Monaghan and Boyd tried numerous takes of their entrance, stressing the word "weed" as they smoked [[List of Middle-earth plants#Pipe-weed|pipe-weed]]. Christopher Lee spent his part of his scene mostly alone, though McKellen and Hill arrived on the first day for a few lines to help.<ref name="Cameras in Middle-earth"/>

Edoras exteriors were shot in October. The Ride of the Rohirrim, where Théoden leads the charge into the Orc army, was filmed in [[Twizel]] with 150 extras on horseback. The Battle of the Pelennor Fields has more extensive use of [[computer-generated imagery]] (CGI), in contrast to the more extensive use of live-action in the [[Battle of the Hornburg|Battle of Helm's Deep]] in the second film. Also filmed were the attempts by Faramir to recapture [[Osgiliath]],<ref>{{cite video |title=Home of the Horse Lords |medium=DVD |publisher=New Line Cinema |year=2004}}</ref> as were scenes in the city itself.<ref>{{cite web |last=Davidson |first=Paul |title=A Slew of The Lord of the Rings news |website=IGN |date=14 November 2000 |url=http://uk.movies.ign.com/articles/034/034276p1.html |access-date=24 October 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110831202506/http://uk.movies.ign.com/articles/034/034276p1.html |archive-date=31 August 2011}}</ref> At this point production was very hectic, with Jackson moving around ten units per day, and production finally wrapped on the Minas Tirith sets, as well as second units shooting parts of the siege. Just as the Hobbit actors' first scene was hiding from a Ringwraith under a tree, their last scene was the [[Chroma key|bluescreened]] reaction shot of the inhabitants of Minas Tirith bowing to them.<ref name="Cameras in Middle-earth"/>

=== Pick-ups ===
The 2003 pick-ups were filmed in the Wellington studio car park, with many parts of sets and blue-screens used to finish off scenes, which the design team had to work 24 hours to get the right sets ready for a particular day.<ref name="Design"/> The shoot continued for two months, and became an emotional time of farewells for the cast and crew. The film has the most extensive list of re-shoots given for the trilogy. Jackson took his time to re-shoot Aragorn's coronation, rushed into a single day under the supervision of second unit director [[Geoff Murphy]] on 21 December 2000. Jackson also re-shot scenes in and around Mount Doom,<ref name="Cameras in Middle-earth"/> and Théoden's death, right after Bernard Hill was meant to wrap.<ref name="Director's commentary"/>

There was also the new character of Gothmog. This was a major new design addition for the film, as Jackson felt the Mordor Orcs were "pathetic" compared to the [[Uruk-hai]] of the second film after watching assembly cuts, and thus Weta Workshop created grotesque new "über Orcs" as antagonists for the audience to focus on. Rivers redesigned the Witch-king; all his scenes were re-shot, because of confusion from non-readers over whether or not Sauron was on the battlefield.<ref name="Weta Workshop"/>

With the positive response to Bloom, Legolas was given a fight with a ''mûmak'',<ref name="Pick-up end">{{cite web |last=Davidson |first=Paul |title=A new ''Return of the King'' poster |website=IGN |date=27 June 2003 |url=http://uk.movies.ign.com/articles/426/426327p1.html |access-date=21 October 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118234017/http://uk.movies.ign.com/articles/426/426327p1.html |archive-date=18 January 2012}}</ref> and Shore appeared in a cameo during Legolas and Gimli's drinking game at Edoras.<ref name="Music">{{cite video |title=Music for Middle-earth |medium=DVD |publisher=New Line Cinema |year=2004}}</ref> The final scenes shot were Aragorn escaping the Skull avalanche, and Frodo finishing his book. The cast also received various props associated with their characters, although [[John Rhys-Davies]] burned his final Gimli prosthetic. [[Viggo Mortensen]] [[headbutt]]ed the stunt team goodbye.<ref name="Cameras in Middle-earth"/> Pick-ups ended on 27 June 2003.<ref name="Pick-up end"/>

Scenes shot afterwards included various live-action shots of Riders for the Battle of the Pelennor Fields and a reaction shot of Serkis as Gollum finally realises Frodo intends to destroy the Ring, shot in Jackson's house.<ref name="Edit">{{cite video |title=Editorial: Completing the Trilogy (Special Extended Edition documentary) |medium=DVD |publisher=New Line Cinema |year=2004}}</ref> For the Extended DVD, in March 2004 Jackson created a few shots of skulls rolling over for the avalanche scene; this was the final piece of footage ever shot for the trilogy, and Jackson noted that it must be the first time a director had shot scenes for a film after it had already won the Oscar.<ref name="Passing of an Age">{{cite video |title=The Passing of an Age (Special Extended Edition documentary) |medium=DVD |publisher=New Line Cinema |year=2004}}</ref>

=== Editing ===
[[Post-production]] began in November 2002, with the completion of the 4½ hour assembly cut of the film that [[Annie Collins]] had been completing over 2001 and 2002, from 4-hour dailies. For example, Théoden leading the charge went from 150 minutes of takes to a finished 90 seconds.<ref>{{cite book |last=Sibley |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Sibley |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Making of the Movie Trilogy |publisher=Harpercollins |year=2002 |isbn=0-00-713567-X |page=158 |no-pp=true}}</ref> Jackson reunited with longtime collaborator [[Jamie Selkirk]] to edit the final film. Like ''The Two Towers'', they would have to deal with multiple storylines, and Jackson paid attention to each storyline at a time before deciding where to intercut. Most importantly they spent three weeks working on the last 45 minutes of the film,<ref name="Edit"/> for appropriate intercutting and leaving out scenes such as the Mouth of Sauron, and the fates of characters like Legolas, Gimli, Éowyn and Faramir.<ref name="Story"/> The film inherited scenes originally planned to go into the second film, including the reforging of [[List of Middle-earth weapons and armour#Narsil|Narsil]], Gollum's backstory, and Saruman's exit. But the Saruman scene posed a structural problem: killing off the second film's villain when the plot has Sauron as the main villain.<ref name="Edit"/> Despite pick-ups and dubs, the scene was cut, causing controversy with fans and Saruman actor Christopher Lee, as well as a petition to restore the scene.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rings director cuts wizard scenes |publisher=BBC News online |date=12 November 2003 |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/film/3265475.stm |access-date=17 October 2006 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060317114116/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/film/3265475.stm |archive-date=17 March 2006}}</ref> Lee nonetheless contributed to the DVDs and was at the [[Copenhagen]] premiere, although he said he would never understand the reason for the cut and his relationship with Jackson was chilly.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wootton|first=Dan|date=30 April 2006|title=I will never forgive Jackson, says LOTR actor|newspaper=New Zealand Herald|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/feature/story.cfm?c_id=594&ObjectID=10379594|url-status=dead|access-date=17 October 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930012208/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/feature/story.cfm?c_id=594&ObjectID=10379594|archive-date=30 September 2007}}</ref> They would, however, later reconcile upon Lee's casting in Jackson's ''Hobbit'' films. Jackson only had a lock on 5 out of 10 reels, and had to churn out 3 reels in 3 weeks to help finish the film. It was finally completed on 12 November 2003.<ref name="End of all Things">{{cite video |title=The End of All Things (Special Extended Edition documentary) |medium=DVD |publisher=New Line Cinema |year=2004}}</ref> Jackson never had a chance to view the film in full due to the hectic schedule, and only saw the film from beginning to end on 1 December at the Wellington premiere; according to [[Elijah Wood]], his response was "yup, it's good, pretty good".<ref name="Passing of an Age"/>

=== Visual effects ===
{{Main|Special effects of The Lord of the Rings film series|l1=Special effects of ''The Lord of the Rings'' film series}}

''The Return of the King'' contains 1,489 visual effect shots, nearly three times the number from the first film and almost twice that of the second. As with the two previous films, [[Jim Rygiel]] served as the visual effects supervisor. Visual effects work began with [[Alan Lee (illustrator)|Alan Lee]] and Mark Lewis compositing various photographs of New Zealand landscape to create the digital arena of the [[Minas Tirith#Pelennor Fields|Pelennor Fields]] in November 2002. Jackson and Rivers used computers to plan the enormous battle up until February 2003, when the shots were shown to Weta Digital. To their astonishment, 60 planned shots had gone up to 250, and 50,000 characters were now 200,000.<ref name="Weta Digital">{{cite video |title=Weta Digital (Special Extended Edition documentary) |medium=DVD |publisher=New Line Cinema |year=2004}}</ref> Nevertheless, they pressed on, soon delivering 100 shots a week, 20 a day, and as the deadline neared within the last two months, often working until 2&nbsp;am.<ref name="End of all Things"/>

For the battle, they recorded 450 motions for the [[MASSIVE (software)|MASSIVE]] digital horses (though deaths were animated), and also had to deal with late additions in the film, such as Trolls bursting through Minas Tirith's gates as well as the creatures that pull Grond to the gate,<ref name="Weta Workshop"/> and redoing a shot of two ''mûmakil'' Éomer takes down that had originally taken six months in two days. On a similar note of digital creatures, Shelob's head sculpture was scanned by a Canadian company for 10 times more detail than Weta had previously been able to capture.<ref name="Weta Digital"/>

Like the previous films, there are also extensive morphs between digital doubles for the actors. This time, there was Sam falling off Shelob, where the morph takes place as Astin hits the ground. Legolas attacking a ''mûmak'' required numerous transitions to and fro, and Gollum's shots of him having recovered the One Ring and falling into the Crack of Doom were fully animated.<ref name="Weta Digital"/> For the latter scene, as well as the scene in which Mount Doom erupts and Frodo and Sam escape from the volcano, the help of the company [[Next Limit Technologies]] and their software [[RealFlow]] was required to simulate the [[lava]]. The King of the Dead is played by an actor in prosthetics, and his head occasionally morphs to a more skull-like digital version, depending on the character's mood. The Mouth of Sauron also had his mouth enlarged 200% for unsettling effect.<ref name="Design"/>

''The Return of the King'' also has practical effects. In the Pyre of Denethor sequence, as the Steward of Gondor throws Pippin out of the Tomb, [[John Noble]] threw a [[Special effects of The Lord of the Rings film series#Size Doubles|size double]] named Fon onto a prostrate [[Billy Boyd]], who immediately pushed his head into camera to complete the illusion. A few burning torches were also reflected off a plate of glass and into the camera for when Gandalf's horse Shadowfax kicks Denethor onto the pyre. Because of Jackson's requirement for complete representation of his fantasy world, numerous miniatures were built, such as 1:72-scale miniature of Minas Tirith, which rises 7m high and is 6.5m in [[diameter]]. 1:14 scale sections of the city were also required, and the Extended Edition scene of the collapsing City of the Dead has 80,000 small skulls, amounting in total to a single cubic meter.<ref name="Big-atures"/> The miniatures team concluded in November with the Black Gate, after 1000 days of shooting, and the final digital effects shot done was the Ring's destruction, on 25 November.<ref name="End of all Things"/>

=== Sound effects ===
The Sound department spent the early part of the year searching for the right sounds. A [[Tasmanian devil]] was used to create Shelob's shriek, which in turn gave inspiration for Weta's animators, while the ''mûmakil'' sound is the beginning and end of a lion roar. Human screams and a donkey screech were mixed into Sauron's fall and broken glass was used for the collapsing sounds. For missile trading during Minas Tirith's siege, construction workers dropped actual 2 ton stone blocks previously lifted by a construction crane. Mixing began at a new studio on 15 August, although unfinished building work caused some annoyances.<ref>{{cite video |title=The Soundscapes of Middle-earth |medium=DVD |publisher=New Line Cinema |year=2004}}</ref> The mixers finished on 15 November, after three months of non-stop work.<ref name="End of all Things"/>

=== Score ===
{{further|The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (soundtrack)|l1=''The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King'' (soundtrack)}}
{{main|Music of The Lord of the Rings film series{{!}}Music of ''The Lord of the Rings'' film series}}

{{listen
| filename = IntoTheWestROTK.ogg
| title = "Into the West" (performed by Annie Lennox)
| description = Written by Fran Walsh, Howard Shore, and Annie Lennox, this selected song won the [[Academy Awards|Oscar]] for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] at the [[76th Academy Awards]]. It also won a [[47th Grammy Awards|Grammy]] for [[Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media|Best Film Song]].
}}

The music, as for the rest of the trilogy, was composed by Shore. He watched the assembly cut of the film,<ref name="Music"/> and had to write seven minutes of music per day to keep up with the schedule.<ref name="End of all Things"/> The score sees the full introduction of the Gondor theme, originally heard during Boromir's speeches at the [[The Fellowship of the Ring#Book II: The Ring Goes South|Council of Elrond]] in ''The Fellowship of the Ring'' and at Osgiliath in ''The Two Towers''{{'}} Extended Edition. Shore also used the Gondor theme with the new ascending coda (which is unique to this film) in his score for the trailer of the film.

The score features the [[London Philharmonic Orchestra]], [[London Voices]], the [[London Oratory School Schola]] and featured vocal soloists. The score is the most expansive of the three: scoring effectively the entire movie length, not including additional music written for the trailer and various alternate versions released to the public. It also uses the biggest forces in the series: sections of the score call for two sets of timpani, eight trumpets<ref>The "fondest recollections" of the principal fiddler, [http://www.gardinerhoulgate.co.uk/lord-of-the-strings/ Dermot Crehan] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170426062555/http://www.gardinerhoulgate.co.uk/lord-of-the-strings/ |date=26 April 2017 }}, were from "an eight strong trumpet session".</ref> (and possibly a similar increase in the size of the horn, trombone and tuba section, as well), 85 singers in the mixed choir<ref>{{cite web|title=Source Songs, Poems and Text|url=http://www.amagpiesnest.com/source_songs/index_source_songs.htm#choirs|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171002195136/http://www.amagpiesnest.com/source_songs/index_source_songs.htm#choirs|archive-date=2 October 2017|access-date=17 October 2017|website=www.amagpiesnest.com}}</ref> with additional players for all-male and all-female sections, over fifty in the boy choir and many instrumentalist "bands" playing Celtic and eastern instruments such as tin whistle or pan flute, on stage or off of it.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.filmmusicsociety.org/news_events/features/2014/121714.html |title=FMS FEATURE [ Howard Shore's Farewell to Middle-earth – by Jon Burlingame] |website=www.filmmusicsociety.org|access-date=17 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313145656/http://filmmusicsociety.org/news_events/features/2014/121714.html|archive-date=13 March 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> One piece of music required an instrument invented and crafted especially for the film: a fiddle with four pairs of strings instead of single strings.<ref>Doug Adams, [http://www.tolkiendil.com/_media/divertissements/adaptations/films/sda_3_livret_de_presentation_de_la_bo_en_anglais_.pdf The Annotated Score Part III: The Return of the King] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170407054056/http://www.tolkiendil.com/_media/divertissements/adaptations/films/sda_3_livret_de_presentation_de_la_bo_en_anglais_.pdf |date=7 April 2017 }}, pp. 15, 50.</ref>

Actors Billy Boyd, Viggo Mortensen and Liv Tyler also contributed to the film's music. Boyd sings on screen as Faramir charges towards Osgiliath, Mortensen sings on screen as he is crowned King, and in the Extended Edition Tyler sings as Aragorn heals Éowyn. [[Renée Fleming]], Ben Del Maestro, [[Sissel Kyrkjebø]] and [[James Galway]] contribute to the soundtrack as featured soloists. Fleming sings as Arwen has a vision of her son, and when Gollum recovers the One Ring. Del Maestro sings when Gandalf lights his staff to save fleeing Gondorian soldiers from Osgiliath as the Nazgûl attack and as the eagles arrive at the Black Gates. Galway plays the flute and whistle as Frodo and Sam climb Mount Doom and as they return to the shire. Sissel sings "Asea Aranion", which was originally meant to score the Houses of Healing scene. The end title song, "[[Into the West (song)|Into the West]]", was composed by Shore with lyrics by Fran Walsh. [[Annie Lennox]] (formerly of [[Eurythmics]]) performed it and also received songwriting credit. The song was partially inspired by the premature death from cancer of a young New Zealand filmmaker named [[Cameron Duncan]] who had befriended Peter Jackson.<ref name="Music"/>

== Release ==
=== Theatrical ===
After two years of attention and acclaim since the release of ''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring|The Fellowship of the Ring]]'', audience and critical anticipation for the final entry was extremely high. The world premiere was held in Wellington's [[Embassy Theatre, Wellington|Embassy Theatre]], on 1 December 2003, and was attended by the director and many of the stars. It was estimated that over 100,000 people lined the streets, more than a quarter of the city's population.<ref>{{cite news |last=Mercer |first=Phil |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/film/3253708.stm |title=How hobbits took over NZ's capital |work=BBC News |date=1 December 2003 |access-date=24 March 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115065013/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/film/3253708.stm |archive-date=15 January 2009}}</ref>

=== Home media ===
The theatrical edition of the film was released on [[VHS]] and [[DVD]] on 25 May 2004 by [[New Line Home Entertainment]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.today.com/popculture/return-king-out-dvd-may-25-wbna4472691|title='Return of the King' out on DVD on May 25|website=Today.com|date=7 March 2004|access-date=31 March 2023|archive-date=31 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331232930/https://www.today.com/popculture/return-king-out-dvd-may-25-wbna4472691|url-status=live}}</ref> The DVD was a 2-disc set with extras on the second disc. The theatrical DVD sets for the two previous films were released eight months after the films were released, but ''Return of the King''{{'}}s set was completed in five because it did not have to market a sequel (the previous films had to wait for footage of their sequels to become available for a ten-minute preview). However, it contained a seven-minute trailer of the entire trilogy.

''The Return of the King'' followed the precedent set by its predecessors by releasing an Extended Edition (252 minutes) on 14 December 2004 in the UK and US, and Blu-Ray in releasing in Extended Edition (264 minutes) and with new editing and added special effects and music, along with four commentaries and six hours of supplementary material.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Susman |first=Gary |date=9 June 2004 |title=Hobbits for the Holidays |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |url=https://ew.com/article/2004/06/09/king-extended-dvd-will-arrive-december/ |url-status=live |access-date=17 February 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070616014640/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0%2C%2C649118%2C00.html |archive-date=16 June 2007}}</ref> The final 11 minutes comprises a listing of the charter members of the official fan club who had paid for three-year charter membership.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patrizio |first=Andy |date=8 December 2004 |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (Special Extended Edition) |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/12/08/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-return-of-the-king-special-extended-edition |access-date=9 October 2023 |website=IGN |archive-date=13 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713005407/http://uk.dvd.ign.com/articles/571/571469p1.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=18 October 2001 |title=Peter Jackson Honors Fans with Their Names in Credits Of Film's DVDs – The Lord of the Rings Fan Club Launches Today |website=The One Ring |url=https://www.theonering.com/peter-jackson-honors-fans-with-their-names-in-credits-of-films-dvds-the-lord-of-the-rings-fan-club-launches-today/ |access-date=9 October 2023 |language=en-US |archive-date=23 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231023111650/https://www.theonering.com/peter-jackson-honors-fans-with-their-names-in-credits-of-films-dvds-the-lord-of-the-rings-fan-club-launches-today/ |url-status=live }}</ref> As with ''The Fellowship of the Ring'', and ''The Two Towers'', the Extended Edition was made available on both DVD and VHS.

A collectors' box set was also released, which included the Extended Set plus a sculpture of Minas Tirith and a bonus 50-minute music documentary DVD, ''Howard Shore: Creating The Lord of the Rings Symphony: A Composer's Journey Through Middle-earth''. The DVD has a [[DTS (sound system)|DTS-ES]] soundtrack. The DVD also features two humorous [[Easter egg (media)|Easter Eggs]], one where Dominic Monaghan plays a German interviewer with Elijah Wood via satellite and another where [[Vince Vaughn]] and [[Ben Stiller]] attempt to convince Jackson to make a sequel, originally shown at the 2004 MTV Movie Awards. Both can be accessed via a Ring icon on the last page of both Disc 1 and 2's scene indexes. In August 2006, a Limited Edition of ''The Return of the King'' was released. This Limited Edition contains two discs; the first is a [[DVD9|two-sided DVD]] containing both the Theatrical and Extended editions of the film. The second disc is a bonus disc that contains a new behind-the-scenes documentary.

The theatrical [[Blu-ray]] release was released in the United States on the sixth of April 2010, though only as part of the complete trilogy release disc.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/The-Lord-of-the-Rings-The-Motion-Picture-Trilogy-Blu-ray/5174/ |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Motion Picture Trilogy Blu-ray: Theatrical Editions |publisher=Blu-ray.com |access-date=18 February 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100225150750/http://www.blu-ray.com/movies/The-Lord-of-the-Rings-The-Motion-Picture-Trilogy-Blu-ray/5174/ |archive-date=25 February 2010}}</ref> The individual Blu-ray disc of ''The Return of the King'' was released on the fourteenth of September 2010 with the same special features as the complete trilogy release, except there was no digital copy.<ref>{{cite web |first=Juan |last=Calogne |url=http://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=4787 |title=Lord of the Rings Movies Get Separate Blu-ray editions |publisher=Blu-ray.com |date=23 June 2010 |access-date=28 November 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100626104403/http://www.blu-ray.com/news/?id=4787 |archive-date=26 June 2010}}</ref> The Extended Edition was released in the United States in June 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.amazon.com/Lord-Rings-Picture-Trilogy-Extended/dp/B0026L7H20 |title=Lord of the Rings Pre-order Now Available |website=Amazon |date=31 May 2011 |access-date=31 May 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110530090916/http://www.amazon.com/Lord-Rings-Picture-Trilogy-Extended/dp/B0026L7H20 |archive-date=30 May 2011}}</ref> It has a runtime of 263 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0167260/ |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King |publisher=IMDb.com |access-date=26 November 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121124120253/http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0167260/ |archive-date=24 November 2012}}</ref>

''The Return of the King'' was released in [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]] on 30 November 2020 in the United Kingdom and on 1 December 2020 in the United States, along with the other films of the trilogy, including both the theatrical and the extended editions of the films.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brew |first=Simon |url=https://www.filmstories.co.uk/news/lord-of-the-rings-and-the-hobbit-set-for-4k-release-in-december/ |title=Lord Of The Rings and The Hobbit set for 4K release in November |website=filmstories.co.uk |date=9 October 2020 |access-date=30 November 2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021183914/https://www.filmstories.co.uk/news/lord-of-the-rings-and-the-hobbit-set-for-4k-release-in-december/ |archive-date=21 October 2020}}</ref>

== Reception ==
=== Box office ===
''The Return of the King'' earned $377 million in the United States and Canada and $741.9 million in other countries for a worldwide total of $1.118 billion in its initial release.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2003/|title=2003 Worldwide Box Office|website=Box Office Mojo|access-date=14 March 2024}}</ref> In the weekend of 20–22 February 2004, the film crossed the $1 billion mark,<ref>{{cite web|last=Kay |first=Jeremy|title=The Return Of The King passes $1bn at the box office|url=https://www.screendaily.com/the-return-of-the-king-passes-1bn-at-the-box-office/4017470.article|access-date=19 February 2022|website=Screen|language=en|archive-date=19 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119005017/https://www.screendaily.com/the-return-of-the-king-passes-1bn-at-the-box-office/4017470.article|url-status=live}}</ref> making it the second film in history to do so, after ''[[Titanic (1997 film)|Titanic]]'' in 1998. Worldwide, it is the [[List of highest-grossing films|27th highest-grossing film of all time]] when not adjusted for inflation,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/chart/top_lifetime_gross/?area=XWW |title=All Time Top Lifetime Grosses Worldwide |work=boxofficemojo.com |access-date=8 March 2023 |archive-date=12 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210412074056/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/chart/top_lifetime_gross/?area=XWW |url-status=live }}</ref> the [[2003 in film|highest-grossing film of 2003]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?view2=worldwide&yr=2003&p=.htm |title=2003 Yearly Box Office Results – Box Office Mojo |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090824224736/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?view2=worldwide&yr=2003&p=.htm |archive-date=24 August 2009 }}</ref> the [[2000s in film|second highest-grossing film of the 2000s]], the highest-grossing entry in [[The Lord of the Rings (film series)|''The Lord of the Rings'' trilogy]], and the highest-grossing film ever to be released by [[New Line Cinema]].<ref name="trilogy">{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/franchises/chart/?id=lordoftherings.htm |title=The Lord of the Rings |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720052657/http://boxofficemojo.com/franchises/chart/?id=lordoftherings.htm |archive-date=20 July 2014}}</ref> It held the record as [[Time Warner]]{{'}}s highest-grossing film worldwide for eight years until it was surpassed by ''[[Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2]]'' in 2011.<ref name="TimeWarner">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/harry-potter-deathly-hallows-part-220419 |first=Pamela |last=McClintock |title='Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 2' Becomes No. 3 Film of All Time at Box Office |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=8 August 2011 |access-date=23 December 2020 |archive-date=28 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128142109/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/harry-potter-deathly-hallows-part-220419 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Box Office Mojo]] estimates that the film had sold over 61 million tickets in the US in its initial theatrical run.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=31 May 2016 |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=returnoftheking.htm&adjust_yr=1&p=.htm |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003) |website=Box Office Mojo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030615/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=returnoftheking.htm&adjust_yr=1&p=.htm |archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

In the US and Canada, it is the 27th highest-grossing film,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/domestic.htm |title=All Time Domestic Box Office Results |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121101065311/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/alltime/domestic.htm |archive-date=1 November 2012}}</ref> the highest-grossing 2003 film,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?yr=2003&p=.htm |title=2003 Yearly Box Office Results – Box Office Mojo |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001050235/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/yearly/chart/?yr=2003&p=.htm |archive-date=1 October 2007}}</ref> and the highest-grossing entry in ''The Lord of the Rings'' trilogy.<ref name="trilogy"/> The film set an opening Wednesday record with $34 million.<ref name="opening">{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1284&p=.htm |title='Return of the King' Rakes in $57.6M Worldwide on Opening Day |date=18 December 2003 |first=Brandon |last=Gray |website=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=20 June 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120215035403/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1284&p=.htm |archive-date=15 February 2012}}</ref> This record was first surpassed by ''[[Spider-Man 2]]'' in 2004 and ranks as the seventh largest Wednesday opening.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/article/ed2322924548/|title='Spider-Man 2' Amazes on Opening Day|date=1 July 2004|first=Brandon|last=Gray|publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201230012107/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/article/ed2322924548/|archive-date=30 December 2020|url-status=live|access-date=30 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/days/?page=wed&p=.htm |title=Opening Wednesday Records at the Box Office |website=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=15 June 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110623165925/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/alltime/days/?page=wed&p=.htm |archive-date=23 June 2011}}</ref> Additionally, it was ranked as the highest December opening day, holding that record for less than a decade before getting dethroned by ''[[The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey]]'' in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=3586&p=.htm|title=Friday Report: 'The Hobbit' Steals $37.5 Million|publisher=Box Office Mojo|first=Ray|last=Subers|access-date=24 December 2012|date=14 December 2012|archive-date=18 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121218071603/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=3586&p=.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> The film opened a day earlier for a midnight showing and accounted for about $8&nbsp;million. This was nearly twice the first-day total of ''The Fellowship of the Ring'' — which earned $18.2&nbsp;million on its opening day in 2001 — as well as a significant increase over ''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers|The Two Towers]]'' — which earned $26.1&nbsp;million on its debut in 2002. Part of the grosses came from the Trilogy Tuesday event, in which the Extended Editions of the two previous films were played on 16 December before the first midnight screening. For two years, ''The Return of the King'' would hold the record for having the highest midnight screenings gross until 2005 when it was given to ''[[Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1824&p=.htm|title='Sith' Destroys Single Day Record|first=Brandon|last=Gray|publisher=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=5 October 2014|archive-date=6 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006073452/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1824&p=.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> The film went on to make an opening weekend of $72.6 million making it the second-highest opening weekend for a New Line Cinema film, behind ''[[Austin Powers in Goldmember]]''.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=returnoftheking.htm |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King |website=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=15 June 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110621192103/http://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=returnoftheking.htm |archive-date=21 June 2011}}</ref> In addition, it had the third-highest opening weekend of 2003, after ''[[The Matrix Reloaded]]'' and ''[[X2 (film)|X2]]''.<ref name="weekend">{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1286&p=.htm |title='King' of the World: $250M in 5 Days |date=22 December 2003 |first=Brandon |last=Gray |website=[[Box Office Mojo]] |access-date=20 June 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120619042637/http://boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=1286&p=.htm |archive-date=19 June 2012}}</ref> Overall, the film ranked number one at the domestic box office during its first weekend, beating out ''[[Mona Lisa Smile]]'', ''[[Something's Gotta Give (film)|Something's Gotta Give]]'', ''[[The Last Samurai]]'' and ''[[Stuck on You (film)|Stuck on You]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2003-dec-22-et-munoz22-story.html|title='Rings' saves biggest for last}}</ref> With a total gross of $125.1 million, the film had the biggest five-day Wednesday opening of all time, surpassing the previous record held by ''[[Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title='Return of the King' tops box office |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/2003/12/22/Return-of-the-King-tops-box-office/4371072069200/ |access-date=6 March 2022 |work=[[United Press International]] |date=22 December 2003 |archive-date=27 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220227212707/https://www.upi.com/Archives/2003/12/22/Return-of-the-King-tops-box-office/4371072069200/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It would hold this record for five months until it was beaten by ''[[Shrek 2]]'' the following May.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.today.com/popculture/shrek-2-success-spawn-more-sequels-wbna5054265|title='Shrek 2' success to spawn more sequels|website=Today.com|date=25 May 2004|access-date=13 March 2022|archive-date=13 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313161521/https://www.today.com/popculture/shrek-2-success-spawn-more-sequels-wbna5054265|url-status=live}}</ref> Its Friday-Sunday opening weekend was a record-high for December (first surpassed by ''[[I Am Legend (film)|I Am Legend]]'').<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/weekends/month/?mo=12&p=.htm |title=Top December Opening Weekends at the Box Office |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110302100817/http://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/weekends/month/?mo=12&p=.htm |archive-date=2 March 2011}}</ref> The film also set single-day records for Christmas Day and New Year's Day (both first surpassed by ''[[Meet the Fockers]]'').<ref>{{cite web|title=Single Day Records: High Grossing Movies on Christmas Day|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/days/holidays.htm?page=xmas&p=.htm|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120701224319/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/alltime/days/holidays.htm?page=xmas&p=.htm|archive-date=1 July 2012|work=boxofficemojo.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/days/holidays.htm?page=newyrs&p=.htm |title=Single Day Records: High Grossing Movies on New Year's Day |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100205134131/http://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/days/holidays.htm?page=newyrs&p=.htm |archive-date=5 February 2010}}</ref> 

Outside the US and Canada, it is the 17th highest-grossing film,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/alltime/world/?pagenum=1&sort=osgross&order=DESC&p=.htm |title=All Time Worldwide Box Office Grosses |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121030220609/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/alltime/world/?pagenum=1&sort=osgross&order=DESC&p=.htm |archive-date=30 October 2012}}</ref> the highest-grossing 2003 film<ref>{{cite web |url=https://boxofficemojo.com/intl/weekend/yearly/?yr=2003&p=.htm |title=2003 Overseas Total Yearly Box Office Results |work=boxofficemojo.com |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121029123034/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/intl/weekend/yearly/?yr=2003&p=.htm |archive-date=29 October 2012}}</ref> and the highest-grossing film of the series.<ref name="trilogy"/> On its first day (Wednesday, 17 December 2003), the film earned $23.5&nbsp;million from 19 countries<ref name="opening"/> and it set an opening-weekend record outside the US and Canada with $125.9&nbsp;million during the five-day weekend as a whole. The combined total gross increased to $250.1 million, making it the highest worldwide opening weekend at the time, knocking out ''[[The Matrix Revolutions]]''.<ref name="weekend"/> It set opening-day records in thirteen of them, including the United Kingdom, Germany, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain, Greece, Switzerland, Scandinavia (as well as separately in Sweden, Finland, Norway and Denmark), Mexico, Chile and Puerto Rico.<ref name="opening"/><ref name="weekend"/> It set opening-weekend records in the United Kingdom ($26.5&nbsp;million in five days), Germany, Spain, Sweden, Denmark and Switzerland. In Singapore, it surpassed ''[[Finding Nemo]]'' to become the country's top-grossing film of 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.screendaily.com/rings-reigns-as-top-singapore-film-of-2003/4016681.article|title=Rings reigns as top Singapore film of 2003|access-date=23 March 2022|archive-date=22 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220322173225/https://www.screendaily.com/rings-reigns-as-top-singapore-film-of-2003/4016681.article|url-status=live}}</ref> In New Zealand, where filming took place, the film set opening day, opening weekend, single-day, Friday gross, Saturday gross and Sunday gross records with $1.7&nbsp;million in four days.<ref name="weekend"/>

The substantial increase in initial box office totals caused optimistic studio executives to forecast that ''The Return of the King'' would surpass ''The Two Towers'' in total earnings. If this proved to be true, then this would be the first blockbuster trilogy for each successive film to earn more at the box office than its predecessor, when all three films were blockbuster successes. ''The Return of the King'' has helped ''The Lord of the Rings'' franchise to become the highest-grossing motion picture trilogy worldwide of all time with over $2.9 billion, beating other notable series such as the original ''[[Star Wars original trilogy|Star Wars Trilogy]]'', and became New Line's highest grossing release.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/lord-rings-movies-records-box-office-awards/ |title=Every Record Lord Of The Rings Broke (& Which Ones The Movies Still Hold) |publisher=Screen Rant |date=6 March 2020 |access-date=31 May 2021 |archive-date=11 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111153334/https://screenrant.com/lord-rings-movies-records-box-office-awards/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Following subsequent reissues, the film has grossed $387 million in the United States and Canada and $761 million in the rest of the world for a worldwide total of $1.149.4 billion.<ref name="BOM" />

These figures do not include income from DVD sales, TV rights, etc. It has been estimated<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.timewarner.com/corp/businesses/detail/new_line_cinema/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070126130514/http://www.timewarner.com/corp/businesses/detail/new_line_cinema/index.html |title=Time Warner: New Line Cinema |date=2 August 2006 |archive-date=26 January 2007 |work=Time Warner}}</ref> that the gross income from non-box office sales and merchandise has been at least equal to the box office for all three films. If this is so, the total gross income for the trilogy would be in the region of $6&nbsp;billion following an investment of $300&nbsp;million ($426&nbsp;million including marketing costs).

=== Critical response ===
On the [[review aggregator]] website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], ''The Return of the King'' holds an approval rating of 94% based on 304 reviews. The website's critics consensus reads, "Visually breathtaking and emotionally powerful, ''The Lord of the Rings – The Return of the King'' is a moving and satisfying conclusion to a great trilogy."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_lord_of_the_rings_the_return_of_the_king |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200517125821/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_lord_of_the_rings_the_return_of_the_king |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003) |website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |archive-date=17 May 2020 |access-date=14 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[weighted average]], gives the film a score of 94 out of 100 based on 41 reviews, indicating "universal acclaim".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-return-of-the-king |title=The Lord of the Rings: Return of the King |website=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=28 April 2020 |archive-date=11 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111202334/https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-return-of-the-king |url-status=live }}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film a rare average grade of "A+" on an A+ to F scale,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |title=Cinemascore |website=[[CinemaScore]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220122629/https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |archive-date=20 December 2018 |access-date=22 March 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref> the highest grade in the trilogy.

Alan Morrison of ''[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]'' gave the film a perfect score of five stars. In his review, he called the film "the resounding climax to a landmark in cinema history" and praised how Peter Jackson had "kept the momentum of the series rolling on and on through the traditionally 'difficult' middle part and 'weak' finale, delivering a climax to the story that's neater and more affecting than what Tolkien managed on the printed page." Morrison also mentioned how fans of the films "who have walked beside these heroes every step of the way on such a long journey deserve the emotional pay-off as well as the action peaks, and they will be genuinely touched as the final credits roll."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/lord-rings-return-king-review/ |title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King Review |date=January 2001 |publisher=www.empireonline.com |access-date=1 August 2021 |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117201544/https://www.empireonline.com/movies/reviews/lord-rings-return-king-review/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Elvis Mitchell]] for ''[[The New York Times]]'' lauded the acting, the craft of the technical crew, and Jackson's direction, describing ''The Return of the King'' as "a meticulous and prodigious vision made by a director who was not hamstrung by heavy use of computer special-effects imagery."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Mitchell|first=Elvis|date=16 December 2003|title=FILM REVIEW; Triumph Tinged With Regret in Middle Earth|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/12/16/movies/film-review-triumph-tinged-with-regret-in-middle-earth.html|access-date=13 February 2022|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=1 December 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091201041724/https://www.nytimes.com/2003/12/16/movies/film-review-triumph-tinged-with-regret-in-middle-earth.html|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' gave the film three and a half stars out of four, saying that it is "such a crowning achievement, such a visionary use of all the tools of special effects, such a pure spectacle, that it can be enjoyed even by those who have not seen the first two films." Talking about the whole trilogy, Ebert said that he admired it "more as a whole than in its parts", and that ''The Return of the King'' certified ''The Lord of the Rings'' as "a work of bold ambition in a time of cinematic timidity".<ref>{{cite web|last=Ebert|first=Roger|date=17 December 2003|title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King – Roger Ebert's review|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/lord-of-the-rings-the-return-of-the-king-2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603053641/http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/lord-of-the-rings-the-return-of-the-king-2003|archive-date=3 June 2013|access-date=13 February 2022|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]}}</ref> In his review for ''[[The Times]]'', James Christopher praised ''The Return of the King'' as "everything a Ring fan could possibly wish for, and much more", and described ''The Lord of the Rings'' as "the greatest film trilogy ever mounted, with some of the most amazing action sequences committed to celluloid".<ref>{{Cite news|last=Christopher|first=James|date=11 December 2003|title=The Return of the King Review|language=en|work=The Times|url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/uk-travel/england/london-travel/the-return-of-the-king-review-qg3nhdfkz9z|access-date=13 February 2022|issn=0140-0460|archive-date=12 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220212122547/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/the-return-of-the-king-review-qg3nhdfkz9z|url-status=live}}</ref> Nev Pierce for the [[BBC]] gave the film five stars out of five, judging it to be the best chapter of the trilogy, since it combined "the 'ooh' factor of ''Fellowship'' with the zippy action of ''Towers''". Pierce described ''The Return of the King'' as "Majestic, moving, and immense", and "an astonishing piece of storytelling".<ref>{{cite web|last=Pierce|first=Nev|date=18 December 2003|title=BBC – Stoke and Staffordshire Films – The Lord of the Rings: Return of the King Review|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/stoke/films/reviews/g_m/lotr_return_of_the_king.shtml|access-date=13 February 2022|website=BBC|archive-date=11 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211234410/https://www.bbc.co.uk/stoke/films/reviews/g_m/lotr_return_of_the_king.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Philip French]], reviewing it for ''[[The Observer]]'', lauded the narrative force, the battle scenes, the language, and the visual style of the film, which he related to "the swirling battle paintings of [[Albrecht Altdorfer]]" and "[[Claude Lorrain]]'s elegiac paintings of maritime departures inspired by classical poets." French wrote about the whole trilogy "Jackson's ''Lord of the Rings'' is indeed a very fine achievement, moving, involving and, to many people, even inspiring. It redeems the debased cinematic notion of the epic."<ref>{{cite web|last=French|first=Philip|date=14 December 2003|title=Film of the week 2: It's that Gondor moment...|url=http://www.theguardian.com/theobserver/2003/dec/14/features.review17|access-date=13 February 2022|website=The Guardian|language=en|archive-date=13 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220213114205/https://www.theguardian.com/theobserver/2003/dec/14/features.review17|url-status=live}}</ref>

In her review for ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'', [[Lisa Schwarzbaum]] gave the film an A grade, and wrote "The conclusion of Peter Jackson's masterwork is passionate and literate, detailed and expansive, and it's conceived with a risk-taking flair for old-fashioned movie magic at its most precious ... as he has done throughout, the director paces scenes of action, intimacy, and even panoramic, geographical grandeur ... with the control of a superb choreographer." Schwarzbaum also said of the whole series "I can't think of another film trilogy that ends in such glory, or another monumental work of sustained storytelling that surges ahead with so much inventiveness and ardor."<ref>url=https://ew.com/article/2003/12/19/lord-rings-return-king-3/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220213163419/https://ew.com/article/2003/12/19/lord-rings-return-king-3/ |date=13 February 2022 }}</ref> [[Richard Corliss]] of ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' named ''The Return of the King'' the best film of the year<ref>{{cite magazine |author=[[Richard Corliss]] |title=The Best Movies |magazine=Time |url=http://www.time.com/time/bestandworst/2003/story.html |access-date=9 November 2007 |date=18 December 2003 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071111183357/http://www.time.com/time/bestandworst/2003/story.html |archive-date=11 November 2007}}</ref> and described the whole trilogy as "The film event of the millennium".<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Corliss|first=Richard|date=8 December 2003|title=Seven Holiday Treats|url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,1101031215-557084,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071114002753/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,1101031215-557084,00.html|archive-date=14 November 2007|access-date=13 February 2022|magazine=Time}}</ref> [[Joe Morgenstern]], for ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', wrote "Never has a filmmaker aimed higher, or achieved more. The third and last instalment of the screen epic based on J.R.R. Tolkien's literary classic redefines – steeply upward – the very notion of a major motion picture."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Morgenstern|first=Joe|date=19 December 2003|title=Now That's an Epic: Jackson Conjures Magical Ending To 'Lord of the Rings' Trilogy|language=en-US|work=The Wall Street Journal|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB107179510887385500|access-date=13 February 2022|issn=0099-9660|archive-date=12 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220212123125/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB107179510887385500|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Peter Bradshaw]], who had been less enthusiastic about the first two chapters of the trilogy,<ref>{{cite web|last=Bradshaw|first=Peter|date=14 December 2001|title=The Lord of the Rings: the Fellowship of the Ring|url=http://www.theguardian.com/film/2001/dec/14/lordoftherings1|access-date=13 February 2022|website=The Guardian|language=en|archive-date=20 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120064030/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2001/dec/14/lordoftherings1|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Bradshaw|first=Peter|date=13 December 2002|title=The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers|url=http://www.theguardian.com/culture/2002/dec/13/artsfeatures.lordoftherings|access-date=13 February 2022|website=The Guardian|language=en|archive-date=12 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220212171253/https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2002/dec/13/artsfeatures.lordoftherings|url-status=live}}</ref> gave ''The Return of the King'' four stars out of five in his review for ''[[The Guardian]]'', commenting "I started the series an atheist and finished an agnostic". Bradshaw wrote of the film "Technically it really is superb", and commented "Hours after watching the film, I can close my eyes and see those incredible battle scenes pulsing and throbbing in my skull ... Maybe [[Kurosawa]]'s battles will one day be described as proto-Jacksonian".<ref>{{cite web|last=Bradshaw|first=Peter|date=19 December 2003|title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King|url=http://www.theguardian.com/film/2003/dec/19/lordoftherings|access-date=13 February 2022|website=The Guardian|language=en|archive-date=3 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203182459/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2003/dec/19/lordoftherings|url-status=live}}</ref>

Some critics had negative opinions of the film. Tom Charity observes in [[Time Out (magazine)|Time Out]], "Some story strands are crudely abbreviated; others fail to develop elements that were already well-established. Given the inordinate running time, it's hard to avoid the feeling that we've already been here, done this."<ref>{{cite web|last=Charity|first=Tom|date=2007|title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King|url= https://www.timeout.com/film/reviews/80706/the_lord_of_the_rings-the_return_of_the_king.html|access-date=3 June 2024|website=Time Out|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071104042644/https://www.timeout.com/film/reviews/80706/the_lord_of_the_rings-the_return_of_the_king.html |archive-date=4 November 2007 |language=en|url-status=live}}</ref> Jonathan Romney noted in [[The Independent]], "[T]here's something not quite palatable about all these intrepid, largely beautiful Europeans boldly fending off the nameless, numberless hordes from the other side of the world, legions of dark-skinned sans-culottes with tribal drums. ... Aside from this, there's plenty to be offended by on an aesthetic level: the film's self-important solemnity, its hyperbolic over-insistence. ... [T]here are no empty spaces, no gaps for thought, no real stimulus to the viewer's imagination. The film has no idea when to stop, either, with its multiple codas and final dying fall into beatific cosiness."<ref>{{cite web|last=Romney|first=Jonathan|date=21 December 2003|title=The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King – OK, Peter. Message received|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/reviews/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-return-of-the-king-83691.html|access-date=3 June 2024|website=The Independent|language=en}}</ref> And Antonia Quirke in the [[Evening Standard]] opined, "Viggo Mortensen's Aragorn is the good king of the title, and while the actor may look fetching in a crown and cloak, he doesn't have half of the gravitas of Sean Bean's Boromir in the first film. Director Peter Jackson has been all but deified for his work on this particular ring cycle, but there is not much personality behind the camera here, merely rampant enthusiasm."<ref>{{cite web|last=Quirke|first=Antonia|date=5 April 2012|title=Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King|url= https://www.standard.co.uk/showbiz/celebrity-news/lord-of-the-rings-the-return-of-the-king-7380983.html|access-date=3 June 2024|website=The Standard|language=en}}</ref>

The most common criticism of ''The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King'' was its running time, particularly the epilogue; even rave reviews for the film commented on its length. [[Joel Siegel]] of ''[[Good Morning America]]'' said in his review for the film (which he gave an 'A'): "If it didn't take forty-five minutes to end, it'd be my best picture of the year. As it is, it's just one of the great achievements in film history."<ref>{{cite news |author=[[Joel Siegel]] |title=Jackson Brings Lord of the Rings to Historic Completion |publisher=ABC News |date=19 December 2003 |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/JoelSiegel/story?id=116553&page=1 |access-date=16 February 2007 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060313130326/http://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/JoelSiegel/story?id=116553&page=1 |archive-date=13 March 2006}}</ref>

In February 2004, a few months following release, the film was voted eighth on ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]''{{'}}s ''100 Greatest Movies of All Time'', compiled from readers' top ten lists. This forced the magazine to abandon its policy of only allowing films being older than a year to be eligible.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=The 100 Greatest Movies of All Time |page=96 |magazine=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |date=30 January 2004}}</ref> In 2007, ''[[Total Film]]'' named ''The Return of the King'' the third best film of the past decade (''Total Film''{{'}}s publication time), behind ''[[The Matrix]]'' and ''[[Fight Club]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Ten Greatest Films of the Past Decade |page=98 |magazine=[[Total Film]] |date=April 2007}}</ref> In July 2025, it ranked number 15 on the "Readers' Choice" edition of ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century."<ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |date=2 July 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref>

=== Accolades ===
{{main|List of accolades received by The Lord of the Rings film series|l1=List of accolades received by ''The Lord of the Rings'' film series}}

The film was nominated for eleven [[Academy Award]]s: [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]], [[Academy Award for Best Original Score|Best Original Score]], [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]], [[Academy Award for Best Visual Effects|Best Visual Effects]], [[Academy Award for Best Production Design|Best Art Direction]], [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design|Best Costume Design]], [[Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling|Best Make-up]], [[Academy Award for Best Sound|Best Sound Mixing]] and [[Academy Award for Best Film Editing|Best Film Editing]]. At the [[76th Academy Awards]] in 2004, the film won all the categories for which it was nominated and it shares the record for highest Academy Award totals along with ''Titanic'' (which also starred Bernard Hill) and ''[[Ben-Hur (1959 film)|Ben-Hur]]'', and holding the record for the highest clean sweep at the Oscars, surpassing the nine awards earned by both ''[[Gigi (1958 film)|Gigi]]'' and ''[[The Last Emperor]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title="Lord of the Rings" Wins 11 Oscars |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/Oscars2005/lord-rings-wins-11-oscars/story?id=116560 |access-date=9 July 2013 |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |publisher=[[The Walt Disney Company]] |date=1 March 2004 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224002917/http://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/Oscars2005/lord-rings-wins-11-oscars/story?id=116560 |archive-date=24 February 2014 }}</ref><ref name="Oscars2004">{{cite web |url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/legacy/ceremony/76th-winners.html |title=The 76th Academy Awards (2004) Nominees and Winners |access-date=20 November 2011 |work=oscars.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929190645/http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/legacy/ceremony/76th-winners.html |archive-date=29 September 2012}}</ref> It was the first fantasy film to win the Academy Award for Best Picture. It also was the last movie for 14 years to win the Academy Award for Best Picture without being chosen as one of the top ten films of the year by the [[National Board of Review]], until the release of ''[[The Shape of Water]]'' in 2017.

The film won four [[Golden Globe Award|Golden Globes]] (including Best Picture for Drama and Best Director),<ref>{{cite news|last=Crean|first=Ellen|date=25 January 2004|title=Golden Globe Spins For 'Rings'|publisher=CBS News|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/golden-globe-spins-for-rings/|url-status=live|access-date=10 March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110129233607/http://www.cbsnews.com/stories/2004/01/25/entertainment/main595626.shtml|archive-date=29 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna4057351 |title=Hail to the 'King' at Golden Globes |publisher=MSNBC |date=26 January 2004 |access-date=10 March 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120925064231/http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/4057351/ns/today-entertainment/ |archive-date=25 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|last=Armstrong|first=Mark|date=25 January 2004|title='Rings,' 'Translation' Rule the Globes|url=http://www.people.com/people/article/0,,627488,00.html|url-status=dead|magazine=People|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309094432/http://www.people.com/people/article/0%2C%2C627488%2C00.html|archive-date=9 March 2011|access-date=10 March 2011}}</ref> five [[British Academy of Film and Television Arts|BAFTAs]], two [[MTV Movie Awards]], two [[Grammy Award]]s, nine [[Saturn Award]]s, the [[New York Film Critics Circle]] award for Best Picture, the [[Nebula Award for Best Script]], and the [[Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation|Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation, Long Form]].

'''''The Passion of the Christ''''' is a 2004 American [[epic film|epic]] [[List of films based on the Bible|biblical]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama film]] co-produced and directed by [[Mel Gibson]] from a screenplay he wrote with [[Benedict Fitzgerald]]. It is the first installment of [[The Passion of the Christ (film series)|''The Passion of the Christ'' film series]]. The film stars [[Jim Caviezel]] as [[Jesus]], [[Maia Morgenstern]] as [[Mary, Mother of Jesus|his mother Mary]], and [[Monica Bellucci]] as [[Mary Magdalene]]. It depicts the arrest, trial and [[crucifixion of Jesus]], largely according to the [[canonical gospels]] as well as additional accounts such as the [[The Dolorous Passion of Our Lord Jesus Christ|purported mystical visions]] by [[Anne Catherine Emmerich]] and the [[Friday of Sorrows]].<ref name="America">{{cite magazine |last=O'Malley |first=John |title=A Movie, a Mystic, a Spiritual Tradition |magazine=[[America (Jesuit magazine)|America]] |date=March 15, 2004 |url=http://americamagazine.org/content/article.cfm?article_id%3D3481%26comments%3D1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005193623/http://americamagazine.org/content/article.cfm?article_id=3481&comments=1 |archive-date=October 5, 2011}}</ref>{{sfn|Corley|Webb|2004|pp=160-161}}<ref name="Garcia">{{cite book |last=Gracia |first=Jorge J. E. |title=Mel Gibson's Passion and philosophy |year=2004 |page=145 |publisher=Open Court |isbn=0-8126-9571-2}}</ref><ref name="Dimare">{{cite book |editor-last=Dimare |editor-first=Philip C. |title=Movies in American History: An Encyclopedia |year=2011 |page=909 |publisher=Abc-Clio |isbn=978-1-59884-296-8}}</ref>

The film primarily covers the final twelve hours before Jesus Christ's death, known as "the Passion". It begins with [[Agony in the Garden|the Agony]] in the [[Garden of Olives]] (i.e., Gethsemane), continues with the betrayal of [[Judas Iscariot]], the [[Flagellation of Christ]], the suffering of Mary as prophesied by [[Simeon (Gospel of Luke)|Simeon]], the [[Crucifixion of Jesus|crucifixion and death of Jesus]], and ends with a brief depiction of [[Resurrection of Jesus|his resurrection]]. The narrative is interspersed with moments in Jesus's life, such as [[the Last Supper]] and [[the Sermon on the Mount]], and moments of Jesus' early life. The film was mostly shot in Italy.<ref>[http://www.movie-locations.com/movies/p/Passion-Of-The-Christ.php "The Passion of the Christ".] ''Movie-Locations''</ref> The dialogue is entirely in reconstructed [[Jewish Palestinian Aramaic|Aramaic]], [[Hebrew]], and [[Latin]]. Although Gibson was initially against it, the film is subtitled.

''The Passion of the Christ'' was released theatrically by [[Newmarket Films]] on February 25, 2004. Critical reception was polarized; some critics called the film a religious and holy experience, praising the performances, Mel Gibson’s direction, production values, and [[John Debney]]'s score, others criticized its graphic depiction of violence, arguing that the brutality was excessive, while some found it [[Antisemitism|antisemitic]], prompting widespread debate and controversy. 

The film grossed $622.3 million worldwide against a $30 million budget,<ref name="Numbers update"/> and became the [[2004 in film#Highest-grossing films|fifth highest-grossing film of 2004]] internationally at the end of its theatrical run.<ref name="BOM"/> It is the highest-grossing [[Christian film industry|Christian film]] of all time (inflation unadjusted), as well as the [[List of highest-grossing independent films|highest-grossing independent film of all time]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/genres/chart/?id=christian.htm|title=Christian Movies at the Box Office|website=Box Office Mojo|access-date=April 23, 2019|archive-date=August 29, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829104513/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/genres/chart/?id=christian.htm|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Barker |first=Stephen |date=October 17, 2020 |title=The 10 Highest-Grossing Independent Films Of All Time |url=https://screenrant.com/highest-grossing-independent-films-ever-indie-movies/ |access-date=October 11, 2022 |website=ScreenRant |language=en-US |archive-date=October 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221011095903/https://screenrant.com/highest-grossing-independent-films-ever-indie-movies/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[List of highest-grossing biographical films#Highest-grossing biopics|fifth highest-grossing biographical film]]. It was the highest-grossing [[Motion Picture Association film rating system#MPA film ratings|R-rated film]] in the US, at $370.8 million, a record which remained unbroken for 20 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/chart/mpaa_title_lifetime_gross/?by_mpaa=R |title=Top Lifetime Grosses by MPAA Rating — R |website=Box Office Mojo |access-date=April 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405041957/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/chart/mpaa_title_lifetime_gross/?by_mpaa=R |archive-date=April 5, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Deadpool & Wolverine" /> It received multiple awards and nominations including three nominations at the [[77th Academy Awards]] in 2005, for [[Academy Award for Best Makeup|Best Makeup]], [[Academy Award for Best Cinematography|Best Cinematography]], and [[Academy Award for Best Original Score|Best Original Score]].<ref>{{Citation|last=Gibson|first=Mel|title=The Passion of the Christ|date=February 25, 2004|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0335345/awards?ref_=tt_awd|access-date=September 1, 2016|archive-date=January 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170128100933/http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0335345/awards?ref_=tt_awd|url-status=live}}</ref> 

Two sequels, ''[[The Resurrection of the Christ: Part One]]'' and [[The Resurrection of the Christ: Part Two|''Part Two'']], are due to be released in 2027 and 2028, with a new cast.

==Plot==
<!-- Per WP:FILMPLOT, plot summaries for film articles should not exceed 700 words. -->
On the night of [[Passover]], [[Jesus]] [[Agony in the Garden|prays]] in [[Gethsemane]], asking for his father to protect him as his followers [[Saint Peter|Peter]], [[James the Great|James]] and [[John the Apostle|John]] fall asleep. After Jesus rebukes [[Satan]] for tempting him to escape his fate, another of his followers, [[Judas Iscariot]], having been bribed by [[Caiaphas]] and the [[Pharisees]] with [[thirty pieces of silver]], leads temple guards to the garden and [[Kiss of Judas|betrays Jesus' identity]]. The guards [[Arrest of Jesus|arrest Jesus]] and beat him on the way to the [[Sanhedrin]]. John informs Jesus' mother, [[Mary, mother of Jesus|Mary]], and [[Mary Magdalene]] of the arrest, and they reunite with Peter, who has followed Jesus and his captors.

Caiaphas [[Sanhedrin trial of Jesus|tries Jesus]], where false accusations are made against him, while Pharisees who secretly support Jesus and object to the trial are expelled from the court. Jesus claims he is the divine [[Son of man (Christianity)|Son of Man]], causing Caiaphas to angrily condemn him to death for blasphemy. As Jesus is brutally beaten, Peter is confronted by the mob and he [[Denial of Peter|denies]] being a follower of Jesus; remembering Jesus precisely predicted this, he weeps bitterly. Guilt-ridden, Judas attempts to return the money to have Jesus freed, but is refused by the priests. Haunted by [[demon]]s in the form of children, Judas hangs himself outside [[Jerusalem]].

Jesus is brought to be condemned to death by [[Pontius Pilate]], the Roman governor of [[Judaea (Roman province)|Judea]]. At the urging of his wife, [[Pontius Pilate's wife|Claudia]], [[Pilate's court|Pilate questions Jesus]] and finds no fault in him, transferring him to the court of [[Herod Antipas]] since Jesus is from Antipas' domain of [[Galilee]]. When Antipas deems Jesus harmless and returns him, Pilate offers the crowd the choice of freeing Jesus or the convicted murderer [[Barabbas]]. When the crowd demands Barabbas be freed and Jesus crucified, Pilate attempts to appease the crowd by ordering Jesus flogged, and he is [[Flagellation of Christ|brutally scourged]] by the Roman guards. Using cloths provided by Claudia, Mother Mary and Mary Magdalene clean up his blood, where Mary Magdalene reminisces on Jesus saving her from a [[stoning]]. 

The guards [[Mocking of Jesus|hurl insults at Jesus]] and place a [[crown of thorns]] on his head. Pilate presents him to the crowd and Caiphas, who all again demand that he be crucified. Unwilling to instigate unrest, Pilate orders Jesus' crucifixion, claiming no responsibility. Jesus carries a [[True Cross|heavy wooden cross]] on the [[Via Dolorosa|road]] to [[Calvary|Golgotha]] with two thieves, [[Penitent thief|Dismas]] and [[Impenitent thief|Gesmas]], following behind. [[Stations of the Cross|Along the way]], he is harassed by the guards and rampant mob, is momentarily comforted by his mother and replenished by [[Saint Veronica|a woman]] who wipes his bloodied face with [[Veil of Veronica|her veil]]. An unwilling [[Simon of Cyrene]] is pressed with helping Jesus carry the cross to Golgotha, where [[Crucifixion of Jesus|Jesus is crucified]] with Mary, Magdalene, John, and others witnessing.

Jesus [[Sayings of Jesus on the cross|prays to God]] to forgive his tormentors who mock him for not being able to come down from the cross, and he also provides salvation to Dismas, crucified beside him, for the latter’s faith and repentance, and comforts his own mother. Finally succumbing to his wounds, Jesus surrenders his spirit and dies. A single droplet of rain falls, triggering an earthquake which damages the [[Second Temple]] and rips the veil covering the [[Holy of Holies]], to the horror of Caiaphas and the Pharisees. The guards seek to expedite the thieves' deaths by breaking their legs and, upon seeing Jesus dead, order tribune [[Longinus|Cassius]] to [[Holy Lance|spear his side]] to be sure. As Satan screams in defeat in a distorted [[hellscape]], Jesus' body is taken down from the cross and [[Burial of Jesus|entombed]]; on the third day, [[Resurrection of Jesus|he rises from the dead]] and exits the tomb.
